title: Manager, Applied AI Engineering  (Enterprise)
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Technical Success team helps OpenAI’s customers realize meaningful and sustained value from our technology. We partner with customers throughout their journey—from initial exploration and solution design to production implementation and organization-wide adoption.

Applied AI Engineers serve as trusted technical partners to customer executives, engineering teams, product leaders, security organizations, and transformation teams. They combine deep technical judgment with strong customer instincts, translating frontier AI capabilities into secure, reliable systems and durable business outcomes.


About the Role

We are seeking a Manager to build, lead, and develop a high-performing team of Applied AI Engineers supporting our enterprise customers.

You will be accountable for the technical success of a broad and strategically important customer portfolio. You will help your team identify high-value opportunities, design and deploy production-grade AI systems, navigate complex technical and organizational constraints, and expand successful implementations across workflows, teams, and business units.

This role requires technical depth, people leadership, customer judgment, and operational rigor. You should be comfortable coaching engineers through architecture and evaluation decisions, engaging directly in high-stakes customer situations, and collaborating with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and Legal.

You will also help define how we serve enterprise customers at scale by developing effective coverage models, reusable implementation patterns, technical enablement, escalation mechanisms, and systems for turning field insights into high-quality product feedback.


In This Role, You Will

  • Build, manage, and develop a high-performing team of Applied AI Engineers supporting large and complex enterprise customers.

  • Own the quality and impact of the team’s work across solution design, implementation, production readiness, adoption, and expansion.

  • Coach the team through decisions involving architecture, model selection, evaluations, reliability, latency, safety, security, governance, and cost.

  • Establish an operating model for prioritizing accounts and engagements according to customer needs, strategic value, technical complexity, and potential for repeatable impact.

  • Serve as a senior technical escalation point during critical launches, production incidents, complex integrations, and high-stakes customer decisions.

  • Partner with customer executives and technical leaders to connect implementation decisions to measurable business and operational outcomes.

  • Help customers progress from experimentation to production systems and sustained adoption across their organizations.

  • Partner closely with Sales and Solutions Engineering to create continuity throughout the customer lifecycle and maintain shared accountability for customer success.

  • Translate customer needs and recurring implementation challenges into actionable feedback for Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and other internal teams.

  • Identify scalable market patterns, distinguish them from bespoke requests, and advocate for investments that can benefit multiple customers.

  • Develop reusable architectures, evaluation methods, playbooks, tooling, and enablement that improve time to value across the enterprise portfolio.

  • Establish mechanisms for measuring production implementations, adoption, customer outcomes, delivery quality, team capacity, and the impact of reusable work.

  • Hire thoughtfully, raise the technical and leadership bar, and foster a culture of accountability, curiosity, collaboration, inclusion, and continuous learning.

  • Represent OpenAI with credibility and sound judgment in conversations with senior customer and internal stakeholders.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

  • Have significant experience managing customer-facing technical teams, such as Applied AI Engineers, Solutions Architects, Forward Deployed Engineers, Customer Engineers, or Technical Account Managers.

  • Have built or led teams responsible for implementing complex software, data, machine learning, or AI systems in enterprise environments.

  • Maintain sufficient technical depth to evaluate architectures, ask incisive questions, challenge assumptions, and coach engineers through difficult implementation decisions.

  • Have experience taking AI, machine learning, or other technically complex systems from prototype to production.

  • Understand production-system requirements, including reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, evaluation, and operational readiness.

  • Have led teams through ambiguity, competing priorities, escalations, and rapidly evolving products or markets.

  • Can translate effectively among technical details, customer needs, product strategy, and business outcomes.

  • Have worked with large organizations involving multiple business units, stakeholder groups, procurement processes, or governance requirements.

  • Demonstrate strong executive presence and can build trust with engineering leaders, business executives, security teams, and other senior stakeholders.

  • Have designed operating models, coverage strategies, prioritization frameworks, or repeatable delivery processes for a growing technical organization.

  • Are a strong cross-functional partner who can navigate disagreement directly while maintaining trust and shared accountability.

  • Use data and clear principles to allocate limited resources across a large portfolio of opportunities.

  • Care deeply about developing people and have a track record of coaching team members, raising performance, and building inclusive teams.

  • Are energized by helping organizations adopt frontier AI responsibly and turn emerging capabilities into durable value.


Relevant Experience May Include

  • Leading teams in applied AI engineering, solutions architecture, forward-deployed engineering, professional services, technical consulting, or customer engineering.

  • Implementing generative AI, machine learning, developer platforms, cloud infrastructure, data platforms, or other complex enterprise technologies.

  • Working with customers in semiconductors, media, entertainment, or similarly complex and technology-intensive industries.

  • Supporting global customers, multi-business-unit implementations, regulated workflows, or large-scale organizational transformations.

  • Building technical enablement, reusable solution patterns, evaluation frameworks, or customer implementation methodologies.

Direct experience in these industries is not required. We value leaders who can recognize common technical and organizational patterns while adapting their approach to different customer environments.

title: Machine Learning Data Scientist - Consumer Forecasting
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Strategic Finance team at OpenAI plays a critical role in shaping the company’s long-term trajectory. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Go-To-Market teams to inform high-stakes decisions through rigorous data science and economic modeling. As part of our expanding Data Science function, we’re building a best-in-class Forecasting capability to drive real-time, data-driven decision-making across user growth, revenue, compute infrastructure, and more.

 

We are developing scalable forecasting infrastructure to help us understand and anticipate business dynamics in an increasingly complex, usage-based world. Our models are foundational to planning, pricing, operational efficiency, and growth strategy - supporting key investment decisions and unlocking OpenAI’s full potential.

 

About the Role

We’re looking for a senior Machine Learning Data Scientist to lead our forecasting initiatives. You’ll be one of the founding members of the Forecasting pillar within Strategic Finance Data Science, responsible for building and scaling robust, interpretable, and production-ready forecasting systems. Your models will power critical business decisions by predicting core metrics such as DAU/WAU, revenue, LTV, compute consumption, and profitability.

 

This is a highly cross-functional role, requiring technical excellence, strong product intuition, and business acumen. You’ll collaborate with product managers, researchers, engineers, and finance leaders to operationalize forecasting insights, influence company-wide strategy, and build foundational forecasting capabilities at OpenAI.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 

In this role, you will:

  • Build statistical and machine learning models to solve forecasting needs across product, finance, infrastructure, and GTM domains.

  • Own the end-to-end modeling lifecycle, including scoping, feature engineering, model development and prototyping, experimentation, deployment, monitoring, and explainability.

  • Develop and productionize scalable, interpretable forecasts for user growth, monetization, compute load, customer lifetime value, and profitability.

  • Contribute to self-service forecasting tools and internal platforms, enabling teams across OpenAI to access and act on real-time predictions.

  • Research and evaluate emerging tools and techniques in the forecasting space, such as TimeGPT, large language model extensions, causal forecasting, and hybrid approaches.

  • Drive strategic insight generation by translating technical outputs into business-aligned recommendations and decision frameworks.

  • Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to ensure forecasts are well-integrated into planning processes, experimentation workflows, and executive decision-making.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Advanced degree (MS or PhD) in a quantitative field (e.g., Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, Operations Research).

  • 7+ years of experience in applied data science, with deep hands-on exposure to forecasting, predictive modeling, or marketplace systems.

  • Expertise in time-series forecasting techniques and practical understanding of model trade-offs across performance, explainability, and scalability.

  • Proficiency in Python, SQL, and tools such as scikit-learn, PyTorch/TensorFlow, and forecasting libraries.

  • Demonstrated experience with model monitoring, debugging, and long-term maintenance in production environments.

  • Strong communication and storytelling skills - able to simplify complexity and influence executive stakeholders.

  • Self-directed, intellectually curious, and comfortable leading ambiguous projects from 0→1.

 

Bonus if you have:

  • Experience building or scaling forecasting platforms in a high-growth company.

  • Familiarity with causal inference, Bayesian forecasting.

  • Experience building agentic decision support systems.

  • Passion for AI and a strong point of view on how machine learning should inform strategic decisions in fast-moving environments.

title: Optical Mechanical Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Optical Mechanical Engineer to design, prototype, and validate high-density fiber interconnects for our AI infrastructure. You’ll work across MT ferrule–based connectors and adapters, optical transceiver mechanical designs, tray-level optical assemblies, and fiber shuffle solutions, translating optical and system requirements into reliable, manufacturable hardware.

This is a hands-on role spanning detailed mechanical design, lab testing, and integration. You’ll partner with optical, mechanical, networking, manufacturing, and data center teams to make fiber connections practical to assemble, route, test, and service—from within a tray or rack to the cabling infrastructure connecting racks.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and test MT ferrule–based fiber connectors and adapters, addressing alignment, tolerances, retention, mating repeatability, and serviceability.

  • Develop mechanical designs for optical transceivers and tray-level optical solutions, balancing packaging density, thermal interfaces, assembly access, and fiber management.

  • Design and validate high-density fiber shuffle assemblies, including shuffle cassettes, with clear connectivity maps, controlled routing, and accessible test interfaces.

  • Define and execute optical-mechanical validation plans, including optical loss measurements, connector inspection, mating cycles, and relevant environmental and mechanical testing.

  • Develop fiber routing within and between racks, accounting for bend radius, strain relief, cable management, labeling, installation, and maintenance access.

  • Partner with data center and network teams to translate fiber layouts and cabling infrastructure requirements into hardware interfaces and integration plans.

  • Work with suppliers and manufacturing partners to build prototypes, resolve failures, improve assembly consistency, and transition validated designs into production.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • You have hands-on experience designing and testing MT ferrule–based fiber connectors and adapters.

  • You have developed and tested fiber interconnects, including high-density fiber solutions, and can connect mechanical design decisions to optical performance.

  • You have experience with the mechanical design and integration of optical transceivers and tray-level optical assemblies.

  • You have designed and validated fiber shuffle solutions, such as shuffle cassettes, including connectivity, routing, assembly, and test considerations.

  • You understand fiber routing within and between racks, including bend-radius constraints, strain relief, connector access, and serviceability.

  • You are familiar with data center fiber layouts and the cabling infrastructure that supports installation, expansion, and operation.

  • You can move between detailed design and hands-on debugging, use measurements to identify root causes, and work with engineering and manufacturing partners to implement practical improvements.

To comply with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidates for this role may need to meet certain legal status requirements as provided in those laws and regulations.

title: Product Operations Manager
descriptionHtml:
About the Team
OpenAI’s Applied AI org is the product development arm of the company, bringing the power of advanced AI models to the world via APIs and user‑interface products (ChatGPT,Codex, etc). The Product Ops team is responsible for providing operational expertise and leverage for product teams bringing solutions to market, and streamlining and automating org operations and information channels (across Applied and with adjacent functions) to set strong foundations for collaboration at scale.

About the Role
This Product Operations Manager role is for a senior IC.
Our ideal candidate has deep experience in Product Operations at one or more scaling tech companies, working very closely with Product/Engineering and XFN partners on both central systems (e.g., launch calendar / launch readiness) and bringing products to market by running betas and launch activities.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Stand up and operate alpha/beta/GA programs with clear entry/exit criteria, recruiting design partners, running internal dogfooding, and transforming qualitative/quantitative insights into prioritized product work.

  • Own the launch calendar and readiness cadence for a product group; run XFN checkpoints across Product, Eng, Research, Safety, Security, Legal, Support, and GTM.

  • Build the systems to capture, triage, and synthesize user feedback into actionable recommendations.

  • Lead coordination for high‑impact moments (e.g., Dev Day demos, rollout waves, partner showcases), managing timelines, resources, and communications to ensure successful outcomes.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Are regularly working with agentic AI tools to increase your leverage (e.g. Dots, Codex)

  • Have an entrepreneurial spirit, bias for action, and high agency; you ship v1s quickly and iterate to quality at scale.

  • Can build systems/tools (via code / no‑code / AI) to make internal processes simple, fast, and reliable.

  • Can self‑prioritize and context switch across multiple projects and stakeholders without losing the thread.

  • Know how to find the line between chaos and bureaucracy when setting up processes.

  • Can nurture a fun, inclusive, high‑ownership team culture.

  • Appreciate the technical nuances of LLM‑powered agents (tool use, evals, telemetry, safety constraints).


Specific technologies / skills that will be helpful in this role

  • Experience with OpenAI tools and APIs (ChatGPT, Codex, text generation, structured outputs, function calling, etc)

title: Growth Client Partner, Scaled Ads (MM - UKI)
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Scaled Ads team helps mid-market advertisers grow on the platform while protecting user trust. Client Partners own commercial relationships, vendor teams optimise delivery and AI agents take on repeatable work.

About the Role

You’ll own a portfolio of mid-size advertisers from their first campaign through renewal and expansion. Your job is to earn the budget owner’s trust and spend your time where a commercial conversation can change the outcome.

In this role, you will:

  • Qualify new advertisers against their goals, budget and ability to measure results. Agree what a successful first campaign would demonstrate.

  • Build relationships with marketing leads and executive sponsors. Use campaign results to make a case for the advertiser’s next investment.

  • Review your book with vendor CSMs. They optimise committed spend while you address renewal risks, negotiate budgets and forecast revenue.

  • Use agent-prepared account briefs and flag recommendations that miss important customer context.

You might thrive in this role if:

  • You’ve owned a revenue target across a portfolio of digital advertisers and can describe a renewal or expansion you earned.

  • You can explain campaign economics to a budget owner and prioritise accounts when several need attention at once.

  • You work well with account managers and know when an advertiser can act independently.

  • You have min. 2-4 years experience selling Ads solutions

What success looks like:

A portfolio with repeat advertisers, credible expansion plans and a forecast grounded in customer commitments.

title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Human Flourishing
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Human Flourishing team’s mission is to ensure AI systems understand and advance human flourishing. As AI becomes more capable and plays a larger role in people’s lives, we want its human benefits to grow with its capabilities. The Human Flourishing team is part of the broader Post Training organization.

Our approach has two parts. Firstly, we measure and improve models’ understanding, capability, and propensity to act according to people’s values and to help them achieve their long-term goals. Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT.

Our recent work includes Beneficial RL, which investigates how training for beneficial behavior generalizes across settings, and MentalHealthBench, a benchmark developed with mental health experts to evaluate realistic conversations.

About the Role

We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher to turn difficult-to-define signals of long-term flourishing into measurable improvements in model behavior. You’ll help set research direction, build what is needed to test your ideas, and drive successful work into the models and products we ship.

We’re especially interested in researchers with deep experience improving frontier models through pretraining or reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, especially on less verifiable problems, or researchers who combine strong LLM skills with deep expertise in domains like education or mental health. Prior experience in these domains is not required.

In this role, you will

  • Develop scalable training methods across the training stack that improve how models understand people’s values, support their agency, and help them achieve long-term goals.

  • Lead high-leverage research from an open question to a shipped improvement: choose a hard-to-define problem, iteratively define success, run experiments, and integrate into frontier models.

  • Build RL environments for difficult-to-verify outcomes, and study whether beneficial behavior generalizes across settings.

  • Create evaluations grounded in human expertise and feedback that reveal capability gaps, unintended incentives in RL, and failures that aggregate scores can miss.

  • Test whether measures of model behavior predict better learning, wellbeing, and other long-term outcomes, and use those findings to guide training.

  • Build new 0→1 capabilities in human domains that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute.

  • Partner with product teams, engineers, partnerships teams, and domain experts to deploy promising methods, measure their effects in real use, and turn what you learn into further improvements.

  • Assess AI’s impacts on human flourishing at the scale of over a billion users.

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Care deeply about helping AI improve people’s lives, and feel this is a responsibility that comes with increasingly capable models.

  • Have an unusually strong research record in pretraining or RL / post-training research, especially in a hard-to-verify area; or combine strong LLM research skills with deep expertise in education, mental health, or a related field of human benefit.

  • Are a hands-on builder who can turn ideas into rigorous experiments, write and debug code, and work directly with data and training infrastructure.

  • Have the taste to choose consequential problems and actionable steps on the path to solving those problems.

  • Take ownership of ambiguous problems and choose methods based on the impact they can deliver, including when the most useful work is unglamorous.

  • Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype.

  • Work well across disciplines and can grok the most important bottlenecks to scaling our impact in a multidisciplinary problem.

If you’re excited about ensuring AI systems advance human flourishing, we’d love to hear from you.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Future of Computing Research team is an applied research team within OpenAI’s Consumer Devices group. We study how AI systems perceive people and their surroundings, and we turn that research into capabilities for future products.

 

Our work spans machine learning, sensing, and hardware, with a focus on building systems that work beyond controlled environments.

We’re looking for a machine learning engineer to help shape how future AI systems understand the physical world and the people in it. The role focuses on multimodal perception and authentication, bringing together signals from cameras, microphones, and other sensors.

title: Staff PLM & Engineering Applications Engineer, Consumer Devices
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Consumer Devices team at OpenAI builds end-to-end hardware and software systems that bring AI into the physical world. We work at the intersection of custom silicon, embedded systems, operating systems, cloud services, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, and product design to deliver reliable, production-ready devices at scale.

Within Consumer Devices, Hardware Engineering eXperience, or HEX, is a new bootstrapped team building the environments, applications, compute, product-data systems, and workflows that let hardware engineers do their work without needing to troubleshoot the machinery underneath.

HEX owns virtual engineering environments, HPC/GPU compute, storage, networking, licensing, MCAD/ECAD/CAE applications, PLM, product data, automation, validation, and support as one connected system.

About the Role

As a Staff PLM & Engineering Applications Engineer, you will be one of the first technical builders of HEX and the primary counterpart to the HEX lead.

You will own the engineering-application and product-data side of the hardware engineering experience, with an initial focus on NX, Teamcenter, licensing, parts import, integrations, packaging, validation, and user workflows.

This is not a traditional Teamcenter administration role and not a Corporate IT application-support role. You will take complex, fragile workflows and turn them into reliable engineering systems.

This role is highly hands-on and systems-oriented. You will not inherit a mature environment and support queue. You will help build a fresh one, replacing manual setup guides, tribal knowledge, repeated support issues, and team handoffs with tested automation and reliable workflows.

In This Role, You Will

  • Own the technical architecture, deployment, configuration, integration, validation, and long-term operation of NX and Teamcenter.

  • Build reliable workflows for parts import, product-data migration, metadata quality, BOMs, revisions, lifecycle states, and release processes.

  • Replace manual setup documentation with automated installation, configuration, validation, diagnostics, and recovery workflows.

  • Build tooling around NX, Teamcenter, MCAD, ECAD, CAE, plugins, licenses, and engineering environments.

  • Define and validate the golden path for hardware engineers: access, open, design, save, retrieve, release, simulate, and get help.

  • Partner with mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, simulation, manufacturing, systems, and product-design teams to understand where workflows break.

  • Work with Compute & Infrastructure-focused HEX Engineers so applications, product data, storage, VDI, HPC, and licenses feel like one coherent system.

  • Partner with contractors and vendors while keeping architecture, requirements, validation, acceptance, and long-term ownership inside HEX.

  • Build health checks, regression tests, observability, diagnostics, and support tooling that make failures easy to detect and recover from.

  • Help establish the technical standards, operating model, and engineering culture for the growing HEX organization.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

  • Have deep hands-on experience with Teamcenter, NX, PLM systems, and CAD workflows in a hardware product-development environment.

  • Have owned PLM architecture, data models, integrations, migrations, parts imports, release workflows, and engineering application platforms.

  • Can write automation in Python, PowerShell, Bash, and similar tools.

  • Have experience with packaging, deployment, licensing, validation, and application integrations.

  • Understand parts, revisions, BOMs, configurations, lifecycle states, and change workflows.

  • Can debug across applications, infrastructure, licenses, VDI, networking, storage, compute, and product data.

  • Prefer building durable tooling and automation instead of managing ticket queues.

  • See a four-page setup guide and immediately want to replace it with a tested installer.

  • Are comfortable in a new bootstrapped team where the environment, standards, workflows, and operating model are still being built.

  • Can work directly with engineers, understand their pain, and turn repeated problems into reliable systems.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Experience with Teamcenter Active Workspace, BMIDE, ITK, SOA/REST, and Teamcenter customization.

  • Experience with NX Open, managed mode, customer defaults, templates, licensing, packaging, and upgrades.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with PLM migrations, legacy part imports, data cleanup, ERP integrations, and ECAD integrations.

  • Experience with MCAD, ECAD, CAE/FEA, HPC, VDI/AVD, GPU workstations, and engineering storage.

  • Experience building internal platforms, developer tooling, infrastructure automation, and self-service systems.

  • Experience in complex hardware-development environments, including consumer devices, robotics, automotive, aerospace, or embedded systems.

title: Strategic Sourcing Lead, Engineering & Research Technology
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Technology Strategic Sourcing team helps Engineering, Research, and other technology teams secure the supplier capabilities they need to scale. We work with technical, finance, legal, security, and business leaders to shape commercial strategy, negotiate critical agreements, and build resilient supplier relationships.

About the Role

Own sourcing strategy for infrastructure software and the Engineering and Research stack. You’ll manage billion-dollar-scale spend, personally lead the most complex commercial negotiations, and deliver measurable savings while protecting the capabilities Engineering and Research rely on.

This is a principal-level individual contributor role with no direct reports at launch. You’ll lead cross-functional deal teams and coach sourcing peers. People management experience is a plus; the role may expand to include management as the team and spend grow.

Build multi-year category strategies across data platforms, observability, developer tools, and software for machine learning research, training, and inference. Use technical roadmaps, demand, and market intelligence to decide where to build, buy, consolidate, compete, or transition. Develop credible alternatives before they’re needed.

Build lasting relationships with senior Engineering and Research leaders and supplier executives, including suppliers that are also OpenAI customers. Work with Sales, Finance, and Legal to align buying and selling strategies while evaluating each decision on its own merits.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Personally lead large, complex infrastructure software and technology negotiations, from developing leverage and modeling deal economics through executive alignment and signature.

  • Keep deals, renewals, dependencies, and decisions organized. Set clear owners and milestones, communicate proactively, and surface risks early enough to act.

  • Find commercial opportunities before requests or renewals come in. Use demand, usage, pricing, and market data to improve commitments, licensing, unit economics, or supplier mix.

  • Partner with Engineering and Research leaders, existing Sourcing owners, and Finance, Legal, Security, IT, and Corporate Development as relevant to align the deal strategy and approval path.

  • Lead 360-degree supplier reviews covering spend, commitments, performance, technical dependencies, risk, and the broader partnership.

  • Shape complex deal structures with cost, equity, revenue, partnership, risk, and long-term strategic implications.

  • Advise executive leadership on where to invest, renegotiate, or walk away. Present credible options, financial and operational trade-offs, and a clear recommendation.

  • Manage strategic suppliers beyond signature, including performance, renewals, escalations, and transitions. Plan migration milestones, overlap costs, exit rights, and fallback options with technical owners.

  • Deliver significant savings and better unit economics, and validate results with Finance against comparable baselines.

  • Build negotiation and supplier-governance practices peers can use independently.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 10+ years of experience leading complex commercial negotiations in strategic sourcing, technology procurement, strategic partnerships, deal strategy, corporate development, or a related field.

  • Use AI in recurring sourcing workflows, such as market analysis, scenario modeling, or negotiation prep. Verify outputs, protect sensitive information, and own the final judgment.

  • Have led experienced peers and cross-functional deal teams without relying on formal authority. You can show how you clarified ownership, coached others, and improved commercial outcomes across multiple complex workstreams.

  • Have personally led large, complex infrastructure software or technology contracts with sophisticated pricing and licensing, capacity or usage commitments, service levels, and commercial protections.

  • Understand enterprise software business models, including usage-based pricing, multi-year commitments, ramp structures, pooled consumption, growth protections, and performance-based economics.

  • Have led complex relationships with suppliers that are also customers. You can evaluate buying economics and customer commitments separately, identify where the two create value or risk, and advise executive leadership on how to proceed.

title: IT Software Architect, SaaS Enablement and Governance
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The SaaS and Software Governance team sits within Corporate IT and helps OpenAI scale from startup-speed tooling to mature enterprise architecture. The team owns practical governance for software, SaaS, integrations, APIs, identity, data access, and agent-enabled workflows, with a mandate to improve security, reduce software sprawl, and help business teams move faster through better foundations.

About the Team

OpenAI is scaling from an emerging, high-velocity startup into a mature enterprise operating model. The IT Software Architect will help shape the software, SaaS, Data integration, and agent-enabled architecture that lets the company move quickly while improving security, compliance, data quality, and customer, partner, and employee experience.

This role is not a traditional ivory-tower architecture function. It is a hands-on governance and enablement role that partners with business teams, IT operations, Security, Procurement, Business Platforms, Applied teams and Data Engineering to guide software decisions, reduce unmanaged sprawl, and build reusable enterprise foundations.

Why This Role Matters

OpenAI’s software footprint is expanding rapidly across SaaS, internally built tools, agents, integrations, APIs, third-party platforms, and application systems that OpenAI. The company needs a stronger tools architecture layer that can help teams make good decisions early, avoid duplicate tools, govern sensitive data and identities, and identify where OpenAI should build instead of buy.

The person in this role will help turn software governance from an approval checkpoint into an enterprise capability: a system that improves speed, reliability, security, and business outcomes.

What You'll Do

  • Own the target architecture for enterprise software, SaaS, integrations, APIs, and agent-enabled business systems across Corporate IT. Drive deprecation and consolidate targets for enterprise software.

  • Build lightweight governance patterns that guide teams before software and integration decisions become hard to unwind.

  • Create architecture standards for identity, access, data movement, API usage, admin rights, auditability, observability, and vendor integration.

  • Partner with Security to ensure software architecture addresses SSO, SCIM, MFA, privileged access, non-human identities, secrets, token storage, data residency, encryption, retention, and incident response readiness.

  • Partner with Procurement and Finance to evaluate renewals, rationalization opportunities, enterprise agreements, and build-versus-buy decisions.

  • Partner deeply with application verticals such as GTM, Finance, Legal, HR, Research, Product, and Operations teams to evaluate agentic business workflows and translate them into scalable enterprise system patterns.

  • Review proposed SaaS and internally built tools for overlap, risk, integration quality, ownership, lifecycle, supportability, and long-term fit.

  • Develop reusable architecture blueprints for common capabilities such as intake, workflow, approvals, knowledge management, customer/partner 360, data integration, reporting, content management, learning, surveys, and collaboration.

  • Help define where OpenAI-native GPT or agent-built solutions should replace or enable point SaaS tools.

  • Create clear decision records and architecture artifacts that are understandable by business leaders, engineers, security reviewers, and procurement partners.

  • Drive software catalog maturity by connecting tool inventory, business owner, system owner, integration path, data classification, access model, renewal, risk posture, and support model.

Core Architecture Domains

  • SaaS governance and software catalog maturity

  • Enterprise integration architecture, including APIs, event flows, middleware, and system-of-record boundaries

  • Identity, access, and admin model design across internal and external users

  • Data architecture for SaaS, customer, supplier, employee, partner, product, consumption, and connected business models.

  • Agentic workflow architecture and GPT-built replacement patterns

  • Vendor architecture reviews and enterprise agreement leverage across strategic platforms.

  • Security, compliance, ITGC, audit evidence, and operational readiness

  • Support model design, ownership, SLAs, escalation paths, and lifecycle management

What You'll Bring

  • 10+ years of experience in enterprise architecture, business systems architecture, IT architecture, SaaS governance, integration architecture, or a related technical leadership role.

  • Strong understanding of SaaS operating models, software lifecycle management, software asset management, and vendor/platform governance.

  • Experience designing integrations across systems, experience in large scale SaaS such as CRM, ERP and Marketplace platforms.

  • Practical knowledge of identity and access patterns including SSO, OIDC, SAML, SCIM, RBAC/ABAC, privileged admin models, service accounts, OAuth apps, and token governance.

  • Ability to evaluate software from multiple angles: business value, architecture fit, security posture, data exposure, cost, supportability, user experience, and vendor strategy.

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity, building structure where little exists, and influencing senior stakeholders without relying only on formal authority.

  • Ability to write clear architecture decision records, governance standards, system diagrams, business cases, and executive-ready recommendations.

  • Strong partner orientation: able to help teams move faster while raising the quality of decisions.

  • Curiosity about AI-native enterprise architecture and where GPT, Codex, and agentic workflows can replace or enable traditional SaaS patterns.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience scaling IT or business systems from startup-stage tooling into mature enterprise architecture.

  • Experience with software rationalization, SaaS enablement and deprecation, vendor consolidation, or enterprise license optimization.

  • Experience with architecting systems in a high-growth environment.

  • Experience building governance for internally developed tools, low-code/no-code platforms, agents, or employee-built automation.

  • Experience working closely with Security, GRC, Legal, Procurement, and Finance on cross-functional risk and control programs.

title: Program Manager, Recruiting Events
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Recruiting Events program powers OpenAI’s top-of-funnel hiring engine through strategic, high-impact experiences that connect exceptional talent with our people, mission, culture, and work. From intimate dinners that build deep connections to conferences that expand our reach, we curate experiences that spark curiosity, showcase our work, and bring “Why OpenAI?” to life.

About the Role

We’re hiring a Program Manager to own a portfolio of recruiting events that supports OpenAI’s hiring priorities. Working closely with the Manager of Recruiting Events Strategy and Recruiting leaders, you’ll shape and scale experiences that attract, engage, and nurture priority talent, helping candidates envision a career at OpenAI.

You’ll translate hiring priorities into a thoughtful portfolio of event experiences and determine which events will most effectively engage the talent we need. You’ll help shape each experience’s goals, format, cross-functional participation, and success metrics, then lead initiatives from planning through delivery, follow-up coordination, and measurement. Your portfolio may evolve across business areas as hiring needs change.

You’ll own end-to-end program delivery and outcomes across your recruiting events portfolio, partnering with the Events team on large-scale production and logistics. You should be comfortable moving between strategic thinking and hands-on execution, with strong judgment, attention to detail, and the ability to influence without owning every aspect of delivery.

This role can be based in San Francisco or New York and requires being in the office three days per week. The role also requires extensive travel depending on the event schedule and workload, with occasional evening work as needed.

In this role, you will:

  • Oversee programming across your recruiting events portfolio. Partner with Recruiting leads and hiring managers to prioritize monthly and quarterly event series based on hiring needs, target audiences, and partnerships. Apply the established program framework and lead initiatives end to end, adjusting plans as priorities evolve.

  • Shape program content and event experiences. Work with recruiters to inform event strategy, audience and invitation plans, and speaker participation. Oversee the development of panels, product showcases, and other programming that reflects OpenAI’s recruiting brand and voice and supports each initiative’s objectives.

title: Product Data Scientist - Youth, Families and Learning
descriptionHtml:
About the role

We’re looking for a product data scientist to help OpenAI create more value and drive sustainable growth for young people, families, and learners. You’ll drive product data science across under-18 audiences, emerging opportunities for children under 13, family experiences, and learning and education more broadly.

You’ll help decide where we should invest, what we should build, and how we’ll know it is working. This means understanding distinct audience needs, identifying promising use cases, and turning evidence into a clear product strategy. Your work will connect discovery and early product development with adoption, retention, and sustained user value.

You’ll partner across Chat Product, Growth, Foundations, SafeSys, and other teams, working closely with product managers, engineers, designers, and researchers. The role focuses and owns product value and growth while dedicated teams own policy and safety.

In this role, you will:

  • Shape strategy and prioritize opportunities. Size unmet needs and growth opportunities across audiences, use cases, and product experiences. Help teams choose where to invest and sequence work based on expected user value, reach, evidence, and effort.

  • Define what value and success mean. Develop an audience-specific measurement framework spanning activation, task success, learning progress, satisfaction, and durable retention. Connect these measures to product goals and assess whether repeat use reflects meaningful benefit.

  • Understand users and growth drivers. Analyze journeys, funnels, and cohorts to uncover where people find value, where they struggle, and what helps them return. Combine behavioral data with surveys and user research to explain differences across ages, family roles, and learning contexts.

  • Measure what changes actually cause. Design experiments and holdouts to evaluate product and model changes. Apply causal methods when randomization is impractical, make assumptions explicit, and account for seasonality, audience composition, and effects that differ across segments.

  • Turn findings into product decisions. Work with partners from initial hypotheses through launch and iteration. Recommend what to build, change, expand, or stop, explaining expected impact, uncertainty, and tradeoffs. Follow through to determine whether decisions delivered the intended results.

  • Build reliable measurement. Partner with engineering on instrumentation, dataset quality, and consistent audience definitions. Create reusable analyses and dashboards that make progress visible and let teams answer recurring questions independently.

  • Create alignment across teams. Bring a coherent view of audience value to work spanning multiple roadmaps. Help partners agree on priorities, success criteria, and the next questions to resolve, even when ownership is distributed and evidence is incomplete.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • A record of influencing product strategy and improving user outcomes through hands-on data science, including work from an ambiguous question to a decision and measurable impact.

  • Strong SQL and Python skills, sound statistical judgment, and practical experience with experiments, causal inference, cohort analysis, and measurement design.

  • The ability to develop useful definitions of product value, validate imperfect proxies, and distinguish short-term metric movement from lasting improvement.

  • Clear communication and strong product judgment. You can make a recommendation, explain its limits, and influence collaborators across functions without relying on formal authority.

  • Comfort setting priorities independently across a broad scope, staying close to users, and moving between strategic questions and detailed analytical work.

Helpful experience

Experience with consumer product growth, youth or family products, learning and education, or generative AI would be valuable. We also welcome experience measuring learning outcomes, combining quantitative and qualitative research, or evaluating products whose value emerges over time.

descriptionHtml:
About the team

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with healthcare organizations to deploy production AI systems across clinical, operational, and member-facing workflows. We work at the boundary of customer deployment and core platform development, using customer engagements to define repeatable architectures, evaluations, integrations, and operating standards for complex, regulated healthcare environments.

About the role

We are hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to own end-to-end deployments of our models within healthcare organizations, including payers, providers, health systems, and healthcare technology companies. You will lead technical discovery, architecture, implementation, evaluation, productionization, and handoff, translating complex customer workflows, data, infrastructure, and regulatory constraints into production AI systems.

You will measure success through production adoption, measurable workflow impact, and evaluation loops that establish customer-specific benchmarks, acceptance criteria, and launch readiness. You’ll collaborate directly with customer technical and operational teams, alongside internal Business, Research, Product, Engineering, and Security partners, to deliver solutions and translate deployment learnings into product improvements. title: Software Engineer, Database Systems
descriptionHtml:
About the Team:

The Database Systems team specializes in high-performance distributed databases. Our team built Rockset, the real-time search, analytics, and vector database that powers all vector search and retrieval augmented generation (RAG) at OpenAI. In addition to retrieval, as an online database, Rockset powers core functionality across all of OpenAI's product lines and many critical internal use cases.

About the Role:

We are looking for engineers passionate about distributed systems, close-to-the-metal performance optimization (our core engine is written in C++), and building scalable database infrastructure from the ground up. As an engineer on the Database Systems team, you'll contribute to the core database engine, driving improvements across ingestion, query execution, indexing, and storage. You'll partner with teams across OpenAI to unlock new product capabilities and help scale online database reliability and throughput as usage grows by orders of magnitude.

In this role you will:

  • Design, build, and operate high-performance distributed systems

  • Identify and resolve performance bottlenecks to scale infrastructure to the next order of magnitude

  • Define long-term technical direction and guide system evolution

  • Collaborate with product, engineering, and research teams to deliver scalable and reliable infrastructure

  • Dig deep into complex production issues across the stack

  • Contribute to incident response, postmortems, and best practices for system reliability

  • Have significant experience building, scaling, and optimizing distributed systems at scale

  • Are curious about database internals, storage engines, or low-latency query systems

  • Enjoy debugging challenging performance issues in complex, high-throughput systems

  • Have experience operating production clusters at scale (e.g., Kubernetes or other orchestration systems)

  • Think rigorously about scalability, correctness, and reliability

  • Thrive in fast-paced environments with high autonomy and impact

  • 4+ years of relevant industry experience, with 2+ years leading large scale, complex projects or teams as an engineer or tech lead

  • Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate across highly technical and cross-functional teams

  • Proficiency in a systems programming language such as C++ (our core engine is written in C++) is strongly preferred

  • Fluency in cloud environments (AWS, GCP, Azure) and IaC tools (Terraform or similar)

title: Art Director, Business Marketing
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Business Marketing helps knowledge workers, developers, and business decision-makers understand and adopt OpenAI’s products, supporting both self-serve growth and our managed sales team. Our creative work makes complex capabilities clear, grounded, and human as they move from the lab into businesses and everyday work.

About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced Art Director to develop and direct creative for OpenAI’s business audiences. You’ll turn product capabilities, customer insights, and marketing briefs into visual ideas that can carry a campaign across channels. That might mean developing the visual concept for a launch, storyboarding a film about how a customer uses AI in their work, or building a campaign system that holds together across a landing page, paid social, and a keynote.

This is a hands-on role. You’ll sketch concepts, build key visuals, and set the visual direction for designers, producers, and external partners. You’ll work closely with writers, Business Marketing, Product Marketing, and product teams to make sure the work is accurate, useful to the audience, and unmistakably OpenAI.

To us, creativity is a team sport. Ideas get better when you talk them through and build on each other’s thinking. We value curiosity over certainty, kindness over ego, and the ability to balance craft with decisiveness.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead visual concept development and art direction for B2B campaigns, product launches, customer stories, and industry events, from brief through final production.

  • Partner with writers and marketers to define the idea around a specific audience, what they need to understand, and what we want them to do next.

  • Work with product and technical partners to show how capabilities work in practice, using product imagery, demos, diagrams, and motion without overstating what the technology can do.

  • Develop campaign visual systems that adapt to different formats and audience needs, from a launch film or event keynote to a product page, paid campaign, or sales presentation.

  • Art direct photography, illustration, motion, and video. Make work yourself when the project calls for it, and give clear direction to internal teams and external partners when others are producing it.

  • Maintain a high visual bar across touch points and help evolve how the OpenAI brand shows up for business audiences.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 8+ years of art direction or related creative experience in-house, at an agency, or both, with a portfolio that shows your role in developing concepts and taking them through production.

  • Have experience creating work for business or technical audiences, with examples of making a complex product, service, or idea clear and compelling.

title: Data Program Manager, Science
descriptionHtml:
About the Team
OpenAI’s Research Data team exists to accelerate the evaluation, safety and capabilities of our models and products. Made up of technical operators and software engineers, we design the methods through which we acquire and create data.

About the Role
As a Data Program Manager, Science, you will help researchers develop and execute scientific data programs, connecting OpenAI’s research priorities with relevant data, expertise and external partners.

You’ll work closely with researchers to understand their needs, assess the scientific and practical value of opportunities, and develop partnerships across the scientific ecosystem. The work could range from acquiring existing datasets to shaping research collaborations. You’ll carry opportunities from initial investigation through commercial discussions, agreements, delivery and research use, exercising sound judgement around sensitive data and relationships.

Our current work focuses particularly on biology and chemistry. We welcome different combinations of scientific, technical and partnership experience.

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop data strategies with Research. Translate research goals, model limitations and evaluation gaps into evidence needs and success criteria. Compare acquisition with internal, public and commissioned alternatives.

  • Find distinctive sources for research. Build trusted local and international relationships across research and industry, including organisations at the scientific frontier.

  • Assess opportunities in scientific context. Inspect samples for provenance, context, quality and completeness. Assess usefulness, involving researchers and specialists as needed.

  • Shape partnerships with lasting scientific value. Understand partners’ ambitions and define pilots, deliverables and acceptance criteria, considering expertise, scientific contribution and continuing relationships alongside commercial terms.

  • Lead commercial and operational execution. Develop proposals, assess pricing and negotiate terms. Coordinate Legal, Privacy, Security, Procurement and engineering to clarify permissions, responsibilities and delivery.

  • Navigate sensitive collaborations. Understand institutional interests and confidentiality. Identify ethical, privacy, security and misuse concerns early, involving specialists to develop responsible arrangements.

  • Follow through into research use. Coordinate preparation, ingestion, access and documentation. Gather researcher feedback to inform whether to expand, change or stop.

  • Make thoughtful portfolio decisions. Recommend options based on research value, cost, timing and capacity. Identify shared needs and opportunities for useful collaboration across projects.

  • Make the work more repeatable. Use code, APIs, automation and AI tools to improve sourcing, assessment and delivery. Resolve recurring blockers with engineers and retain partner knowledge and research feedback.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have substantial grounding in biology, chemistry or related sciences through research, industry or equivalent experience, and engage critically with methods and evidence.

  • Have delivered complex scientific, data or partnership projects, with depth in one or more of scientific data and evaluation, commercial partnerships or research collaborations across organisations.

  • Exercise sound judgement: test claims, match evidence to research needs and make clear recommendations while acknowledging uncertainty.

  • Work directly with data: inspect unfamiliar files, investigate quality and use Python, SQL, APIs and AI-assisted coding to answer questions and reduce manual work.

  • Build trust through careful listening, precise questions and thoughtful negotiation. You bring relevant local and international relationships, or a demonstrated ability to develop them, and understand what partners value beyond the transaction.

  • Exercise discretion, recognising the limits of your expertise and authority and when scientific, ethical or safety questions need specialist input.

  • Thrive in a fast-moving environment, taking broad ownership across multiple projects and moving readily between scientific, technical and commercial questions. You prioritise thoughtfully as needs change, making clear decisions about where to focus and what can wait.

  • Enjoy getting your hands dirty, bringing energy and creative problem solving to unfamiliar or ambiguous opportunities. You turn them into practical plans and follow through on the details.

  • We welcome different combinations of scientific, technical and partnership experience. You do not need equal depth in every area.

title: Component and Product Quality Engineer, Interconnects
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

OpenAI's Hardware organization builds supercompute platforms from silicon and boards to full rack-scale systems to power advanced AI workloads. This role owns end-to-end quality for high-speed interconnect hardware across the product lifecycle: early design influence, supplier/contract manufacturer readiness, qualification, ramp, and fleet quality in lab and data center environments.

You will be the quality lead for advanced interconnect components and assemblies, including high-speed copper cables, cable cartridges, patch panels, backplane/cable-backplane solutions, high-speed connectors, and related electro-mechanical interfaces. You will partner closely with electrical, mechanical, SI/PI, systems, reliability, operations, and external vendors to prevent escapes and drive rapid, data-driven containment and corrective action.

In this role you will:

  • Own quality for advanced interconnect components and assemblies: high-speed connectors, high-speed copper cables, cable cartridges (e.g., cable cassette style assemblies), patch panels & optics, and backplane/cable-backplane interconnect solutions.

  • Drive quality-by-design: participate in design reviews, DFM/DFx, tolerance stacks, material and plating selections, connector mating strategy, strain relief, and assembly methods to reduce variation and field failures.

  • Define and track quality and reliability metrics (DPPM, yield, escapes, RMA/FRACAS trends, Cpk/Ppk where applicable) for interconnects across NPI and mass production.

  • Build and execute qualification strategies for cables/connectors/patch panels (mechanical, environmental, electrical, and reliability), including test coverage, sample plans, clear pass/fail criteria, defining installation criteria and processes, optics termination quality management and setting fiber standards criteria.

  • Partner with engineering and operations to drive smooth ramp: risk assessments, pilot build learnings, change control, and readiness reviews (EVT/DVT/PVT/MP or equivalent phases).

  • Own supplier and CM performance management: scorecards, audits (process and quality system), and follow-up to close findings with verified effectiveness

  • Work with suppliers to improve manufacturing throughput, stability, and yields for cable and connector assembly processes (e.g., wire prep, welding/crimping, overmolding/injection molding, plating, and assembly fixturing).

  • Lead rapid containment and root-cause investigations for failures found during bring-up, system integration tests, reliability testing, and fleet deployments.

  • Own the end-to-end corrective action process (8D, 5-Whys, Ishikawa, DOE as needed): define problem statements, isolate variables, validate root cause, implement fixes, and verify effectiveness.

  • Partner with SI/PI and test teams to correlate electrical performance issues (e.g., link margin, BER, eye closure, impedance discontinuities, PAM4, TDR and VNA) with manufacturing and mechanical drivers (connector wear, plating, contamination, misalignment, cable routing, assembly variation).

  • Support integration and deployment of OpenAI supercompute racks in lab and data center environments; identify quality risks tied to shipping, handling, installation, and service operations.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • 7+ years of experience in quality engineering, manufacturing quality, supplier quality, or reliability for interconnects or high-speed hardware used in servers, networking, storage, or high-performance compute systems.

  • Hands-on experience with high-speed copper interconnect products: connectors and/or cable assemblies; familiarity with patch panels or backplane/cable-backplane solutions is a plus

  • Strong command of problem-solving and quality tools: 8D, 5-Whys, Fishbone, PFMEA/control plans, SPC/MSA (gauge R&R), and change control.

  • Ability to read and interpret mechanical drawings, GD&T basics, and electrical/interface specifications; comfortable working across ME/EE/SI disciplines.

  • Experience driving supplier/CM improvements (audits, scorecards, CAPA) and managing nonconformance/MRB workflows.

  • Clear written and verbal communication skills; ability to drive alignment across internal teams and external partners.

  • Experience with cable manufacturing and assembly processes (wire treatment, resistance welding/laser welding, crimping, overmolding/injection molding, braiding/shielding, plating, and automated test).

  • Experience with optical interconnects (AOC/DAC, pluggable modules such as QSFP/OSFP), fiber termination quality, optical return loss, end-face inspection standards (IEC 61300), and contamination control practices.

  • Ability to travel internationally and work effectively across time zones with ODM/JDM and supplier partners.

About the Team

The Physical Engineering team sits within OpenAI’s Enterprise Verticals organization. We’re exploring how frontier AI can help people design, simulate, and build better physical products—shortening development cycles, improving product performance, and expanding what engineering teams can accomplish.

Our initial focus is on mechanical and electrical engineering. We’re building experiences within ChatGPT and integrations with engineering software to help engineers move from early concepts through design, simulation, and preparation for production.

We operate as a small founding team within OpenAI, working directly with customers and closely with research, design, and forward deployed engineers. We learn by building, putting products in users’ hands, and using their feedback to guide our next steps.

As a Founding Full Stack Software Engineer, you’ll help define and build the product and technical foundations of this new vertical. You’ll work across frontend experiences, backend services, and integrations to bring AI into complex engineering workflows.

You’ll combine strong software engineering fundamentals with product judgment and an eye for intuitive user experiences. Working directly with engineers and design partners, you’ll identify valuable problems, prototype solutions, and develop them into reliable products.

title: Organizational Design Lead
descriptionHtml:
About the team

The People team helps OpenAI build the teams, capabilities, and working practices needed to deliver on our mission. As AI changes what people and organizations can accomplish, we’re exploring how roles, teams, and ways of working should evolve and putting those ideas into practice within OpenAI.

About the role

We’re looking for an Organizational Design Lead to help build our organizational design capability and shape how people and AI agents work together.

You’ll partner with leaders and People colleagues to understand business goals, examine how work gets done, and design the roles, structures, decision processes, and workflows that help teams succeed. This includes exploring where AI can expand people’s capabilities, how responsibilities should evolve, and where human judgment and accountability are essential.

This is a hands-on role. You’ll move between understanding organizational challenges, developing new approaches, testing them with teams, and turning what works into practical tools and methods others can use. You’ll bring a thoughtful perspective on organizations and the ability to make change happen.

In this role, you will:

  • Translate business goals into organizational choices. Help leaders identify the work, capabilities, roles, and team structures needed to achieve their goals.

  • Design how people and AI agents work together. Rethink workflows, responsibilities, handoffs, and decision rights as AI capabilities evolve, with clear ownership and human accountability.

  • Improve team effectiveness. Understand where unclear boundaries, coordination costs, or decision processes slow teams down, and develop practical ways to address them.

  • Test ideas in real working environments. Partner with teams to prototype new operating practices, gather feedback, and refine approaches before applying them more broadly.

  • Connect organizational design with technology. Work with People partners, analytics colleagues, and technical teams to turn ideas into useful tools, workflows, and working practices.

  • Build capability across People and leadership. Develop simple frameworks, facilitate working sessions, and help others make sound organizational design decisions.

  • Measure and share what works. Assess changes through business outcomes, quality, speed, team effectiveness, and employee experience, and translate learning into repeatable practices.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have meaningful experience in organizational design, operating model development, or organizational effectiveness, with examples of changes you helped implement.

  • Understand organizations as interconnected systems of people, work, technology, incentives, and decisions.

title: Senior Special Programs Security Manager (CSSO/CPSO)
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Industrial Security team enables OpenAI’s classified and national security work by building secure, compliant programs that support government customers and protect sensitive information. We partner across Security, Legal, People, Facilities, Engineering, IT, and program leadership to translate complex government requirements into practical operating models that allow important work to move forward responsibly. Our work spans personnel security, classified facilities, special programs, government customer engagement, and the safeguards required to operate in highly regulated environments.

About the Role

As a Senior Special Programs Security Manager, you will lead security operations for OpenAI’s Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) and Special Access Programs (SAP), serving in customer-designated roles such as Contractor Special Security Officer (CSSO) or Contractor Program Security Officer (CPSO). You will help shape how OpenAI operates across the Intelligence Community and other national security environments, building the relationships, processes, and security foundations required to support classified work at scale.

We’re looking for someone who brings deep special programs expertise, sound operational judgment, and the credibility to work directly with government customers and senior internal stakeholders. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone comfortable navigating ambiguity, helping build the function, mentoring future team members, and finding compliant paths forward when mission needs and security requirements intersect.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, or Washington, DC. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. Additional onsite presence and occasional travel may be required based on classified program, facility, and government customer needs.

This position requires active Top Secret eligibility, current SCI access, and a current counterintelligence (CI) polygraph at the time of application. Candidates must also be able to obtain and maintain additional customer-required accesses, including a full-scope polygraph if required.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead SCI and SAP security operations across the program lifecycle, including access administration, indoctrinations and debriefings, security plans, classification requirements, incident reporting, inspections, and program closeout.

  • Serve as the designated CSSO, CPSO, or equivalent program security official for assigned government customers and classified programs.

  • Oversee the establishment, accreditation, operation, modification, and inspection readiness of Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities and Special Access Program Facilities.

  • Translate government regulations, contract requirements, DD Forms 254, security classification guides, and customer direction into practical policies, procedures, and operating decisions.

  • Coordinate closely with personnel security, information systems security, classified IT, Facilities, Legal, and program teams to establish clear ownership and integrated safeguards.

  • Lead self-inspections, security inquiries, corrective actions, customer assessments, and escalation of risks that could affect access, accreditation, or program execution.

  • Advise Industrial Security leadership, independently represent the security function, and provide operational continuity across critical programs and customer relationships.

  • Mentor and develop special programs security personnel while establishing the staffing, metrics, governance, and operating rhythms needed to support continued growth.

  • Enable classified work through risk-informed decisions while maintaining the judgment and authority to stop or escalate activity that would violate security requirements.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have substantial experience leading contractor security for SCI and SAP programs, including direct experience as a CSSO, CPSO, CSPSO, SSO, or comparable customer-designated security official.

  • Understand how Intelligence Community customers operate, including sponsor relationships, access processes, reciprocity, customer-specific requirements, and appropriate escalation channels.

  • Have strong working knowledge of the NISPOM, ICDs 703, 704, and 705, Intelligence Community technical specifications for SCIFs, DoDM 5205.07, applicable Security Executive Agent Directives, and related customer guidance.

  • Have established, accredited, operated, or modified SCIFs or SAPFs and can coordinate facility, physical security, information security, and technical accreditation requirements.

  • Have successfully managed government customer relationships and can communicate clearly with security officials, technical teams, program leaders, and senior executives.

  • Have led security inspections, customer reviews, incident response, corrective actions, and closure of complex compliance findings.

title: Manufacturing Quality Engineer, Data Center Equipment
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI and its capital and technology partners are building a global network of data centers for demanding AI workloads. The Infrastructure Quality team sets and verifies quality, reliability, and performance requirements for equipment across that network.

We work with manufacturing partners, general contractors, engineers, and operations staff from supplier qualification through commissioning. Together, we verify that equipment arrives ready for installation, startup, and long-term service.

About the Role

As a Manufacturing Quality Engineer, you will oversee the quality of data center equipment at supplier factories. You will use production data, audits, and test results to identify systemic, recurring, or safety-related issues and work with suppliers to address them through Closed Loop Learning (CLL).

You will work with suppliers and internal teams to define inspections and factory tests for each type of equipment. You will coordinate issue resolution before shipment and manage deviations across multiple suppliers and project sites.

Key Responsibilities

Manufacturing Monitoring and Supplier Improvement

  • Manufacturing monitoring: Work with Manufacturing Operations to monitor production progress, quality controls, inspection results, and test readiness. Flag emerging risks and coordinate a response with suppliers.

  • Product and process audits: Audit products and processes during and after production against engineering requirements, critical-to-quality (CTQ) characteristics, approved procedures, and quality standards. Document findings and track corrective actions to closure.

  • Manufacturing coordination: Agree on production checkpoints and inspection and testing requirements with suppliers, engineering, sourcing, supply chain, commissioning, and quality teams. Escalate risks to equipment acceptance or delivery.

  • Manufacturing scorecards: Develop supplier and product scorecards with Manufacturing Operations. Review audit findings, test results, recurring defects, and open issues with suppliers to prioritize improvements.

  • Drive continuous improvement: Lead the CLL process with suppliers. Track root cause analyses and corrective and preventive actions in a shared register. Verify that each action addresses the underlying problem before closing it.

Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT)

  • Standardize requirements and formats: Develop product-specific FAT requirements and standard test formats with equipment suppliers and OpenAI’s engineering, commissioning, quality, and Manufacturing Operations teams.

  • Define critical quality requirements: Document the CTQ characteristics each test must verify in an OpenAI-accepted format. Use CLL findings to revise FAT procedures so future tests check for known failure modes.

  • Ensure auditable supplier records: Require suppliers to retain test results and make them available for OpenAI audits.

  • Manage documentation and revision control: Review final FAT records and audit reports for each piece of equipment and maintain a controlled revision history.

  • Conduct periodic supplier audits: Check that suppliers follow approved test procedures and that their records accurately reflect the tests performed.

Factory Witness Testing (FWT)

  • Align checklists and stakeholders: Develop standard FWT checklists with OpenAI subject matter experts, installing contractors, and the construction management team. Agree on requirements before testing begins.

  • Manage documentation and reporting: Collect and review final witness test reports and supporting records from participants.

  • Before shipment, confirm that each witness-test issue is resolved or covered by a documented deviation. Log systemic, recurring, or safety-related findings in the CLL tracker and verify the effectiveness of corrective actions with the supplier.

Deviation Management

  • Assess short shipments and missing or failed tests in partnership with Manufacturing Operations.

  • Coordinate supplier support to resolve issues at the project site.

  • Document each deviation and track the agreed actions through closure.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical, mechanical, or industrial engineering.

  • At least 10 years of data center industry experience spanning quality engineering and project management.

  • Experience coordinating FAT and FWT with suppliers and resolving equipment quality issues.

  • Ability to develop test checklists, define CTQs, review test results, and maintain auditable quality records.

  • Experience monitoring supplier production, auditing products and processes during and after production, and using scorecards to improve supplier and product quality. Experience managing controlled documents and deviations.

  • Ability to coordinate supplier schedules and plan inspections and tests across multiple pieces of equipment.

  • Ability to communicate quality requirements and coordinate decisions across suppliers, engineering, commissioning, sourcing, supply chain, manufacturing, operations, quality, and construction teams.

  • Willingness and ability to travel approximately 40–60% of the time to supplier manufacturing facilities and data center project sites.

Preferred Skills

  • Technical knowledge of data center infrastructure, including mechanical, electrical, and controls systems.

  • Experience in supplier performance management for mission-critical facilities.

  • ASQ Certified Quality Engineer, Quality Manager, or Quality Auditor.

  • PMP or equivalent project management certification.

  • Experience in industrial or high-volume manufacturing environments.
