descriptionHtml:
About the Role

We’re hiring a Data Scientist to support Real Estate & Workplace (REW), a fast-moving global team focused on creating workplaces that help OpenAI’s people do their best work while scaling the company’s real estate and workplace operations. Our work is grounded in understanding how people use space and services, collaborate across physical and digital environments, and experience the workplace.

REW’s scope spans portfolio strategy, design and construction, space planning, sustainability, workplace experience, and global operations. You’ll work comfortably across this broad, sometimes messy data landscape and build trusted relationships across the domain. The work informs high-impact decisions with immediate, visible effects—from where teams work and how space and services are allocated to which investments move forward and how workplace experiences evolve. Working at the forefront of AI-native analytics, you’ll help define the future of workplace operations at OpenAI rather than follow an established playbook. title: Vendor Security Technical Program Manager
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI's Vendor Security team helps internal teams work securely with external products, services, and partners. Our work spans software, infrastructure, hardware, professional and managed services, vendor-provided workforces, data, and research. We build the programs and products that help teams understand vendor risk and put effective safeguards in place, protecting our customers, employees, and the company.

About the Role

We are looking for a Vendor Security Technical Program Manager who can make sound security decisions and turn recurring vendor-security problems into tools and practices that work.

You will independently lead vendor-security engagements: understand the business need, investigate the actual data and access, recommend a practical path, and work with the responsible owners until the safeguards are verified. You will also use what you learn to build and improve bounded tools and workflows, with priorities agreed with the Vendor Security lead.

This is an individual-contributor role for someone who combines technical judgment with useful delivery. You should be comfortable taking a position, explaining the tradeoff, and changing your mind when the evidence changes. Success means internal teams can use vendors securely, reuse work that still applies, and understand what needs to happen next.

In this role, you will:

  • Own vendor security engagements from understanding the business need through scoping, assessment, decision, treatment, and reassessment when material facts change. Make assessment decisions independently and use judgment about when to involve peers, specialists, or leadership. Route formal exceptions and risk acceptance to the appropriate decision owners.

  • Understand vendor use cases, workflows, user journeys, data flows, identities, access, integrations, and supply-chain dependencies. Identify plausible attack paths and their consequences for OpenAI.

  • Assess relevant architectures, configurations, controls, logs, and operational practices. Test whether the evidence supports the security claims that matter to the engagement, and make gaps and uncertainty clear.

  • Develop practical treatments, including changes to the operating model, data exposure, access, architecture, vendor choice, controls, or containment. Drive implementation with the responsible owners and verify that the treatment works.

  • Build reusable security patterns with clear applicability, safeguards, evidence requirements, exceptions, and review triggers.

  • Work with Legal, Procurement, and vendors on security addenda. Evaluate proposed terms and deviations against the engagement, explain their security implications, and develop workable positions with the appropriate decision owners. Legal leads wording and negotiation.

  • Learn from internal customers, agree priorities with the Vendor Security lead, and define the requirements, roadmap, and success measures for the bounded programs, products, and services you own.

  • Use Codex or comparable AI-assisted tools to build, inspect, test, and maintain practical improvements to scoping, evidence checks, routing, decision reuse, or treatment tracking. Investigate failures and own the result through adoption, continued operation, and explicit handoff or retirement.

  • Lead delivery across Security and partner teams. Translate goals into technical requirements, milestones, and delivery plans; influence implementation choices; identify systemic risks; resolve dependencies and disagreements; and carry commitments through completion.

  • Use casework, incidents, threat information, and customer feedback to improve decisions and the program. As priorities change, recommend what to do next and explain the tradeoffs and effects on existing commitments.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have independently assessed consequential third-party, supply-chain, or comparable security risks, and can apply that judgment to unfamiliar vendor technologies and operating models.

  • Understand security principles and controls, including data protection, access management, application security, prevention, detection, and response. Can reason about architecture, identity, APIs, data flows, logging, integrations, and whether controls work.

  • Know relevant frameworks and standards, including ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, and SOC 2, and can use them to inform an assessment of the actual engagement.

  • Have translated security findings and requirements into practical contractual positions with Legal, Procurement, and vendor representatives.

  • Have delivered useful products or workflow improvements, tested expected behavior and failure cases, learned from users, and owned performance after launch.

  • Can use Codex or comparable AI-assisted development tools to build, run, inspect, and test working solutions.

  • Have independently delivered cross-functional programs, turned ambiguity into technical requirements and plans, and adapted priorities to achieve measurable outcomes. Can judge when to build, use existing systems, or engage partners to resolve blockers.

  • Build constructive relationships with Security, Engineering, Product, Privacy, Legal, business teams, and vendors. Communicate complex security issues clearly in writing and conversation, including your recommendation, supporting evidence, and relevant tradeoffs.

  • Question assumptions, try thoughtful new approaches, investigate unfamiliar systems, and revise your judgment when new evidence changes the situation.

descriptionHtml:

Dots is building personal AI agents that help people make progress on their goals, including when they are away from ChatGPT. These agents can learn preferences, maintain context, work across applications, and use cloud computers to carry out tasks.

Our team brings together product engineering, design, and research to turn frontier model capabilities into useful everyday experiences. title: Software Engineer, Manufacturing Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

We're seeking a Software Engineer to join our First-Party Hardware team. In this role, you will design, build, integrate, and validate the software used to manufacture, qualify, and deliver our hardware from the factory.

You will work across the stack to create the infrastructure that runs internally and externally to coordinate all aspects of the production process. You will create the critical tools and procedures to execute, capture, process, and present the data resulting from the end to end assembly and validation of our hardware across multiple vendors and sites.

This role is hands-on and high-ownership. You will work closely across teams both internal and external to define the standards that will be used across our products to ensure the velocity and quality of our 1P hardware. You will own the implementation, deployment, and output of these systems as well their continued maintenance and SLAs.

Location: San Francisco, CA (Hybrid: 3 days/week onsite). Relocation assistance available.

In this role, you will:

  • Design, develop, and maintain the software infrastructure for manufacturing process execution and data export.

  • Own integration across internal customers and vendor systems and processes.

  • Build and maintain the CI, release, and delivery pipeline of tooling to external partners.

  • Build and maintain internal systems to ingest, process, deliver, and visualize critical data for internal teams and systems.

  • Build system health monitoring, telemetry, remote diagnostics, and recovery paths that make manufacturing failures traceable and actionable.

  • Develop automation frameworks and monitoring for board bring-up, rack bring-up, qualification, manufacturing readiness, deployment readiness, and long-term reliability.

  • Package engineering releases into manufacturing-ready software recipes: images, versions, logs, limits, remediation mapping, provisioning hooks, secure artifact handling, and traceable data export.

  • Debug complex production issues spanning hardware, firmware, kernel, services, networking, power, thermals, boot, provisioning, manufacturing, test, and cloud services.

  • Partner with hardware, firmware, security, networking, infrastructure, manufacturing, operations, and external engineering teams to define software contracts, unblock bring-up, and drive issues to closure.

  • Produce durable architecture notes, runbooks, validation records, and decision documents that help OpenAI and partner teams reproduce, operate, and improve the platform.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 7+ years of hands-on experience, or exceptional accomplishments demonstrating equivalent expertise, in system software, platform software, hardware diagnostics, and cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong programming skills in C, C++, Rust or similar systems languages, with experience building reliable software for real hardware.

  • Familiarity with scripting in languages such as shell and python as used in automation systems.

  • Familiarity with Linux-based hardware platforms, OpenBMC, Redfish, firmware update systems, kernel drivers, and fleet management software.

  • Demonstrated ability to debug live hardware using logs, packet captures, firmware traces, bus captures, lab hosts, BMC journals, Linux tooling, and carefully controlled experiments.

  • Experience with hardware bring-up, manufacturing or qualification testing, system diagnostics, release validation, or deployment of high-performance compute, accelerator, server, networking, storage, or embedded platforms.

  • Ability to reason across software, firmware, hardware, manufacturing, and operations boundaries, and to turn ambiguous problems into clear requirements, designs, tests, and decisions.

  • Proven track record working with external vendors, manufacturing partners, or partner engineering teams to define deliverables, review technical work, and drive issues to closure.

  • Familiarity with platform security topics such as secure boot, firmware signing, device provisioning, attestation, certificate handling, trusted update flows, or access-control design is a plus.

To comply with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidates for this role may need to meet certain legal status requirements as provided in those laws and regulations.

title: Datacenter Networking Technician, AI Compute Deployment - Stargate
descriptionHtml:
About the Team:

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital partners, is embarking on a journey to build the world’s most advanced AI infrastructure ecosystem. Our Stargate program develops and deploys massive, state-of-the-art data center campuses in partnership with industry leaders today—and through future OpenAI infrastructure projects tomorrow. We design for scale, speed, and reliability, and we need experienced technicians who can translate network blueprints into physical reality.

About the Role:

We are seeking a Senior Data Center Networking Technician who thrives in fast-moving build environments and is eager to roll up their sleeves during active datacenter deployments.
Your first assignment will focus on the physical bring-up of network infrastructure at a large partner-operated campus, collaborating with partner teams and their delivery vendors to achieve agreed performance and reliability targets. As that campus reaches steady state, you will transition to lead network deployment for future OpenAI data center projects, defining standards and guiding implementation across multiple locations.

Candidates must be able to sit onsite in Abilene, Texas 5 days per week

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as OpenAI’s technical lead technician during the current campus build, partnering with internal engineers and external contractors on design reviews, installation plans, and acceptance criteria.

  • Spend significant time on the data-center floor performing inspections, assisting with cable routing/termination when needed, conducting fiber testing (OTDR, power levels, continuity), and resolving installation challenges in real time.

  • Troubleshoot and optimize cabling routes, patching, and equipment turn-up to ensure clean, reliable handoff to network operations.

  • Contribute to design discussions and peer reviews for structured cabling and physical network layouts, providing practical field feedback to engineering teams.

  • Develop repeatable engineering standards, as-built documentation, and deployment playbooks to accelerate future OpenAI campuses

  • Transition to hands-on design and deployment leadership for upcoming OpenAI data center expansions, owning network physical-layer deployment from design through commissioning.

Qualifications

  • Have 7+ years of experience in large-scale datacenter network deployment, structured cabling, or physical-layer installation.

  • Possess deep knowledge of fiber/copper plant design, cabling standards, and hyperscale network best practices.

  • Excel in field work while applying seasoned technical judgment to solve complex installation and testing issues.

  • Adapt quickly to changing build conditions and enjoy learning emerging networking technologies.

  • Communicate clearly with construction, engineering, and operations teams to drive projects to completion.

  • Are willing to be based at a partner campus during the initial build phase and to travel to future OpenAI data center projects.

Preferred Skills

  • Exposure to automation tools (Ansible, SaltStack) or scripting (Python, Shell) for configuration or documentation.

  • Experience with hyperscale Clos fabrics or large-scale network design.

  • Familiarity with routing and switching concepts (BGP, OSPF, EVPN/VXLAN) and basic Linux/network troubleshooting.

  • Industry certifications such as BICSI, CCNA/CCNP, or equivalent.

title: Technical Certification Lead
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Customer Education helps customers build the practical skills and confidence to use AI and OpenAI products safely and effectively. We bring together customer insight, learning and enablement expertise, product signals, and measurement to help organizations move from access to durable adoption.

Within Customer Education, the Certification team helps individuals demonstrate competence for in-demand AI skills and helps customers and partners validate that their workforce has the skills they need to meet their AI-enabled business goals. Our work centers on the belief that learners should understand where to go to build skills and capabilities, how to demonstrate them, and what to pursue next. Similarly, Enterprise leaders should understand what each credential signifies and how it supports workforce readiness. We do this with transparency for the overall OpenAI credential framework and providing trusted, role-based certifications that verify practical capability.

About the Role

As Technical Certification Lead, you will lead the design, development, and ongoing quality of OpenAI’s technical role-based certifications. Your work will make clear what each certification validates and what candidates must demonstrate to earn it.

This is a hands-on people manager role on the Certification team. You will manage the Certification Assessment Specialists building technical assessments across the certification portfolio, setting priorities, coaching team members, and holding the team accountable for quality and delivery. You will personally turn shared certification frameworks into certification-specific competency models, job-task analyses, assessment blueprints, scoring rubrics, and passing criteria.

You will apply program-wide certification standards to individual technical certifications and partner with operations and platform teams to prepare assessments for delivery. You will align learning content to competency models and blueprints while keeping confidential assessment content separate from learning development.

You will take certifications from role analysis through pilot, launch readiness, and ongoing maintenance. As AI tools and technical roles evolve, you will keep the assessments relevant to the work people actually do.

Success means each certification makes a clear claim about what someone can do, the assessment supports that claim, and the curriculum gives candidates a practical way to build the skills they need.

In this role, you will:

  • Build and maintain competency models and facilitate job-task analyses for technical roles. Work with practitioners and subject matter experts (SMEs) to identify critical tasks, define the skills and proficiency each role requires, and keep the models current.

  • Define and maintain assessment blueprints and write scoring rubrics. Translate competencies into realistic tasks, define what evidence candidates must produce, and set clear criteria for evaluating performance in line with shared certification standards.

  • Lead standard-setting with subject matter experts and a psychometrician or measurement specialist, using a shared methodology to recommend the passing standard for each assessment.

  • Validate AI-assisted scoring against judgments from calibrated human reviewers. Define when scores require human review, and revalidate scoring after material changes to the model, assessment task, or rubric.

  • Manage and develop Certification Assessment Specialists across technical certifications. Set priorities, review their work, and guide the build and maintenance of assessment tasks, environments, evidence capture, and scoring workflows.

  • Secure and manage SME commitments for role analysis, task design, technical review, pilot feedback, and maintenance. Define what each expert is contributing and when it is needed.

  • Share competency models and permitted blueprint information with learning content developers, and review their content for alignment. Coordinate assessment and curriculum changes through the technical lead rather than direct sharing of confidential assessment details between assessment and learning teams.

  • Own ongoing assessment quality for each technical certification within shared program standards. Use pilot results, scoring consistency, technical reviews, and candidate feedback to identify issues. Partner with certification and measurement teams to calibrate rubrics and decide what needs updating or revalidation.

  • Provide technical input when candidates challenge an assessment task. Partner with operations to oversee fixes and validation for confirmed defects.

  • Define what credential holders must demonstrate to stay certified, when they must demonstrate it, and what evidence counts. Work with the team to align those requirements with shared standards, and with learning, platform, and operations teams to make appropriate renewal options available.

  • Make evidence-based readiness recommendations for pilots, launches, and updates. Document what has been tested, what risks remain, and which issues must be resolved before release. Coordinate technical handoff and delivery readiness with operations and platform teams.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have led the development and maintenance of role-based technical certifications or other high-stakes technical assessments, from role analysis through pilot, launch, and post-launch improvement.

  • Have directly managed and developed engineers or technical assessment specialists, including setting priorities, providing performance feedback, and improving the quality of the team’s work.

  • Have experience working at a technology company in a fast-paced environment, setting priorities and delivering work amid changing requirements and evolving business needs.

  • Have personally built competency models, facilitated job-task analyses, and used them to define assessment blueprints and write scoring rubrics.

  • Have designed hands-on assessments for software engineering, AI, cloud, or technical implementation roles, and can distinguish authentic evidence of capability from completion of a task.

  • Have built or validated AI-assisted scoring for assessments, with appropriate human review.

  • Have recruited and coordinated subject matter experts across teams, secured their time, and turned differing expert views into clear assessment decisions.

  • Have used evidence from pilots and live assessments to improve tasks and scoring, and can explain what would make you recommend a launch, a narrower pilot, or a delay.

  • Have worked with learning content developers to map curriculum and practice to competencies while maintaining the separation between preparation and assessment content.

  • Communicate technical and measurement tradeoffs clearly to engineers, learning teams, operations partners, and leaders.

  • Can review technical assessment work directly and coach others through design decisions without becoming the bottleneck.

  • Have maintained multiple technical assessments as products, tools, or job expectations changed, and know when to update or retire a task.

  • Care deeply about accessible assessments, consistent scoring, and making only the claims the evidence supports.

It’s a plus if you have experience:

  • Designing practical assessments for AI application development, agentic workflows, or customer-facing AI deployments.

  • Working with psychometricians on standard setting, rubric calibration, or validation of performance assessments.

  • Launching hands-on assessments across live and virtual delivery environments.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI's Industrial Compute organization is building and operating the infrastructure foundation for the next generation of AI. Infrastructure Operations works across facilities, hardware, network operations, incident management, data center engineering, delivery teams, and external partners to bring capacity online safely, understand its operational state, and improve it over time.

As OpenAI's data center portfolio grows across first-party and partner-delivered capacity, the organization needs clear goals, trusted data, repeatable processes, and systems that make ownership, risk, readiness, and performance visible. This role will help build the operating mechanisms that allow Infrastructure Operations to scale with rigor.

About the Role

We are seeking a Technical Program Manager to own the systems, data, reporting, governance, and program-management backbone for Infrastructure Operations. Reporting to the Delivery & Operations Lead, you will translate strategy into executable goals and operating cadences, turn operational needs into software and data solutions, and create the mechanisms that keep a rapidly evolving organization aligned and accountable.

This role will also own the current 1P+3P delivery-tracking layer within Operations: milestones, delivery timelines, quantity forecasts, risks, decisions, and executive reporting. You will partner closely with 1P Delivery Program Management, Compute TPMs, Data Center Engineering, construction, commissioning, and operations leaders to ensure that delivery information becomes complete, usable input for readiness, handover, and ongoing operations.

You will own program health and the operating system around it: the goals, data definitions, workflows, reporting, decision paths, and follow-through that help functional DRIs execute. The ideal candidate is comfortable in ambiguity, technically fluent enough to implement real systems, and relentless about converting scattered information into durable mechanisms.

Key Responsibilities

Establish and run Infrastructure Operations' goal-setting and operating cadence, including quarterly goals, weekly performance reviews, prioritization, action tracking, decision logs, escalation paths, and closure criteria.

About the Team

Safety Systems manages the complete lifecycle of safety efforts for OpenAI’s frontier models, ensuring our models are deployed responsibly and have a positive impact on society. Our work spans diverse research and engineering initiatives—from system-level safeguards and model training to evaluation and red-teaming—all aimed at mitigating misuse and maintaining our high bar for safety. About the Role

The Safety Measurement Research Program Manager drives OpenAI’s strategy for safety measurement and evaluations, partnering closely with safety research, data science, and engineering to advance how we measure harm and safeguard efficacy across research and production.

You will work directly with researchers, data scientists, policy owners, and product teams who contribute to or use our measurement systems, identifying the most important problems to solve and shaping the data, dashboards, tools, and workflows we build for them. title: Software Engineer, Shop/Feed Ads
descriptionHtml:
About the team

The Monetization team is a new cross-functional group spanning engineering, product, research, and design. We are building the foundational systems that will help OpenAI scale access to intelligence responsibly.

Our mission is to create user-first, privacy-preserving monetization products—including next-generation ads experiences—that strengthen trust, expand economic opportunity, and support OpenAI’s long-term innovation. We believe monetization should deliver clear user value, uphold rigorous privacy and safety standards, and sustain a healthy ecosystem for developers and businesses.

The team operates in a greenfield environment, moving quickly through prototyping, experimentation, and iterative deployment. We partner closely across Product, Design, and Research to bring new capabilities into real-world systems at global scale.


About the role

We’re looking for an experienced Software Engineer to lead the design and development of the systems that turn advertiser feeds (eg. retail feeds, travel feeds etc.) into relevant, reliably delivered ads. In this foundational role, you will build across the full ads lifecycle—from ingesting and organizing retailer or travel catalogs into efficient retrieval systems, supporting ranking models, and serving ads at scale.

This role is well suited to an engineer with direct experience in product ads retrieval, ranking, and delivery, along with a strong understanding of merchant feeds and shopping systems such as Google Shopping, YouTube product ads, or Amazon. We also welcome engineers with Senior Staff-level or greater scope who have deep ownership of large-scale catalogs, search and indexing, ads serving, or closely related distributed systems.

You will independently own complex systems, make sound technical tradeoffs, and help define the architecture and roadmap for Shopping/Travel/Feed Ads. You will collaborate closely with Ads ML, Ads Delivery, Product, Design, and Research to connect accurate, fresh advertiser feed information with useful ads experiences in ChatGPT.

This role is based in San Francisco and Mountain View. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.


In this role, you will

  • Design and build pipelines that ingest, validate, normalize, and refresh merchant product feeds, keeping catalog information accurate and available for serving.

  • Develop scalable catalog storage and indexing systems that make large inventories searchable and reflect changes in product availability, pricing, and attributes.

  • Build search and retrieval systems that efficiently identify relevant, eligible products across merchant catalogs.

  • Partner with Ads ML to connect product retrieval with ranking models through dependable interfaces, features, and serving infrastructure.

  • Engineer low-latency, high-throughput ads delivery systems with strong reliability and correctness guarantees.

  • Design real-time event pipelines and distributed storage that support catalog freshness, serving decisions, and downstream feedback.

  • Build observability and quality controls to detect feed errors, stale inventory, indexing delays, and serving issues.

  • Define technical direction and drive complex projects from early prototypes through production deployment and operation.

  • Operate systems with high engineering rigor through testing, monitoring, privacy and security reviews, and strong operational practices.

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Have extensive experience building and operating large-scale distributed systems, with direct ownership of product ads retrieval, ranking infrastructure, or delivery.

  • Understand merchant feeds and shopping systems, including how catalog quality, product availability, and freshness affect relevance and ads performance.

  • Have built systems for shopping or product ads at platforms such as Google Shopping, YouTube, Amazon, or a comparable environment.

  • Alternatively, have operated at Senior Staff-level scope or above, leading the architecture and delivery of large-scale catalogs, search and indexing platforms, ads serving, or related backend systems.

  • Have built low-latency, high-throughput services and data pipelines with demanding reliability and correctness requirements.

  • Can reason across ingestion, storage, indexing, retrieval, ranking, and serving, and make thoughtful tradeoffs between freshness, relevance, latency, and cost.

  • Are comfortable partnering with machine-learning teams to bring ranking models and signals into dependable production systems.

  • Can define technical direction in an ambiguous 0→1 environment and independently drive complex work across teams.

  • Communicate clearly and make technical decisions grounded in user value, merchant experience, and long-term system health.

About the Team

The ChatGPT Library team is building the place where people can save, organize, rediscover, and build on the content they create with ChatGPT. Our goal is to make ChatGPT more useful over time by helping users seamlessly return to important files, images, conversations, and other content across their devices.

 

The team works at the intersection of product engineering, design, and AI research to create intuitive, personalized experiences that make users’ content easy to find and act on. On Android, we are focused on delivering fast, reliable, and deeply native experiences that put a user’s evolving body of work at their fingertips.

 

About the Role

We are looking for a senior Android engineer to help build the future of ChatGPT Library on mobile. You will own high-impact product experiences across the Android stack, shaping how millions of people save, organize, discover, and interact with their content in ChatGPT.

title: Power Generation Design Engineer, Electrical & Mechanical
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital and delivery partners, is building the infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems. The Data Center Engineering team defines repeatable technical standards and carries them through design, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness. The team works across data center facilities, power generation, compute infrastructure, construction, procurement, and operations to deliver reliable capacity at unprecedented scale and speed.

About the Role

We are seeking a Power Generation Design Engineer to help design and integrate generation plants and balance-of-plant systems for large AI data center campuses. This role spans electrical and mechanical systems, including generation equipment, campus and grid interfaces, fuel and auxiliary systems, cooling, controls, and data center loads.

The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in either electrical or mechanical engineering, along with the cross-disciplinary judgment to evaluate how the full plant operates as an integrated system. You will establish technical requirements, assess vendor and EPC solutions, resolve design interfaces, and carry systems from concept through commissioning and validated operation.

Travel: 50%

Responsibilities

  • Develop and review generation-plant basis-of-design documents, design criteria, specifications, diagrams, calculations, and reference architectures.

  • Define and coordinate interfaces among generation equipment, substations, campus distribution, grid connections, fuel systems, cooling, controls, and data center loads.

  • Evaluate generation technologies and operating modes, including grid-connected and islanded operation, synchronization, load sharing, black start, and restoration.

  • Lead or review discipline-specific engineering analyses. Electrical studies may include load flow, short circuit, arc flash, protection coordination, transient, grounding, and motor starting. Mechanical analyses may include thermal performance, hydraulics, pressure drop, ventilation, vibration, acoustics, and heat recovery.

  • Review OEM and EPC proposals, equipment ratings and performance data, operating envelopes, failure modes, test plans, maintenance strategies, and lifecycle tradeoffs.

  • Translate data center load profiles and operating requirements into generation-system capacity, redundancy, performance, and control requirements.

  • Coordinate with electrical, mechanical, controls, CSA, fuel, utility, environmental, fire-protection, and data center engineering teams to resolve design and delivery interfaces.

  • Support procurement, factory acceptance testing, construction, startup, energization, commissioning, performance testing, and root-cause investigations.

  • Develop repeatable technical standards and reference designs that improve reliability, maintainability, and deployment speed across future projects.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of engineering experience in power generation, utilities, industrial systems, microgrids, oil and gas, or mission-critical infrastructure.

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field.

  • Deep technical expertise in either electrical power systems or mechanical/process systems, with experience collaborating across the other discipline.

  • Electrical expertise may include generators, transformers, HV/MV switchgear, protection and controls, grounding, auxiliary power, grid interconnection, and power-system studies.

  • Mechanical expertise may include rotating equipment, fuel and fluid systems, piping, heat transfer, cooling, ventilation, lubrication, water treatment, exhaust, and mechanical auxiliaries.

  • Experience evaluating OEM data, equipment performance, operating scenarios, failure modes, and maintenance requirements.

  • Experience carrying engineering designs through construction, startup, commissioning, and operational validation.

  • Ability to communicate technical risks and tradeoffs clearly across engineering, vendors, construction, and operations.

Preferred Skills

  • Professional Engineer license.

  • Experience with gas turbines, reciprocating engines, battery systems, combined heat and power, heat recovery, or hybrid generation plants.

  • Familiarity with relevant codes and standards, including NEC, NFPA, IEEE, NERC, ASME, API, ASHRAE, and utility requirements.

  • Proficiency with applicable analysis or modeling tools, such as ETAP, PSCAD, PSS/E, SKM, EasyPower, process simulation, hydraulic modeling, or CFD.

  • Experience supporting high-density data center loads and rapidly changing AI compute demand.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Integrity team builds the systems OpenAI uses to understand, prevent, and respond to misuse across our products. We partner with Product, Policy, Safety Systems, User Operations, Security, Legal, Privacy, OpenAI for Government, and research teams to turn policy and threat models into product controls, review workflows, measurement systems, and enforcement paths.

About the Role

We are hiring a Product Manager to own Integrity's product strategy for sensitive deployments: contexts where model capability, customer or deployment setting, privacy constraints, and misuse potential make the operating bar unusually high. This includes government and other high stakes deployments, regulated or high-trust enterprise contexts, zero data retention and privacy-constrained environments, and agentic workflows where harm can unfold across many steps rather than a single prompt.

title: People Research Scientist
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s People team hires, engages, and retains world-class talent to safely build and deploy AGI that benefits all of humanity. The People Analytics team helps leaders make better, evidence-based talent decisions.

About the Role

As a People Research Scientist, you will bring deep expertise in research design, measurement, experimentation, and applied data science to OpenAI’s most important People programs. You will design studies, evaluate people processes, and help leaders better empower employees, strengthen organizational systems, and deliver exceptional employee experiences.

This is a high-ownership individual contributor role combining hands-on research, methodological leadership, and scalable people science capabilities. We’re looking for an experienced researcher who can turn ambiguous People questions into rigorous designs, validated insights, and actionable recommendations.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA or Mountain View, CA, with occasional travel to our San Francisco office.

What You’ll Do:

  • Design rigorous research and evaluation strategies for recruiting, organizational health, manager effectiveness, employee experience, and talent outcomes.

  • Apply advanced statistical modeling, machine learning, and research methods to inform program design, evaluate effectiveness, and quantify business impact.

  • Partner with People Operations, data engineering, and people systems teams to define data requirements, improve data quality, establish documentation standards, and ensure research datasets are governed, reproducible, and privacy-preserving.

  • Build scalable people science infrastructure, including self-service agentic tools, automated validation workflows, reusable research datasets and analytical pipelines.

  • High proficiency in R or Python and SQL, with experience working across complex, messy datasets.

title: Manufacturing Quality Engineer, Data Center Modular Builds
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI and its capital and technology partners are building a global network of data centers for demanding AI workloads. The Infrastructure Quality team sets and verifies quality, reliability, and performance requirements for equipment across that network.

We work with manufacturing partners, general contractors, engineers, and operations staff from supplier qualification through commissioning. Together, we verify that equipment arrives ready for installation, startup, and long-term service.

About the Role

As a Manufacturing Quality Engineer for Data Center Modular Builds, you will own supplier manufacturing and integration quality for modular systems, including hot aisle containment (HAC), modular cooling units (MCUs), and electrical skids. Working with mechanical and electrical integrators and their suppliers, you will lead supplier qualification, support product and process development, and translate engineering requirements into manufacturing controls, inspections, and acceptance criteria.

You will partner with cross-functional teams to monitor production and integration quality, conduct audits, and resolve risks to integrated products acceptance and delivery. You will also serve as the primary quality contact for site escalations involving manufacturing or integration defects in modular systems and(OFCI) components. Through structured root-cause investigations, corrective action, and closed-loop learning (CLL), you will drive resolution and feed field lessons back into supplier processes to prevent recurrence and improve future builds.

Key responsibilities

Modular Systems Quality and Supplier Development

  • Lead supplier qualification and support product and process development for mechanical and electrical integrators.

  • Oversee manufacturing and integration quality for modular builds, including HACs, MCUs, and electrical skids.

  • Work with integrators and suppliers to translate engineering requirements and critical-to-quality (CTQ) characteristics into practical manufacturing controls, inspection points, and acceptance criteria.

  • Develop and drive supplier improvement plans (SIPs) using the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) approach to strengthen manufacturing and integration processes.

  • Use production data, audit findings, test results, and supplier scorecards to identify systemic or recurring issues, prioritize improvements, and measure sustained results.

Site Escalations and Corrective Action

  • Serve as the primary quality point of contact for escalated site issues attributable to manufacturing and integration failures, coordinating containment and resolution with site teams and supplier factories.

  • Lead root-cause and corrective-action (RCCA) investigations using structured methods such as 8D and 5 Whys. Verify root causes, track corrective and preventive actions to closure, and confirm their effectiveness.

  • Apply closed-loop learning (CLL) to incorporate field findings and lessons learned into supplier and integrator manufacturing controls and future builds, preventing recurrence.

Manufacturing and Integration Monitoring

  • Partner with Quality Program and Manufacturing Operations teams to monitor production and integration progress, quality controls, inspection results, and factory test readiness. Identify emerging risks and coordinate timely action with suppliers.

  • Conduct product and process audits during and after manufacturing and integration to verify compliance with engineering requirements, approved procedures, and quality standards. Document findings and track corrective actions to closure.

  • Align production checkpoints, inspections, and factory testing requirements with suppliers, engineering, sourcing, supply chain, commissioning, and quality teams. Coordinate deviation resolution and escalate risks to equipment acceptance or delivery.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical, mechanical, or industrial engineering.

  • At least 10 years of data center industry experience spanning quality engineering and manufacturing engineering.

  • Experience working with integrators and suppliers across multiple tiers to manage quality throughout the product lifecycle, from OFCI component manufacturing through integration and site issue resolution, and drive product and process improvements.

  • Ability to define CTQs and acceptance criteria, develop inspection and test checklists, review test results, and maintain auditable quality records.

  • Experience monitoring supplier production, conducting product and process audits, managing controlled documents and deviations, and using supplier scorecards to drive improvement.

  • Demonstrated experience leading root-cause investigations and corrective actions for manufacturing or field issues using structured methods such as 8D and 5 Whys, and driving continuous improvement through PDCA.

  • Ability to coordinate supplier schedules and plan inspections and tests across multiple equipment programs.

  • Ability to communicate quality requirements, resolve issues, and coordinate decisions across suppliers, engineering, commissioning, sourcing, supply chain, manufacturing, operations, and construction teams.

  • Willingness and ability to travel approximately 40% of the time to supplier manufacturing facilities and data center project sites.

Preferred Skills

  • Technical knowledge of data center infrastructure, including mechanical, electrical, and controls systems.

  • Experience in supplier performance management for mission-critical facilities.

  • ASQ Certified Quality Engineer, Quality Manager, or Quality Auditor.

  • Experience in industrial or high-volume manufacturing environments.

title: Machine Learning Engineer, API Multicloud
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s API Multicloud team is responsible for extending OpenAI’s API platform into strategic cloud environments, starting with AWS. The team’s mission is to distribute OpenAI’s API broadly and safely by enabling key API technologies in AWS-native environments, in close partnership with Amazon and internal teams across Codex, Research, Safety Systems, and Applied.

The team is focused on bringing core developer and enterprise capabilities into cloud-native environments, including AWS-hosted Codex, model customization / post-training as a service, and new stateful runtime environments for agentic workloads. This work sits at the intersection of production ML systems, developer platforms, model behavior, and large-scale infrastructure.

About the Role

We’re hiring Machine Learning Engineers to build and improve the AI systems that help strategic partners adapt OpenAI models to important use cases in cloud-native environments. This role spans post-training workflows, evaluation, data pipelines, model behavior, and API/infrastructure integration.

You’ll work at the boundary between partner needs and core ML systems: helping teams understand what is and isn’t working, diagnosing issues in training and evaluation workflows, and turning those learnings into improvements to the underlying platform. You should enjoy working with external technical partners, extracting the real goal from messy requests, and pushing back or reframing when the requested experiment is not the highest-leverage path. You’ll collaborate closely with Research, Applied, Safety Systems, infrastructure teams, and external technical partners to solve ambiguous model-performance problems. When you succeed, strategic partners and internal teams will be able to improve model behavior with confidence, driving measurable product improvements while the systems behind that work become more reliable, scalable, and effective over time.

In this role, you will

  • Partner with strategic customers and internal teams to define target model behaviors, diagnose failure modes, and translate real-world needs into training, evaluation, and system requirements.

  • Build and scale production ML systems for model customization, post-training, and fine-tuning-as-a-service workflows.

  • Design, run, and interpret experiments to see whether training and customization workflows are producing the intended outcomes, and identify changes to data, evaluation, training, or infrastructure that improve performance.

  • Partner with backend and infrastructure engineers to integrate ML capabilities into AWS-native API environments.

  • Feed learnings from partner deployments back into the platform by proposing and implementing improvements to post-training systems, tooling, APIs, and developer workflows.

  • Work closely with Research and Applied teams to bring model improvements, training workflows, and evaluation best practices into production.

  • Help design systems that allow strategic partners and enterprise customers to safely customize OpenAI models for high-value use cases.

  • Debug and improve complex systems spanning model behavior, training data, APIs, distributed infrastructure, and customer-facing product surfaces.

  • Operate with high ownership in a 0→1 environment where requirements are ambiguous, systems are evolving quickly, and reliability matters.

Your background might look something like:

  • Master’s or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • 3+ years of professional engineering experience in relevant ML, infrastructure, or product-driven engineering roles.

  • Strong ML engineering experience building, training, fine-tuning, evaluating, or deploying production AI systems, with hands-on experience in deep learning, transformer models, and frameworks like PyTorch or TensorFlow.

  • Hands-on experience with training and fine-tuning large language models, including methods like supervised fine-tuning, distillation, preference optimization, reinforcement learning, or other post-training techniques.

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, systems design, and high-quality production code in Python, Rust, or similar languages.

  • Experience with model customization, evaluation systems, data pipelines, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, or production ML platform tradeoffs.

  • Ability to operate across model behavior, APIs, and infrastructure, while collaborating closely with Research, Safety, product engineering, infrastructure, and external technical partners.

  • Comfort moving quickly through ambiguity, owning problems end-to-end, and learning whatever is needed to get the job done.

title: Lead Revenue Accounting, Technical (Strategic Partnerships)
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI Finance helps ensure the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission of ensuring that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

Within Finance, the Technical Revenue team partners with Product, Strategic Partnerships, Business Development, Growth, Legal, Deal Desk, GTM, Strategic Finance, Revenue Accounting, and Finance Systems to enable scalable, audit-ready monetization. We advise on commercial and contract design, establish defensible accounting positions under ASC 606, and translate those conclusions into repeatable processes, systems, controls, and reporting.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Senior Manager of Revenue Recognition to lead revenue strategy and technical accounting for OpenAI’s strategic commercial deals.

Reporting to the Head of Technical Revenue, you will serve as the primary revenue advisor for large, bespoke, and non-standard deals outside OpenAI’s standard product and service offerings. Your portfolio may include strategic collaborations, cloud marketplaces, platform and distribution deals, licensing and revenue-share models, joint go-to-market initiatives, research collaborations, and other emerging commercial structures.

You will engage early in the deal lifecycle to help shape commercially viable, accounting-compliant, and operationally scalable outcomes. You will establish the accounting posture, identify required contract and product terms, define reporting and control requirements, and ensure that deal economics, billing flows, and revenue recognition remain aligned as the business evolves.

This role requires strong technical accounting judgment, commercial fluency, executive communication, and the ability to create clarity and ownership in areas where precedent may not yet exist.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Own technical revenue accounting for strategic commercial deals, including large, bespoke, and non-standard transactions outside OpenAI’s standard product and service offerings.

  • Serve as the primary revenue advisor for strategic collaborations, cloud marketplaces, platform and distribution deals, licensing and revenue-share models, and other emerging commercial structures.

  • Partner early with Strategic Partnerships, Product, GTM, Strategic Finance, Legal, Deal Desk, and Tax to understand and influence deal economics, pricing, contract terms, and operational design.

  • Evaluate complex and ambiguous transactions under ASC 606, including principal-versus-agent considerations, gross-versus-net presentation, performance obligations, variable consideration, contract combinations, commitments, credits, incentives, and related-party considerations.

  • Translate technical conclusions into practical commercial guardrails and establish clear intake, escalation, and decision-making frameworks for material deals and amendments.

  • Define the data, reporting, billing, settlement, reconciliation, and control requirements needed to operationalize new commercial models and support accurate revenue recognition.

  • Draft audit-ready technical accounting memos and policies, lead discussions with external auditors, and clearly communicate conclusions and trade-offs to senior stakeholders.

  • Manage and develop team members and external resources, prioritize concurrent high-value deals, and strengthen the team’s ability to influence commercial decisions proactively.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 10+ years of technical revenue accounting or related advisory experience, with deep ASC 606 expertise and experience leading complex workstreams or teams.

  • Significant experience supporting large, bespoke commercial deals, strategic collaborations, cloud marketplaces, platform distribution, licensing, revenue-share models, or other multi-party transactions.

  • A track record of influencing commercial strategy, pricing, product design, and contract terms before launch or signature.

  • Experience navigating emerging monetization models such as advertising revenue, marketplaces/commerce platforms, or other multi-sided ecosystems is a strong plus.

  • Strong command of principal-versus-agent analysis, gross-versus-net presentation, variable consideration, consideration payable to a customer, contract combinations, and complex performance-obligation assessments.

  • A track record of influencing commercial strategy, pricing, product design, and contract terms before launch or signature.

  • Experience translating evolving commercial models into scalable billing, accounting, reconciliation, reporting, systems, and control requirements.

  • Strong commercial judgment and executive communication skills, with the ability to explain complex accounting issues and practical trade-offs to senior non-accounting stakeholders.

title: Strategic Sourcing Leader, Professional Services
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI Finance helps ensure the organisation is positioned for long-term success as we pursue our mission. The Strategic Sourcing & Procurement team helps OpenAI scale responsibly and at speed by choosing the right external partners, structuring strong commercial agreements and building resilient supplier relationships. We partner with teams across the company to turn rapidly evolving needs into practical, economically sound solutions.

Professional Services provides specialist expertise and capacity across OpenAI, spanning consulting and advisory, finance and accounting, legal, people-related services and managed services. Our sourcing team helps business leaders define the outcomes they need, select capable partners and establish clear commercial and delivery accountability.

About the Role

We are seeking a Strategic Sourcing Leader to lead and develop the Professional Services sourcing team and set direction across its portfolio. This is a people-management role with accountability for team performance, commercial quality, stakeholder experience and sustained business outcomes. You will translate business priorities into category strategies, achievable delivery plans and clear decision authority, while developing the judgement and independence of experienced sourcing professionals.

You will oversee a broad portfolio, from strategic advisory relationships and enterprise programmes to a high volume of statements of work and renewals. You will remain hands-on in selected complex negotiations and critical decisions, while enabling the team to own and deliver its work. Working with senior leaders across Finance, Accounting, Legal, People, Extended Workforce and the business, you will create clarity from incomplete information, resolve competing priorities and adapt the team's approach as OpenAI grows.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead and develop the team: set clear objectives and expectations, delegate with appropriate decision boundaries, provide regular feedback, review performance and address persistent gaps. Build development and coverage plans that strengthen capability and reduce reliance on individual experts.

  • Set the Professional Services portfolio strategy and roadmap, connecting business objectives, demand, spend, supplier markets and risk. Guide category plans and decisions on where to compete, consolidate, retain specialist partners or change the service delivery model.

  • Manage the team's pipeline and capacity across strategic negotiations, supplier governance and recurring SOWs. Allocate work by capability, complexity and risk; make resource constraints and dependencies visible; and agree priorities and recovery plans before commitments become unachievable.

  • Personally lead selected critical negotiations and set standards for commercial quality across the team. Review strategy and assumptions early, using credible alternatives and comparable economics to shape scope, resource mix, pricing, deliverables, acceptance criteria, change controls, audit rights and exit protections.

  • Build proportionate intake, tiering, preferred-partner models, playbooks and review pathways with Procurement Operations, Contract Management, Enablement and control functions. Agree decision rights and usable handovers so repeatable work moves efficiently and material exceptions receive the right attention.

  • Strengthen supplier relationships and accountability through segmentation, competition, performance reviews and improvement plans. Agree post-signature owners with the business and use service evidence, concentration risk, renewal exposure and transition options to guide supplier decisions. Assess supplier productivity proposals for their effect on staffing, fees, quality and delivery risk.

  • Partner with Finance and Accounting on spend visibility, demand scenarios, forecasting, approval discipline and invoice-to-contract alignment. Test fee models, staffing assumptions, change exposure and total economics, with clear baselines for savings, cost avoidance and realized value.

  • Partner with Legal, People and Extended Workforce to select appropriate service models and distinguish Professional Services from contingent labour or hiring needs. Translate specialist guidance into practical safeguards for service delivery, intellectual property, confidentiality and workforce-related risk.

  • Establish a concise view of portfolio and team performance covering commercial and service outcomes, pipeline health, cycle time, risk, stakeholder experience and team capability. Use evidence to improve decisions, commitments and delivery; distinguish negotiated benefits from value realized.

  • Build trusted senior stakeholder relationships and challenge demand, scope or supplier preferences constructively. Resolve difficult trade-offs on value, speed, quality and risk, and escalate decisions beyond your authority with clear options and a recommendation.

  • Personally use approved AI tools and lead adoption of improved sourcing workflows across the team, including supplier research, proposal analysis, negotiation preparation and reporting. Validate sources and calculations, retain human commercial judgement, and measure adoption and gains in quality, speed or capacity.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 10+ years of progressive strategic sourcing, procurement or category management experience, with substantial depth across multiple Professional Services categories and ownership from strategy through supplier performance.

  • Bring 5+ years of people leadership experience, including formal responsibility for objectives, performance, development and delegation. Can demonstrate stronger team capability, independent judgement and sustained delivery through your leadership.

  • Have personally led complex services negotiations and can explain the alternatives, commercial decisions and measurable outcomes, while showing how you coach others to deliver comparable quality.

  • Understand consulting, advisory, managed services and project-based commercial models, including experience with large multidisciplinary firms such as the Big Four and specialist providers. Bring breadth across areas such as finance, accounting, legal, healthcare or benefits-related services, alongside sound judgement on workforce boundaries.

  • Have turned category strategies into practical operating improvements, balancing standardization with flexibility and strategic work with recurring demand. Can show adoption, reliable delivery and stronger stakeholder experience.

  • Influence senior stakeholders through trust, structured thinking and concise communication. Can work through disagreement, make trade-offs explicit and seek decisions at the right level.

  • Bring strong financial and analytical judgement, using imperfect spend, supplier and performance data to compare options, test assumptions and verify business value beyond negotiated savings.

  • Lead effectively through ambiguity, rapid change and limited structure. Can reset priorities, invite challenge and adapt working practices to different company stages, operating models and organisational cultures.

  • Have practical experience using AI to redesign sourcing work and helping others adopt it, with clear human review, quality checks and evidence of improvement.

  • Create an inclusive team environment with clear expectations, constructive feedback and room for respectful challenge. Combine accountability with coaching, recognize progress and build resilience through prioritization and dependable support.

title: Technical Program Manager, Capacity Analytics & Tooling
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Compute Infrastructure team runs the GPU fleet and large-scale compute clusters that serve the models backing ChatGPT and the API, while also supporting training workloads for our next generation models. We operate a large, modern GPU fleet and provide a unified platform for other OpenAI teams to run production Applied AI and Research training workloads.

We seek to learn from deployment and distribute the benefits of AI, while ensuring that this powerful tool is used responsibly and safely. Safety is more important to us than unfettered growth.

About the Role

You will join the Compute Infrastructure TPM team as a Technical Program Manager for Capacity Analytics & Tooling. You will serve as the product manager for our supply and demand planning tools, owning the strategy, roadmap, and delivery of the systems teams use to forecast demand, understand supply, and plan allocations. Your users will include Product TPMs, Capacity TPMs, and Compute TPMs, alongside partners across Finance, Accounting, Leadership, Engineering, and Research.

This role combines product management, technical program leadership, data engineering, and applied data science. You will partner with engineering and data teams to build reliable data foundations, improve forecasting and scenario planning, and scale our tools and success metrics across CPU, storage, network, and GPU resources. You will help teams make informed capacity decisions across AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI, and other infrastructure providers.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the product strategy and roadmap for supply and demand planning tools. Understand user needs, set priorities, define success measures, and guide delivery from initial requirements through adoption and ongoing improvement.

  • Build useful planning workflows. Translate complex processes into tools for demand intake, forecasting, supply tracking, scenario analysis, and allocation planning. Help teams understand what infrastructure they need, when it will be available, and which gaps require action.

  • Scale the data infrastructure behind capacity planning. Partner with engineering on ingestion, transformation, storage, and delivery of planning data. Guide technical tradeoffs as the number of resources, providers, data sources, and users grows.

  • Make planning data consistent and trustworthy. Establish shared data models and definitions for supply, demand, allocations, utilization, and cost. Drive data cleaning, validation, reconciliation, and traceability so users can understand and trust planning outputs.

  • Advance forecasting and analytical capabilities. Work with engineering and data partners to connect product and research plans to infrastructure demand. Make assumptions, uncertainty, forecast accuracy, and capacity constraints visible to decision makers.

  • Define and scale meaningful success metrics. Measure data quality, forecast performance, planning speed, and tool adoption. Establish consistent ways to track capacity availability, utilization, and efficiency across CPU, storage, network, and GPU resources.

  • Support planning across multiple cloud providers. Build capabilities that account for differences in resource types, regions, availability, commercial commitments, and deployment constraints across AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI, and other providers.

  • Lead delivery across data, infrastructure, and planning teams. Manage dependencies, technical tradeoffs, migrations, risks, and releases. Keep teams aligned on priorities and the decisions needed to move work forward.

  • Drive adoption and reduce manual planning work. Develop simple workflows, documentation, training, and feedback mechanisms. Identify recurring reconciliation and reporting work that can be improved through better data and automation.

  • Make capacity tradeoffs clear to leadership and partner teams. Provide useful views of gaps between supply and demand, allocation options, and their financial and operational consequences. Partner with Finance and Accounting to align planning data with budgeting and reporting needs.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 5+ years of experience leading technical programs or products in data platforms, infrastructure, capacity planning, or a related field, with a record of delivering systems that teams rely on.

  • Have owned an internal product or platform roadmap and translated complex operational needs into requirements, priorities, and releases that users adopt.

  • Have direct experience with capacity planning, including demand forecasting, supply planning, allocations, and resource constraints. You understand how utilization, performance, availability, and cost affect planning decisions.

  • Understand modern data infrastructure, including ingestion, transformation, batch and streaming processing, and analytical storage. You have worked with technologies such as Fivetran, dbt, Spark, Kafka, or comparable systems and can discuss their architectural tradeoffs.

  • Have practical experience with data modeling, data cleaning, validation, and reconciliation. You can use SQL and Python or similar tools to investigate discrepancies, validate assumptions, and prototype analyses.

  • Have applied quantitative methods to forecasting, scenario analysis, or optimization. You can assess model assumptions and uncertainty, evaluate forecast performance, and explain the limitations of an analysis.

  • Understand the capacity, performance, and cost characteristics of compute, storage, networking, and accelerators. You have experience working across multiple cloud environments and can account for differences between providers.

  • Can lead complex programs with many technical dependencies and align teams with different priorities. You communicate technical tradeoffs clearly to engineers, researchers, finance partners, and leaders.

  • Are resourceful in ambiguous environments, exercise sound product judgment, and build simple, scalable ways to solve complex planning problems.

  • Are interested in and thoughtful about the impacts of AGI.

descriptionHtml:
About the team

The Strategic Finance Data Science team helps OpenAI understand business performance and make informed decisions about growth, revenue, and resource allocation. We partner with Strategic Finance, Data Engineering, and business teams to build trusted metrics, explain what is changing, and support forecasting, planning, pricing, and investment decisions.

About the role

We’re looking for a Data Scientist, Analytics Enablement to turn complex financial and business questions into reliable data products, clear analyses, and actionable recommendations. You will work across the analytical workflow: define the question, establish trustworthy metrics and datasets, investigate the drivers, and help partners act on the findings.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You will combine the technical depth of analytics engineering with strong analytical judgment and close partnership with Strategic Finance. Your work will serve both executive reviews and the teams making day-to-day business decisions.

In this role, you will

  • Define and maintain trusted metrics and analytical datasets for revenue, usage, customer performance, compute consumption, and margin, with clear definitions and appropriate product, customer, and cohort detail.

  • Build automated dashboards and recurring reporting that help Finance leaders and operating teams understand performance, spot changes, and prioritize investigation.

The Data Understanding team is responsible for creating the high quality datasets and their quantized representation for OpenAI. title: Applied Data Scientist, Personalization & Machine Learning
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

We work across product, growth, and monetization to help people get more value from OpenAI’s products. We identify opportunities for machine learning, build and test early solutions, and partner with engineering and product to bring successful approaches into production.

About the Role

We’re looking for a data scientist who can enter an unfamiliar product area, find a useful ML application, and turn it into a working product intervention. You will own the work from problem definition and data preparation through modeling, experimentation, and launch evaluation.

Projects will include personalization, next-best-action recommendations, lifecycle management, promotion targeting, and models of retention and customer lifetime value. You will help identify opportunities, build proofs of concept, evaluate, and iterate.

In this role, you will:

  • Identify opportunities with product and business partners, define the decision a model will inform, and prioritize work by user value, feasibility, and expected impact.

  • Build datasets, features, reproducible training workflows, and models. You’ll use a combination of tools appropriate to the task at hand. 

  • Translate predictions into product actions. Design experiments and use causal reasoning to establish whether those actions improve user and business outcomes.

  • Partner with engineers on integration, serving or batch scoring, monitoring, and rollout. Stay involved through launch and iteration.

  • Explain results and limitations clearly, document decisions, and build reusable methods that other teams can adopt.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have built and evaluated applied ML systems that influenced a product or business decision, with clear ownership of the modeling work.

  • Write effective Python and SQL and can investigate imperfect data, debug models, and make pragmatic implementation choices. 

  • Build and schedule production scoring pipelines using dbt, airflow, and flyte.

  • Understand supervised learning, evaluation, experimentation, and the difference between predicting an outcome and changing it.

  • Can scope ambiguous problems, work across disciplines, and explain technical tradeoffs to colleagues with different backgrounds.

title: Trusted Access Specialist, Critical Harm Operations
descriptionHtml:
About the team

Trusted Access helps eligible customers access and use advanced AI capabilities with appropriate safeguards. Within User Safety & Risk Operations, we connect customer onboarding, eligibility review, access provisioning, and support into a service customers can navigate with confidence.

We work with Product, Engineering, technical support, regional operations, and customer-facing teams to resolve difficult access problems and improve the systems behind them. Our work combines sound judgment on individual cases with better products, clearer guidance, and automation that reduces unnecessary friction.

About the role

We’re looking for a senior operator to own and improve the customer access workflow for an assigned Trusted Access program. You will connect application and eligibility review, approvals, appeals, provisioning coordination, and support so customers can reach a clear, reliable outcome.

Your primary focus will be improving how the program works. You’ll use complex customer cases to uncover recurring problems, then deliver product, automation, self-service, and support-process improvements. You’ll also own difficult eligibility and access escalations, helping customers and account teams understand what is blocking progress and driving the right partners toward resolution.

This role combines independent workflow ownership with hands-on operational judgment. Success means customers reach usable access with fewer avoidable delays, decisions remain accurate, and the workflow runs reliably through the people and systems you enable.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the operational workflow for an assigned Trusted Access program, from application through confirmed access and subsequent changes. Identify where customers get stuck and prioritize improvements by customer impact, risk, and effort.

  • Investigate complex eligibility, onboarding, and access cases. Reconcile approval, verification, account, workspace, and provisioning records; apply approved requirements within your authority and bring exceptions to the appropriate decision-maker.

  • Drive customer and account-team escalations through resolution. Establish the blocker, maintain clear ownership across handoffs, communicate realistic next steps, and confirm that the customer can use the intended capability.

  • Turn recurring case patterns into product and process changes with Product, Engineering, and customer-facing partners. Define the problem and requirements, help validate the fix, and measure whether it reduced repeat contacts or manual work.

  • Build guidance that makes reliable resolution repeatable: support playbooks, help-center content, training, and quality checks. Enable frontline and outsourced support teams to handle more cases accurately and independently.

  • Use data to distinguish fast ticket closure from better access outcomes. Diagnose delays, rework, and decision errors, and use the findings to refine your workflow and priorities.

  • Develop and validate AI-assisted workflows and automation with technical partners. Establish checks, human review, and fallback paths appropriate to the decisions involved.

  • Maintain clear documentation and qualified backup across programs. Share what you learn so improvements continue working when another specialist takes ownership.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have independently owned and improved customer support, onboarding, access, risk, or product-operations workflows in a complex service environment.

  • Can show durable improvements you delivered through product changes, self-service, automation, or partner enablement, with evidence of adoption and better customer outcomes.

  • Exercise sound judgment when records conflict, requirements are unclear, or customers need urgent help. You can separate what the evidence supports from what still needs an authorized decision.

  • Are comfortable investigating across customer, account, approval, and access systems, and can translate operational problems into clear requirements for technical partners.

  • Use operational data to identify root causes, prioritize work, and evaluate whether a change improved the service.

  • Communicate with clarity and empathy under pressure, and can explain a difficult access decision or unresolved blocker without making unsupported commitments.
