title: Software Engineer, Product Infrastructure - Agent Runtime
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Agent Runtime builds the shared agent primitives and compute runtime that power OpenAI products and applications. As agents take on more complex, longer-running tasks, we build the systems that let them maintain state, use tools, and work reliably in the environments they need.

We work closely with Research, Product, and infrastructure teams to turn advances in model capabilities into useful products. Our work combines deep systems engineering with a clear understanding of customer needs, creating reusable foundations that help teams build and scale new agent experiences.

About the Role

We’re looking for a software engineer with strong product infrastructure experience to build the services, APIs, and runtime capabilities behind persistent agents. You’ll focus on the product infrastructure that makes agent workflows reliable and scalable, including persistent state, asynchronous execution, orchestration, and visibility into work in progress.

You’ll bring product judgment to infrastructure decisions: understanding how people and developers use agents, translating those needs into clear abstractions, and owning systems from design through launch and production operation. You’ll work closely with partner teams to deliver new capabilities while strengthening the shared foundations they depend on.

In this role, you will:

  • Design, build, and operate backend services, APIs, and reusable runtime primitives that support agent experiences across products.

  • Build systems for persistent agent state, asynchronous execution, orchestration, and progress reporting so agents can carry work forward over time.

  • Develop infrastructure that connects agents with tools and execution environments, with clear interfaces and safe, reliable behavior.

  • Improve reliability, scalability, and performance through observability, production debugging, failure recovery, and thoughtful system design.

  • Partner with Product, Research, and engineering teams to turn emerging capabilities and customer needs into reusable infrastructure.

  • Own projects end to end, balancing rapid iteration with maintainable architecture and the operational demands of systems used across products.

Your background might look something like:

  • 7+ years of professional software engineering experience, with substantial ownership of backend systems, product infrastructure, or developer platforms.

  • A track record of designing, shipping, and operating production services, APIs, and data models that support complex product workflows.

  • Strong distributed systems fundamentals and experience reasoning about state, concurrency, asynchronous work, and failure recovery.

  • Experience building production systems in Python, Go, Rust, TypeScript, or similar languages, and the ability to work across service and infrastructure boundaries.

  • Experience improving reliability and performance, using observability and debugging to understand system behavior and resolve production issues.

  • Strong product judgment and developer empathy, with an ability to translate ambiguous needs into clear APIs, useful abstractions, and pragmatic technical tradeoffs.

  • An ability to collaborate across product and infrastructure teams, communicate design decisions clearly, and take ownership from early exploration through production.

  • Interest in AI agents and how they execute real work. Experience with agent runtimes, workflow orchestration, or execution environments is helpful but not required.

title: Compliance Program Manager — Regulatory Compliance
descriptionHtml:
About the team

Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) builds compliance programs and provides assurance for OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We combine technical understanding with practical operations to reduce risk, support product and research teams, and produce reliable evidence of how our controls work.

About the role

As a Regulatory Compliance Program Manager, you will build and operate programs that turn regulatory requirements into clear responsibilities, effective processes, and evidence that can withstand external scrutiny.

Your work will focus on AI safety/security and content moderation, with privacy operations as an adjacent area. You will partner with Legal and the teams that build and operate our products to scope the work, maintain accurate control narratives, prepare regulatory responses, and lead external assessments for your assigned portfolio.

You should be comfortable owning delivery, explaining tradeoffs, and changing your recommendation when the evidence changes. Success means controls have accountable owners, evidence stays current, and teams can respond accurately without repeatedly rebuilding the same work. The initial portfolio and expectations will be agreed with the hiring manager.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead an agreed portfolio of AI safety/security and content-compliance work, including programs associated with the EU AI Act, DSA, OSA, and SB 53, with Legal and relevant experts confirming applicable requirements.

  • Translate requirements into scoped programs, operating processes, control and evidence responsibilities, milestones, and clear escalation paths.

  • Build and maintain accurate control narratives and traceable evidence for regulatory requests, reporting, audits, and assessments.

  • Lead preparation and delivery for external compliance assessments, coordinate the responsible teams, and track gaps through verified resolution or an explicitly owned decision.

  • Prioritize the work that materially improves compliance outcomes and reduces risk; explain what should proceed, change, or wait and why.

  • Develop evidence-backed recommendations with Legal, Product, Security, Safety, Integrity, Privacy, and other functional teams. Obtain decisions from the authorized owners for legal interpretation, external representations, and risk acceptance.

  • Improve operational workflows for content and privacy compliance while keeping implementation and operation of controls with the appropriate functional owners.

  • Simplify and automate repeated administrative work, test the results, and verify that the improvement is adopted and produces accurate, reliable outputs.

  • Learn the GRC security-control environment and participate in the team’s on-call rotation, with scope and expectations explained during the hiring process.

  • Communicate clearly, surface uncertainty early, incorporate feedback, and develop the domain knowledge needed for the next priority.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have practical experience building and operating AI safety/security and content-moderation programs, and can explain your own decisions, contribution, and results.

  • Have used agentic tooling to automate and improve to scaled processes

  • Understand relevant technical concepts across model evaluation, training and release, safety controls, content moderation, and post-launch operations, and can explain where specialist input is needed.

  • Have a strong understanding of relevant AI safety, content, and privacy requirements, including the EU AI Act, DSA, OSA, and SB 53, and experience translating them into operating processes and controls with domain experts and Legal.

  • Have led regulatory responses and external compliance audits, and can distinguish supported claims from evidence gaps.

  • Have delivered complex cross-functional programs, scoped practical first increments, and adapted priorities when constraints changed.

  • Have improved or automated an operational workflow and verified its accuracy, usefulness, and ongoing ownership.

  • Can maintain precise records, navigate technical/compliance documentation and contract language, follow through on commitments, and judge what to resolve directly or escalate.

  • Communicate clearly in writing and conversation with technical teams, Legal, leadership, and external stakeholders; explain evidence, uncertainty, recommendations, and tradeoffs.

  • Work constructively through disagreement, learn from feedback, and take responsibility for outcomes. Privacy program-management experience is a plus.

title: Applied AI Engineer, Codex
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. For software engineering organizations, this means helping customers adopt Codex and other OpenAI capabilities across the software development lifecycle—transforming how teams plan, build, test, review, and deliver software.

We work directly with engineering leaders and hands-on developers to identify high-value opportunities, design and implement AI-powered development workflows, and scale what works across engineering organizations. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products, reusable architectures, and technical patterns that help developers everywhere get more value from Codex.

About the Role

As an Applied AI Engineer focused on Codex, you will partner directly with leading engineering organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that transform how software is developed. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from workflow and use-case selection through prototyping, evaluation, production rollout, and scaled adoption.

You will work alongside engineering teams to build advanced AI coding workflows, integrations, automations, and evaluation systems—often using Codex itself as part of your development process. You will help customers make technical decisions involving model behavior, agentic workflows, developer environments, security, reliability, evaluation, and operational readiness, while ensuring deployments translate into measurable improvements in engineering productivity and software delivery.

You will work closely with OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, Sales, and the broader Codex organization, translating real-world deployment experience into high-signal product and model feedback. Success is measured by production systems, sustained developer adoption, and meaningful improvements to how engineering organizations build software—not simply successful demonstrations or enablement activity.

This role is based in our Munich office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Partner directly with engineering leaders and hands-on developers to identify high-value opportunities for Codex and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

  • Design, build, and deploy AI-powered software development workflows that improve how engineering teams plan, write, test, review, debug, and deliver software.

  • Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, workflow automations, and production accelerators—often using Codex as part of your own development process.

  • Help customers progress from promising experiments to reliable production workflows, sustained developer adoption, and scaled impact across engineering organizations.

  • Design systematic approaches for evaluating AI coding systems using representative software engineering tasks, automated graders, production signals, and developer feedback.

  • Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, tools, developer environments, integrations, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and operational readiness.

  • Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive technical blockers toward resolution.

  • Lead technical deep dives, workshops, and hands-on enablement that help engineering teams understand and adopt advanced AI coding workflows effectively and safely.

  • Gather high-fidelity insights from real-world Codex deployments and translate them into clear product proposals, model feedback, and technical requirements for OpenAI Product, Research, and Engineering teams.

  • Create reusable architectures, tooling, examples, guides, and technical patterns—including contributions to resources such as the OpenAI Cookbook—that accelerate future Codex deployments.

  • Influence customer engineering strategy by helping technical leaders understand how AI coding systems can reshape their software development lifecycle, engineering practices, and organizational workflows.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering software or AI systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, developer tooling, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting.

  • Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, integrations, or production engineering—not only program, enablement, or stakeholder management.

  • Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across modern software development environments; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.

  • Are an active user of AI coding tools and have developed a strong point of view on how AI can improve developer productivity and software engineering workflows.

  • Enjoy building high-signal prototypes, integrations, automations, and production solutions that demonstrate and deliver what AI coding systems can enable.

  • Understand how to evaluate AI coding systems systematically, including designing representative tasks, automated evaluations, production signals, and mechanisms for incorporating developer feedback.

  • Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as developer tooling integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.

  • Can connect technical decisions to developer workflows, adoption, engineering productivity, and measurable business outcomes.

  • Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, engineering leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.

  • Are comfortable leading technical workshops and hands-on sessions that help engineering organizations adopt new development workflows and technologies.

  • Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous and rapidly evolving environments.

  • Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; deep prior experience with OpenAI products is not required.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The ChatGPT organization at OpenAI supports our mission by bringing advanced AI capabilities to hundreds of millions of users worldwide. The Image Generation team is responsible for one of the fastest-growing experiences in ChatGPT, enabling users to create, edit, and transform images through natural language.

Recent breakthroughs in multimodal AI have dramatically improved image quality, instruction following, editing precision, consistency, and text rendering. We're building the systems and experiences that turn these research advances into products used daily by creators, professionals, businesses, and consumers around the world.

Our team sits at the intersection of research, product, design, and infrastructure. We work closely with model researchers, mobile engineers, frontend engineers, and platform teams to build intuitive experiences and scalable systems that power image generation at global scale. Whether users are creating marketing assets, visualizing ideas, editing photos, designing products, or simply exploring their creativity, our goal is to make visual creation feel as natural as having a conversation.

descriptionHtml:

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure the responsible and widespread adoption of artificial intelligence. In support of that mission, the Marketing team helps deeply understand customer audiences and market dynamics, influence the development of the right products, build sustainable and customer-aligned monetization models, and drive awareness, adoption, and usage across OpenAI’s products and platform.

We’re looking for a Marketing Scientist to join OpenAI’s Ads Marketing Science function. Reporting to Marketing Science leadership, you’ll be a senior individual contributor who combines rigorous measurement expertise with strong client judgment and hands-on execution.

Your focus is sustained capability: helping sellers understand customer problems, create value, develop champions and navigate complex buying decisions, rather than simply completing training or communicating launches.

You will work with regional enablement leadership, sales managers and Readiness Strategy & Design to diagnose needs, shape learning, deliver it and reinforce application in real deals. The role combines direct field credibility with hands-on facilitation, coaching and commercial judgment.

This role is based in our Singapore office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role you will

  • Diagnose commercial capability gaps. Use deal reviews, customer conversations, pipeline and conversion evidence, and manager feedback to identify where stronger selling skills would improve execution. Distinguish learning needs from product, process, territory or coverage issues and bring those issues to the appropriate owner.

  • Deliver practical sales learning. Facilitate workshops, role plays, customer scenarios and deal clinics that build discovery, problem identification, qualification, value articulation, champion development and executive engagement. Make sessions relevant to OpenAI’s executive-led, rapidly changing sales environment rather than importing a playbook unchanged.

  • Coach application in live opportunities. Help sellers apply established enterprise sales disciplines to their own accounts and customer conversations. Partner with managers on follow-through and observable next steps while leaving deal ownership, forecast accountability and people management with the field.

  • Build manager reinforcement. Give managers practical coaching prompts, observation criteria and follow-up exercises. Help them recognise strong execution and diagnose specific gaps, so capability development continues between formal sessions rather than depending on an enablement event.

  • Own assigned local onboarding delivery. Run practical exercises, facilitation and readiness checks within global programme standards and pathways. Coordinate with the regional lead, onboarding team and Readiness Design on schedules, learner needs and assessments; use observed proficiency to identify targeted support.

  • Co-create relevant learning with shared quality. Give Readiness Strategy & Design clear commercial briefs and real customer scenarios. Adapt approved examples, language and delivery formats within agreed guardrails; obtain qualified review for new product, technical, pricing or other substantive claims.

  • Connect capability building to sales plays and activation. Help teams practise the customer conversations and behaviours a play requires, working with the sales plays and activation owners. Protect committed coaching and reinforcement time and surface the impact when urgent launches would displace it.

  • Choose the delivery route that serves the learner. Blend human coaching, workshops and approved in-workflow learning where appropriate. Use agentic delivery only for accepted services with clear content ownership and a human fallback; retain responsibility for the capability gaps that require direct support.

  • Assess demonstrated proficiency and commercial application. Combine practical assessments, observed selling, manager feedback and relevant performance evidence. Do not equate attendance with readiness or attribute commercial results to training alone. Identify where content, delivery or a wider business constraint needs to change.

  • Close the field and design feedback loop. Return prioritised improvements and reusable examples to Readiness Strategy & Design. Agree owners and review dates, test revised materials with the field and retire duplicate local versions once improvements are incorporated into the shared source.

You may thrive in this role if you

  • Have personally sold to enterprise customers and can bring credible experience of discovery, qualification, stakeholder management and progressing complex opportunities.

  • Have delivered dedicated in-house sales enablement in an enterprise technology business, improving field behaviour beyond launch communications or event coordination.

  • Bring experience working within an established enterprise sales frameworks and can adapt its disciplines thoughtfully to AI products, consumption and evolving customer needs.

  • Can facilitate practical adult learning, coach sellers and equip managers to reinforce skills using real customer situations.

title: Program Manager, Local Community Impact
descriptionHtml:
About the team

Our Community team builds direct relationships with people who use OpenAI’s technology, helps others learn from their experiences, and brings their insights back to product and research teams. Our programs connect communities with trusted partners who help organizations adopt AI effectively.

About the role

We’re hiring a Program Manager to build and run our partner network. You will turn an early program into a reliable operation: recruit and onboard partners, coordinate agreements and payments, manage external service providers, support local events and marketing, review service quality, and improve the program as we learn.

This partner network will be on the ground in communities helping people–from small businesses, non-profits, and community organizations–experience concrete benefits from our technology. They will set up useful workflows, learn OpenAI tools and become more confident, independent users.

You should be as comfortable helping a partner resolve an onboarding issue as you are designing the systems that prevent it from happening again. You will work with local operators and internal teams to make sure commitments are clear, work gets done, and the people we serve receive useful, high-quality support.

What you will do

  • Build the partner operating model, from sourcing and selection of partners through onboarding, ongoing support, renewal and exit. Establish clear expectations, owners, timelines and escalation paths. Create a scalable operating model that supports program growth and evolving partner needs.

  • Run partner onboarding with Legal, Finance and Procurement: track agreements, required information, vendor setup, readiness and start dates so partners can begin work and receive payments through approved processes.

  • Manage partner payments, reporting and related operational processes.

  • Plan and support local workshops, deployments and events with partners. Coordinate audiences, venues, budgets, materials, staffing and follow-up while preserving local ownership.

  • Coordinate program marketing and communications with Community, Marketing and content partners. Develop clear partner guidance, route brand and messaging approvals, and help useful stories and practices reach the right audiences.

  • Build trusted relationships with local operators and the organizations they serve. Coach partners, answer questions, address service-quality concerns and set clear boundaries around access, funding and program participation.

  • Create practical systems for the partner community: intake, a shared knowledge base, service logs, regular check-ins and reusable playbooks that reduce manual work without sacrificing quality.

  • Develop and operate partner review processes with the hiring manager and relevant teams. Combine verified service delivery, beneficiary feedback and sustained product use to understand performance and improve support.

  • Collaborate with analytics and product teams to assess program impact using appropriate data and feedback.

  • Manage budgets, vendors, risks and dependencies across the program. Keep stakeholders informed, surface decisions early and bring recurring partner feedback into program and product improvements.

You might thrive in this role if you

  • 8+ years owning a complex partner, community or operational program from early design through execution at scale, with clear examples of what you personally built and improved.

  • Bring strong operational judgment and follow-through across onboarding, financial workflows, events and multiple stakeholder groups.

  • Can earn trust with small-business owners, local technical operators and community leaders, explain expectations plainly and have difficult conversations when needed.

  • Have practical familiarity with ChatGPT, Codex and AI-enabled workflows, and can work credibly with technical specialists while explaining tools to people with less technical experience.

  • Use data and qualitative feedback to distinguish meaningful outcomes from activity counts, and can improve a process without making it unnecessarily bureaucratic.

  • Write clearly, communicate risks early, work independently through ambiguity and collaborate effectively across teams.

  • Have experience creating playbooks, support systems or automation that lets a high-touch program scale.

  • Operating a local-services, small-business, nonprofit, fellowship, ambassador or distributed partner program.

title: Engineering Manager, Distillation & Detection Platform
descriptionHtml:
About the role

We’re looking for an engineering manager to lead a team building software systems that detect and prevent harmful misuse of frontier AI models—before incidents occur. This is a builder’s role: you’ll lead engineers shipping production services, detection pipelines, and mitigation mechanisms that protect frontier model integrity and reduce high-severity misuse risk.

While this work intersects with frontier model development, security and risk, we’re explicitly seeking someone with a software engineering foundation who is comfortable building reliable systems that can operate at billions of users scale.

In this role you will:

  • Lead a team of software engineers building detection + mitigation systems for frontier model misuse, with an emphasis on model IP protection / distillation detection and emerging risk surfaces from autonomous agents.

  • Set the technical roadmap and execution strategy: prioritize, design, ship, iterate, measure impact.

  • Build production systems: services, pipelines, tooling, instrumentation, and automation that scale with frontier model usage.

  • Partner deeply with Research and Product to translate evolving model capabilities into concrete tests, signals, and mitigations that can be deployed at scale.

  • Drive strong engineering fundamentals: architecture, reliability, monitoring, performance, and operational excellence.

  • Hire and grow an exceptional team across backend, data systems, and applied ML engineering domains as needed.

  • Anticipate what breaks at scale as agentic workflows become more capable.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Experience building systems in adversarial, fast-evolving environments

  • Are comfortable with ambiguity and novelty

  • Have experience adjacent to security (e.g., abuse prevention, fraud, integrity, platform defense, auth/identity, malware/spam, adversarial environments)

  • Communicate clearly and build trust quickly with senior stakeholders—pragmatic, collaborative, and calm under scrutiny.

  • Significant experience leading engineering teams and delivering production systems end-to-end.

  • Strong technical judgment in system design, distributed systems, data pipelines, observability, and operational reliability.

title: Researcher, Training - London
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI's Training team is responsible for producing the large language models that power our research, our products, and ultimately bring us closer to AGI. Achieving this goal requires combining deep research into improving our current architecture and optimization techniques, alongside long-term bets aimed at improving the efficiency and capability of future generations of models. We are responsible for integrating these techniques and producing model artifacts used by the rest of the company, and ensuring that these models are world-class in every respect.

About the Role

As a member of the training team, you will push the frontier of LLM development for OpenAI's flagship models, enhancing intelligence, efficiency, and adding new capabilities.

Relevant interests may include areas such as architecture design, long-context and efficient attention, optimization and the science of scaling.

Ideal candidates have a deep understanding of LLM architectures, a sophisticated understanding of model inference, and a hands-on empirical approach. A good fit for this role will be equally happy coming up with a creative breakthrough, investing in strengthening a baseline, designing an eval, debugging a thorny regression, or tracking down a bottleneck.

This role is based in London. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Design, prototype and scale up new architectures to improve model intelligence

  • Execute and analyze experiments autonomously and collaboratively

  • Study, debug, and optimize both model performance and computational performance

  • Contribute to training and inference infrastructure

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have experience landing contributions to major LLM training runs

  • Can thoroughly evaluate and improve deep learning architectures in a self-directed fashion

  • Are motivated by safely deploying LLMs in the real world

title: Software Engineer, Codex Core Agents
descriptionHtml:
About the Team
The Codex Core Agent team builds the kernel of Codex. We own making the agent better, accelerating research, and making those improvements real in production for our users.

That means working across the systems that make Codex actually function as an agent in the real world: the production performance envelope around tokens, latency, reliability, cost, and capacity; the core execution loop and interfaces that turn models into useful behavior; the shared infrastructure that enables other teams to build on Codex; and the feedback loops that turn real-world usage into better models and better agent behavior over time.

About the Role
We’re looking for engineers to build the infrastructure that powers Codex agents in production. This role focuses on the systems that let models safely execute code, interact with tools, complete long-running tasks, and operate reliably and efficiently at scale.

You’ll design and operate the infrastructure behind sandboxed execution, orchestration, stateful workflows, app-server and SDK boundaries, and model rollouts. You’ll work at the intersection of distributed systems, developer tooling, and AI, building primitives that make Codex faster, safer, more reliable, and easier for the rest of the organization to build on.

What You’ll Do

  • Design and build execution environments for AI agents, including sandboxing, isolation, and reproducibility.

  • Develop systems for agent orchestration across multi-step, tool-using workflows.

  • Build infrastructure for running, testing, and debugging code generated by models.

  • Create state and memory systems that allow agents to persist context across long-running tasks.

  • Optimize tokens, latency, reliability, and cost across Codex’s production fleet.

  • Support model rollouts, capacity planning, and the core tradeoffs between quality, speed, and economics to manage a fleet of frontier agents at scale.

  • Build shared platform capabilities that unblock product teams, partner teams, and open source Codex.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

  • Have strong experience in distributed systems or infrastructure engineering.

  • Have built systems involving containers, sandboxing, or virtualization.

  • Are comfortable working across backend systems, APIs, and developer tooling.

  • Care deeply about system reliability, performance, and security.

  • Enjoy working on ambiguous, zero-to-one problems.

  • Want to help build the systems that turn model capability into a dependable software engineering agent.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with code execution platforms, CI/CD systems, or build systems.

  • Experience coding in Rust

  • Familiarity with LLMs, agents, or tool-use frameworks.

  • Background in security engineering or isolation systems.

  • Experience building developer platforms, IDE tooling, or open source infrastructure.

title: Technical Operations Analyst, User Safety & Risk Operations
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

At OpenAI, our User Safety & Risk Operations (USRO) team helps protect our products and users from abuse, fraud, safety risks, and other forms of misuse. We translate real-world user and operational signals into timely decisions, practical interventions, and improvements to our products and systems.

This role sits on the Risk Incubation & Systems (RIS) team, which investigates emerging risks, builds data and automation capabilities, and develops workflows that can scale into durable operational homes.

About the Role

You’ll build and maintain the data pipelines and shared datasets that teams across USRO use for analysis, measurement, and automation. Working with operational teams and engineers, you’ll turn data from different systems into reliable sources that colleagues can use in their work.

You’ll take projects from initial requirements through to production use, with responsibility for testing and documentation. As teams’ needs change, you’ll help maintain and extend the systems you build.

Location / work model: San Francisco based with three days in the office. 

Please note: This role may involve exposure to sensitive or concerning content. Strong discretion, good judgment, and resilience are essential.

In This Role, You Will

  • Work with USRO teams to understand their data needs and define requirements for datasets and reporting.

  • Build, maintain, and monitor production data pipelines and Airflow DAGs, including scheduling, dependencies, backfills, and troubleshooting failures. 

  • Build and maintain reusable data models, reporting cubes, and shared operational reporting metrics, so teams can use consistent definitions across dashboards and analyses.

  • Set up data quality and freshness checks, document lineage and ownership, and make the work supportable after handoff.

  • Document data sources and transformations so colleagues can trace results back to the underlying records.Apply access and privacy requirements when designing datasets and reporting.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

  • Have strong SQL skills and practical experience using Python to build and maintain data pipelines.

  • Have built and debugged scheduled pipelines that other people depend on.

  • Practical understanding of data modeling, joins, deduplication, tests, and monitoring.

  • Ability to trace a surprising metric back to its inputs and explain what downstream users can and can’t conclude.

  • Experience partnering with non-engineers to turn ambiguous needs into dependable data products.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with Airflow or similar workflow orchestration tools.

  • Experience transferring prototypes or new workflows into reliable, scaled operations.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Creative Partnerships function builds trusted relationships with influential people, brands and institutions across entertainment, sports, fashion, music, media, publishing, and the creator economy. Working closely with Product, Marketing, Communications, Legal, Policy, Safety, Finance, Procurement, and other teams across OpenAI, the function creates responsible, culturally resonant programs that help people understand and use AI.

Creative Partnerships moves quickly across a wide range of priorities, and this role will sit close to both the leadership and the work. We’re looking for a highly strategic, analytical, and collaborative Strategy and Operations Lead to partner with the Creative Partnerships leadership team.

You’ll help leadership determine where the team should focus, connect its ambitions to the resources and investments required to deliver them, and ensure decisions turn into coordinated action. title: Lead, Technical Accounting (Compute Infrastructure)
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI Finance is responsible for ensuring the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission. The Technical Accounting team plays a crucial role in helping OpenAI navigate complex, judgmental, and rapidly evolving accounting matters with rigor and clarity. We aim to bring both technical excellence and strong business partnership to some of the most novel accounting questions in the industry.

About the Role

As Senior Manager, Technical Accounting, Compute Infrastructure, you will lead the evaluation, documentation, and operationalization of complex accounting matters related to OpenAI's compute infrastructure, strategic investments, and other non-routine business activities..

This role sits at the intersection of U.S. GAAP technical accounting, infrastructure strategy, financial reporting, controls, and cross-functional execution. Key areas may include cloud compute arrangements, data center and colocation arrangements, lease accounting under ASC 842, power purchase agreements, strategic investments, consolidation evaluations under ASC 810, financial instruments, and other emerging or non-standard arrangements.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead technical accounting analysis for complex, judgmental, and non-routine transactions under U.S. GAAP.

  • Evaluate accounting implications for compute infrastructure arrangements, including cloud compute, data center, colocation, lease, PPA, infrastructure procurement, and related commercial arrangements.

  • Partner with Controllership, Tax, Legal, FP&A, Procurement, Infrastructure, and other cross-functional teams to assess the accounting implications of new products, commercial arrangements, strategic transactions, and business initiatives.

  • Prepare and review technical accounting memoranda, position papers, and other auditor-ready documentation.

  • Help design scalable accounting processes, controls, policies, and documentation to support OpenAI's continued growth.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Enjoyment in solving complex accounting questions that do not have obvious answers and building scalable accounting frameworks for new and evolving business activities.

  • Ability to move between technical U.S. GAAP research and practical business execution.

  • Comfortability in partnering with both accounting teams and non-accounting stakeholders.

  • Strong judgment, clear communication, and the ability to document conclusions in a way that supports audit, reporting, and operational needs.

  • CPA or equivalent accounting qualification.

  • 10+ years of progressive accounting experience.

  • Prior public accounting experience at the manager or senior manager level.

  • Strong technical accounting foundation under U.S. GAAP.

  • Hands-on experience preparing or reviewing technical accounting memoranda and supporting accounting conclusions with external auditors.

  • Experience with ASC 842 lease accounting.

  • Experience with complex or non-routine accounting transactions involving multiple accounting standards.

title: Software Engineer, Search Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Search Product Infrastructure team builds the systems that power search experiences across ChatGPT. We partner with teams developing models, operating inference infrastructure, building specialized search experiences, and maintaining search indexes to bring advances in models and retrieval into production. Our work spans search orchestration, model serving, experimentation, and distributed systems, with direct impact on answer quality, responsiveness, reliability, and efficiency at ChatGPT scale.

About the Role

As a senior engineer on the Search Product Infrastructure team, you will design, build, and operate the systems that connect models with search at ChatGPT scale. You will tackle challenges in search orchestration, inference efficiency, experimentation, and production reliability, making tradeoffs that directly shape answer quality and user experience. Working closely with researchers and partner engineering teams, you will own projects from technical design through launch and iteration, evolving the architecture as models, product capabilities, and demand grow.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

  • Build experimentation tooling and automation to run reproducible A/B tests, define success metrics, and measure product impact. Use shadow traffic and load testing to validate system behavior, estimate capacity needs, and support safe production rollouts.

  • Own production reliability through observability, resilient fallback behavior, incident response, and automation that improves launch safety and reduces operational toil.

  • Build search APIs and tool interfaces that enable models and agents to retrieve information reliably while respecting access controls and preserving source attribution.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have significant experience designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems, with depth in performance, reliability, or resource efficiency.

title: Product Manager, API Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:
About the Team:

The OpenAI API team builds the foundation that enables every developer to harness OpenAI’s models safely, reliably, and at scale. We design and operate the systems that power model serving, API access, billing, developer tooling, and enterprise integrations—forming the connective tissue between OpenAI’s research breakthroughs and real-world products.

Our mission is to make it effortless for anyone to build with OpenAI technology. We’re responsible for the infrastructure and product layers that allow millions of developers to integrate GPT models, fine-tune behavior, manage data, and deliver transformative experiences to their users. We collaborate across product, research, and engineering teams to ensure that innovation in model capabilities translates directly into value for customers.

The API team spans multiple disciplines, including product management, infrastructure engineering, developer experience, and data systems. We care deeply about reliability, scalability, and simplicity—creating tools that let developers focus on their ideas while we handle the complexity of running world-class AI systems.

title: Account Director, Large Enterprise
descriptionHtml:
About the team

OpenAI’s mission is to build safe artificial general intelligence (AGI) which benefits all of humanity. This long-term undertaking brings the world’s best scientists, engineers, and business professionals into one lab together to accomplish this.

In pursuit of this mission, our Go To Market (GTM) team is responsible for helping customers learn how to leverage and deploy our highly capable AI products across their business. The team is made up of Sales, Solutions, Support, Marketing, and Partnership professionals who work together to bring AI to as many users as possible.

About the role

Our Sales team helps customers understand how highly capable AI can transform their businesses. As an Account Director, Large Enterprise, you’ll work with some of our largest accounts across a variety of industries, winning new business and expanding adoption within existing customers.

This role combines technical understanding, executive engagement, and ownership of complex enterprise sales. You’ll create demand, develop opportunities, and lead deals from initial engagement through negotiation, deployment, and expansion. You’ll help executives move from curiosity about AI to a clear understanding of how it can change the way their businesses operate—and build a practical path to realizing that value.

We’re looking for someone with a hunter mentality who takes initiative and creates momentum. You’re comfortable opening doors, building relationships across business units, and bringing commercial and technical stakeholders together around an enterprise transformation strategy. Success means both winning business and helping customers turn their commitments into sustained adoption and consumption.

This role can be based in our San Francisco, New York City or Seattle offices. We are also considering applications to work remotely from within the U.S. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you’ll:

  • Own a portfolio of large enterprise accounts across industries, developing account strategies that drive new business, enterprise adoption, and expansion.

  • Create demand through proactive prospecting, executive outreach, and a deep understanding of each customer’s business priorities.

  • Own complex deals end to end, including opportunity development, qualification, business case creation, technical evaluation, negotiation, and close.

  • Help senior executives understand AI’s potential to transform their business, identify priorities, and build alignment around a roadmap for investment and deployment.

  • Build relationships across business units and functions, connecting executive sponsors, business leaders, technical teams, and procurement to advance shared goals.

  • Partner with solutions engineering to translate complex technical capabilities into customer programs with measurable business outcomes.

  • Win initial deployments and expand successful use cases across teams, business units, and geographies.

  • Own a consumption revenue target, partnering across the customer lifecycle to turn signed agreements into production usage and sustained growth.

  • Maintain rigorous account plans, opportunity management, and revenue forecasts, taking responsibility for moving opportunities forward and resolving obstacles.

  • Bring customer and market insights to product, engineering, and GTM teams to inform our roadmap and approach to enterprise customers.

  • Help build the processes, practices, and culture of a growing, high-ownership sales organization.

We’re seeking someone with experience including:

descriptionHtml:
About the team

OpenAI’s Transformation Leads help customers rethink what their business could do with AI. We work with executives and Heads of AI to build business reinvention roadmaps. For this, we provide Leadership Advisory and Collaborative Design support, with the objective to secure and accelerate new business models, including process redesign and culture change.

title: Forward Deployment Strategy and Operations
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Forward Deployment Strategy & Operations team closely partners with GTM leadership and Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) to help organizations move from AI ambition to durable production outcomes. We combine technical depth, deployment expertise, and commercial and operational discipline to solve complex problems in customer environments and accelerate adoption of OpenAI’s models and products.

We also work across Technical Success, Finance, Product, Legal, Data, Systems, and external delivery partners to build a forward deployed motion that is customer-centered, commercially rigorous, operationally scalable, and tightly connected to product adoption.

About the Role

We are seeking a senior operator to build and scale OpenAI’s forward deployed business. You will lead some of our highest-priority strategic initiatives across the company, tackling ambiguous and complex questions about how to bring the full capabilities of our models to the world’s largest and most consequential institutions.

This is a foundational, hands-on individual contributor role at the intersection of business strategy, finance, go-to-market, and technical delivery. You will shape where and how we engage, how we structure and commercialize deployments, how we scale the motion, and where we invest—turning open-ended questions into clear strategies, decisions, and operating models.

You will own business planning, commercial strategy, forecasting and modeling, partner strategy, and cross-functional strategic initiatives. You will also build integrated views of demand, staffing, revenue, margin, and deployment performance; replace one-off analyses with durable processes; and establish operating cadences that help leaders act early.

You will be a trusted partner to FDE, GTM, Technical Success, Finance, Product, Legal, Revenue Operations, and Data leaders. The right person combines experience with complex customer deployments, rigorous analytics, executive communication, and the willingness to build the model, process, or dashboard themselves.

You’ll be responsible for:

  • Define and drive the business and GTM strategy for the forward deployed motion, including target customer needs, engagement portfolio, positioning, commercial models, partner motions, and where to standardize versus tailor deployments.

  • Lead high-priority, cross-company strategic initiatives that shape how OpenAI scales the FDE business and brings the capabilities of its models to the world’s largest and most complex institutions, from problem definition through implementation.

  • Own long-range, annual, and quarterly planning, translating goals into bookings, revenue, margin, capacity, utilization, role mix, geography, hiring, and investment assumptions.

  • Build and maintain integrated demand, capacity, staffing, and revenue models; develop scenarios and sensitivities; improve bottom-up forecast accuracy; and turn the output into clear executive recommendations.

  • Design the management system for the business, including KPIs, source-of-truth reporting, dashboards, pipeline and staffing reviews, and monthly and quarterly operating cadences.

  • Improve the end-to-end engagement lifecycle—from opportunity intake and scoping through commercial design, contracting, staffing, deployment, and expansion—in partnership with Revenue Operations and Systems.

  • Partner with Finance, Legal, GTM, FDE, Technical Success, and delivery leaders on business cases, deployment economics, deal tradeoffs, resource allocation, and investment decisions.

  • Translate recurring customer and deployment patterns into inputs for product strategy, enablement, partner strategy, and more repeatable product-plus-deployment offerings that accelerate durable adoption.

We’re looking for someone with:

  • 8+ years of experience in management consulting, Business Operations, Strategic Finance, or a comparable role, including direct experience in a forward-deployed engineering, enterprise implementation, technical consulting, systems-integration, or managed-services organization.

  • Deep command of deployment economics and operating levers such as pipeline, bookings, backlog, revenue timing, gross margin, utilization, capacity, staffing mix, delivery quality, and customer outcomes.

  • Exceptional quantitative modeling skills: you can build auditable demand, staffing, revenue, and scenario models; work fluently in spreadsheets; and use SQL, BI, or other data tools to test assumptions and improve decisions.

  • Strong commercial and GTM judgment across engagement design, pricing and packaging, forecasting, resource allocation, and complex enterprise deployment motions.

  • A record of leading complex, ambiguous strategic initiatives and turning them into clear choices, scalable operating models, and measurable results.

  • Excellent executive communication and influence; you can frame choices, surface assumptions, and drive alignment across technical and non-technical leaders.

  • Demonstrated leadership of complex cross-functional programs and teams. People-management experience is helpful, but this role is initially scoped as a senior individual contributor.

  • A low-ego, high-ownership working style, comfort with rapid change, and genuine interest in how frontier AI can create durable customer value.

title: Principal Security Engineer, Infrastructure Security
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Security is at the foundation of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The Security team protects OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We are technical in what we build but are operational in how we do our work, and are committed to supporting all products and research at OpenAI. Our Security team tenets include: prioritizing for impact, enabling researchers, preparing for future transformative technologies, and engaging a robust security culture.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a Principal Security Engineer to join our Infrastructure Security (InfraSec) team. InfraSec protects the foundations of OpenAI’s research and production environments, spanning GPU supercomputing clusters, multi-cloud infrastructure, datacenters, networking, storage, and the critical services that power our frontier AI models. Our charter includes securing everything from bare-metal hardware and firmware, to Kubernetes clusters and service meshes, to data storage and access pathways for highly sensitive model weights and user data.

As a principal engineer, you will set technical direction and drive execution on high-impact infrastructure security programs, partnering across various orgs at OpenAI to deliver durable controls that raise the security bar at OpenAI scale.

In this role, you will:

  • Own end-to-end security outcomes for one or more critical infrastructure areas, including multi-quarter strategy, roadmap, and delivery.

  • Design and build security controls across diverse layers (e.g., physical hardware, firmware/BMC, OS, Kubernetes, networks, and CI/CD) to defend against sophisticated adversaries and insider threats.

  • Lead cross-functional programs to deploy security enhancements and control changes across broad-scale infrastructure, balancing security guarantees with reliability and velocity.

  • Take a generalist approach to building security controls, balancing a mix of security expertise and broad technical skillsets to adapt to evolving challenges.

  • Lead and/or drive threat modeling and design reviews for major infrastructure changes, ensuring strong security foundations and operational excellence.

  • Mentor and level up engineers across InfraSec and partner teams, contributing to a strong security culture through guidance, reviews, and technical leadership.

You will thrive in this role if you have:

  • Deep understanding of security principles, best practices, and common vulnerabilities, including strong security judgment under ambiguity

  • A proactive mindset, with the ability to identify and address security gaps or inefficiencies through automation and tooling.

  • Expertise and curiosity about using frontier models and agents to effectively solve security challenges.

  • A track record of leading large, cross-org initiatives from concept to rollout, including navigating tradeoffs, driving alignment, and delivering measurable risk reduction.

  • Deep expertise in the security of cloud platforms (e.g., Amazon AWS, Microsoft Azure), especially securing multi-cloud networks and infrastructure, and designing cloud-agnostic systems.

  • Experience securing on-prem deployments and datacenters from construction to multi-tenant use.

  • Familiarity with container security, orchestration security, and authentication/authorization.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with an ability to think critically and objectively assess security risks.

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to convey complex security concepts to executive, technical, and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Excitement about collaborating with cross-functional teams to build secure, reliable systems that scale globally.

title: Fire Protection Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI's Industrial Compute organization delivers the infrastructure that powers frontier AI models. Within Infrastructure Delivery, we turn engineering concepts into safe, reliable, and operational AI campuses by working across design, construction, utilities, commissioning, operations, and external partners.

The fire protection function establishes the life-safety and property-protection strategy for these campuses. The team connects code requirements and engineering standards to practical design, construction, testing, incident readiness, and long-term operations.

About the Role

We are seeking a Fire Protection Engineer to lead owner-side fire and life-safety engineering across large-scale data center programs. You will establish design criteria, review complex fire protection systems, coordinate with authorities and delivery partners, and ensure that fire and life-safety requirements remain clear from early design through construction, commissioning, and operational handover.

This role requires strong technical judgment across detection, alarm, suppression, smoke control, water supply, emergency response, and code compliance. You will work closely with engineering, construction, safety, security, commissioning, and operations teams to resolve risks quickly without compromising life safety, reliability, or schedule.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain fire protection and life-safety design criteria, technical standards, and review requirements for self-build data center campuses.

  • Review fire protection drawings, specifications, code analyses, fire and life-safety narratives, hydraulic calculations, equipment submittals, and sequences of operation across all project phases.

  • Provide owner-side engineering direction for fire detection and alarm, automatic suppression, fire pumps and water storage, smoke control, emergency communication, and related life-safety systems.

  • Integrate fire protection requirements with architectural, structural, electrical, mechanical, controls, security, hardware, and operational systems.

  • Partner with code officials, authorities having jurisdiction, insurers, consultants, contractors, and equipment vendors to resolve code interpretations and approval risks.

  • Support constructability reviews, RFIs, submittals, field inspections, deficiency resolution, and change management during active construction.

  • Define commissioning, integrated-system testing, acceptance, turnover, and operational-readiness criteria for fire and life-safety systems.

  • Assess fire and life-safety risks associated with high-density compute, battery and energy-storage systems, generators and fuel systems, utility infrastructure, cooling systems, hazardous materials, and construction activities.

  • Support incident response, root-cause reviews, corrective actions, and lessons learned, translating operational findings into improved designs and standards.

  • Maintain clear records of design decisions, code positions, approvals, testing results, open risks, and turnover requirements.

  • Travel regularly to project sites to support design reviews, field execution, testing, commissioning, and operational readiness.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Fire Protection Engineering or a related engineering discipline, or equivalent practical experience delivering fire and life-safety systems.

  • 8+ years of fire protection engineering experience supporting data centers, industrial facilities, advanced manufacturing, energy infrastructure, or other mission-critical environments.

  • Strong knowledge of applicable building and fire codes and standards, including IBC, IFC, NFPA requirements, and local authority approval processes.

  • Technical depth in fire alarm and detection, water-based suppression, special-hazard suppression, fire pumps and water supply, smoke control, egress, and integrated life-safety systems.

  • Experience reviewing fire protection designs, specifications, hydraulic calculations, equipment submittals, testing procedures, and commissioning results.

  • Demonstrated ability to work with authorities having jurisdiction, engineering consultants, contractors, insurers, vendors, and internal stakeholders.

  • Experience resolving field issues and design changes while maintaining clear code compliance, safety, quality, schedule, and documentation.

  • Strong written and verbal communication, sound engineering judgment, and the ability to create clarity when requirements or ownership are ambiguous.

  • Professional Engineer licensure in Fire Protection Engineering, or the ability to obtain licensure in relevant jurisdictions.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience with hyperscale data centers, high-density compute environments, or global multi-site infrastructure programs.

  • Experience with battery rooms, energy-storage systems, generator plants, fuel systems, high-voltage substations, or other campus utility infrastructure.

  • Familiarity with performance-based design, fire and smoke modeling, quantitative risk assessment, or fire-hazard analysis.

  • Experience leading integrated testing and coordinating fire alarm, suppression, controls, security, mechanical, and electrical interfaces.

  • Experience developing reusable standards, design templates, commissioning requirements, and incident-prevention programs across multiple sites.

title: Partner Applied AI Engineer, Google Cloud
descriptionHtml:
About the team

The Applied AI Engineering team helps developers and enterprises deploy generative AI safely and effectively. We serve as trusted technical advisors, helping customers and partners move from early experimentation to production-scale AI systems.

As a Partner Applied AI Engineer focused on Google Cloud, you will help customers build with OpenAI in the cloud environment they already use. You will work with Google Cloud and its partner ecosystem to turn early implementations into repeatable approaches that field teams can deliver independently.

About the role

We are looking for an experienced technical leader to serve as a primary technical counterpart to Google Cloud Customer Engineers, AI specialists, and partner technical teams.

You will shape joint technical strategy, define engagement models, and build systems that scale beyond individual deals. Working across pre- and post-sales, you will guide enterprise customers from discovery through production while enabling Google Cloud and its partners to lead subsequent deployments.

This role combines hands-on engineering, technical judgment, and ecosystem leadership. You will bring deep familiarity with Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI), particularly Model Garden and its Python SDK tooling, and help customers choose supported OpenAI integration paths based on workload requirements, model capabilities, security controls, and operational needs.

In this role, you will:

Strategic Google Cloud engagement and influence

  • Build trusted relationships with Google Cloud field leadership, Customer Engineers, AI specialists, and partner teams across regions.

  • Influence joint account strategy and identify new opportunities where OpenAI can improve customer outcomes within Google Cloud environments.

  • Define engagement models and prioritization frameworks that concentrate technical effort on high-impact opportunities and reusable solutions.

  • Help teams distinguish model access through Model Garden, purchasing through Google Cloud Marketplace, and direct OpenAI offerings.

Complex deal leadership and execution

  • Lead technical strategy for complex enterprise engagements, from use-case discovery and architecture design to prototyping, evaluation, and production deployment.

  • Resolve integration and operational blockers with OpenAI and Google Cloud counterparts, giving account teams clear decisions and next steps.

  • Validate model and feature availability, regional requirements, access controls, data handling, quotas, and support boundaries for each workload.

  • Prioritize opportunities and allocate technical resources according to customer impact and the potential to scale through the ecosystem.

Solution architecture and hands-on building

  • Design and build OpenAI-powered applications that integrate with Google Cloud services, including Cloud Run or Google Kubernetes Engine, Cloud Storage, and BigQuery where appropriate.

  • Develop reference implementations for supported Model Garden access to OpenAI through the Responses API, alongside direct OpenAI integration patterns where those better meet customer requirements.

  • Use the Vertex AI SDK for Python / Agent Platform SDK to discover deployable Model Garden models, inspect deployment configurations, and deploy supported open models to endpoints. Validate project, region, machine and accelerator choices, credentials, permissions, and test inference; distinguish this workflow from managed model API access.

  • Maintain supported SDK dependencies and adapt examples as Google updates its SDKs. Use Google Gen AI SDK for Google generative-AI capabilities migrated out of legacy Vertex AI modules, and the documented OpenAI API or SDK for OpenAI integration paths.

  • Build retrieval-augmented generation and tool-using workflows, connecting approved enterprise data and services with clear authorization boundaries.

  • Establish evaluation, observability, CI/CD, and operational practices that address output quality, safety, reliability, latency, and cost.

  • Make identity, networking, secrets management, and data governance explicit in architectures rather than assuming controls transfer between services or providers.

Ecosystem enablement and scale

  • Create workshops, demos, playbooks, and reference architectures that Google Cloud teams and systems integrators can use independently.

  • Teach partner engineers how to evaluate model choices in Model Garden and select deployment approaches based on customer needs.

  • Pair with field teams on early deployments, then transfer delivery ownership as patterns mature.

  • Scale through global and regional systems integrators and independent software vendors, maintaining reusable assets as integrations evolve.

Cross-functional leadership and feedback

  • Work with Alliances, Product, Engineering, GTM, and Enablement to align technical priorities and execution.

  • Turn recurring customer and partner issues into evidence-backed product feedback and specific requests.

  • Maintain clear guidance on validated capabilities, preview limitations, and unresolved gaps, and follow decisions back to the field.

You'll thrive in this role if you:

  • Have substantial technical consulting or equivalent experience, including relationships with senior technical and business leaders in complex organizations.

  • Have hands-on experience with Model Garden and the Vertex AI SDK for Python / Agent Platform SDK, including programmatic model discovery, deployment configuration, endpoint deployment, and inference testing. Understand how this tooling differs from Google Gen AI SDK and OpenAI API/SDK integration paths.

  • Can build production applications using Python or another relevant language, APIs, containers, and cloud services.

  • Have practical experience with LLM evaluation, retrieval, tool use, and secure enterprise integration.

  • Balance hands-on delivery with strategic influence, know when to go deep and when to enable others, and build trust with engineers, architects, and executives.

  • Prefer repeatable solutions, take ownership of ambiguous problems, and measure success through customer outcomes and partner self-sufficiency.

title: Connectivity Software Engineer, Consumer Devices
descriptionHtml:
About the Team
The Connectivity Software Engineering team is responsible for enabling seamless, secure, and high-performance wireless connectivity across OpenAI’s products. We design and optimize Bluetooth, BLE, Wi-Fi, and emerging wireless technologies to ensure robust device pairing, network performance, and interoperability. Our work spans kernel drivers, system services, and user-level tools, with a focus on real-world performance, scalability, and reliability.

About the Role
OpenAI is seeking a Connectivity Software Engineer to design, implement, and optimize wireless connectivity features across our product ecosystem. You’ll work at the intersection of systems software, wireless standards, and hardware integration—building robust pairing and provisioning flows, debugging low-level protocols, and driving performance under real-world RF constraints. You will also support certification, field interoperability, and fleet-scale connectivity infrastructure.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 4 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Design, implement, and debug Bluetooth/BLE and Wi-Fi features across kernel drivers, BlueZ/wpa_supplicant/hostapd, and systemd/D-Bus services

  • Deliver robust pairing, bonding, and provisioning flows (GATT/GAP, LE Audio/LC3, WPA3/802.1X, captive portals, NAN)

  • Optimize link performance: throughput, latency, jitter, roaming, coexistence (BT↔Wi-Fi), and power modes (TWT, WoWLAN)

  • Build reliable network management using NetworkManager/nmcli, nl80211/cfg80211/mac80211, DNS/DHCP/mDNS, P2P/SoftAP

  • Instrument and analyze with packet captures and tooling (btmon/hcidump, Wireshark, iperf, eBPF/perf, spectrum sniffers)

  • Drive interoperability and certification readiness (Bluetooth SIG, Wi-Fi Alliance) and resolve field issues with root-cause fixes

  • Contribute to OTA-safe configuration, telemetry, and diagnostics for fleet-scale operation

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have deep experience shipping wireless features on Linux-based products

  • Are highly proficient in C/C++ with scripting experience (Python or shell) and systems debugging (gdb, strace, logs, packet traces)

  • Possess deep knowledge of Bluetooth Classic/BLE (HCI, L2CAP, GATT/GAP, profiles) and Wi-Fi (802.11 a/b/g/n/ac/ax, WPA2/3, nl80211, NAN)

  • Bring hands-on experience with BlueZ, wpa_supplicant/hostapd, NetworkManager, and driver bring-up on ARM64 or x86 platforms

  • Have a proven track record of improving real-world performance and reliability under RF constraints

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience with LE Audio (LC3), BLE Mesh, advanced roaming (802.11k/v/r), QoS/WMM, multicast/IGMP

  • Coexistence tuning across radios (BT/Wi-Fi/UWB/mmWave) and antenna/RF fundamentals with test equipment workflows

  • Familiarity with UWB (IEEE 802.15.4z, FiRa) ranging/integration; mmWave/Wi-Gig (802.11ad/ay)

  • Experience with security and provisioning at scale (EAP-TLS, device identity, secure boot, disk/network hardening)

  • Background in building factory test, interoperability, and certification test plans; upstream/open-source contributions

title: Researcher, Safety Oversight
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Safety Systems team is responsible for various safety work to ensure our best models can be safely deployed to the real world to benefit the society, and is at the forefront of OpenAI's mission to build and deploy safe AGI, driving our commitment to AI safety and fostering a culture of trust and transparency.

The Safety Oversight Research team aims to fundamentally advance our capabilities to maintain oversight over frontier AI models, and leverage these advances to ensure OpenAI’s deployed models are safe and beneficial. This requires a breadth of new ML research in the areas of human-AI collaboration, reasoning, robustness, and scalable oversight to keep pace with model capabilities.  We invest heavily in developing novel model and system-level methods of identifying and mitigating AI misuse and misalignment. 

Our goal is to learn from deployment and distribute the benefits of AI, while ensuring that this powerful tool is used responsibly and safely.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a senior researcher with a passion for AI safety and experience in safety research. Your role will set directions for research to maintain effective oversight of safe AGI and work on research projects to identify and mitigate misuse and misalignment in our AI systems. You will play a critical role in defining how a safe AI system should look in the future at OpenAI, making a significant impact on our mission to build and deploy safe AGI.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop and refine AI monitor models to detect and mitigate known and emerging patterns of misuse and misalignment.

  • Set research directions and strategies to make our AI systems safer, more aligned, and more robust.

  • Evaluate and design effective red-teaming pipelines to examine the end-to-end robustness of our safety systems, and identify areas for future improvement.

  • Conduct research to improve models’ ability to reason about questions of human values, and apply these improved models to practical safety challenges.

  • Coordinate and collaborate with cross-functional teams, including T&S, legal, policy and other research teams, to ensure that our products meet the highest safety standards.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Are excited about OpenAI’s mission of building safe, universally beneficial AGI and are aligned with OpenAI’s charter

  • Show enthusiasm for AI safety and dedication to enhancing the safety of cutting-edge AI models for real-world use.

  • Bring 4+ years of experience in the field of AI safety, especially in areas like RLHF, human-AI collaboration, fairness & biases.

  • Hold a Ph.D. or other degree in computer science, machine learning, or a related field.

  • Thrive in environments involving large-scale AI systems.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to build safe artificial general intelligence (AGI) which benefits all of humanity. This long-term undertaking brings the world’s best scientists, engineers, and business professionals into one lab together to accomplish this.

In pursuit of this mission, our Go To Market (GTM) team is responsible for helping customers learn how to leverage and deploy our highly capable AI products across their business. The team is made of Sales, Solutions, Support, Marketing, and Partnership professionals that work together to create valuable solutions that will help bring AI to as many users as possible.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Account Director to join our Startups Go To Market team. You will play a critical role in owning relationships with top startup customers and supporting them in building successfully on the OpenAI platform.

We believe that many of the most disruptive and category-defining AI applications will be created by startups. The Startup Go To Market team’s mission is to help startups harness the power of AI models to drive these advances. You will support startups building effectively with OpenAI’s APIs, and provide access to OpenAI teams and expertise to support their growth.

This role is a mixture of technical understanding, vision, partnership, and strategy. You’ll be responsible for serving as the primary relationship owner for a set of strategically important startup customers, as well as working across the OpenAI organization to help these startups accelerate their progress and be successful using our models. You’ll work cross-functionality with product, research, engineering, support, and solutions architecture to help customers get the most out of our models.

In this role, you will:

  • Manage a portfolio of startups accounts, developing and executing strategies for a comprehensive account plan.

  • Partner with solutions and research engineering to build and execute complex customer programs and projects.

  • Own a consumption revenue target.

  • Manage consumption revenue forecasts.

  • Analyze key account metrics to create reports and provide insights to internal and external stakeholders.

  • Closely monitor the industry landscape (people, competitors, partners, etc.) to contribute to product roadmap and other corporate strategies.

  • Collaborate with solutions, marketing, communications, business operations, people operations, finance, product management, and engineering.

  • Serve as an advocate for improving the startup experience building with OpenAI, synthesizing product feedback from insights captured from our work with startups.

  • Closely monitor the industry landscape and startup landscape to contribute to product roadmap and other corporate strategies.

  • Support the recruitment and onboarding of other teammates.

  • Support the development of company culture.

We're seeking someone with experience in:

  • 6+ years selling platform-as-a-service and/or software-as-a-service.

  • Designing and executing complex deal strategies.

  • Experience working in or around the startup ecosystem, preferably as either a founder of a startup, an employee of a startup, or someone who worked with startup customers.

  • Supporting the growth of fast-growing, high-performance companies.

  • Working directly with C-level executives.

  • Communicating technical concepts to customers and internal stakeholders.

  • Leading high-visibility customer events (CAB, conferences, product launches, etc.).

  • Gathering, distilling, and processing complex market (industry, competitor, customer, prospect) intelligence.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Are customer-centric. You are motivated to deeply understand your customer’s priorities and help them achieve their vision for using our models to improve their products and services. You build strong relationships with executives and professionals across functions and serve as a trusted advisor.

  • Have a passion or deep curiosity in artificial intelligence. You embrace the opportunity to help deploy our technology in a way that benefits humanity. You’re excited to educate our customers on AI and how to plan for the future.
