title: Software Engineer, Developer Productivity - Inference Runtime
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

We’re hiring a Developer Productivity engineer to support OpenAI’s Inference Runtime teams. These teams own the systems responsible for serving models reliably, efficiently, and safely across Codex, ChatGPT, API, and internal research workloads. We’re hiring a Developer Productivity Engineer to help scale the engineering systems, safeguards, and developer workflows that enable our teams to move quickly without compromising reliability or performance.

This role sits at the intersection of developer experience, CI/CD infrastructure, release engineering, production readiness, and inference systems reliability. You’ll work on the tooling and operational foundations that support model launches, inference optimizations, cloud provider integrations, and large-scale deployments across a rapidly evolving inference stack.

About the Role

We’re looking for an autonomous, high-ownership engineer who cares deeply about making other engineers faster, safer, and more confident.

A major focus of this role will be improving the tooling and infrastructure around deploy gates for inference engine images. These systems help ensure that every image released to production and research is correct, numerically sound, free of regressions, and performant across key metrics like time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-between-tokens (TBT).

You’ll help harden the systems that catch issues before they reach production, reduce noise from flaky or infrastructure-related test failures, and improve automation around triage, ownership, debugging, and escalation when failures occur. You’ll also work on improving observability, rollout safety, release automation, and developer self-service tooling across a rapidly evolving inference stack.

This is not generic internal tools work. The systems you build directly impact OpenAI’s ability to support new model launches, safely ship inference optimizations to the world, onboard new infrastructure providers, and operate one of the largest and most performance-sensitive inference platforms in the world.

In this role, you will:

  • Improve systems that ensure inference engine releases are correct, performant, and regression-free by evolving tooling and infrastructure for deploy gate validation

  • Bring rigor to release, validation, branching, and deployment processes across the inference stack

  • Improve canary, async, and large-scale validation workflows for inference systems

  • Harden CI, testing, and validation infrastructure so failures are actionable and trustworthy

  • Reduce noisy or flaky failures caused by infrastructure instability, GPU scheduling, or test environment issues

  • Build automation for failure triage, ownership detection, debugging, and escalation

  • Partner closely with inference teams, research developer productivity, engine acceleration, and infrastructure teams to improve release quality and rollout safety

  • Reduce developer friction in testing, debugging, and release workflows so engineers can move faster with confidence

You might thrive in this role if:

  • You have strong experience with CI/CD systems, testing infrastructure, release tooling, developer productivity, or large-scale build and validation systems

  • You are excited by high-impact infrastructure where small regressions in correctness, latency, or reliability meaningfully affect production systems

  • You care about building systems engineers can trust, not just systems that technically function

  • You have strong developer empathy and enjoy improving workflows, reducing friction, and making engineers more effective

  • You demonstrate high ownership and proactively identify problems, drive improvements, and follow issues through resolution

  • You are comfortable working in Python-heavy environments and debugging complex distributed systems

  • You enjoy building automation that reduces manual triage, improves signal quality, and scales operational effectiveness

  • You are comfortable operating in ambiguous areas without a fully predefined roadmap

  • You enjoy partnering closely with engineers to understand workflows, pain points, and operational challenges

  • You are pragmatic, collaborative, and motivated by helping teams move faster with more confidence

  • You are excited to learn about large-scale inference systems, even if you have not worked directly on inference before

Python experience is highly relevant, as much of the current deploy gate and validation infrastructure is Python-based. C++ experience is helpful, especially for working near inference engine code, CI build issues, or performance-sensitive systems, but it is not required.

Prior inference experience is not required.

The ideal candidate is someone with strong instincts around developer productivity, testing, release engineering, and automation who is excited to apply those skills in a deeply impactful inference environment. We’re looking for someone who is technically curious, comfortable navigating ambiguous, cross-functional operational problems, and is motivated to improve the reliability, safety, and developer experience of large-scale production infrastructure.

title: Novel Abuse Red Teamer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Intelligence and Investigations team is dedicated to ensuring the safe, responsible deployment of AI by rapidly detecting and mitigating abuse. Our team leverages cutting-edge testing methodologies to uncover vulnerabilities and emerging threats, helping safeguard OpenAI’s products and users. We work closely with cross-functional partners across product, policy, and engineering to drive a comprehensive defense strategy against evolving adversarial challenges.

About the Role

As a Novel Abuse Red Teamer, you’ll advance our pre- and post-deployment testing efforts at OpenAI, ensuring our models and products remain resilient against evolving, real-world adversarial threats.

We are seeking a self-starter to design, execute, and refine innovative adversarial testing and simulation protocols that leverage state-of-the-art tools and a hands-on red team approach. In this role, you will simulate threat actor methodologies and conduct rigorous application testing to uncover novel abuse vectors.

You will serve as a critical technical bridge between our security, product, and policy teams by employing an attacker mindset and advanced red team tactics to drive actionable insights that strengthen our detection mechanisms and overall product defenses. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in application security or penetration testing, with hands-on experience in web application security and proficiency in tools such as Burp Suite, Metasploit, and similar.
We value professionals with excellent communication skills, a commitment to continuous learning, and a passion for securing AI technologies through innovative testing methodologies.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and execute high-fidelity, realistic attack simulations that emulate sophisticated threat actor methodologies, uncovering hidden exploitation vectors through advanced red teaming and application testing techniques.

  • Analyze testing outcomes and generate actionable insights to refine our detection mechanisms, ultimately bolstering our overall security posture.

  • Serve as a crucial technical bridge between our security, product, and policy teams, ensuring that insights from adversarial testing inform broader defense strategies and remediation efforts.

  • Develop and integrate automation tools to streamline testing workflows and enable rapid iteration in response to emerging threats.

  • Collaborate closely with internal stakeholders to align testing strategies with evolving product needs and security objectives.

You might thrive in this role if you have / are:

  • Experience in application security, penetration testing, or red team operations, with a proven track record of executing adversarial testing and simulation protocols.

  • A strong technical background in web application security, coupled with hands-on expertise performing security testing of web applications, AI systems, and highly unique attack surfaces.

  • An attacker mindset and a passion for identifying novel abuse vectors in live environments, along with the ability to translate complex technical findings into actionable insights.

  • Demonstrated success in working cross-functionally within fast-paced, dynamic environments, managing complex product ecosystems, and driving rapid security enhancements.

  • Committed to continuous learning, innovation, and the pursuit of cutting-edge security methodologies to protect and advance AI technologies.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s GTM Partnerships team builds a strategic global partner ecosystem designed to accelerate customer success, support secure AI adoption, and drive growth in support of OpenAI’s mission. We collaborate closely across Sales, Technical Success, Product, Marketing, Operations, and leadership teams to turn strategic partnerships into durable commercial outcomes.

Within that ecosystem, AWS is one of OpenAI’s most strategic partners. Our opportunity extends beyond the direct alliance relationship: we aim to enable AWS teams and the surrounding services-partner ecosystem to build, deliver, and scale OpenAI-powered solutions on AWS infrastructure.

Success requires close collaboration across AWS Japan alliance and field teams, AWS-focused SI practices, cloud architects, field sellers, delivery leaders, OpenAI’s Japan Partner Director, and OpenAI GTM teams. It requires strong operating discipline, scalable co-sell execution, and the ability to translate a strategic alliance into measurable customer outcomes.

About the Role

We are hiring a Partner Director to shape and execute OpenAI’s AWS alliance partnership in Japan. This person will own the direct relationship with AWS Japan while mobilizing AWS Japan field teams and the broader services-partner ecosystem around high-value customer opportunities.

This is a hands-on individual-contributor role operating through influence in Japan. You will work alongside OpenAI’s Japan Partner Director to develop Japan GTM strategies, drive joint account planning, coordinate AWS-related opportunities, and operationally manage selected cross-functional initiatives.

You will build and own the Japan GTM strategy with AWS, translating the alliance into repeatable OpenAI and AWS solutions, field playbooks, governance structures, and co-sell motions that can be adopted across Japan’s customer segments and GTM teams. The right candidate combines alliance leadership with a builder’s mindset and the ability to move comfortably between executive engagement and detailed execution.

title: Physical Network & Structured Cabling Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI is on a bold mission to build the world’s most advanced AI infrastructure. We are seeking a Data Center Network and Structured Cabling Engineer with 10+ years of experience in designing and implementing optimized network and structured cabling solutions at large data centers buildings and data center campuses.

The Data Center Engineering team is central to this mission defining infrastructure strategy, driving technical innovation, working with research to set performance benchmarks, and developing reference designs that enable rapid, scalable global deployment.

As part of this team, you will help design and deliver next-generation data center infrastructure optimized for AI workloads. You’ll collaborate across research, site selection, design, construction, commissioning, hardware engineering, deployment, operations, and global partners to bring OpenAI’s infrastructure vision to life.

Role Summary

As a Physical Network & Structured Cabling Engineer, you will own the design, implementation, and quality assurance of structured cabling and physical network infrastructure across OpenAI’s global data center footprint. This role bridges design, construction, and operations, ensuring that every layer of our physical networking from fiber trunks to copper patching meets the highest standards of performance, reliability, and scalability.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and specify physical network infrastructure across data center buildings and campuses, including fiber and copper cabling, network rooms, rack layouts, cable trays, and duct bank pathways. Coordinate with other engineering disciplines to ensure network infrastructure space, power, cooling, and operational requirements are incorporated into the overall design

  • Develop standards, reference designs, and installation guidelines for structured cabling and physical network deployments.

  • Translate logical network architectures and hardware connectivity requirements into scalable physical designs, including fiber topology, port connectivity, patching, redundancy, and capacity planning, in partnership with network engineering and operations teams.

  • Provide technical direction to design consultants, cabling vendors, and installation contractors, resolving scope gaps and ensuring designs are constructible and meet network requirements.

  • Define installation quality and acceptance criteria, and oversee inspection, testing, commissioning, and turnover of structured cabling systems.

  • Lead physical network design reviews, coordinate clash detection and resolution with other disciplines, and conduct site inspections to verify installation quality and conformance with design and operational requirements.

  • Troubleshoot and resolve issues during build, commissioning, and handover phases to ensure network readiness.

  • Develop and maintain physical network documentation, including design requirements, drawings, port maps, cable schedules, bills of materials, labeling standards, and as-built records.

  • Provide feedback to design and operations teams to drive continuous improvement of physical network standards.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Telecommunications, or related field, or equivalent experience.

  • 10+ years of experience designing and delivering physical network infrastructure and structured cabling systems for large-scale data centers, including responsibility for design decisions, construction coordination, and operational readiness.

  • Strong understanding of data center network topologies and high-speed optical connectivity, including transceivers, fiber types, breakout configurations, connector and polarity schemes, and optical loss budgets.

  • Expertise in industry standards such as ANSI/TIA, BICSI and other relevant structured cabling guidelines.

  • Proven ability to coordinate with cross-functional teams and external vendors on large-scale projects.

  • Strong skills in reviewing and interpreting technical drawings, cable schedules, and documentation management.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Willingness to travel frequently to global data center sites.

Preferred Skills

  • Master’s degree in Engineering, or relevant certifications such as BICSI, RCDD, or equivalent.

  • Experience with hyperscale cloud, AI, or high-performance computing environments.

  • Proficiency in 2D and 3D engineering tools (e.g., CAD, Revit) for infrastructure design and clash detection analysis.

  • Experience with structured connectivity data and automation for generating and validating port maps, cable schedules, bills of materials, and labels.

  • Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills for physical layer systems and issues.

title: Software Engineer, Workload Enablement
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Scaling team is responsible for the architectural and engineering backbone of OpenAI’s infrastructure. We design and deliver advanced systems that support the deployment and operation of cutting-edge AI models. Our work spans system software, networking, platform architecture, fleet-level monitoring, and performance optimization.

About the Role

We’re hiring an SW Engineer to enable production workloads and end-to-end testing on new platforms. This role will include creating new test harnesses and platform stress benchmarks, porting existing inference and training workloads to new, sometimes early-access, systems/hardware, analyzing performance and bottlenecks, and characterizing the end-to-end behavior of new systems (compute, comms, storage, control plane, and failure modes).

Key Responsibilities

  • Port and validate key inference and training workloads on new platforms/SKUs as they arrive; drive correctness, performance, and stability to an internal readiness bar.

  • Build a suite of benchmarks and stress tests that capture real E2E behavior of our workloads by exercising all aspects of a system, including CPU, GPU, memory subsystem, frontend, scale-up, and scale-out networking (including WAN traffic, NVlink and RDMA collectives), storage, thermals, and any other relevant parts.

  • Deep-dive performance on distributed training/inference:

    • Collective performance and tuning (across NCCL/RCCL and internal libraries)

    • Overlap of compute/communication, kernel-level bottlenecks, memory bandwidth and scheduling effects

  • Create repeatable test harnesses that run in CI / lab environments and produce actionable outputs (pass/fail, performance score, regression detection).

  • Partner with systems + fleet bring-up engineers to ensure the platform is not only stable and performant, but also operationally usable and scalable (containerization, K8s integration, telemetry hooks, failure triage loops).

  • Work cross-functionally with vendors and internal stakeholders by producing clear bug reports, minimal repros, and prioritized issue lists.

Qualifications

  • BS in CS/EE (or equivalent practical experience).

  • 5+ years in one or more of: ML systems, performance engineering, distributed systems, or HPC.

  • Strong hands-on experience with:

    • PyTorch and modern LLM training/inference stacks

    • Large-scale distributed training concepts (data/model/pipeline parallel, collective comms)

    • Experience with RDMA and debugging/optimizing comms libraries (NCCL or RCCL) and their interaction with hardware/network

  • Proficiency in Python plus comfort reading/writing performance-critical code (C++/CUDA/HIP is a plus).

  • Strong profiling/debugging skills (e.g., Nsight, rocprof, perf, flamegraphs; ability to reason from traces/counters).

Preferred Skills

  • Experience building workload-shaped benchmarks and stress/fault tests that correlate to production behavior (not just synthetic loops or microbenchmarks).

  • Familiarity with RDMA networking and transport tuning; understanding of how network topology and congestion impact collectives.

  • Experience running and validating workloads in Kubernetes, and bridging “research code” into robust, repeatable infrastructure.

  • Hands-on lab experience with early hardware (new NICs, new GPUs/accelerators, early racks).

title: Network Infrastructure Engineer, Global Network Infra (WAN)
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI's Global Network Infrastructure team is responsible for building and operating the global network backbone that connects our rapidly expanding compute infrastructure. Our work enables reliable, high-performance connectivity across data centers, cloud service providers, and network points of presence (PoPs), supporting the infrastructure behind OpenAI's research and products.

As OpenAI continues to scale its compute footprint globally, we are expanding our network infrastructure to meet increasing demands for capacity, reliability, and operational efficiency. Our team works across physical network design, carrier connectivity, network deployment, and operational troubleshooting to deliver resilient infrastructure at exceptional scale.

About the Role

We are looking for a hands-on Network Infrastructure Engineer to help design, deploy, activate, and operate OpenAI's global wide area network (WAN) infrastructure.

In this role, you will take direct ownership of bringing new network connectivity online, working closely with fiber providers, cloud service providers, and internal infrastructure teams to establish reliable connectivity across our global backbone.

You will be involved in everything from physical network design and circuit provisioning to troubleshooting complex connectivity issues across Layer 1, Layer 2, and Layer 3. You will play a critical role in expanding our network footprint, bringing new PoPs online, and ensuring that our infrastructure operates reliably as OpenAI continues to grow.

We're looking for engineers who enjoy working close to the infrastructure, thrive on solving difficult networking problems, and bring an automation-first mindset to scaling network operations.

In This Role, You Will:

  • Design, deploy, and support WAN infrastructure across data centers, network PoPs, and cloud connectivity environments.

  • Own the end-to-end activation and turn-up of network circuits, working directly with fiber carriers and cloud service providers to establish and validate connectivity.

  • Troubleshoot complex network issues across physical, Layer 2, and Layer 3 infrastructure, including optical signal problems, FEC errors, routing issues, and connectivity failures.

  • Diagnose and isolate network failures across carrier, cloud provider, and internal infrastructure boundaries, driving issues through resolution.

  • Contribute to physical network infrastructure design, including port mappings, fiber and cable layouts, optical distribution frames (ODFs), and connectivity planning.

  • Monitor network health, circuit utilization, and performance to proactively identify capacity constraints and reliability risks.

  • Build automation and tooling to streamline network provisioning, deployment validation, troubleshooting, and operational workflows.

  • Collaborate with network engineering, data center infrastructure, and external service providers to support the expansion of OpenAI's global backbone.

  • Participate in an on-call rotation to maintain the reliability and availability of critical network infrastructure.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You:

  • Have hands-on experience deploying, activating, and troubleshooting WAN circuits with telecommunications carriers, fiber providers, or cloud service providers.

  • Have a strong understanding of networking fundamentals, including optical networking, Ethernet, TCP/IP, BGP, and Layer 2/3 connectivity.

  • Are comfortable debugging network issues across multiple layers, from physical fiber connectivity and optical errors to routing and traffic forwarding.

  • Have experience working with data center networking, carrier infrastructure, cloud interconnects, or large-scale WAN environments.

  • Understand physical network infrastructure concepts such as fiber cabling, port mappings, optical distribution frames, and network equipment connectivity.

  • Can independently investigate ambiguous connectivity problems, isolate root causes, and work across internal and external teams to restore service.

  • Have experience with scripting or automation tools and are motivated to reduce manual work through repeatable, scalable processes.

  • Enjoy working directly with infrastructure and take pride in owning technical problems from initial deployment through operational resolution.

  • Thrive in a fast-moving environment where infrastructure requirements evolve rapidly and engineering decisions have a direct impact on global scale.

Nice to Have

  • Experience building or operating large-scale backbone networks, hyperscale data center networks, or cloud provider interconnect infrastructure.

  • Familiarity with optical transport technologies, network telemetry, and advanced troubleshooting of physical network links.

  • Experience automating network operations using Python, Go, or infrastructure automation frameworks.

  • Experience deploying new network PoPs or supporting large-scale network expansion projects.

  • Experience collaborating with carriers, colocation providers, and cloud networking teams on complex connectivity deployments.

Why This Role Matters

OpenAI's ability to advance AI research and deliver products at global scale depends on reliable, high-performance infrastructure.

As a member of the Global Network Infrastructure team, you will help build the connectivity foundation supporting some of the world's most demanding compute environments. Your work will directly contribute to expanding OpenAI's global network footprint, bringing critical infrastructure online, and ensuring the reliability of the systems powering frontier AI.

This is an opportunity to work on challenging infrastructure problems, take meaningful ownership of global network deployments, and help shape the next generation of OpenAI's network backbone.

title: Growth Marketing Manager - Web & Organic, SMB Ads
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI is building the next generation of advertising for an AI-powered world. As AI changes how people discover information, explore possibilities, and make decisions, we believe this presents a huge opportunity for small and medium-sized businesses to connect with customers in new ways.

The SMB Ads Marketing team is building this opportunity from the ground up. We define how businesses discover OpenAI’s advertising platform, become successful advertisers, and grow their investment over time. Working closely with Product, Ads Engineering, Data Science, and Sales, we combine customer insight, rigorous experimentation, and fast execution to turn early opportunities into scalable growth.

About the Role

We are seeking a Growth Marketing Manager to build the web and organic growth engine for SMB advertisers at OpenAI. This is a zero-to-one opportunity to shape how businesses discover our advertising platform, understand its value, and become successful advertisers.

You will own the SMB Ads web strategy and experimentation roadmap, combining customer insight, analytical rigor, and product judgment to grow qualified discovery and improve conversion. Your scope spans web experiences, organic search, generative engine optimization (GEO), and the journey from first visit through signup and activation. You will work closely with Product, Design, Ads Engineering, Content, and Data Science to turn opportunities into shipped experiences, operating with the speed and ownership of a startup.

In This Role, You Will

  • Own the SMB Ads web strategy and roadmap to grow qualified discovery, signup, and advertiser activation.

  • Grow organic discovery through search, content, and GEO. Test new ways to help businesses find and evaluate OpenAI’s advertising offering.

  • Analyze journeys, funnels, and cohorts to identify conversion barriers and prioritize high-impact improvements.

  • Run experiments across landing pages, messaging, navigation, personalization, offers, and conversion flows. Use results to guide the roadmap.

  • Improve the journey from website visit to signup, onboarding, and first campaign with Product and Ads Engineering.

  • Define instrumentation, test design, attribution, and reporting with Data Science and marketing systems teams to measure incremental activation and advertiser value.

  • Launch useful web experiences with Content, Product Marketing, Design, Engineering, and specialist agencies. Evaluate capabilities such as personalization, chat, and experimentation tools.

  • Connect landing experiences to in-product, referral, and cross-sell acquisition programs. Coordinate onboarding and engagement with Lifecycle Marketing.

  • Use AI to accelerate research, prototyping, content, analysis, and experimentation. Scale successful tests and communicate results clearly.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

  • Bring 4–7 years of experience in growth marketing, web strategy, organic acquisition, conversion optimization, or product growth, with measurable acquisition, activation, or revenue impact.

  • Apply strong analytical judgment across funnels, cohorts, customer behavior, and incremental impact to prioritize growth opportunities.

  • Demonstrate ownership of web experiences and experimentation programs that improve conversion from discovery to activation.

  • Connect SEO, content-led discovery, and GEO with customer insight, web strategy, and product judgment.

  • Translate business opportunities into clear roadmaps and launched experiences with Product, Design, Engineering, Data Science, and Marketing.

descriptionHtml:
About the Role

OpenAI’s largest and most strategic customers are turning AI ambition into deployments that change how their organizations work. As a Delivery Lead, you will own delivery of priority AI initiatives for these customers, leading complex, high-impact deployments from planning through launch and adoption.

You’ll establish an integrated delivery plan, drive execution against launch commitments, resolve blockers, and lead progress toward measurable customer value. You’ll partner closely with account and technical teams, FDEs, customers, and delivery partners to turn customer priorities into successful deployments. descriptionHtml:

About the Team:

We build foundational platform software that enables reliable, secure, and performant products. The team works across system layers and partners closely with adjacent engineering groups to deliver robust capabilities from concept through launch.

We’re seeking an Embedded Systems Software Engineer to design, implement, and debug core platform components and the pipelines that build and update system images. You’ll work across operating system layers, focusing on performance, security, and deep system debugging to ship production‑grade systems.

title: Applied AI Engineer, Codex
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. For software engineering organizations, this means helping customers adopt Codex and other OpenAI capabilities across the software development lifecycle—transforming how teams plan, build, test, review, and deliver software.

We work directly with engineering leaders and hands-on developers to identify high-value opportunities, design and implement AI-powered development workflows, and scale what works across engineering organizations. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products, reusable architectures, and technical patterns that help developers everywhere get more value from Codex.

About the Role

As an Applied AI Engineer focused on Codex, you will partner directly with leading engineering organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that transform how software is developed. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from workflow and use-case selection through prototyping, evaluation, production rollout, and scaled adoption.

You will work alongside engineering teams to build advanced AI coding workflows, integrations, automations, and evaluation systems—often using Codex itself as part of your development process. You will help customers make technical decisions involving model behavior, agentic workflows, developer environments, security, reliability, evaluation, and operational readiness, while ensuring deployments translate into measurable improvements in engineering productivity and software delivery.

You will work closely with OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, Sales, and the broader Codex organization, translating real-world deployment experience into high-signal product and model feedback. Success is measured by production systems, sustained developer adoption, and meaningful improvements to how engineering organizations build software—not simply successful demonstrations or enablement activity.

  • Influence customer engineering strategy by helping technical leaders understand how AI coding systems can reshape their software development lifecycle, engineering practices, and organizational workflows.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering software or AI systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, developer tooling, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting.

title: Certification Architect
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Customer Education helps customers build the practical skills and confidence to use AI and OpenAI products safely and effectively. We bring together customer insight, learning and enablement expertise, product signals, and measurement to help organizations move from access to durable adoption.

Within Customer Education, the Certification team helps individuals demonstrate competence for in-demand AI skills and helps customers and partners validate that their workforce has the skills they need to meet their AI-enabled business goals. Our work centers on the belief that learners should understand where to go to build skills and capabilities, how to demonstrate them, and what to pursue next. Similarly, Enterprise leaders should understand what each credential signifies and how it supports workforce readiness. We do this with transparency for the overall OpenAI credential framework and providing trusted, role-based certifications that verify practical capability.

About the Role

As Certification Architect, you will define the framework, standards, and assessment architecture that make OpenAI certifications a trusted signal of demonstrated capability.

This is a senior hands-on role on the Certification team that will build reusable foundations for a growing portfolio: clear competency standards, defensible assessments, scalable in-product delivery, and evidence of continued competence.

You will work closely with certification specialists, technical subject matter experts, learning product and engineering teams, operations and policy partners, and stakeholders across the go-to-market organization.

The AI Architect team partners with organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact. We work with customers across industries and digital-native businesses to identify where AI can create value, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption. title: Advanced Manufacturing Technology Lead
descriptionHtml:
About the Team:

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role:

We’re looking for an Advanced Manufacturing Technology Lead to develop the fabrication and assembly capabilities behind next-generation high-density, high-speed, high-power compute boards. You will own the manufacturing technology roadmap across bare printed circuit board (PCB) fabrication and board assembly, qualifying critical materials, structures, and processes before product designs are locked.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role spanning early experiments, test vehicles, pilot builds, and transfer to new product introduction (NPI) teams. You’ll partner with board design, signal integrity, packaging, and reliability engineers, along with PCB fabricators, assembly partners, and equipment suppliers, to translate manufacturing evidence into practical design rules and robust production processes.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the manufacturing technology roadmap for next-generation compute boards, identifying gaps across bare PCB fabrication and board assembly and developing capabilities ahead of product needs.

  • Partner with board design, signal integrity, packaging, and reliability teams to qualify materials, stackups, via structures, and interconnects before layout freeze, translating results into design rules suppliers can build to.

  • Prototype and validate assembly, inspection, and rework methods for large, complex ASIC packages, establishing process windows that address warpage and solder-joint integrity.

  • Validate defect-detection methods using known-good and known-defect samples, defining inspection coverage, repeatability, and acceptance criteria.

  • Lead test-vehicle and pilot builds with PCB fabricators, assembly partners, and equipment suppliers, qualifying processes against yield, capability, reliability, and throughput targets.

  • Transfer validated process windows, tooling requirements, inspection methods, and process controls to NPI teams with clear qualification evidence and handoff documentation.

  • Serve as a technical lead for advanced PCB fabrication and board assembly, mentoring engineers, guiding stackup and process decisions, and turning cross-functional failure analysis into reusable design rules and controls.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have developed and qualified advanced PCB fabrication and board assembly processes, taking new technologies from experiments and test vehicles through pilot builds and production transfer.

  • Bring strong technical depth in PCB materials, stackups, via structures, and interconnects, and understand how fabrication choices affect electrical performance, manufacturability, and reliability.

  • Have hands-on experience with assembly of large, complex ASIC packages, including package-to-board interactions, warpage, solder-joint integrity, and process-window development.

  • Have developed or qualified inspection and rework methods, using representative samples and failure-analysis evidence to understand detection limits and verify process effectiveness.

  • Use structured experiments, measurement-system validation, and statistical process analysis to establish capability and make clear qualification decisions.

  • Work effectively with fabricators, assembly partners, and equipment suppliers, balancing technical risk, yield, reliability, and throughput while transferring processes into production.

  • Lead through technical judgment and collaboration, with experience mentoring engineers and influencing board design, signal integrity, packaging, and reliability decisions early in development.

title: Motion Designer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.


This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a Motion Designer to help tell the stories behind our research. You’ll translate complex ideas, emerging capabilities, and the work of our researchers into clear, engaging motion across films, launches, demos, and other communications.

Working within the creative team, you’ll partner with Research, Brand, and production teams to shape work from early concepts through final delivery. You’ll explore visual approaches, develop original design and animation, and help bring other artists’ contributions together into a cohesive result.

This is a hands-on role for someone with strong motion craft, curiosity about unfamiliar subjects, and confidence working with open-ended briefs. Alongside your own execution, you’ll provide feedback to fellow artists, help establish creative standards, and take ownership of motion quality across assigned projects.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop motion concepts for research stories, working with creative partners and subject matter experts to make complex ideas visually clear while preserving their underlying meaning.

  • Design and produce high-quality 2D and 3D motion for research films, launches, demos, and supporting content, from storyboards and animatics through final delivery.

  • Apply compositing and VFX expertise to develop and execute complex visual sequences.

  • Apply and extend OpenAI’s visual and motion language, balancing consistency with the needs of each story.

  • Take ownership of motion quality across assigned projects, bringing individual contributions together into a cohesive result. Help establish and maintain shared standards for craft and visual consistency through project reviews, references, and practical guidance.

  • Provide actionable creative and technical feedback, mentor fellow artists to strengthen their craft, and share techniques while remaining hands-on.

  • Collaborate closely with designers, filmmakers, editors, producers, and researchers to shape work from early concepts through final delivery.

  • Work with producers to scope projects, communicate dependencies, and maintain a high standard of craft as priorities and timelines evolve.

  • Present work clearly, explain creative decisions, and incorporate feedback from creative and technical partners.

  • Develop reusable assets, templates, and workflows where they improve quality and make recurring work easier to produce.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 7+ years of experience in motion design across films, campaigns, launches, or other narrative work.

  • A strong portfolio demonstrating design judgment, animation craft, and the ability to carry an idea from concept through finished execution.

  • The ability to explore an open-ended brief, develop a clear visual approach, and refine it through collaboration.

  • Experience providing constructive feedback to other artists and bringing multiple contributors’ work together into a cohesive result.

  • Proficiency in After Effects and experience with Cinema 4D or comparable 3D tools, alongside editing and compositing workflows.

  • Comfort working in Figma and sharing work across design and production teams.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The IP Infrastructure team builds and operates the systems that enable OpenAI to share research and engineering technology securely and reliably with strategic partners. Our work spans continuously running pipelines for model weights, configurations, code, and container images.

We work closely with research, security, developer infrastructure, and partner engineering teams to turn complex requirements into dependable software. We’re a small, collaborative team with direct ownership of systems that support important partnerships.

About the Role

We’re looking for a software engineer to build and improve the backend services behind these workflows. You’ll work primarily in Python, take projects from design through production, and make our systems more reliable and easier to operate as partner integrations evolve.

The work combines hands-on engineering with careful judgment. You’ll translate requirements about what can be shared into clear, testable business logic, debug problems across system boundaries, and collaborate with the teams that build and use the underlying infrastructure.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week.

In this role, you will:

title: Product Manager, Core Models
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Core Models team helps shape how OpenAI’s frontier models are built, measured, and launched. We work across Research, Engineering, Model Design, Data Science, and Product to turn advances in model capabilities into reliable, useful experiences for people. Our scope includes model planning and launches as well as building data flywheels, evaluations and measurement systems to ensure our models have strong capabilities and behavior.

About the Role

As a Product Manager for the Core Models team, you'll be at the forefront of defining and guiding the future of how our AI models work in real-world applications. You will connect user needs to model and systems decisions: how prompts are understood; how information is aggregated and made useful for training and evaluation data; and how capabilities move from research prototypes into the mainline model and launch stack. You will operate comfortably across research, infrastructure, and consumer product surfaces, creating clarity where ownership and technical boundaries are still emerging.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Translate user and product goals into clear model requirements, system architecture choices, and research priorities across query understanding, indexing, retrieval, ranking, tool boundaries, data, training, inference, and evaluation.

  • Build closed learning loops that turn product usage, explicit feedback, and other user signals into datasets, evaluations, experiments, training priorities, and launch decisions.

  • Define success across offline evaluations and online product metrics, balancing model quality, usefulness, latency, safety, reliability, and cost.

  • Partner closely with post-training research, applied product engineering, Model Design, and Data Science to integrate capabilities into the mainline model stack.

  • Create reusable platforms and operating systems for evaluation, experimentation, and signal collection so that new capabilities improve faster over time.

  • Use concrete product failures and emerging user needs to identify gaps, form hypotheses, and shape the next wave of research and product investment.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have deep expertise in product management or closely related experience, including ownership of technically complex products or platforms.

  • Bring deep fluency in one or more relevant domains: search and information retrieval, recommendation or personalization systems, ML platforms, large-scale data systems, model evaluation, or AI product infrastructure.

  • Know how to pair offline evaluation with online experimentation and user signals, and can distinguish a useful metric from a convenient one.

  • Earn the trust of researchers and engineers through technical depth, crisp judgment, and a willingness to engage directly with the details.

  • Combine consumer product taste with systems rigor, and care about both the quality people feel and the infrastructure that makes it repeatable.

  • Move quickly in ambiguous environments, communicate directly, and help teams make sound decisions without waiting for perfect information.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Senior Support Engineering team is responsible for ensuring that developers and enterprises can reliably build mission critical solutions using OpenAI models. We provide technical guidance, resolve complex issues and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our highly-capable models. We work closely with Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. We think from an automation-first mindset and leverage the latest in AI to scale our support operations. Join the Senior Support Engineering (SSE) team at OpenAI and help shape the future of Technical Support in the age of AI.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Support Engineering Manager to build and guide a high-performing team of experienced Senior Support Engineers with backgrounds in software engineering, site reliability engineering, and systems architecture. These engineers are trusted to operate with autonomy, tackle deeply technical challenges, and serve as the final escalation point before Engineering.

In this role, you'll lead a team focused on deep problem-solving, proactive reliability work, and customer-specific troubleshooting. You’ll drive the design and operations of OpenAI’s incident management processes, including tooling, automations, and training, and ensure they are scalable and resilient. title: Applied AI Software Engineer, GTM Growth Engineering
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

GTM Growth Engineering builds AI-native products that help OpenAI's go-to-market and B2B marketing organizations scale with greater speed, intelligence, and operational effectiveness.


We apply OpenAI models to real business workflows and build the systems that make those applications useful and dependable: customer context, agent behavior, feedback, evaluation, experimentation, and appropriate human oversight.


Our work brings together software engineering, applied AI, product, data, and GTM operations. We measure success through the quality of customer engagement, pipeline, conversion, and the effectiveness of our sales and marketing teams.

 

About the Role

We're looking for an Applied AI Engineer to build production systems that help AI-powered go-to-market workflows improve over time. You will connect agent behavior, customer and operator feedback, evaluation, experimentation, and business outcomes to make these systems more effective, reliable, and responsive to evolving customer needs.

This is a deeply technical, cross-functional role with end-to-end ownership of the agent improvement loop: understand production behavior, identify failure modes, improve how the system decides or acts, and validate the resulting impact.

You will partner with Engineering, Product, Data Science, Sales, and B2B Marketing to turn real-world signals into safer, more effective agent behavior and measurable improvements in customer engagement, conversion, qualified pipeline, and team productivity.

 

In this role, you will:

  • Own the production improvement loop across agent behavior, customer and operator feedback, evaluation, experimentation, and verified business outcomes.

  • Instrument agent workflows so model interactions, tool use, decisions, failures, human edits, and downstream outcomes can be understood in context.

  • Define meaningful quality standards, representative evaluation datasets, regression coverage, and production monitoring for real GTM workflows.

  • Investigate why agents underperform across context, knowledge, instructions, tools, routing, guardrails, or workflow design.

  • Design and ship targeted behavior improvements, including changes to prompting, context construction, decision logic, tool use, and human-review paths.

  • Build backend services, APIs, data models, and feedback pipelines that make agent behavior observable, steerable, and reproducible.

  • Run controlled experiments, production replays, or staged rollouts to measure whether changes improve quality and downstream business results.

  • Partner with Product, Data Science, Sales, and B2B Marketing to prioritize high-value problems and define customer and business success.

  • Ship with appropriate safeguards for privacy, security, reliability, human oversight, and safe operational rollout.

 

You might be a great fit if you have:

  • 4+ years of software, backend, applied AI, or product-engineering experience building reliable production systems.

  • Experience building AI agents, LLM-powered applications, or other model-driven workflows that operated on real production traffic.

  • Experience diagnosing and improving agent behavior using production traces, user feedback, evaluation, experimentation, or careful systems design.

  • Practical experience with evaluation design, regression testing, human or model grading, online quality signals, or controlled experiments.

  • Strong backend engineering skills across Python, APIs, data pipelines, stateful workflows, and production services.

  • Strong product judgment and the ability to connect technical changes to customer experience, conversion, qualified pipeline, or operational efficiency.

  • Comfort working across model behavior, context, knowledge, tools, workflow state, and human-in-the-loop decisions.

  • The ability to work closely with technical and non-technical partners across Engineering, Product, Data Science, Sales, and B2B Marketing.

  • A pragmatic mindset: you can scope ambiguous problems, ship useful improvements, and build toward a durable system.

 

You Might Thrive If

  • You want to build AI systems that improve from real usage instead of stopping at a successful prototype.

  • You enjoy tracing messy production failures back to the decision, context, tool interaction, or workflow issue that caused them.

  • You think evaluation is valuable when it helps teams make better product decisions and improve real outcomes.

  • You are comfortable moving between applied AI, backend engineering, experimentation, and product judgment.

  • You like partnering with operators, sales teams, and marketers to understand the work your systems need to improve.

  • You can move from an ambiguous problem to a focused experiment, measured result, and durable implementation.

  • You care about trustworthy deployment, clear human-review paths, and reliable production systems.


Nice to Have

  • Experience building agent evaluation, observability, experimentation, or AI infrastructure products.

  • Experience with production replay, LLM grading, human-labeled datasets, shadow evaluation, or staged rollout.

title: Principal Software Engineer, ChatGPT Education and Learning
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The ChatGPT Learning team creates the next generation of learning experiences within ChatGPT. Millions of people use ChatGPT each week to explore concepts, practice skills, and work through challenges, making learning one of the platform’s largest consumer use cases.

We want ChatGPT to support sustained learning and progress over time, beyond answering individual questions. We’re exploring how AI can make powerful learning tools more accessible, helping people understand the world, develop skills, and pursue their goals.

Our work brings together product engineering, design, AI research, and education to serve learners around the world.

About the Role

As a Principal Software Engineer on the ChatGPT Learning team, you will set technical direction and lead the design and development of products that help millions of people learn with ChatGPT.

You’ll remain hands-on across the stack, building polished interfaces and scalable backend services. Working closely with product managers, designers, researchers, and platform teams, you’ll bring new model capabilities into everyday learning experiences.

You’ll drive product and design decisions alongside your cross-functional partners, helping define what we build, how it works, and how it serves learners. We’re looking for an engineer with strong product judgment who can turn ambiguous opportunities into clear direction, lead complex initiatives from concept through launch, and raise the quality of the team’s technical work.

This position is based in San Francisco or New York City, with three days each week in the office. Relocation assistance is available to new employees.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead end-to-end development of learning experiences in ChatGPT, from early exploration through production and iteration.

  • Drive product and design decisions with product managers and designers, bringing technical insight, user feedback, and sound judgment to priorities and tradeoffs.

  • Set technical direction for complex initiatives and guide architecture decisions that support rapid experimentation and long-term reliability.

  • Build multimodal learning capabilities that combine text, images, voice, and interactive interfaces.

  • Develop scalable services and APIs to support learning features throughout ChatGPT.

  • Work with researchers, platform teams, designers, and engineers to prototype ideas and bring new AI capabilities to users.

  • Improve performance, reliability, and usability across ChatGPT’s learning surfaces, using experiments and user feedback to guide improvements.

  • Support other engineers through mentorship, code reviews, and clear technical guidance.

  • Have led complex technical initiatives and made architecture decisions that balance product needs, development speed, and maintainability.

  • Have experience driving product and design decisions in close partnership with product managers and designers.

  • Enjoy building consumer products and taking ownership from initial concept through production.

  • Bring clarity to ambiguous problems and translate them into practical product solutions.

  • Have strong product engineering instincts and care deeply about the quality of the user experience.

  • Have experience building interactive educational tools or learning products.

  • Have experience developing AI-powered applications or systems built around large language models.

  • Want to build products with meaningful global impact and expand access to education and learning opportunities.

title: Software Engineer, Compute Foundations
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Compute Foundations builds the software that manages OpenAI’s GPU compute infrastructure across sites, data centers, and infrastructure providers, supporting model training and inference. Our systems turn large, heterogeneous fleets of machines into dependable compute for research and products.

We build Kubernetes-based control planes, controllers, services, and APIs that coordinate the lifecycle of machines and clusters. We connect global infrastructure management with the realities of bare-metal systems, giving clients consistent interfaces across differences in hardware, topology, and provider behavior.

About the Role

You will build distributed systems that provision, configure, and manage compute throughout its lifecycle. Your work will connect global services and Kubernetes controllers with the systems that bring machines online, update them safely, and recover them when something goes wrong.

This role combines software architecture with an understanding of how machines and data centers work. You might design a lifecycle API, improve controller performance under high concurrency and provider rate limits, or trace a provisioning failure from an API through reconciliation to network boot or host configuration. You will help these systems remain reliable as the fleet expands across sites and generations of GPU hardware.

We value depth in relevant systems and the ability to connect layers. You do not need to arrive as an expert in every component of the stack.

In this role, you will:

  • Design, build, and operate Kubernetes-based controllers and distributed services that coordinate infrastructure across sites, isolate failures, and scale as GPU capacity grows.

  • Define APIs and resource models that let clients request and track lifecycle operations through consistent interfaces across hardware platforms and providers.

  • Build provisioning and configuration services that coordinate network boot, hardware management interfaces, and the deployment of firmware, operating-system images, drivers, and host configuration.

  • Develop lifecycle management for discovery, allocation, provisioning, upgrades, maintenance, recovery, and decommissioning, integrating with health and validation systems.

  • Design reliable reconciliation and recovery through concurrent changes, interrupted operations, and partial failures, with staged rollouts that limit disruption across nodes, racks, and clusters.

  • Improve control-plane throughput, API latency, and the time infrastructure takes to reach its desired state, while respecting the limits of site systems and provider APIs.

  • Build the software integrations that bring new sites and GPU hardware generations into the platform, partnering with hardware, networking, data-center, and other infrastructure teams.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have strong software engineering fundamentals and experience designing, implementing, and owning production distributed systems or infrastructure services.

  • Have experience developing infrastructure systems that use Kubernetes APIs and reconciliation to manage resources.

  • Understand how a bare-metal node moves from power-on to a configured, workload-ready system, with depth in one or more areas such as PXE, DHCP/DNS, baseboard management controllers (BMCs), firmware, Linux, drivers, images, or configuration management.

  • Can design reliable APIs and asynchronous workflows, reasoning about concurrency, consistency, idempotency, and failures across service and provider boundaries.

  • Can diagnose reliability and performance problems across service, operating-system, and machine boundaries, turning production evidence into lasting software improvements.

  • Work effectively across engineering specialties and communicate system behavior and technical tradeoffs clearly.

Bonus points if you:

  • Have built infrastructure control planes that coordinate operations across multiple sites or regions.

  • Have worked with GPU or HPC infrastructure, including topology and shared dependencies across machines, racks, or clusters.

  • Have integrated multiple hardware platforms or infrastructure providers into a common service or resource model.

title: Site Operations Technician
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI's Industrial Compute organization is building the world's most advanced AI infrastructure ecosystem. Working alongside our cloud partners, infrastructure providers, and internal engineering teams, we operate hyperscale AI campuses that support the training and deployment of frontier AI models.

The Site Operations team serves as OpenAI's on-site operational presence, helping ensure campuses operate safely, efficiently, and in alignment with Industrial Compute standards. We work closely with Hardware Operations, Infrastructure Delivery, Network Operations, Security, Facilities, Construction, and our infrastructure partners to support day-to-day site execution and maintain operational readiness.

As Industrial Compute continues to expand globally, Site Operations plays a critical role in ensuring each campus is prepared to support reliable AI infrastructure at scale.

About the Role

We are seeking a Site Operations Technician to support the daily operation of Industrial Compute campuses. This role acts as OpenAI's on-site technical representative, helping coordinate activities across hardware operations, facilities, construction, logistics, security, and external service providers.

You will perform routine site inspections, support asset tracking, coordinate vendor activities, assist with operational readiness, document site conditions, and help ensure infrastructure issues are identified and resolved quickly.

The ideal candidate enjoys working in highly technical environments, is detail-oriented, and thrives in fast-paced operational settings where no two days are the same.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform routine walkthroughs of Industrial Compute facilities to verify operational readiness and identify potential issues.

  • Monitor site conditions and report abnormalities involving hardware spaces, network rooms, utilities, logistics areas, and common infrastructure.

  • Support coordination of vendors, contractors, and partner organizations performing work on-site.

  • Assist with hardware deliveries, inventory movements, asset tracking, and equipment staging.

  • Document operational issues and coordinate follow-up with Hardware Operations, Facilities, Infrastructure Delivery, or external partners.

  • Support physical audits of racks, equipment, inventory, and infrastructure assets.

  • Assist with site access coordination and ensure work activities comply with established operational procedures.

  • Maintain accurate operational documentation, logs, and site records.

  • Participate in operational readiness activities for new deployments, expansions, and infrastructure upgrades.

  • Escalate operational risks that may impact availability, safety, or project schedules.

  • Partner with cross-functional teams to continuously improve operational processes and site execution.

Qualifications

  • Have an Associate's degree, technical certification, military experience, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Have 2+ years supporting data center operations, facilities, hardware operations, manufacturing, industrial operations, or mission-critical infrastructure.

  • Have experience working in technical or operational environments requiring strong attention to detail.

  • Are able to document issues clearly and communicate effectively across technical and non-technical teams.

  • Are comfortable working in active data center or industrial environments.

  • Are able to lift equipment, move hardware, climb ladders, and perform physical work as required.

  • Are willing to work flexible schedules, including occasional evenings or weekends during major deployments.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience supporting hyperscale data centers or cloud infrastructure.

  • Familiarity with server hardware, networking equipment, racks, and structured cabling.

  • Experience using inventory management or asset tracking systems.

  • Knowledge of basic safety procedures for mission-critical facilities.

  • Experience coordinating contractors or external vendors.

  • Familiarity with ticketing systems and operational workflows.

  • OSHA, First Aid, or similar operational certifications are a plus.

title: Product Manager, Native Learning and Credentials
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Customer Education helps customers build the practical skills and confidence to use AI and OpenAI products safely and effectively. We bring together customer insight, learning and enablement expertise, product signals, and measurement to help organizations move from access to durable adoption.

We are exploring how learning, practice, assessment, and evidence of capability can become part of the product experience for people using ChatGPT, Codex, and other OpenAI products at work. Our work focuses on helping people build useful AI skills in the flow of work while giving organizations a clearer view of progress, capability, and readiness.

About the Role

As Product Lead, Native Learning & Credentials, you will define and drive a new product area at the intersection of AI, enterprise learning, assessment, and safe and beneficial use.

This is a senior individual-contributor role for someone who is at their best close to the work. You will take a broad customer and business opportunity and make it concrete: identify the first problem worth solving, define the learner and enterprise journeys, sequence an initial product, and lead the work through engineering alignment, launch, measurement, and iteration. You will work with a small, cross-functional group.

We’re looking for people who combine product depth with GM-level ownership. You should be comfortable moving between customer needs, product strategy, technical architecture, operating design, evidence standards, and business outcomes. You will partner closely with engineering, design, program, learning, and assessment experts, bringing the judgment to make sound tradeoffs while respecting their domain expertise.

The area is early, and the path is not predetermined. Success will come from simplifying ambiguity, shipping focused product proofs, and using evidence to guide investment. If the area earns sustained investment, this role can grow into broader leadership of the product and program over time.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Define the customer, learner, and business problem for Native Learning and Credentials, starting with enterprise adoption and workforce capability.

  • Own the product strategy and roadmap across learning, applied practice, assessment, credential decisions and issuance, learner state, and enterprise reporting.

  • Personally own the product brief, user journeys, requirements, PRDs, roadmap, milestones, non-goals, and decision records that turn an ambiguous opportunity into an executable plan.

  • Partner deeply with engineering and design to define the experience and technical foundations, make architecture and sequencing tradeoffs, and deliver high-quality products.

  • Decide which capabilities OpenAI should build, buy, or access through partners, balancing speed, differentiation, trust, quality, and operational simplicity.

  • Work with learning, assessment, legal, safety, privacy, security, and accessibility partners to establish credible evidence standards and a trustworthy learner experience. Ensure that credential claims are supported by reliable evidence of capability.

  • Establish instrumentation and evaluation across product quality, learner progress, application to real work, adoption, and enterprise value. Use these measures to guide iteration and investment.

  • Create a coherent experience across OpenAI product surfaces and relevant learning, credential, and partner systems, with clear system boundaries and ownership.

  • Remain accountable beyond launch, working with data, support, and operations partners to improve the product, refine the business model, and develop a resource plan grounded in evidence.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have significant product leadership experience in technically complex, user-facing products, including leading a 0-to-1 product from an unclear opportunity through engineering execution, launch, measurement, and meaningful adoption.

  • Have strong technical product judgment across user experience, architecture, services and APIs, identity and state, data, telemetry, evaluation, reliability, and operational readiness.

  • Have personally written or directly owned high-quality product requirements, roadmaps, and technical decision documents.

  • Earn engineers’ trust by defining problems clearly, making sound scope choices, exposing uncertainty, and following through.

  • Have experience building for enterprise or professional users, including the needs of organizational buyers and administrators across reporting, support, security, integrations, and deployment.

  • Communicate clearly across executive, customer, design, engineering, and operational audiences, and lead across organizational boundaries without relying on formal authority.

  • Work effectively with a small team, creating clarity through focused scope, reusable foundations, and an explicit decision cadence.

  • Exercise sound judgment with incomplete information and constrained resources, distinguishing reversible experiments from consequential commitments.

  • Care deeply about the integrity of products that measure or represent human capability and work effectively with learning, assessment, credentialing, and trust experts.

  • Want to build the foundations of a product area and have the range to take on broader program or team leadership as it grows.

Additional experience that would be helpful includes:

  • Building learning, assessment, credentialing, coaching, onboarding, behavior change, developer education, or workforce development products.

  • Building AI or LLM products, agent-assisted workflows, model evaluations, or personalized experiences.

  • Working with identity verification, credential issuance, learning records, skills systems, enterprise integrations, or assessment integrity.

  • Building products that serve both individual users and organizations, or growing a new product area from individual-contributor ownership into broader leadership.
