OpenAI’s mission is to build safe artificial general intelligence (AGI) which benefits all of humanity. This long-term undertaking brings the world’s best scientists, engineers, and business professionals into one lab together to accomplish this.

In pursuit of this mission, our Go To Market (GTM) team is responsible for helping customers learn how to leverage and deploy our highly capable AI products across their business. The team is made of Sales, Solutions, Support, Marketing, and Partnership professionals that work together to create valuable solutions that will help bring AI to as many users as possible.

About the Role

Our Sales team has a unique mission to help customers understand the deep impact that highly capable AI models can bring to their business and users. This role is a mixture of technical understanding, vision, partnership, and value-driven strategy.

You’ll be a key driver of opportunities through the entire sales cycle, from pipeline generation to closure. You’ll work with researchers, engineers, and solution strategists to help customers evolve their industry with AI.

In this role, you will:

  • Manage a small number of complex accounts, developing and executing strategies for a comprehensive account plan

  • Lead our enterprise prospects’ journeys from consideration to successful deployment

  • Partner with solutions and research engineering to build and execute complex customer programs and projects

  • Own a consumption revenue target

  • Manage consumption revenue forecasts

  • Analyze key account metrics to create reports and provide insights to internal and external stakeholders

  • Closely monitor the industry landscape (people, competitors, partners, etc.) to contribute to product roadmap and other corporate strategies

  • Collaborate with solutions, marketing, communications, business operations, people operations, finance, product management, and engineering

  • Support the recruitment and onboarding of other teammates

  • Support the development of company culture

We're seeking someone with experience including:

  • 10+ years selling platform-as-a-service and/or software-as-a-service

  • Achieving revenue targets >$2M per year for more than 3 years

  • Designing and executing complex deal strategies

  • Supporting the growth of fast-growing, high-performance companies

  • Working directly with c-level executives

  • Communicating technical concepts to customers and internal stakeholders

  • Leading high-visibility customer events (CAB, conferences, product launches, etc.)

title: Commissioning Project Lead, Data Center Delivery
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Industrial Compute organization is building the infrastructure required to support the next generation of frontier AI systems. Through a combination of strategic partnerships and self-built data center campuses, we are scaling the power, cooling, electrical, mechanical, and controls infrastructure needed to deliver compute at unprecedented scale.

The Commissioning organization is responsible for ensuring this infrastructure is safely tested, validated, integrated, and transitioned into reliable operations. For our self-build campuses, the team operates through a hybrid delivery model: OpenAI provides commissioning leadership, discipline ownership, governance, and project integration, while commissioning partners provide field and test engineering capacity to support inspections, startup, testing, and turnover.

About the Role

We are seeking a Commissioning Project Lead to own the commissioning strategy and execution for a large-scale, self-build data center project.

You will lead the overall commissioning program from early construction planning through startup, functional testing, integrated systems testing, and final turnover. You will establish the commissioning execution plan, integrate commissioning activities into the master project schedule, coordinate multidisciplinary readiness, and lead the vendor commissioning partners providing field and test engineering capacity.

This role serves as the primary commissioning interface to project leadership, construction management, contractors, equipment vendors, operations, and commissioning partners. You will be responsible for creating clarity across organizations, identifying readiness and schedule risks early, and ensuring the facility progresses through testing and turnover against clearly defined acceptance criteria.

The role will initially support planning and coordination in a hybrid capacity and transition to full-time onsite presence as construction, inspections, startup, testing, and turnover become active.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the project commissioning strategy and execution plan, including scope, governance, acceptance criteria, responsibilities, sequencing, and escalation paths.

  • Lead the hybrid OpenAI and commissioning-partner delivery model, establishing clear RACI ownership, staffing requirements, performance expectations, and issue-management processes.

  • Integrate commissioning into the master project schedule, including construction readiness, energization, equipment startup, functional testing, integrated systems testing, and turnover milestones.

  • Lead commissioning coordination across construction management, contractors, design teams, equipment vendors, operations stakeholders, and field/test engineering teams.

  • Drive multidisciplinary commissioning readiness across electrical, mechanical, controls, and supporting infrastructure, identifying dependencies and resolving blockers before they affect testing.

  • Own visibility into commissioning risks, including schedule constraints, readiness gaps, design and submittal issues, safety constraints, resource bottlenecks, deficiencies, and documentation quality.

  • Coordinate QA/QC inspections and test execution with discipline commissioning leads, contractors, equipment vendors, and commissioning partners.

  • Review commissioning plans, test procedures, readiness checklists, deficiency logs, test reports, turnover packages, and other commissioning deliverables against established acceptance criteria.

  • Provide clear project and executive reporting on commissioning readiness, staffing, test progress, open risks, issue aging, and turnover status.

  • Drive final system acceptance, turnover readiness, closeout, and lessons learned to support a reliable transition from construction into operations.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in commissioning, construction, engineering, technical program management, or project delivery for mission-critical facilities or similarly complex technical infrastructure.

  • Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary commissioning programs through construction readiness, startup, functional performance testing, integrated systems testing, and turnover.

  • Strong working knowledge of electrical and mechanical commissioning workflows, with the ability to coordinate dependencies across power, cooling, controls, and supporting systems.

  • Experience integrating commissioning activities into construction schedules, lookaheads, energization plans, equipment startup sequences, and turnover milestones.

  • Strong owner, contractor, equipment vendor, and commissioning-agent management skills, including the ability to drive accountability across organizations without direct authority.

  • Experience managing commissioning documentation, test procedures, deficiency resolution, issue tracking, acceptance criteria, and quality governance.

  • Ability to identify commissioning and operational-readiness risks early and translate technical issues into actionable schedule and project decisions.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience communicating technical readiness, risk, and recovery plans to senior project leadership.

  • Owner-side commissioning experience and experience establishing or scaling hybrid owner/vendor commissioning delivery models are strongly preferred.

  • Professional credentials such as a PE license, QCxP, CxA, BCxP, CCP, PMP, or other relevant commissioning, engineering, construction, or project management certification are preferred.

Location

This role will support one of OpenAI’s self-build data center campuses in the Savannah, Georgia metro area or Abilene, Texas area. The initial planning and ramp period may operate in a hybrid capacity, with the role transitioning to full-time onsite presence as the project enters active construction, startup, testing, and commissioning.

Travel to project sites, vendor facilities, and other locations may be required based on project needs.

We partner with technical, product and commercial leaders to build the financial foundations for new businesses. Our work spans planning, investment analysis, pricing and operating performance across software and hardware-enabled products.

title: Applied AI Architect, Cyber
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Applied AI Architecture team is responsible for helping developers and enterprises safely and effectively deploy OpenAI technologies in production. We act as trusted technical advisors and thought partners for customers, working side by side with their teams to identify high-value use cases, design practical architectures, and move from prototype to durable deployment.

Cybersecurity is one of the most urgent domains where AI can help. Security teams are under pressure to reason across code, logs, infrastructure, tickets, alerts, and vulnerability data faster than ever. As frontier models become more capable, organizations need deep technical guidance on how to evaluate, validate, and safely deploy AI systems in security-critical workflows.

About the Role

We are looking for a Cybersecurity Applied AI Architect to partner with customers and help them apply OpenAI models, APIs, Codex, and agentic workflows to real cybersecurity use cases. You will work with CISOs, security executives, application security leaders, SOC teams, security engineering teams, and hands-on practitioners to identify where AI can create measurable security outcomes.

This is a customer-facing technical role for someone who can move fluidly between executive strategy, practitioner-level cyber depth, and hands-on solution design. You will help customers evaluate and deploy workflows such as secure code review, vulnerability triage, threat modeling, remediation, SOC and incident response workflows, detection engineering, cloud security, GRC automation, and security validation.

You will collaborate closely with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Engineering, Research, and Security to turn customer needs into safe deployment patterns, reusable field assets, and product feedback.

In this role, you will:

  • Deeply embed with strategic customers as the technical lead for AI-enabled cybersecurity workflows, serving as a trusted partner to both security executives and technical practitioners.

  • Lead discovery across AppSec, DevSecOps, vulnerability management, SOC/IR, detection engineering, red team, cloud security, identity, and GRC automation use cases.

  • Build and deliver customer-facing demos, prototypes, workshops, proofs of concept, and reference architectures using OpenAI APIs, Codex, agents, scripts, CLIs, GitHub workflows, CI/CD systems, logs, tickets, scanners, and common security tools.

  • Translate between CISO-level outcomes and practitioner-level implementation details so each audience understands value, risk, and practical next steps.

  • Create reusable field assets such as demo narratives, playbooks, FAQs, objection handling, qualification guides, assessment templates, and competitive positioning.

  • Validate, synthesize, and deliver high-signal feedback to Product, Engineering, Research, Security, and GTM teams based on recurring customer requirements, blockers, product gaps, and emerging cyber workflows.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 5+ years of technical consulting, solutions engineering, security architecture, cyber advisory, deployment engineering, professional services, or equivalent customer-facing technical experience.

  • Have hands-on experience building prototypes or production systems with APIs, Python or JavaScript, agents, scripts, CLIs, GitHub workflows, CI/CD systems, logs, tickets, scanners, or other common security tooling.

title: Strategic Delivery Lead, Cyber
descriptionHtml:
About the team

The OpenAI for Government team is a dynamic, mission-driven group leveraging frontier AI to transform how governments achieve their missions. Our team works to empower public servants with secure, compliant AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Gov) and mission-aligned deployments that meet government technical requirements with strong reliability and safety.

As part of the OpenAI for Government team you will work across the U.S. national security and cyber ecosystem, helping to accelerate adoption through hands-on support, tailored training, and early insights—so civil servants can spend less time on red tape and more on meaningful work. You will partner with government organizations to identify high-impact opportunities, translate complex cyber mission challenges into AI-enabled solutions, and drive secure deployments that help cyber professionals move faster and operate more effectively. If you're passionate about responsibly deploying frontier AI to uplift public institutions, strengthen cyber resilience, and transform how the government serves the American people, we want you on our team.

 

About the Role

The Strategic Delivery Lead (Cyber) will identify and deliver on some of OpenAI’s most complex and high-impact deployments for the U.S. national security and cyber enterprise. In this role, you will work closely with our national security partners and cyber mission owners to make their hardest problems solvable on the OpenAI Platform API and ChatGPT Enterprise.

The role is highly cross-functional and customer-facing: You’ll partner with Research, Engineering, Go-to-Market, Forward Deployed Engineers, Solutions Architects, security teams, and external stakeholders to align on scope, unblock delivery, and communicate progress at every level, from technical teams to C-suite.

You will own and drive execution of technical delivery workstreams led by internal teams (Forward Deployed Engineers, Researchers, Solutions Architects), ensuring clear problem-framing, crisp milestone definitions, proactive risk identification, rapid issue resolution, and effective translation between business objectives and cyber mission requirements and technical solutions, while consistently communicating clear progress and demonstrating tangible value to national security customers. Accountability for contractual milestones and acceptance criteria sits with you.

This is a high-trust, high-autonomy role. Success requires deep program management expertise, executive presence, experience operating in cyber or national security environments, and a passion for making novel technology deliver real-world value.

 

In this role, you will:

  • Forge and manage strategic partnerships with key national security and cyber mission users to identify and deliver on the most impactful AI and AGI use cases.

  • Serve as the accountable lead for delivering high-impact national security and cyber-focused engagements tied to defined contractual milestones.

  • Act as a key translator between technical teams and business stakeholders, clearly articulating technical progress, risks, requirements, and dependencies in language accessible to both senior executives and technical practitioners.

  • Work with government, defense, industry partners, and academia to identify key concepts for national security AI use including cyber defense, threat intelligence, security operations, incident response, and vulnerability management workflows and then translate them into actionable delivery plans that align technical feasibility with national security impact.

  • Partner deeply with technical teams (FDEs, SAs, Research) to frame complex business and technical problems into actionable, scoped projects, serving as a strategic sounding board and thought leader to guide technical direction, anticipate blockers, and align teams proactively.

  • Establish best practices around milestone tracking, internal coordination, and delivery operations at scale.

  • Build internal consensus across teams with competing priorities, secure commitments from stakeholders you do not manage, and drive complex projects to completion with limited dedicated resources

  • Lead regular progress reviews with national security and cyber stakeholders, ensuring transparency and confidence in delivery.

  • Identify delivery risks early and work cross-functionally to mitigate blockers and maintain program velocity.

  • Navigate ambiguity and evolving requirements with composure, helping internal and external teams stay aligned.

  • Help shape the future of how OpenAI engages with national security and cyber customers through milestone-based delivery programs.

 

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

  • Active U.S. Government TS/SCI clearance, with a strong preference for an active Counterintelligence or Full Scope Polygraph

  • Have 10+ years of experience in cybersecurity, national security consulting, delivery leadership, or senior program management roles, driving complex technical initiatives across cross-functional teams to deliver results for national security missions.

  • Are willing to travel up to 50% and work on-site with national security and cyber customers to build strong relationships and deeply understand their needs.

  • Have experience leading organizational transformation initiatives (AI, digital, or business transformation) directly with national security departments or agencies.

  • Have led complex national security or cyber-focused programs in enterprise SaaS, AI/ML, consulting, cybersecurity, or transformation environments.

  • Have a proven track record influencing and shaping customer decision-making at executive/board level and the ability to drive clarity, accountability, and alignment at senior levels.

  • Demonstrated experience delivering outcomes in lean, fast-moving environments by influencing without authority, making thoughtful tradeoffs, and mobilizing cross-functional teams around the highest-priority work.

  • Strong track record of execution in delivering ambitious goals on complex cross-functional projects.

  • Prior experience managing large scale AI/ML or enterprise API-based deployments.

  • Are passionate about how AI and AGI can enhance the national security mission and strengthen cyber capabilities.

  • Thrive in extremely ambiguous, fast-moving environments and can create clarity and momentum where none yet exists.

title: Software Engineer, Build Systems / CI
descriptionHtml:
About the Role

The Engineering Acceleration team builds and operates the foundational systems that engineers use to build, test, and ship ChatGPT, the API, and OpenAI's infrastructure.

We are looking for an engineer to help evolve OpenAI's build and continuous integration systems for a fast-growing engineering organization. This role sits at the intersection of developer productivity, build systems, distributed infrastructure, and software quality. You will work on the systems that determine how quickly and confidently engineers can move: Bazel-based builds, Buildkite pipelines, test selection, remote caching and execution, CI observability, and tooling that helps engineers understand and fix failures quickly.

Our mission is to make OpenAI one of the most productive engineering organizations in the world while preserving a high bar for correctness, reliability, and safety. The best version of this work is invisible when it succeeds: builds are fast, tests are trusted, CI failures are understandable, and engineers can focus on shipping useful systems instead of fighting infrastructure.

In This Role, You Will

  • Own and evolve Bazel-based build and test workflows across a large, polyglot monorepo.

  • Design and maintain Starlark rules, macros, toolchains, and integrations that make builds reproducible, hermetic, and easy for product teams to adopt.

  • Improve CI performance and reliability across Buildkite pipelines, including queue time, build time, cache hit rates, test sharding, retry behavior, and flake isolation.

  • Build systems that reduce unnecessary CI work through affected-target detection, dependency graph analysis, test selection, caching, batching, and smarter scheduling.

  • Improve local development workflows so engineers can reproduce CI behavior, debug build failures, and iterate quickly without learning every detail of the build stack.

  • Operate and optimize build infrastructure across Docker/OCI images, Kubernetes-based runners, cloud resources, and remote cache/execution systems.

  • Instrument build and CI systems with metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, and analytics so we can measure speed, reliability, cost, and developer impact.

  • Partner directly with product, infrastructure, and research engineering teams to understand pain points, onboard projects, debug hard build issues, and remove systemic bottlenecks.

  • Use modern AI tools to rethink CI failure analysis, flaky test debugging, PR triage, automatic remediation, and developer-facing explanations.

  • Own the reliability of the systems you build, including participating in an on-call rotation for critical developer infrastructure.

Technologies Commonly Used In This Environment Include

  • Bazel and Starlark for build and test workflows

  • Buildkite for CI orchestration

  • Docker and OCI images for build and runtime packaging

  • Kubernetes for CI runners and infrastructure orchestration

  • Python, Go, TypeScript, Rust, C++, and other languages in a large monorepo

  • Terraform for infrastructure as code

  • Remote caching, remote execution, artifact storage, and build telemetry systems

  • Postgres, Kafka, and internal services used to power engineering platforms

You May Be A Strong Fit If You

  • Have 5+ years of software engineering experience, including significant experience building infrastructure or tooling for developers.

  • Have hands-on experience with Bazel, Buck, Pants, Gradle, or similar build systems, and understand the tradeoffs of hermetic builds, dependency graphs, caching, sandboxing, and remote execution.

  • Have built or operated CI systems at scale, especially in environments where build time, queue time, test flakiness, and developer trust materially affect engineering velocity.

  • Are comfortable writing production software for internal platforms, not just configuring tools. We expect this role to involve code, design, debugging, operations, and long-term ownership.

  • Can debug distributed build and CI failures across source control, dependency management, containers, runners, remote caches, test frameworks, and service infrastructure.

  • Care deeply about developer experience and have empathy for the small sources of friction that slow teams down or create operational toil.

  • Are pragmatic about platform adoption: you know how to build paved paths that teams want to use because they are faster, clearer, and more reliable.

  • Communicate clearly across teams and can turn ambiguous productivity problems into concrete technical plans.

  • Are excited to apply AI to developer infrastructure in ways that make engineers faster without weakening quality, reliability, or safety.

descriptionHtml:
About the team

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team partners with global pharma and biotech, CROs, and research institutions to deploy existing expertise across the R&D value chain to help customers design and ship production-grade AI systems. We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development, converting early deployments into repeatable system standards and evaluation practices that scale across regulated environments.

About the role

We are hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to push the frontier on what is possible today across drug discovery (e.g., target identification, molecular design, pre-clinical) and development (e.g., trial design, trial ops, biostats) by leading end-to-end deployments of our models inside life sciences organizations and research institutions. You will work with customers who are deep experts in their scientific or operational domains, translating real-world data, infrastructure, and constraints into production systems.

You will measure success through production adoption, measurable workflow impact, and eval-driven feedback loops, including evaluation benchmarks and acceptance criteria, that inform product and model roadmaps. You’ll work closely with our Product, Research, Partnerships, GRC, Security, and GTM to deliver in regulated contexts, including inspection readiness with audit trails and traceable evidence.

This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and ship production systems around models, owning integrations, data provenance, reliability, and on-call readiness across research, clinical, and operational workflows.

Safety Systems manages the complete lifecycle of safety efforts for OpenAI’s frontier models, ensuring our models are deployed responsibly and have a positive impact on society. title: Growth Marketing Manager, B2B SEO & AEO
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Growth team drives adoption and revenue for ChatGPT. This role focuses on B2B and small-business growth: helping business owners, functional leaders, and teams discover how ChatGPT can solve their work challenges and deliver value. We partner across product, engineering, product marketing, content, design, and analytics to turn customer insights and disciplined experimentation into sustainable growth.

About the Role

We are seeking a growth marketer with deep expertise in search engine optimization (SEO) and a strong experimental approach to answer engine optimization (AEO) to grow ChatGPT adoption among small businesses. You will own the strategy and execution for reaching business buyers through organic search and AI-powered answers, connecting discovery to evaluation, workspace creation, and paid adoption.

You will build an organic acquisition program around how small businesses research problems, compare solutions, and choose tools for their teams. Your remit spans technical SEO, search and question research, content strategy, and AEO experimentation. You will partner with SMB Product Marketing and Content Marketing to translate business use cases, industry needs, and customer proof into useful discovery experiences, and with Web Growth to improve the path from organic discovery to conversion.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the B2B / SMB SEO and AEO roadmap, prioritizing opportunities by business audience, use case, industry, buying intent, and potential contribution to customer acquisition and revenue.

  • Lead keyword, question, and audience research across the small-business buying journey—from identifying a business problem to comparing solutions and evaluating pricing, team adoption, and business requirements. Translate findings into prioritized content briefs and page opportunities.

  • Own the technical SEO roadmap with web and engineering partners, including crawlability, indexing, rendering, site architecture, internal linking, structured data, and migration readiness. Build durable foundations for discovering and understanding our business content.

  • Develop and test AEO approaches that help business buyers find accurate, useful information about ChatGPT in AI-powered search and answer experiences. Improve answer-focused content, product information, and supporting evidence; track visibility, citations, and referral quality while distinguishing observed results from hypotheses.

  • Partner with SMB Product Marketing and Content Marketing on use-case and industry pages, comparison and evaluation content, practical guides, and customer stories. Bring search insights and clear briefs; maintain accuracy, originality, and usefulness as the program scales.

  • Build measurement with Analytics that connects organic discovery to qualified business traffic, workspace creation, activation, paid conversion, and revenue. Segment performance by intent, audience, and market, and use experiments and cohort analysis to assess impact and attribution limits.

  • Partner with Web Growth, Design, and Product on landing-page and conversion experiments that help business visitors take the right next step. Align messaging, proof points, calls to action, and onward journeys with buyer intent, then evaluate downstream customer quality.

  • Build AI-assisted workflows for research, briefing, content refreshes, technical audits, and reporting, with human review and quality controls. Use programmatic approaches where they create distinct value for business audiences.

  • Coordinate execution across engineering, product marketing, content, web, and analytics partners. Establish a regular testing and learning cadence, and partner on localization to expand proven SEO and AEO approaches into priority markets.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 10+ years in SEO or growth marketing, with a track record of growing qualified organic acquisition for B2B software or products serving small businesses. Experience with self-serve or product-led business acquisition is especially relevant.

  • Deep technical SEO expertise, including site architecture, crawling and indexing, structured data, migrations, and internal linking, combined with strong judgment about search intent and content quality.

  • Hands-on experience testing visibility in AI-powered search and answer experiences. You can design an AEO measurement approach, evaluate citations and referrals, and explain what the evidence does—and does not—show.

  • A strong understanding of small-business buyers and how their needs vary by role, company size, and industry. You can turn customer problems, solution comparisons, and buying questions into a focused organic growth strategy.

  • Strong collaboration with product marketing, content, engineering, design, web growth, and analytics teams. You can turn insights into clear briefs, prioritize shared roadmaps, and take initiatives through launch and iteration.

  • Strong analytical and experimentation skills, including search and web analytics, funnel and cohort analysis, and landing-page testing. You connect traffic and visibility to activation, paid adoption, and revenue rather than optimizing for rankings alone.

  • Hands-on experience publishing, refreshing, and measuring content through a CMS, including landing pages, reusable templates, and localized experiences. You are comfortable moving between strategic planning, technical audits, and page-level QA.

  • Experience using AI-assisted workflows and programmatic SEO to improve execution while preserving factual accuracy, original value, and a high-quality customer experience.

  • A test-and-learn mindset, clear communication, and comfort operating in a fast-changing environment. You balance curiosity about new discovery channels with disciplined prioritization and measurement.

title: Dedicated Support Engineer - London
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s User Operations team shepherds our customers’ adoption of AI and ensures that our customers' product experience is nothing short of exceptional. We are building the very first post-AGI support team. We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others, to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises.

About the Role

The Support Engineering team works closely with Engineering, Product, Technical Success, Go-to-Market, and other teams to deliver an exceptional experience for our most strategic customers. We combine deep technical troubleshooting with durable customer context, proactive reliability work, and clear ownership during critical moments. We use automation, agents, and our own technology to help build the future of technical support.

We’re looking for experienced, deeply curious technical problem-solvers to serve as trusted support partners for our Premium Support customers. You’ll work directly with customers on novel, ambiguous, and high-impact technical issues, using logs, telemetry, reproduction, and systems-level investigation to isolate causes and drive issues toward resolution.

Beyond resolving individual issues, you’ll use your deep understanding of OpenAI’s infrastructure and products, together with each customer’s architecture and operating context, to anticipate risk and make their workloads more resilient over time. You’ll proactively monitor integrations, identify emerging failure patterns and architectural breakpoints, and work with customers and internal teams to address them before they become incidents. Success means that as a customer’s workloads mature and scale, the day-to-day effort required to support them decreases through better monitoring, runbooks, automation, and preventative improvements.

In this role, you will:

  • Work directly with Premium Support customers to troubleshoot their most complex technical issues, including API failures, integration challenges, authentication errors, unexpected product behavior, performance degradation, and production incidents.

  • Provide end-to-end technical ownership by analyzing logs and system behavior, reproducing errors, testing hypotheses, and isolating the likely failure domain. Where possible, you’ll identify the root cause before escalating to Engineering; where that is not possible, you’ll provide a clear hypothesis and the evidence needed to accelerate Engineering’s investigation.

  • Become a trusted expert on OpenAI’s products and systems, serving as a critical escalation point and a technical backstop for our most strategic customers.

  • Own the customer-specific response to high-impact incidents. You’ll assess severity and business impact, initiate the appropriate response path, coordinate cross-functional responders, maintain clear ownership, and ensure issues move through mitigation, resolution, and post-incident follow-through.

  • Communicate clearly and proactively during periods of uncertainty, providing accurate updates to customer technical teams, business stakeholders, executives, and internal partners.

  • Develop a detailed understanding of each customer’s architecture, integrations, dependencies, critical workloads, and operational constraints. You’ll document this context and make it accessible to Support, Product, and Engineering teams.

  • Partner with Go-to-Market and Technical Success teams to understand the business importance of customer workloads and ensure that relevant commercial context informs severity, prioritization, and communication without bypassing established support processes.

  • Represent Support Engineering in relevant customer meetings, including QBRs, and partner closely with account teams to communicate technical health, surface risks and blockers early, coordinate follow-up, and provide customers and internal stakeholders with clear, proactive updates.

  • Monitor customer integrations and support trends to identify emerging risks, recurring failure patterns, and readiness gaps before they become major escalations.

  • Prepare for important launches, migrations, traffic increases, and business events by developing account-specific runbooks, validating escalation paths, coordinating support readiness, and providing heightened monitoring where needed.

  • Lead or contribute to incident reviews and postmortems, identify opportunities to prevent recurrence, and track corrective actions through closure.

  • Translate recurring customer pain into clear, evidence-backed feedback for Product and Engineering, with a particular focus on improving the reliability and performance of existing products, integrations, and deployments.

  • Turn what you learn from customer investigations into scalable improvements, including troubleshooting guides, monitoring, internal tooling, support workflows, and AI-powered automation.

  • Help shape the operating model, technical standards, and tooling for Premium Support as the function grows globally.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have significant experience in Support Engineering, Solutions Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or another role involving hands-on diagnosis of complex production issues.

  • Have expert-level troubleshooting skills and a strong track record of resolving ambiguous technical problems across APIs, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise integrations.

  • Are comfortable working with logs, metrics, traces, API requests, authentication flows, and customer-provided code or configurations to understand system behavior and test hypotheses.

  • Have experience leading or playing a central role in customer-impacting incidents, including severity assessment, technical coordination, stakeholder communication, root-cause analysis, and post-incident follow-through.

  • Can write code or scripts to reproduce issues, interrogate systems, automate repetitive work, and improve internal tools. Experience with Python, JavaScript, or similar languages is valuable.

  • Can communicate complex technical issues clearly to engineers, customer technical teams, business stakeholders, and senior leaders—especially when information is incomplete or evolving.

  • Build strong, high-trust relationships with customers and cross-functional partners while maintaining clear and scalable ownership boundaries.

  • Look beyond the immediate issue to identify patterns, improve the system, and prevent the same problem from recurring.

  • Thrive in ambiguity, update quickly as new information emerges, and are willing to learn whatever is needed to get the job done.

  • Bring a humble, team-first mindset, strong judgment, and a genuine eagerness to help both customers and colleagues succeed.

  • Are excited to use OpenAI’s products, agents, and emerging AI capabilities to transform how technical support operates at scale.

We work across Sales, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Product, Marketing, Operations, and partner organisations to turn strategic partnerships into measurable customer and commercial outcomes.

About the Role

We are hiring a Partnerships Lead, Southern Europe to lead our partner sales and development team for Southern EMEA. Reporting to the Head of GTM Partnerships, Europe you will manage and develop a regional team, own the regional partner business, and work alongside OpenAI Sales leadership and strategic partners to generate pipeline, advance complex pursuits, and drive revenue and customer adoption.

This is a people management role that combines team leadership, partner business development, co-sell execution, and operational discipline. You will translate broader partnership priorities into a focused regional plan, set team goals and account coverage, and coach your team to engage the right partners at the right point in the customer journey. You will build relationships with partner field leaders and remain hands-on in priority pursuits, working with technical and delivery teams to turn commercial commitments into sustained customer value.

You will be accountable for both regional business performance and the success of your team. We are looking for an experienced people manager who can hire and develop talent, establish clear expectations, manage performance, and build a culture of accountability, collaboration, and customer focus.

title: Client Platform Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Client Platform Engineering team builds and operates the platforms that make employee devices secure, reliable, and easy to use. Our work spans device posture and trust, onboarding, application delivery, operating-system updates, fleet telemetry, and employee-facing remediation. We partner with Security, IT, Research, Applied, and specialized engineering teams to reduce friction while protecting OpenAI’s systems and data.

About the Role

As a Client Platform Engineer, You will build and own agentic solutions that automate OAI fleet operations and reduce employee friction, with measurable outcomes and reliability. You will develop first-party software, integrate commercial and open-source tools, and own changes from design and testing through deployment and production operations. Your work will improve security, reliability, and the employee experience.

We’re looking for people who are passionate about automation, endpoint security, and building scalable solutions that improve employee experience. You should have deep experience securing and managing heterogeneous fleets at scale, with strong software engineering skills to automate security controls and fleet operations across environments with different compliance requirements. Your problem-solving mindset and attention to detail will be key to success in this role.

In this role, you will:

Build the platforms that help employees do their best work on devices they can trust.

  • Own the design, development, deployment, and operation of secure endpoint management systems across environments with different compliance requirements.

  • Create magical employee experiences by building agentic workflows with OpenAI products and models that use fleet telemetry to anticipate issues, guide remediation, and design friction out of everyday work.

  • Make new hires productive from day one, using OpenAI products to simplify device setup, software delivery, and onboarding support.

  • Build secure, reliable workflows with scoped access, human review for sensitive changes, traceable actions, and tested recovery.

  • Partner with IT, Security, Research, and Engineering to deliver consistent provisioning, updates, and support across our heterogeneous fleet.

  • Develop first-party software and integrate commercial and open-source tools for software packaging, deployment, and application management.

  • Manage fleet configuration as code through GitOps, version control, peer review, and automated validation.

  • Build and operate CI/CD pipelines for fleet infrastructure across Azure, AWS, and GCP, with staged deployments and tested rollback.

  • Use fleet telemetry to proactively improve performance and reliability, detect configuration drift, and verify deployment outcomes.

  • Participate in engineering on-call, own incident resolution, and turn operational lessons into lasting improvements that reduce recurring failures and manual work.

You may be a fit for this role if you have: 

  • Built, shipped, and operated production software or automation for an endpoint fleet using Python, Go, or another modern programming language.

  • Managed and secured an endpoint fleet at scale, with deep experience in at least one operating system and hands-on work in areas such as enrollment, policy enforcement, software delivery, OS updates, or device trust.

  • Demonstrated success with open-source endpoint tools for configuration, device and application management, and telemetry.

  • Rolled out fleet changes safely using version-controlled configuration, automated testing, staged deployments, and tested rollback. Used telemetry to verify changes and diagnose failures.

  • Deep experience managing infrastructure at scale with IaC and GitOps, using tools such as Terraform, Ansible, and Chef.

  • Experience integrating and operating fleet infrastructure with CI/CD and DevOps workflows.

  • Operated infrastructure that supports endpoint management in at least one public cloud, such as Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud.

  • Familiarity with compliance frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, and NIST.

  • Initiative, analytical judgment, and the ability to turn problems into practical improvements.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s B2B Marketing team helps businesses understand, adopt, and get value from our products. We work across Product Marketing, Partnerships, Sales, Product, Engineering, Communications, and Marketing to connect advances in AI with the problems organizations are trying to solve.

We’re building our partner marketing function as OpenAI’s products and ecosystem evolve. Our work starts with understanding what OpenAI and our partners can build together, where those solutions solve meaningful customer problems, and how to bring them to market.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Partner Marketing Manager to own go-to-market strategy and execution with strategic technology partners and independent software vendors (ISVs). You’ll bring a product marketer’s approach to the work. You’ll get hands-on with OpenAI’s products and partner integrations, learn how shared customers work, and develop a clear point of view on where the combined solution offers differentiated value.

You’ll turn that work into joint positioning, launch plans, demos, customer stories, campaigns, and sales enablement. You’ll work with OpenAI’s Product Marketing teams to extend our core product narratives into partner-specific use cases, and with Partnerships and your counterparts at partner companies to agree on priorities, coordinate execution, and measure results.

title: Research Program Manager, Frontier Assurance
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Frontier Assurance team brings independent scrutiny into OpenAI’s safety decisions and helps the public understand and assess our safety work. We lead third-party assessments and safeguard testing for OpenAI’s flagship launches, pilot new assurance mechanisms such as embedded auditing, run our misalignment disclosure process, and incorporate independent expert input as evidence for critical safety decisions.

About the Role

As a Research Program Manager on the Frontier Assurance team, you will build programs that bring independent expertise into frontier AI safety decisions and make the evidence behind those decisions understandable to the public. You will lead external research partnerships and third-party assessments, coordinate public safety documentation, and develop new approaches to independent scrutiny and transparency. Working across research, engineering, product, policy, and communications, you will help ensure external findings inform concrete decisions and that our public explanations accurately reflect the evidence, limitations, and remaining uncertainty.

We’re looking for people with deep experience in research partnerships and program management with technical and research teams. This role combines partnership management, cross-functional coordination, an understanding of AI safety research, alignment, and evaluations, and strong communication skills. You will work with researchers and engineers within OpenAI and across the external community to initiate projects, set ambitious goals and milestones, and drive execution across multiple teams.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and run third-party assessment programs for frontier models and safeguards, including independent evaluations, adversarial testing, and new approaches such as embedded auditing. Work with researchers and external partners to define assessment questions, scope, access, timelines, and deliverables.

  • Build and manage strategic research partnerships with third-party evaluators, academic labs, and other independent experts, prioritizing expertise, independence, and diversity of perspectives. Enable rigorous research, including work that challenges internal assumptions.

  • Bring external findings to safety decision-makers and translate them into actionable recommendations for safeguards, deployment, product, and policy. Track follow-up actions and ensure partners understand how their input was considered.

  • Partner with research, product, policy, and communications teams to explain the evidence behind OpenAI’s safety approach: what we tested, what we learned, how findings shaped safeguards and deployment decisions, and where limitations and uncertainty remain. Translate complex technical results into accurate, accessible communication for expert and public audiences.

  • Lead public transparency programs, including system cards, summaries of third-party assessments, and updates on significant findings and follow-up actions. Develop approaches to sharing methods, results, and limitations while protecting privacy, security, and sensitive information.

  • Create channels for researchers and civil society to ask questions, provide feedback, and inform future assessments and transparency efforts, including beyond individual launches.

  • Own program goals, milestones, dependencies, and risks across assessment and transparency work, keeping internal and external stakeholders informed and resolving obstacles to execution.

You might thrive in this role if you: 

  • Have an understanding of AI evaluations and measurement, and can engage with technical teams on evaluation design and results.

  • Can interpret evaluation findings and communicate what they do and do not establish, including methodological limitations, uncertainty, and disagreement.

  • Have experience building research partnerships and managing external stakeholders, especially academic researchers and independent experts.

  • Can synthesize technical and social science research into clear executive summaries and accessible explanations for public audiences.

  • Have experience delivering technical publications or public reports across multiple contributors, and exercising judgment about what to share, with whom, and when.

  • Have worked cross-functionally across product, research, and engineering teams and can coordinate complex programs with policy and communications partners.

  • Have an understanding of and interest in frontier AI safety and policy.

title: Robotics Test Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.

About the Role

As a Test Engineer on the Robotics team, you will help shape the next generation of embodied AI. You’ll design and run rigorous, exploratory and requirements-driven tests—building custom test equipment, analyzing results, and translating findings into actionable insights that drive design breakthroughs and mitigate risks across hardware and software. This role offers the opportunity to directly influence how our AI scales beyond simulation, ensuring that every design, test, and iteration brings us closer to truly adaptive, versatile robotic systems.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and build custom test benches to evaluate system performance under realistic operating conditions; proficient in CAD and familiar with GD&T.

  • Analyze and interpret test data to identify trends, anomalies, and root causes.

  • Develop and maintain comprehensive test plans that validate mechanical performance against product requirements.

  • Execute validation and verification testing, capturing both quantitative and qualitative data with high fidelity.

  • Author clear, actionable test reports that summarize results, highlight risks, and recommend design or process changes.

  • Partner with engineering, product, and leadership teams to inform design iterations and strategic decisions.

  • Design and execute compliance and regulatory testing campaigns, informing in-house vs 3rd party testing strategy

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have strong intuition for mechanical and electromechanical systems and how they fail, degrade, or vary in real-world operation.

  • Enjoy hands-on lab work designing, instrumenting, operating, and debugging test equipment and robotic hardware.

  • Can turn evolving requirements and ambiguous failures into repeatable tests, trustworthy data, and clear engineering decisions.

  • Balance rigorous validation, safety, and traceability with rapid hardware iteration.

  • Communicate clearly across mechanical, electrical, software, controls, and manufacturing teams, and build alignment on risks and corrective actions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in hardware testing or validation, including at least 2 years working with robotics hardware components and systems.

  • Bachelor’s or graduate degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Experience designing test fixtures and stands using CAD, engineering drawings, and GD&T.

  • Hands-on experience integrating sensors, instrumentation, and data acquisition (DAQ) systems, including calibration and measurement traceability.

  • Experience developing automated or hardware-in-the-loop tests using Python, C/C++, or AI coding tools for test execution, data collection, and analysis.

  • Experience designing reliability, accelerated life, environmental, and hardware qualification tests for robotic or electromechanical systems.

  • Experience supporting EVT, DVT, PVT, pilot production, or sustaining hardware validation.

  • Experience using root cause analysis, FMEA, or FEA to guide design improvements.

  • Experience executing product standards compliance certification campaigns.

title: B2B Marketing Manager, DACH
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Like every team at OpenAI, the Marketing team contributes directly to our mission of responsible and widespread AI adoption.

The EMEA B2B Marketing team translates global priorities into regionally relevant programs that drive awareness, consideration, pipeline, adoption, and long-term customer trust. We partner closely with Sales and GTM, Product Marketing, Field and Executive Marketing, Content, Customer Marketing, Partner Marketing, Comms, Events, Marketing Operations, and regional leadership.

DACH is one of OpenAI’s most important markets in EMEA. Our opportunity spans major enterprises and digital natives, ambitious startups, developers, partners, and a highly influential business community navigating the adoption of AI.

About the Role

As the B2B Marketing Manager for DACH, you will own the integrated B2B marketing strategy and execution for Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

You will be a close commercial partner to local Sales and GTM leadership, translating market insight, revenue priorities, target-account needs, and global launches into locally relevant programs that create pipeline, accelerate complex opportunities, deepen customer relationships, and grow adoption.

You will carry clear pipeline goals and be accountable for Marketing’s measurable contribution to commercial outcomes in DACH. These goals will be established through the regional planning process and will evolve with the priorities and maturity of the market. You will be expected to understand the pipeline, make informed investment decisions, and demonstrate how marketing activity creates, influences, or accelerates revenue opportunities.

This is a generalist role spanning field and executive marketing, demand generation, account-based programs, content, customer marketing, partnerships, events, and product launches. You will bring these channels together into a focused DACH B2B plan, drawing on specialist capabilities within the EMEA B2B Marketing team in London and global Marketing teams. A particularly important partnership will be with the DACH Consumer Marketing Lead: together, you will align market strategy, narratives, launches, audience priorities, channels, and major moments so B2B and B2C activity is coordinated, complementary, and mutually reinforcing.

Close partnership with Marketing Operations will be crucial. Together, you will establish campaign infrastructure, audience and account segmentation, attribution, reporting, and operating rhythms that give Sales and Marketing a reliable view of performance and inform where the team should invest next.

The role requires someone who can move comfortably between strategy and execution: shaping the market plan, participating in pipeline reviews, developing a priority-account program, adapting a global campaign, briefing an agency, supporting an executive event, and personally unblocking delivery when needed.

This role is preferably based in Munich. Berlin may be considered for an exceptional candidate. Regular travel within DACH and to London will be required.

In this role, you will:

  • Own and execute the integrated DACH B2B marketing plan, aligned with regional priorities, local revenue goals, market opportunities, and customer needs. Partner closely with the DACH Consumer Marketing Lead to ensure B2B and B2C strategies and activities are coordinated and complementary, while retaining clear accountability for B2B pipeline and revenue outcomes.

  • Develop locally relevant customer stories and advocacy opportunities in partnership with Sales, Customer Success, Customer Marketing, Comms, and senior customer stakeholders.

  • Build joint programs with strategic technology, consulting, and implementation partners where they can extend reach, strengthen customer value, or contribute to pipeline.

  • Own the operating rhythm for DACH B2B marketing, including planning, budget management, agency coordination, campaign pacing, performance reporting, and prioritisation.

  • Build repeatable playbooks and share market learning across EMEA, helping the wider organisation understand what resonates with DACH customers and decision-makers.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 12+ years of experience in integrated B2B, regional, field, demand generation, or account-based marketing, ideally in enterprise technology, cloud, AI, or SaaS.

We partner closely with Sales, Finance, Enablement, Data, Growth Strategy, and Systems teams to improve business execution, accelerate growth, and operationalize key go-to-market initiatives across the Enterprise organization.

You will partner closely with Enterprise Sales leadership and the GTM Strategy & Operations, Enterprise Lead to support strategic planning, improve business execution, and help operationalize key GTM initiatives across the Enterprise organization.

You’ll help manage core sales cadences, analyze business performance, and drive cross-functional initiatives that improve efficiency and accelerate growth. title: Trusted Access Lead, Critical Harm Operations
descriptionHtml:
About the team

Trusted Access helps eligible customers access and use advanced AI capabilities with appropriate safeguards. Within User Safety & Risk Operations, we connect customer onboarding, eligibility review, access provisioning, and support into a service customers can navigate with confidence.

We work with Product, Engineering, technical support, regional operations, and customer-facing teams to resolve difficult access problems and improve the systems behind them. Our work combines sound judgment on individual cases with better products, clearer guidance, and automation that reduces unnecessary friction.

About the role

We’re looking for a senior operations leader to own the Trusted Access operating strategy and lead a team of risk-operations specialists. You will set priorities across programs, build a reliable customer access service, and hire, manage, and develop your direct reports.

This role combines program ownership with formal people management. You will establish shared commitments with technical support and regional escalation leaders, who manage their own teams, and bring those groups together around customer outcomes. You’ll stay close enough to complex cases to challenge assumptions while giving specialists the ownership and capacity to fix recurring problems.

Success means customers reach the right access outcome with clear communication, teams make consistent decisions, and the service scales with less avoidable escalation and manual work.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the operating strategy and roadmap across Trusted Access programs, translating customer needs and organizational priorities into clear service commitments, ownership, and investment decisions.

  • Build a coherent customer journey from application and eligibility review through approval, provisioning coordination, and confirmed access, including appeals and subsequent access changes. Establish clear handoffs and route exceptions to authorized decision-makers.

  • Hire, coach, and develop your team. Set expectations, delegate meaningful ownership, give direct feedback, address performance gaps, and build the capabilities needed as programs grow.

  • Make capacity and prioritization decisions across urgent customer needs, launch readiness, and lasting improvements. Coordinate regional coverage, vendor support, and backup with partner teams while protecting time to eliminate recurring work.

  • Lead consequential customer escalations, bringing incomplete or conflicting evidence into a clear decision process. Align owners on the next action and ensure customers receive accurate updates and a clear resolution.

  • Turn support patterns into a prioritized roadmap with Product and Engineering: improve onboarding, provisioning workflows, tooling, self-service, and AI-assisted operations. Validate that changes work before expanding them.

  • Establish measures of service health and decision quality. Distinguish fast responses from actual resolution, investigate persistent delays, and use evidence to change priorities.

  • Prepare new programs and customer channels for launch and scale. Align support responsibilities, review standards, customer guidance, and technical dependencies; make readiness gaps and tradeoffs clear to leadership.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have built and run complex customer support, onboarding, access, risk, or service operations, with measurable improvements beyond handling more volume.

  • Have formally managed people through hiring, development, difficult feedback, and performance decisions, and can show how your leadership increased the team’s capability and ownership. 5+ years of management experience preferred.

  • Can make defensible tradeoffs among customer commitments, safeguards, service quality, and capacity, even when stakeholders disagree or the evidence is incomplete.

title: Researcher, Cyber Safety Training
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Safety Research at OpenAI is responsible for ensuring our most capable models can be safely deployed in the real world. The Safety Training team develops the research and engineering methods that shape model behavior through post-training, reinforcement learning, evaluation, and deployment feedback.

Our work focuses on making models helpful, reliable, and aligned with safety policies across model types, modalities, and product surfaces. We work across both longer-term safety research and the core post-training work needed to improve production models.

About the Role

You’ll work directly on the large training runs that shape OpenAI’s frontier models. Your focus will be teaching models to help people do legitimate security work while recognizing when their assistance could enable harm. A model that refuses to help a defender investigate a security issue can fail in a different way from one that helps someone misuse it. You’ll study both kinds of mistakes and use what you learn to improve the next training run.

We’re looking for someone with hands-on machine learning experience who wants to bring security judgment into model training. You might come from cybersecurity and want to go deeper on post-training, or from reinforcement learning and want to build substantial expertise in cybersecurity.

In this role, you will

  • Work with cybersecurity researchers to identify situations where context changes what help a model should give.

  • Design complex and realistic cyber safety evaluations.

  • Research post-training techniques that robustly improves the cyber safety of the frontier models.

  • Work with the core post-training team to bring promising methods into large model runs and verify that the safety improvements hold at scale.

  • Coordinate and collaborate with cross-functional teams, including T&S, legal, policy and other research teams, to ensure that our products meet the highest safety standards.

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Have trained or fine-tuned models yourself and can describe an experiment where you used the results to change how you trained the next model.

  • Bring practical security judgment from industry work, a research project, collaboration with a security team, or capture-the-flag competitions. We also welcome reinforcement learning practitioners motivated to develop that judgment alongside security researchers.

  • Can build and debug the code behind a training experiment, from preparing data to checking whether a change in the results reflects a real change in model behavior.

  • Enjoy working through ambiguous cases with domain experts and translating what you learn into concrete decisions about how a model should respond.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI Finance ensures the organization is positioned for long-term success as we pursue our mission. The Revenue team plays a critical role in enabling OpenAI to scale commercial offerings by overseeing billing operations, deal desk, revenue systems, revenue accounting, and controllership. We work cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Go-To-Market, Tax, Legal, and Technical Accounting to support new monetization strategies, improve operational efficiency, and maintain financial integrity as the business grows.

About the Role

This senior leader will own key elements of Ads revenue accounting from technical assessment through operational execution. The role will guide accounting for products, pricing, contracts, incentives, credits, refunds, makegoods, international expansion, and new go-to-market motions. It will establish governance and translate approved accounting positions into launch, billing, data, close, reconciliation, and control requirements. Success requires deep technical revenue expertise, strong business partnership, and the ability to build durable 0-to-1 processes in a fast-changing environment.

Advertising is a critical and growing monetization vector for OpenAI, and this role will help shape the financial foundations that enable Ads to scale responsibly and transparently.

This role can be based in San Francisco or New York City. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead technical accounting assessments for Ads products and commercial arrangements, including performance obligations, variable consideration, allocation, principal-versus-agent, collectibility, contract modifications, refunds, incentives, credits, makegoods, and revenue presentation.

  • Own and continuously evolve Ads revenue accounting policies and operating guidance as product behavior, pricing, contracting, incentive programs, and billing models change.

  • Establish governance for new products and accounting decisions, including intake, decision rights, materiality and escalation thresholds, launch approvals, policy versioning, decision logs, and post-launch monitoring.

  • Translate accounting conclusions into clear requirements for product design, contracting, billing, data, estimates, close, reconciliations, controls, and reporting.

  • Use data, AI, and automation to improve research, monitoring, policy maintenance, issue tracking, documentation, and repeatable Finance workflows with appropriate review controls.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Track record building 0-to-1 accounting processes, governance, close mechanisms, reconciliations, and controls that scale.

title: Applied AI Engineer, Codex
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. For software engineering organizations, this means helping customers adopt Codex and other OpenAI capabilities across the software development lifecycle—transforming how teams plan, build, test, review, and deliver software.

We work directly with engineering leaders and hands-on developers to identify high-value opportunities, design and implement AI-powered development workflows, and scale what works across engineering organizations. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products, reusable architectures, and technical patterns that help developers everywhere get more value from Codex.

About the Role

As an Applied AI Engineer focused on Codex, you will partner directly with leading engineering organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that transform how software is developed. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from workflow and use-case selection through prototyping, evaluation, production rollout, and scaled adoption.

You will work alongside engineering teams to build advanced AI coding workflows, integrations, automations, and evaluation systems—often using Codex itself as part of your development process. You will help customers make technical decisions involving model behavior, agentic workflows, developer environments, security, reliability, evaluation, and operational readiness, while ensuring deployments translate into measurable improvements in engineering productivity and software delivery.

You will work closely with OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, Sales, and the broader Codex organization, translating real-world deployment experience into high-signal product and model feedback. Success is measured by production systems, sustained developer adoption, and meaningful improvements to how engineering organizations build software—not simply successful demonstrations or enablement activity.

This role is based in our Madrid office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Partner directly with engineering leaders and hands-on developers to identify high-value opportunities for Codex and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

  • Design, build, and deploy AI-powered software development workflows that improve how engineering teams plan, write, test, review, debug, and deliver software.

  • Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, workflow automations, and production accelerators—often using Codex as part of your own development process.

  • Help customers progress from promising experiments to reliable production workflows, sustained developer adoption, and scaled impact across engineering organizations.

  • Design systematic approaches for evaluating AI coding systems using representative software engineering tasks, automated graders, production signals, and developer feedback.

  • Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, tools, developer environments, integrations, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and operational readiness.

  • Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive technical blockers toward resolution.

  • Lead technical deep dives, workshops, and hands-on enablement that help engineering teams understand and adopt advanced AI coding workflows effectively and safely.

  • Gather high-fidelity insights from real-world Codex deployments and translate them into clear product proposals, model feedback, and technical requirements for OpenAI Product, Research, and Engineering teams.

  • Create reusable architectures, tooling, examples, guides, and technical patterns—including contributions to resources such as the OpenAI Cookbook—that accelerate future Codex deployments.

  • Influence customer engineering strategy by helping technical leaders understand how AI coding systems can reshape their software development lifecycle, engineering practices, and organizational workflows.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering software or AI systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, developer tooling, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting.

  • Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, integrations, or production engineering—not only program, enablement, or stakeholder management.

  • Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across modern software development environments; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.

  • Are an active user of AI coding tools and have developed a strong point of view on how AI can improve developer productivity and software engineering workflows.

  • Enjoy building high-signal prototypes, integrations, automations, and production solutions that demonstrate and deliver what AI coding systems can enable.

  • Understand how to evaluate AI coding systems systematically, including designing representative tasks, automated evaluations, production signals, and mechanisms for incorporating developer feedback.

  • Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as developer tooling integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.

  • Can connect technical decisions to developer workflows, adoption, engineering productivity, and measurable business outcomes.

  • Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, engineering leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.

  • Are comfortable leading technical workshops and hands-on sessions that help engineering organizations adopt new development workflows and technologies.

  • Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous and rapidly evolving environments.

  • Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; deep prior experience with OpenAI products is not required.

This role is for software engineers who want to build and evolve backend systems operating at significant scale. You’ll write production code, design shared infrastructure, and solve technical challenges involving performance, distributed systems, and system reliability.

You’ll also own how those systems behave in production: how changes are rolled out, how issues are detected and diagnosed, and how recurring operational problems can be addressed through better software and system design.
