Lead the development of assessments and credentials with internal experts and external learning partners, setting clear standards for quality and evidence of learning.

title: Head of India Policy, Global Affairs
descriptionHtml:
About the Team:
OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence (AGI) benefits all of humanity. Achieving this goal requires more than cutting-edge research—it demands deep, ongoing engagement with the policymakers, communities, and institutions shaping the future of AI.

The Global Affairs team leads this engagement. We cultivate authentic, collaborative relationships with public officials, regulators, multilateral bodies, civil society leaders, and the broader AI policymaking community to ensure that diverse perspectives inform our work. By bringing external insights into OpenAI and sharing our own learnings transparently, we help advance thoughtful regulation, responsible industry standards, and governance frameworks that promote the safe and beneficial development of AI technologies.

In close partnership with our research, product, and policy colleagues, we work across regions to anticipate emerging issues, craft forward-looking strategies, and champion policies that align technological progress with human values. Our mission is to help shape the global conversation on AI and ensure that the benefits of this transformative technology reach people everywhere.

 

About the Role

As Head of India Policy, Global Affairs you will lead OpenAI’s public policy strategy, government engagement, and policy partnerships in India. You will help shape an environment that supports safe AI development and deployment, expands access to its benefits, and advances India’s ambitions for innovation and economic opportunity.

You will serve as a senior policy representative to Indian institutions and build partnerships that turn shared priorities into practical results. Working with Global Affairs leaders worldwide and colleagues in India, you will connect national and state priorities with OpenAI’s work on responsible adoption, public services, AI skills, and research.

This role is based in New Delhi, India, and requires travel within India and internationally.

  • Set and execute OpenAI’s India policy strategy, translating global priorities into focused national campaigns with clear goals, milestones, and measures of policy progress and public benefit.

  • Build durable relationships with central and state governments, Parliament, regulators, industry, and civil society. Engage constructively across political perspectives and bring local insights into OpenAI’s decisions.

  • Anticipate political and regulatory developments and give leadership clear, actionable advice on risks, opportunities, and tradeoffs affecting OpenAI and the people who use our products.

  • Design and deliver partnerships with government, universities, nonprofits, and industry that strengthen AI fluency, support research, and improve public services. Advance local-language access and measure sustained use and outcomes for underserved communities.

  • Coordinate policy engagement around product launches and sensitive issues, including youth safety, election integrity, and cybersecurity. Partner with central response teams to ensure timely, accurate engagement with public institutions.

  • Represent OpenAI in policy forums and support senior executive engagements. Lead cross-functional projects and external advisers with disciplined prioritization, resource management, and follow-through.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

  • 10 or more years of relevant experience in public policy, government, technology, or international affairs, including responsibility for senior stakeholder engagement in India.

  • Understand India’s political institutions, central and state policymaking, and digital economy, and have a record of building trust with senior public officials and diverse communities.

  • Have delivered meaningful policy outcomes and complex partnerships, with evidence of your ability to set strategy, build coalitions, and carry work through implementation.

descriptionHtml:

The Support Engineering team works closely with Engineering, Product, Technical Success, Go-to-Market, and other teams to deliver an exceptional experience for our most strategic customers. We combine deep technical troubleshooting with durable customer context, proactive reliability work, and clear ownership during critical moments. We use automation, agents, and our own technology to help build the future of technical support.

We’re looking for experienced, deeply curious technical problem-solvers to serve as trusted support partners for our Premium Support customers. You’ll work directly with customers on novel, ambiguous, and high-impact technical issues, using logs, telemetry, reproduction, and systems-level investigation to isolate causes and drive issues toward resolution.

Beyond resolving individual issues, you’ll use your deep understanding of OpenAI’s infrastructure and products, together with each customer’s architecture and operating context, to anticipate risk and make their workloads more resilient over time. You’ll proactively monitor integrations, identify emerging failure patterns and architectural breakpoints, and work with customers and internal teams to address them before they become incidents. Success means that as a customer’s workloads mature and scale, the day-to-day effort required to support them decreases through better monitoring, runbooks, automation, and preventative improvements.

This Toronto-based role is currently remote and is expected to transition to an in-office arrangement.

In this role, you will:

  • Work directly with Premium Support customers to troubleshoot their most complex technical issues, including API failures, integration challenges, authentication errors, unexpected product behavior, performance degradation, and production incidents.

  • Provide end-to-end technical ownership by analyzing logs and system behavior, reproducing errors, testing hypotheses, and isolating the likely failure domain. Where possible, you’ll identify the root cause before escalating to Engineering; where that is not possible, you’ll provide a clear hypothesis and the evidence needed to accelerate Engineering’s investigation.

  • Become a trusted expert on OpenAI’s products and systems, serving as a critical escalation point and a technical backstop for our most strategic customers.

  • Own the customer-specific response to high-impact incidents. You’ll assess severity and business impact, initiate the appropriate response path, coordinate cross-functional responders, maintain clear ownership, and ensure issues move through mitigation, resolution, and post-incident follow-through.

  • Communicate clearly and proactively during periods of uncertainty, providing accurate updates to customer technical teams, business stakeholders, executives, and internal partners.

  • Develop a detailed understanding of each customer’s architecture, integrations, dependencies, critical workloads, and operational constraints. You’ll document this context and make it accessible to Support, Product, and Engineering teams.

  • Partner with Go-to-Market and Technical Success teams to understand the business importance of customer workloads and ensure that relevant commercial context informs severity, prioritization, and communication without bypassing established support processes.

  • Represent Support Engineering in relevant customer meetings, including QBRs, and partner closely with account teams to communicate technical health, surface risks and blockers early, coordinate follow-up, and provide customers and internal stakeholders with clear, proactive updates.

  • Monitor customer integrations and support trends to identify emerging risks, recurring failure patterns, and readiness gaps before they become major escalations.

  • Prepare for important launches, migrations, traffic increases, and business events by developing account-specific runbooks, validating escalation paths, coordinating support readiness, and providing heightened monitoring where needed.

  • Lead or contribute to incident reviews and postmortems, identify opportunities to prevent recurrence, and track corrective actions through closure.

  • Translate recurring customer pain into clear, evidence-backed feedback for Product and Engineering, with a particular focus on improving the reliability and performance of existing products, integrations, and deployments.

  • Turn what you learn from customer investigations into scalable improvements, including troubleshooting guides, monitoring, internal tooling, support workflows, and AI-powered automation.

  • Help shape the operating model, technical standards, and tooling for Premium Support as the function grows globally.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have significant experience in Support Engineering, Solutions Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or another role involving hands-on diagnosis of complex production issues.

  • Have expert-level troubleshooting skills and a strong track record of resolving ambiguous technical problems across APIs, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise integrations.

  • Are comfortable working with logs, metrics, traces, API requests, authentication flows, and customer-provided code or configurations to understand system behavior and test hypotheses.

  • Have experience leading or playing a central role in customer-impacting incidents, including severity assessment, technical coordination, stakeholder communication, root-cause analysis, and post-incident follow-through.

  • Can write code or scripts to reproduce issues, interrogate systems, automate repetitive work, and improve internal tools. Experience with Python, JavaScript, or similar languages is valuable.

  • Can communicate complex technical issues clearly to engineers, customer technical teams, business stakeholders, and senior leaders—especially when information is incomplete or evolving.

  • Build strong, high-trust relationships with customers and cross-functional partners while maintaining clear and scalable ownership boundaries.

  • Look beyond the immediate issue to identify patterns, improve the system, and prevent the same problem from recurring.

  • Thrive in ambiguity, update quickly as new information emerges, and are willing to learn whatever is needed to get the job done.

title: Developer Experience Engineer, Cyber
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Developer Experience team at OpenAI has a singular focus: empowering developers globally. Our mission is to provide every developer and startup on the planet with the most delightful and seamless experience to integrate AI into their applications and products. We ensure developers have the tools, resources, and support they need to unlock AI’s full potential.

We create inspiring demos, developer tools, sample applications, and technical content that show developers how to build with Codex and frontier models like GPT-6 Astra, GPT-Live, and GPT-Image-2.5 to create powerful agents and AI-native applications.

We collaborate closely with product, engineering, research, and GTM teams to ensure the developer journey, from onboarding with Codex to first API call to production deployment, is seamless, effective, and delightful.

About the Role

As a Developer Experience Engineer, Cyber, you will create technical content, developer tools, and sample applications that help developers and security teams secure the software they build and depend on. You will turn OpenAI’s cybersecurity capabilities, including Codex Security, into clear, runnable examples and useful learning experiences.

You will work directly with developers, security practitioners, and technical founders to understand their needs and show how AI can improve secure development and defensive security workflows. We’re looking for a hands-on engineer who combines strong software skills, creativity, developer empathy, and curiosity about cybersecurity, and who can own projects from the first prototype through release and ongoing improvement.

In this role, you will:

  • Build demos, sample applications, and developer tools that demonstrate practical ways to use Codex, OpenAI’s APIs, and Cyber products for secure software development and defensive workflows.

  • Create tutorials, blog posts, videos, and code samples that help developers understand security findings, validate and prioritize vulnerabilities, review proposed changes, and verify fixes.

  • Develop reference integrations that connect AI-assisted security workflows to source control, code review, and continuous integration, helping teams move from initial setup to repeatable use.

  • Partner with Cyber engineers and security researchers to make examples technically accurate and results understandable, with clear guidance on evidence, validation, and the limitations of model-generated findings.

  • Demonstrate sound security practices in examples and tooling, including appropriate permissions, credential handling, protection of sensitive code and data, and human review of agent actions.

  • Engage developers and security practitioners through events, workshops, and online communities, serving as an approachable technical resource and advocate.

  • Gather and synthesize practitioner feedback to identify friction, inform product priorities, and improve the journey from onboarding to everyday use.

  • Contribute directly to developer-facing interfaces, documentation, and tooling, working with product, engineering, and go-to-market partners to help users adopt and succeed with OpenAI’s developer products.

Your background might look something like:

  • Strong engineering fundamentals and a track record of shipping useful software, developer tools, or products for technical users.

  • Experience building applications with AI models, APIs, or agent workflows, and translating experimentation into reliable, maintainable code.

  • Experience with application security, vulnerability management, secure development workflows, or security tooling.

  • A portfolio of technical content, compelling demos, sample applications, or developer tooling that helps others learn and build.

The Applied Foundations team at OpenAI is dedicated to ensuring that our cutting-edge technology is not only revolutionary but also secure from a myriad of adversarial threats. We strive to maintain the integrity of our platforms as they scale.

title: Software Engineer, Native Learning Experiences
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Customer education helps customers and partners build the practical skills and confidence to use AI and OpenAI products safely and effectively. The team focuses on role- and skill-based learning paths, practical content, and product experiences that accelerate learning in the workplace. It brings together learning and enablement expertise, field insight, product signals, and measurement to improve learner and business outcomes.

Together, these experiences will help enterprise users build practical AI skills, apply them with confidence in their work, and demonstrate what they can do. Employers will gain a clearer view of workforce skills and progress, helping them recognize capability, focus development where it matters most, and build confidence in workforce readiness.

About the Role

We’re looking for a full-stack engineer to define and build a new class of learning experiences. This is an early-stage product area where technical judgment, product sense, and learner empathy are critical. You will be setting a technical vision for how people use AI to learn how to use AI, safely and beneficially.

This is a hands-on, 0-1 product engineering role with broad technical and product ownership. You’ll set direction, make foundational decisions, and ship the first versions of experiences that can grow into the default way people learn at work. You will drive full-stack product experiences end to end, from prototype through launch, instrumentation, iteration, and production hardening. The work spans interaction design, frontend implementation, backend APIs and services, learner state, content and runtime integration, telemetry, evaluation, reliability, safety, accessibility, and launch readiness.

You’ll work closely with our education, GTM, and engineering teams to translate how people learn into products people want to use. bring role- and skill-based learning paths into the product, designing coaching, feedback, and adaptive support which responds to each learner’s goals, context, and progress. You’ll lead focused experiments, measure what helps learners progress and where they struggle, and use that evidence to shape what comes next.

Strong candidates will be product engineers with experience and a strong interest in education, learning science, assessment, behavior change, or AI literacy. You’ll help shape how OpenAI supports structured, adaptive learning in the flow of work, from a learner’s first entry point through practice, feedback, progress, and repeated use.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the vision and execution for OAI’s native learning offering

  • Build and launch end-to-end product experiences that help users build and apply AI skills through real work, starting in ChatGPT.

  • Design the core systems behind those experiences, including learner state, progress and re-entry, content and runtime integration, experimentation, telemetry, and evaluation

  • Create reusable components and internal tools that allow education and content partners to develop, configure, test, and improve learning experiences

  • Build and test clear entry points, realistic hands-on practice, useful feedback, telemetry, and evaluation. Use evidence from real use to decide which capabilities for saved context, progress, re-entry, and reuse are needed next.

  • Partner closely with colleagues across Customer Readiness, EDU Engineering, learning science, research, design, data, content, support, and customer-facing teams. Reuse technical and learning patterns where they help while keeping the experience grounded in professional and enterprise use cases.

  • Work closely with design and users to turn product and learning goals into clear requirements, prototypes, milestones, reusable UI patterns, and product metrics, then refine the experience through evidence.

  • Define the learner intent and problem for each release, then use product data, learner feedback, and operational signals to evaluate product quality, learning, transfer to real work, and adoption against that intent.

  • Make pragmatic tradeoffs across speed, quality, scalability, and operational simplicity in a 0-to-1 product area.

Qualifications:

  • Have 5+ years of experience as a software engineer working on applied AI or user-facing systems

  • Former founder, or early engineer at a startup who built a product from scratch is a plus

  • Substantial experience building and operating high-quality user-facing products with a record of staff-level technical leadership and hands-on delivery

  • Strong full-stack engineering skills, including modern frontend technologies such as TypeScript and React, backend services and APIs, relational databases, stateful user flows, and instrumentation, with practical judgment about distributed systems, reliability, and performance.

title: Research Scientist / Research Engineer - Web Understanding and Structured Retrieval, Search
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Foundations Research team works on high-risk, high-reward ideas that could shape the next decade of AI. Our goal is to advance the science and data that enable our training and scaling efforts, with a particular focus on future frontier models. We push the boundaries of data, scaling laws, optimization techniques, model architectures, model + search co-design and efficiency improvements to propel our science.

The Search team sits within Foundations, building agentic search by co-designing model-system interfaces with the core search stack: serving, indexing, and retrieval. We research and develop large-scale systems that transform and index vast corpora, enabling models to most effectively find and reason over information.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Researcher to work on semi-structured knowledge graphs within Search. You’ll research and develop methods for mining structured information from heterogeneous, unstructured and semi-structured web content, making that information more accessible and useful to AI models.

The core questions are: What structure helps models find and use information? How can we extract it reliably at web scale? And how do we measure whether it improves the model’s ability to reason and answer questions? How do we design the system to be optimizable end-to-end?

You’ll work across research, data, and systems, exploring how advances in AI and compute can improve the way knowledge is extracted, organized, and retrieved. This work will support retrieval across OpenAI products and internal research efforts, with opportunities for scientific publication.

Responsibilities

  • Develop methods to extract and connect structured information across diverse web sources, including entities, attributes, and relationships.

  • Build scalable approaches for transforming noisy, inconsistent content into useful knowledge representations.

  • Explore how models and compute can improve extraction quality and reduce the manual work involved in building knowledge systems.

  • Design evaluations that measure both the quality of extracted knowledge and its usefulness for retrieval and model reasoning.

  • Partner with researchers and engineers to integrate structured knowledge into Search and use model performance to guide improvements.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have

  • Deep experience in knowledge extraction, knowledge graphs, entity resolution, or related work that derives structure from large, heterogeneous datasets.

  • Strong machine learning and research skills, with experience developing and evaluating methods for real-world data.

  • A track record of building or scaling data and ML systems, particularly for web-scale extraction, indexing, or retrieval.

  • Experience independently driving open-ended technical problems from an initial idea through experimentation and implementation.

  • A first-principles approach to using AI and compute, with a willingness to rethink established methods as model capabilities improve.

  • A strong interest in how the representation of information shapes what models can find, understand, and use.

title: Dedicated Support Engineer - San Francisco
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s User Operations team shepherds our customers’ adoption of AI and ensures that our customers' product experience is nothing short of exceptional. We are building the very first post-AGI support team. We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others, to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises.

About the Role

The Support Engineering team works closely with Engineering, Product, Technical Success, Go-to-Market, and other teams to deliver an exceptional experience for our most strategic customers. We combine deep technical troubleshooting with durable customer context, proactive reliability work, and clear ownership during critical moments. We use automation, agents, and our own technology to help build the future of technical support.

We’re looking for experienced, deeply curious technical problem-solvers to serve as trusted support partners for our Premium Support customers. You’ll work directly with customers on novel, ambiguous, and high-impact technical issues, using logs, telemetry, reproduction, and systems-level investigation to isolate causes and drive issues toward resolution.

Beyond resolving individual issues, you’ll use your deep understanding of OpenAI’s infrastructure and products, together with each customer’s architecture and operating context, to anticipate risk and make their workloads more resilient over time. You’ll proactively monitor integrations, identify emerging failure patterns and architectural breakpoints, and work with customers and internal teams to address them before they become incidents. Success means that as a customer’s workloads mature and scale, the day-to-day effort required to support them decreases through better monitoring, runbooks, automation, and preventative improvements.

In this role, you will:

  • Work directly with Premium Support customers to troubleshoot their most complex technical issues, including API failures, integration challenges, authentication errors, unexpected product behavior, performance degradation, and production incidents.

  • Provide end-to-end technical ownership by analyzing logs and system behavior, reproducing errors, testing hypotheses, and isolating the likely failure domain. Where possible, you’ll identify the root cause before escalating to Engineering; where that is not possible, you’ll provide a clear hypothesis and the evidence needed to accelerate Engineering’s investigation.

  • Become a trusted expert on OpenAI’s products and systems, serving as a critical escalation point and a technical backstop for our most strategic customers.

  • Own the customer-specific response to high-impact incidents. You’ll assess severity and business impact, initiate the appropriate response path, coordinate cross-functional responders, maintain clear ownership, and ensure issues move through mitigation, resolution, and post-incident follow-through.

  • Communicate clearly and proactively during periods of uncertainty, providing accurate updates to customer technical teams, business stakeholders, executives, and internal partners.

  • Develop a detailed understanding of each customer’s architecture, integrations, dependencies, critical workloads, and operational constraints. You’ll document this context and make it accessible to Support, Product, and Engineering teams.

  • Partner with Go-to-Market and Technical Success teams to understand the business importance of customer workloads and ensure that relevant commercial context informs severity, prioritization, and communication without bypassing established support processes.

  • Represent Support Engineering in relevant customer meetings, including QBRs, and partner closely with account teams to communicate technical health, surface risks and blockers early, coordinate follow-up, and provide customers and internal stakeholders with clear, proactive updates.

  • Monitor customer integrations and support trends to identify emerging risks, recurring failure patterns, and readiness gaps before they become major escalations.

  • Prepare for important launches, migrations, traffic increases, and business events by developing account-specific runbooks, validating escalation paths, coordinating support readiness, and providing heightened monitoring where needed.

  • Lead or contribute to incident reviews and postmortems, identify opportunities to prevent recurrence, and track corrective actions through closure.

  • Translate recurring customer pain into clear, evidence-backed feedback for Product and Engineering, with a particular focus on improving the reliability and performance of existing products, integrations, and deployments.

  • Turn what you learn from customer investigations into scalable improvements, including troubleshooting guides, monitoring, internal tooling, support workflows, and AI-powered automation.

  • Help shape the operating model, technical standards, and tooling for Premium Support as the function grows globally.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have significant experience in Support Engineering, Solutions Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or another role involving hands-on diagnosis of complex production issues.

  • Have expert-level troubleshooting skills and a strong track record of resolving ambiguous technical problems across APIs, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise integrations.

  • Are comfortable working with logs, metrics, traces, API requests, authentication flows, and customer-provided code or configurations to understand system behavior and test hypotheses.

  • Have experience leading or playing a central role in customer-impacting incidents, including severity assessment, technical coordination, stakeholder communication, root-cause analysis, and post-incident follow-through.

  • Can write code or scripts to reproduce issues, interrogate systems, automate repetitive work, and improve internal tools. Experience with Python, JavaScript, or similar languages is valuable.

  • Can communicate complex technical issues clearly to engineers, customer technical teams, business stakeholders, and senior leaders—especially when information is incomplete or evolving.

  • Build strong, high-trust relationships with customers and cross-functional partners while maintaining clear and scalable ownership boundaries.

  • Look beyond the immediate issue to identify patterns, improve the system, and prevent the same problem from recurring.

  • Thrive in ambiguity, update quickly as new information emerges, and are willing to learn whatever is needed to get the job done.

  • Bring a humble, team-first mindset, strong judgment, and a genuine eagerness to help both customers and colleagues succeed.

  • Are excited to use OpenAI’s products, agents, and emerging AI capabilities to transform how technical support operates at scale.

title: Technical Product Manager, GRC Systems
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI's Governance, Risk, and Compliance team works within Security to connect obligations and customer commitments to effective controls and reliable evidence. We partner across the organization to make security easier to put into practice and easier to understand.

About the Role

We are hiring a Technical Product Manager to own the vision and build the systems behind GRC and Security. You will discover what users need, decide what to build and sequence first, and personally implement data models, integrations, and working workflows. You will carry those products through testing, adoption, and operation.

Much of this work is a data problem: understanding what exists, how it changes, which information can be trusted, and what should happen next. You will apply product design and solution architecture to make security controls part of everyday work and produce reliable evidence through their operation. That evidence should support organizational excellence, audits, customers, and regulatory needs and help our audience understand and use the security information relevant to them.

You should be comfortable moving between implementation detail and consequential decisions. You may spend one part of the day debugging a data flow and another explaining the architecture, evidence, and tradeoffs to leadership or an external audience. You will begin as a hands-on individual contributor, setting direction and helping colleagues build effectively.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the product vision and technical direction for an agreed portfolio of GRC systems, discovering user needs and deciding what to build and sequence first.

  • Design and build scalable data models, integrations, and workflows that connect requirements, systems, people, controls, actions, and evidence.

  • Establish data quality, ownership, history, and freshness practices so changes and missing information produce accurate, useful behavior.

  • Build approved security requirements into usable workflows, automate appropriate checks and actions, and verify that controls operate as intended with the teams that own them.

  • Create clear employee experiences that reduce duplicate requests and make the secure path easy to complete.

  • Develop evidence capabilities for auditors, regulators, and customers, including understandable views and structured outputs with appropriate access, scope, and disclosure boundaries.

  • Carry work through testing, release, adoption, monitoring, and maintenance; improve the system when scale or new requirements expose weaknesses.

  • Explain architecture, security outcomes, evidence, and tradeoffs to technical teams and senior or external audiences; create reusable patterns that help others deliver independently.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have personally designed, built, and scaled products or operational systems and can explain the decisions, failures, and outcomes you owned.

  • Can still build and troubleshoot data models, queries, integrations, or workflows, even if your current role is not software engineering.

  • Understand how data identity, relationships, quality, history, and access affect the correctness of a system and its outputs.

  • Can turn an ambiguous need into a product direction, buildable requirements, a practical first release, and evidence that people benefit from it.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The AI Architect team partners with organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact. We work with retail and consumer businesses to identify where AI can create value, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption. The team brings together technical strategy, customer partnership, and practical deployment expertise, working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and specialist delivery teams.

descriptionHtml:

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. For software engineering organizations, this means helping customers adopt Codex and other OpenAI capabilities across the software development lifecycle—transforming how teams plan, build, test, review, and deliver software.

We work directly with engineering leaders and hands-on developers to identify high-value opportunities, design and implement AI-powered development workflows, and scale what works across engineering organizations. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products, reusable architectures, and technical patterns that help developers everywhere get more value from Codex.

As an Applied AI Engineer focused on Codex, you will partner directly with leading engineering organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that transform how software is developed. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from workflow and use-case selection through prototyping, evaluation, production rollout, and scaled adoption.

title: Software Engineer, Product Velocity
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The ChatGPT Velocity team owns the health of the end-to-end developer and deploy loop for ChatGPT-facing services. Our mission is to help ChatGPT engineers ship confidently with a fast, lightweight development cycle and a trusted path to production.

ChatGPT development depends on a long chain: local environments, Bazel builds, CI, tests, merges, release candidates, deploys, synthetics, alerts, and production health. When any link is slow, flaky, or unclear, engineers lose hours, fixes reach users later, and on-call load rises. This team turns that cross-cutting drag into owned, measured, and durable improvements.

About the Role

We are hiring an experienced infrastructure engineer to make ChatGPT development dramatically faster and more reliable. You will work across local development, build systems, CI, deployment infrastructure, test ownership, and production safety signals to reduce the time and attention required to move a healthy change from development to production.

This is not a narrow tooling role. The best person for this job will be comfortable diagnosing messy distributed systems, reading developer pain signals from Slack and metrics, building reliable automation, negotiating ownership across teams, and making tradeoffs between velocity and production safety. You should enjoy treating engineers as users and turning confusing workflow failures into clear, measured systems.

In this role, you will:

  • Reduce local development startup and iteration latency for ChatGPT engineers

  • Improve Bazel and build performance for local machines, devboxes, and CI, including cache effectiveness, reproducibility, disk usage, remote cache behavior, and observability into invalidations.

  • Improve CI reliability and merge throughput by reducing unrelated failures, tail latency, flaky or mis-owned tests, quarantine friction, and repeated manual reruns.

  • Build agents that help PRs make forward progress: rebasing, conflict resolution, CI triage, safe reruns, owner routing, and clear identification of external blockers.

  • Make deploy pipelines more self-healing, especially when transient alerts, known-bad clusters, recovered synthetics, stale RCs, or noisy gates should not require human babysitting.

  • Improve deploy observability so engineers can quickly tell where a change is, what is blocking it, whether the signal is trustworthy, and who owns the next action.

  • Establish lightweight metrics for before-and-after impact, such as commit-to-prod latency, deploy-window throughput, CI tail latency, local bootup time, failure rates, manual interventions, false-positive gates, and developer-reported pain.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have strong experience with large-scale developer infrastructure, build systems, CI/CD, deployment systems, or production reliability.

  • Can debug across local machines, devboxes, remote caches, monorepos, service dependencies, auth systems, and distributed deploy pipelines.

  • Are comfortable with systems like Bazel, Buildkite, Kubernetes, Temporal, Python/TypeScript services, GitHub workflows, and large monorepo tooling, or can ramp quickly on equivalents.

  • Think in product loops as much as systems loops: you care whether developers can understand and trust the workflow, not just whether a subsystem is technically healthy.

  • Know how to replace repeated manual intervention with policy-backed automation while preserving production safety.

  • Communicate well across teams and can turn ambiguous "this is slow/broken/flaky" reports into crisp owners, hypotheses, metrics, and shipped fixes.

  • Prefer practical measurement over vibes, while still knowing that developer frustration is often the first signal of a real systems problem.

  • Are energized by high-leverage work where a small improvement can save hundreds of engineering hours.

Nice to have:

  • Experience improving developer experience in a very large monorepo.

  • Experience with remote execution, remote caching, hermetic builds, or cache reproducibility.

  • Experience designing CI quarantine, test ownership, merge queue, or auto-revert systems.

  • Experience with progressive delivery, canary/preview/stable deploy pipelines, synthetics, alert quality, and deploy-manager style workflows.

  • Experience building agent-assisted developer workflows, such as automated PR babysitting, CI triage, or conflict resolution.

  • Familiarity with security and access-control constraints around secrets, internal auth, VPN/exit-node networking, and local development.

About the Team

The Identity team builds the foundational infrastructure that powers how people access and interact with OpenAI’s products. With more than one billion weekly active users across our products, Identity is one of the most critical platform layers at OpenAI, enabling secure, reliable, and seamless access to ChatGPT, Codex, and the broader OpenAI ecosystem.

We operate at the intersection of large-scale distributed systems, security, and consumer product engineering. Our systems must support unprecedented user growth, increasingly personalized experiences, and an expanding ecosystem of AI-powered products and agents. Our mission is to build an identity platform that scales with OpenAI’s ambitions while maintaining the highest standards of reliability, performance, security, and user trust.

About the Role

As a Software Engineer on the Identity Platform team, you will design, build, and scale the mission-critical distributed systems that power identity across OpenAI. You will own foundational infrastructure spanning authentication, authorization, session management, account lifecycle, and access control for one of the largest and fastest-growing consumer technology platforms in the world.

You’ll tackle complex engineering challenges across high-throughput services, globally distributed data systems, low-latency request paths, and fault-tolerant architectures. You will help evolve our existing infrastructure to support the next billion users while building the foundational capabilities that enable entirely new products and experiences.

This is a highly technical, hands-on role with significant architectural ownership, broad cross-functional impact, and the opportunity to shape the long-term direction of Identity at OpenAI.

In this role, you will:

  • Architect, build, and operate highly available, low-latency distributed systems that power identity and account infrastructure at global consumer internet scale.

  • Evolve our core authentication, authorization, session management, and account lifecycle services to support continued hypergrowth and an expanding product ecosystem.

  • Solve complex infrastructure challenges involving distributed data consistency, caching, fault tolerance, capacity planning, and performance optimization.

  • Drive foundational architectural investments and large-scale migrations while maintaining reliability and continuity for over a billion users.

  • Build reusable platform primitives, APIs, and tooling that enable engineering teams across OpenAI to develop and launch new products securely and efficiently.

  • Establish and elevate engineering standards around system reliability, observability, operational excellence, and security.

  • Provide technical leadership, mentor engineers, and influence the long-term architectural direction of OpenAI’s identity platform.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 7+ years of software engineering experience, with a strong track record of designing, building, and operating large-scale backend or infrastructure systems.

  • Have deep expertise in distributed systems, including service-oriented architectures, distributed databases, caching, consistency models, and fault tolerance.

  • Have experience scaling mission-critical, high-throughput services in environments with demanding availability, latency, and correctness requirements.

  • Have led significant architectural initiatives, infrastructure migrations, or platform modernization efforts in complex production environments.

title: BIM Designer & Coordinator: Civil
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Industrial Compute develops the infrastructure that powers OpenAI’s AI systems. Our Design organization connects engineering, construction, and digital delivery to support complex data center campuses from initial planning through deployment.

Working with internal teams, design consultants, and construction partners, we develop coordinated designs that address site constraints, infrastructure requirements, and future growth. Our BIM team provides the models and workflows needed to deliver consistently across the portfolio.

About the Role

We are seeking a hands-on Civil BIM Designer & Coordinator with a minimum of 8 years of relevant experience to support the planning and design of large-scale, mission-critical data center campuses and associated power generation, energy storage, and utility facilities.

In this role, you will develop, coordinate, and maintain civil models using Civil 3D and AutoCAD. Your scope will include site layouts, grading, drainage, roads, and utilities, coordinating buildings with generating equipment, battery energy storage systems (BESS), water treatment plants, gas metering and conditioning facilities, substations, and cooling systems.

You will work closely with civil engineers, BIM team, discipline designers, equipment vendors, and delivery partners to turn engineering requirements into clear models and deliverables. Your work will support early design reviews, resolve site coordination challenges, and establish repeatable civil BIM practices across concurrent projects. Detailed engineering requirements and specialist analyses will be provided by the responsible engineers.

We are looking for a hands-on civil specialist who can independently manage modeling assignments, communicate design dependencies, and maintain quality as projects evolve.

Key Responsibilities

  • Advance feasibility, constructability, and phasing: Prepare layout, grading, routing, and earthwork options for early design reviews; incorporate noise, exhaust dispersion, heat-rejection, safety, and environmental constraints. Model heavy-equipment delivery routes, turning movements, crane areas, laydown, maintenance clearances, staged construction, temporary-to-permanent generation transitions, and future expansion.

  • Lead civil site development: Create and maintain surfaces, grading and earthwork models, equipment and building pads, roads, alignments, profiles, and corridors. Incorporate flood protection, stormwater management, and containment or separation process-drainage requirements.

  • Develop and coordinate plant utility systems: Model gravity and pressure networks for gas supply, cooling and process water, fire water, wastewater, electrical duct banks, and communications. Coordinate utility models, routes, corridors, crossings, connections, and clearances with engineers, consultants, utility providers, vendors, and construction partners.

  • Integrate campus and power-generation infrastructure: Coordinate civil models with buildings, power plants, BESS, substations, water treatment plants, gas metering and conditioning facilities, cooling systems, and other site utilities. Support simple-cycle and combined-cycle gas turbine, reciprocating engine, and CHP layouts while incorporating equipment separation, service access, and fire access.

  • Coordinate equipment, foundation, and thermal interfaces: Integrate vendor general arrangements, foundation footprints, equipment elevations, trenches, pits, and pipe-support locations with inputs from structural, geotechnical, mechanical, and electrical engineers. Coordinate civil interfaces for heat-recovery steam generators, steam-turbine facilities, heat exchangers, cooling towers, air-cooled condensers, radiator arrays, and thermal-distribution corridors.

  • Govern civil model data and multidisciplinary alignment: Manage Civil 3D data shortcuts, external references, coordinate systems, styles, templates, and parts libraries. Coordinate Civil 3D, Revit, vendor, and combined-discipline models; verify coordinates, origins, elevations, units, orientation, and model alignment in Navisworks.

  • Drive coordination and quality: Lead model reviews, investigate clashes and spatial conflicts, communicate design changes, and track issues through resolution. Review civil models and drawings for completeness, reference integrity, consistency, and compliance with project BIM requirements.

  • Deliver and improve civil BIM: Prepare plans, profiles, sections, model exports, review packages, and model-based quantities appropriate to each project phase. Maintain reusable content, document workflows, and improve delivery across data center, power-generation, energy-storage, and utility projects.

Qualifications

  • Minimum 8 years of civil design, BIM modeling, or civil infrastructure drafting experience, plus a relevant degree/diploma or equivalent practical experience.

  • Experience supporting mission-critical facilities or complex industrial infrastructure across multiple disciplines.

  • Advanced Civil 3D and AutoCAD proficiency, including grading, corridors, utility networks, sheet production, data shortcuts, references, coordinate systems, and model dependencies.

  • Experience with site-survey data, GIS, point clouds, NavVis or similar laser-scanning/reality-capture workflows.

  • Experience with Navisworks, Revizto, and Autodesk Forma for model coordination, issue tracking, and markups.

  • Ability to independently deliver civil packages, interpret engineering and vendor information, identify missing inputs, and escalate engineering decisions appropriately.

  • Strong communication and organizational skills across changing priorities and concurrent projects.

Preferred Skills

  • Direct experience with hyperscale, colocation, or other mission-critical data center campuses, from conceptual site planning through detailed design and construction coordination.

  • Experience supporting civil design and model coordination for one or more of the following: gas turbine or reciprocating engine power plants, combined-cycle or CHP facilities, BESS installations, water treatment plants, gas metering and conditioning facilities, or comparable industrial infrastructure.

  • Familiarity with OEM installation requirements, equipment and foundation interfaces, maintenance envelopes, and balance-of-plant infrastructure.

  • Familiarity with Revit-to-Civil 3D workflows, including building locations, elevations, utility interfaces, and phased campus development.

  • Experience with GIS, survey data, point clouds, and civil data exchange workflows.

  • Experience reviewing consultant models, BIM execution plans, levels of development, model quality, and common data environments.

  • Experience improving production through Dynamo, scripting, or other automation tools.

  • For candidates with deeper experience, the ability to guide complex civil modeling packages, mentor colleagues, and improve shared standards.

What Success Looks Like

You deliver dependable civil models and drawings, identify coordination issues early, and maintain clear ownership of civil BIM production and standards. Your work enables coordinated delivery of data center campuses and associated power, energy storage, and utility infrastructure across the portfolio.

title: Applied Scientist, Product Policy Research & Measurement
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Product Policy team develops and implements policies that shape how OpenAI’s technology is built and used. We work with teams across the company to turn complex questions about AI’s benefits and risks into practical guidance for responsible research, product development, and deployment.

About the Role

We are hiring a senior applied scientist to study how AI affects people and society using OpenAI production data, experiments, and social science methods. This role sits at the intersection of applied social science, AI, and product policy. The scientist will own research from an ambiguous question through study design, data collection and analysis, methodological validation, and recommendations. Their work will inform product and policy decisions and, where appropriate, contribute to external publications. We are looking for a hands-on empirical social scientist with exceptional methodological judgment.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop and execute a research agenda on AI’s social impact, including effects on well-being, learning, social connection, trust, and human decision-making, in partnership with product and policy teams.

  • Own empirical studies end to end: define the question and estimand, choose the design, build the dataset, conduct the analysis, and explain what the evidence supports.

  • Analyze large-scale production and behavioral data, linking them to experiments, surveys, or external outcomes when appropriate to measure real-world effects.

  • Design randomized experiments and credible observational studies; test identification assumptions, quantify uncertainty, and distinguish association from causal effects.

  • Develop and validate measures of social outcomes, including human and LLM-assisted annotations; assess measurement error, subgroup performance, and drift.

  • Translate findings into concrete product and policy recommendations, with clear limits on causal interpretation, generalizability, and decision confidence.

  • Partner with Product Policy, Research, Product, Data Science, Engineering, UXR, Legal, and domain experts; contribute rigorous work to external publications when appropriate.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • A PhD or equivalent research experience in sociology, political science, psychology, communication, computational social science, or a related empirical field, with demonstrated independent research ownership.

  • Deep expertise in research design, causal inference, experimentation, statistical analysis, and measurement, demonstrated through work you can personally explain and defend.

  • Strong SQL and Python or R skills, with experience independently constructing and analyzing complex behavioral datasets and producing reproducible research.

  • A record of research that informs consequential decisions about technology and people, with the judgment to identify both useful findings and unresolved uncertainty.

  • Clear writing for technical and policy audiences, and experience producing rigorous research papers or equivalent public technical work.

  • The ability to move quickly, collaborate across functions, and maintain scientific independence when findings are sensitive or inconvenient.

descriptionHtml:

We’re hiring a Principal Software Engineer to help define and build the next generation of AI-powered software development workflows.


“Full stack” in this role extends well beyond traditional frontend and backend development. You will set technical direction and lead major product initiatives spanning user interfaces, developer tooling, workflow orchestration, agent and prompt design, backend systems, and cloud infrastructure.


This is a highly product-oriented technical leadership role. You will identify the highest-leverage opportunities across the software development lifecycle, turn ambiguous user and technical problems into durable product and system strategies, and lead execution across multiple engineers and partner teams. You will operate as a senior individual contributor: remaining deeply involved in design and implementation while raising the technical judgment, execution quality, and ambition of the broader team.

About the Role

We’re looking for a resourceful partnerships professional who combines strong external relationship skills with the judgment and organizational ability to move complex initiatives forward.

You will manage designated external relationships and lead the day-to-day delivery of partnerships across the team’s portfolios and Working with portfolio leads, you will translate agreed objectives into practical programs, represent OpenAI in partner conversations, coordinate internal contributions, and carry commitments through delivery. 

You will also step into emerging priorities: helping launch a new collaboration, advancing an existing partnership, preparing a senior leader for an external engagement, or coordinating a project involving several teams. Your portfolio will evolve with team priorities, with clear ownership and agreed outcomes for each assignment.

This role requires someone who enjoys building relationships and doing the detailed work that makes those relationships productive. You should be comfortable working independently, learning unfamiliar issues quickly, and knowing when to seek expertise or escalate a decision.

In this role, you will:

  • Own external relationships. Build and manage trusted relationships with nonprofit organizations, civic leaders, community institutions, and other partners across a range of diverse perspectives and communities.

  • Develop and deliver partnerships. Translate shared interests into practical collaborations with clear objectives, scope, responsibilities, timelines, and measures of success.

  • Represent OpenAI externally. Lead partner meetings and briefings, participate in convenings, and communicate clearly about AI’s opportunities and safe and responsible use.

  • Contribute across the team’s priorities. Take ownership of defined projects across different portfolios, support colleagues during major initiatives, and help establish new areas of engagement.

  • Connect partners with internal expertise. Work with policy, product, safety, legal, communications, and education colleagues to develop substantive engagements and secure the contributions needed for delivery.

  • Turn stakeholder insight into action. Identify concerns and opportunities, synthesize what we hear, bring relevant feedback to internal owners, and close the loop with partners.

  • Deliver funded partnership programs. Translate agreed commitments into feasible workplans with clear owners, milestones, and outcomes. Work directly with partners and portfolio leads to resolve program questions, coordinate implementation, and assess results, including recommendations for improvement or renewal.

  • Coordinate partnership implementation across teams. Bring together relationship owners and colleagues in policy, legal, finance, procurement, product, and communications to move agreements, funding processes, and program launches forward; track dependencies, resolve or escalate blockers, and keep partners and internal teams informed of progress.

  • Maintain reliable follow-through. Manage workplans, partner commitments, budgets, and approval processes for your projects; surface dependencies and risks early and recommend solutions.

  • Exercise sound prioritization. Assess incoming opportunities against team goals, recommend where to invest time and resources, and adjust plans as circumstances change.

  • Bring 6+ years of relevant experience in partnerships, external affairs, public policy, campaigns, government, nonprofits, or community engagement, or equivalent experience demonstrating these capabilities.

title: Machine Learning Engineer, Implicit Signals
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Our team builds classification and evaluation systems that give post-training and research teams fast, reliable feedback on model behavior. We combine machine learning and production engineering to make these capabilities accurate, efficient, and useful at scale, helping researchers assess changes and improve models and products.

We work closely with research teams to develop useful measurements and make them practical to run. Our work spans classifier development, rigorous evaluation, and efficient production inference, with ownership from initial experimentation through deployment and continued improvement.

About the Role

We’re looking for a machine learning engineer to develop new classification and evaluation capabilities and bring them into production. You’ll help turn open-ended questions about model behavior into well-defined ML problems, build methods that address them, and establish how reliably those methods work.

This role combines traditional machine learning, model evaluation, and real-time engineering. You’ll own classifiers throughout their lifecycle, including supervised fine-tuning, distillation, evaluation, deployment, and production inference. You’ll work closely with researchers to identify valuable problems and with software engineers to make promising approaches useful at scale.

In this role, you will:

  • Build, deploy, and operate production classification and evaluation systems that provide useful feedback to post-training and research teams.

  • Optimize production inference, including model serving, batching, caching, throughput, latency, compute utilization, and cost.

  • Train and optimize classifiers using supervised fine-tuning and distillation, validating quality and efficiency before deployment.

  • Own the reliability and observability of deployed classifiers, diagnose production issues, and improve their performance over time.

  • Design rigorous evaluations that assess accuracy, calibration, generalization, and potential measurement bias while guiding production tradeoffs.

  • Partner with software engineers to integrate models into reliable execution systems and support safe rollouts.

  • Build reusable engineering tools that make classifier training, evaluation, deployment, and iteration faster and more repeatable.

  • Work with post-training researchers and data scientists to translate their needs into modeling objectives, evaluation criteria, and production requirements.

Your background might look something like

  • Experience taking ML projects from problem formulation and experimentation through production deployment.

  • Strong foundations in supervised learning, statistics, and experimental design.

  • Practical experience evaluating models, investigating systematic errors, and working with imperfect labels.

  • Strong software engineering skills and the ability to build maintainable production ML systems.

  • Experience reasoning about inference performance and the tradeoffs between quality, latency, and compute cost.

  • The ability to combine careful scientific judgment with a practical approach to shipping and operating software.

  • Comfort working closely with researchers and engineers on open-ended problems.

  • Fluency in using AI agents to move quickly across multiple workstreams in a fast-paced environment.

  • Experience with model distillation, representation learning, calibration, or efficient inference is a plus.

Monetization plays a critical role in enabling OpenAI to continue pushing the boundaries of AI capabilities while ensuring the benefits of AGI are broadly shared. title: Software Engineer, API Agents
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

API Agents builds the shared agent harness, tools, and infrastructure that turn OpenAI’s frontier models into systems that can reliably complete real work. We carry the capabilities behind Codex into a much broader set of products and workflows across software engineering, research, finance, healthcare, enterprise operations, and more. Our work spans search and connected context, computer use, memory, delegation and multi-agent coordination, and safe execution. Sitting at the intersection of Research, Codex, infrastructure, and applied product teams, we build reusable agent capabilities that compound across the ecosystem.

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced backend software engineer to build the core systems behind the next generation of agents. You will design reliable services and abstractions that help agents find the right context, use tools and computers, retain knowledge, coordinate over long-running workflows, and take action safely. The role combines deep backend and infrastructure work with strong product judgment, with opportunities to work across agent runtimes, orchestration, search, execution environments, identity and permissions, observability, and evaluations. This is software and systems engineering rather than model training: success comes from strong backend fundamentals, high agency, and the ability to turn fast-moving research capabilities into dependable production primitives.

In this role, you will:

  • Design, build, and operate the shared agent harness and backend infrastructure that power long-running, high-value workflows across OpenAI and third-party products.

  • Build reusable capabilities across search and connected context, computer use, memory, tool execution, delegation, subagents, and multi-agent orchestration.

  • Establish the foundations agents need to operate safely in production, including secure execution environments, identity and permissions, observability, evaluations, reliability, and cost and latency efficiency.

  • Proficiency in one or more backend languages such as Python, Go, Rust, TypeScript, or similar, with the ability to move comfortably across service, platform, and product boundaries.

title: Software Engineer, Caching Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

At OpenAI, we’re building safe and beneficial artificial general intelligence. We deploy our models through ChatGPT, our APIs, and other cutting-edge products. Behind the scenes, making these systems fast, reliable, and cost-efficient requires world-class infrastructure.

The Caching Infrastructure team is responsible for building a caching layer that powers many critical use cases at OpenAI. We aim to provide a high-availability, multi-tenant cache platform that scales automatically with workload, minimizes tail latency, and supports a diverse range of use cases.

We’re looking for an experienced engineer to help design and scale this critical infrastructure. The ideal candidate has deep experience in distributed caching systems (e.g., Redis, Memcached), networking fundamentals, and Kubernetes-based service orchestration.

In This Role, You Will:

  • Design, build, and operate OpenAI’s multi-tenant caching platform used across inference, identity, quota, and product experiences.

  • Define the long-term vision and roadmap for caching as a core infra capability, balancing performance, durability, and cost.

  • Collaborate with other infra teams (e.g., networking, observability, databases) and product teams to ensure our caching platform meets their needs.

You Might Thrive In This Role If You:

  • Have 5+ years of experience building and scaling distributed systems, with a strong focus on caching, load balancing, or storage systems.

  • Have deep expertise with Redis, Memcached, or similar solutions, including clustering, durability configurations, client-side connection patterns, and performance tuning.

  • Have production experience with Kubernetes, service meshes (e.g., Envoy), and autoscaling systems.

  • Think rigorously about latency, reliability, throughput, and cost in designing platform capabilities.

The Data Center Engineering team defines the strategy, reference architectures, technical requirements, and delivery standards for the large-scale data centers that support OpenAI research, products, and infrastructure partners.

As a Controls Engineer for BMS & EPMS, you will program, configure, integrate, and commission the controls systems that support high-density AI data centers. You will work hands-on with mechanical or electrical controls, partnering with mechanical, electrical, IT/networking, security, commissioning, operations, and external delivery teams.

About the Role

We are seeking hands-on, early-career controls engineers with practical experience in building management systems (BMS) and mechanical controls, or electrical power monitoring systems (EPMS) and electrical controls. This role focuses on implementing and commissioning control systems, including PLCs, field devices, instrumentation, and sequences of operation, rather than owning OT/IT network or cybersecurity architecture.

The ideal candidate has day-to-day experience programming and commissioning controls, ideally with a controls systems integrator. We welcome depth in either BMS/mechanical or EPMS/electrical controls; expertise in both is not required. You will work with experienced engineers and delivery partners to turn design requirements into reliable, tested systems.

Key Responsibilities

  • Program and configure PLCs and control systems for mechanical/BMS or electrical/EPMS applications in AI data center campuses.

  • Implement and test sequences of operation, control logic, alarms, and interlocks against approved functional requirements.

  • Review and maintain controls documentation, including control diagrams, I/O and point lists, instrumentation details, sequences of operation, and commissioning records.

  • Integrate field devices, sensors, instrumentation, equipment controllers, and supervisory systems; validate point mapping, communications, and data quality.

  • Maintain control programs, configuration backups, version history, change records, and rollback procedures to support safe commissioning and operations.

  • Partner with mechanical, electrical, IT/networking, cybersecurity, and operations teams to resolve integration issues and implement approved OT connectivity and security requirements.

  • Configure and troubleshoot relevant industrial communications, such as BACnet/IP, BACnet MS/TP, Modbus TCP/RTU, OPC UA, or IEC 61850, according to the system and controls discipline.

  • Work directly with controls integrators, equipment vendors, contractors, and commissioning teams to resolve programming, installation, and functional performance issues.

  • Execute and document factory and site acceptance testing, point-to-point checks, sequence verification, and integrated systems testing; troubleshoot control logic, instrumentation, alarms, and device communication failures.

Qualifications

  • Practical hands-on experience programming, configuring, integrating, or commissioning control systems in data centers, industrial automation, buildings, or other critical infrastructure environments.

  • Working knowledge of PLC programming and control logic, with the ability to implement and troubleshoot sequences of operation.

  • Experience in either BMS/mechanical controls or EPMS/electrical controls, with an understanding of the equipment and operating sequences in that discipline.

  • Experience configuring field devices and instrumentation, validating I/O and point mapping, and diagnosing control system behavior.

  • Working knowledge of relevant industrial communication protocols and basic OT networking needed to connect and troubleshoot control systems.

  • Ability to read control diagrams, equipment documentation, I/O lists, and functional specifications, and keep implementation records accurate.

  • Hands-on experience with functional testing, commissioning, and systematic troubleshooting using trends, alarms, logs, and field observations.

  • Ability to work closely with integrators, vendors, construction teams, and operations, communicate issues clearly, and follow safe work and change-control practices.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Controls or Automation Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience at a controls systems integrator, with regular responsibility for programming, configuration, field integration, and commissioning.

  • Experience delivering BMS/mechanical or EPMS/electrical controls for data centers or other mission-critical facilities.

  • Familiarity with supervisory controls, HMI/SCADA configuration, telemetry, and historian integrations.

  • Familiarity with OT cybersecurity practices and working with networking or security specialists to implement approved access and connectivity requirements.

  • Experience with scripting, APIs, or automation tools that improve controls testing, integration, documentation, or troubleshooting.

Work Environment and Travel

  • This role requires periodic travel to data center campuses, vendors, labs, construction sites, commissioning activities, and controls/network cutovers.

  • The engineer should be comfortable working across office, lab, construction, and live data center environments, including PPE, lockout/tagout, cyber hygiene, and change-control requirements.

  • Work may include time-sensitive support during commissioning, startup, vendor testing, cutovers, network changes, telemetry issues, automation failures, and operational events.

Travel: 50%

title: Software Engineer, HSM Infrastructure Security, Consumer Devices
descriptionHtml:
We are hiring a Security Software Engineer to design and implement the hardware-backed security foundations used across OpenAI’s device ecosystem.

A central focus of this role is hardening the boundary between our policy systems and the HSMs that protect sensitive cryptographic keys. This boundary determines which operations may be performed, what may be signed, which policies must be satisfied, and how changes to trusted software and policy are authorized.

You will develop security-critical software and firmware within, or immediately adjacent to, an HSM trust boundary. Depending on your background, this may include HSM trusted applications, firmware services, cryptographic mechanisms, device drivers, PKCS#11 components, secure-provisioning protocols, or signing-policy enforcement systems.

This is a hands-on software-engineering role. You will be expected to design systems, write and review production code, debug across hardware and software boundaries, and carry projects from initial requirements through deployment. It is not an HSM administration, PKI operations, compliance, or architecture-only position.

In This Role, You Will

  • Design and implement security-critical software and firmware for HSMs, secure elements, trusted execution environments, and hardware roots of trust.

  • Build and harden the policy-to-HSM boundary responsible for authorizing certificate issuance and cryptographic signing operations.

  • Develop HSM trusted applications, firmware components, host interfaces, device drivers, SDKs, or cryptographic service integrations.

  • Implement or extend cryptographic interfaces such as PKCS#11, OpenSSL providers or engines, platform key-storage APIs, or comparable hardware-security interfaces.

  • Build firmware and software that cryptographically enforces key generation, provisioning, usage, rotation, recovery, and destruction policies.

  • Design and implement HSM-backed certificate authority, code-signing, key-management, and device-identity systems.

  • Develop end-to-end cryptographic protocols spanning devices, secure hardware, policy services, and backend infrastructure.

  • Build security capabilities supporting device attestation, secure boot, factory provisioning and restoration, user registration, and authentication.

  • Design controls that make trusted software and policy changes verifiable, auditable, and subject to appropriate multi-party authorization.

  • Write, review, test, and audit secure embedded software for resource-constrained environments.

  • Develop test harnesses, emulators, fuzzers, and fault-injection tooling to validate security properties and failure behavior.

  • Threat-model hardware and software trust boundaries and translate findings into concrete engineering improvements.

  • Partner with hardware, firmware, infrastructure, application, and security teams to integrate secure-by-default capabilities into production systems.

  • Help establish engineering standards for HSM development, applied cryptography, secure key management, and certificate infrastructure.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 5+ years experience building secure embedded firmware for constrained environments

  • Deep programming experience in C, C++, or Rust.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have

  • A strong track record of designing, implementing, debugging, and shipping production systems software.

  • Hands-on experience developing security-critical software or firmware within, or directly adjacent to, an HSM, secure element, TEE, or hardware root of trust.

  • Experience developing one or more of the following:

    • HSM firmware or trusted applications

    • Cryptographic mechanisms or hardware-accelerated cryptographic services

    • HSM device drivers, host libraries, SDKs, or middleware

    • PKCS#11 providers, mechanisms, or integrations

    • Secure key-provisioning or key-injection protocols

    • HSM-backed certificate authority or code-signing systems

    • Signing-policy enforcement within a hardware-backed trust boundary

  • Strong knowledge of applied cryptography, digital signatures, key hierarchies, secure key management, and cryptographic protocol design.

  • Experience with PKI, X.509 certificates, certificate authorities, certificate issuance, and certificate lifecycle protocols.

  • Familiarity with secure boot, measured boot, device identity, remote attestation, or hardware-backed storage.
