title: Engineering Manager, ChatGPT Space
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The ChatGPT Space team is rethinking what work looks like when teams and agents can create together. We are building a shared workspace where a rough idea can become a polished, editable artifact, from Pages, Sheets, and Slides to entirely new kinds of work products.

Our ambition is to build the best place for teams and agents to turn ideas into things they could not make alone. The work should keep evolving after the first draft, drawing on shared context, improving through collaboration, and staying current as a project moves forward.

This is a high-agency team working across product, design, and research. We partner closely with model training teams to shape how frontier models create and edit artifacts, then bring those capabilities into a coherent experience across Pages, files, and tools. The work spans full-stack product engineering, editing and rendering systems, model integration, and collaboration, with a high bar for taste, correctness, and speed.

About the Role

As Engineering Manager, ChatGPT Space, you will lead and grow the product engineering team defining this experience. You will help shape both the product and the team that builds it, turning an ambitious, evolving vision into software people love to use.

You will partner with product and design on what great collaboration between teams and agents should feel like, with research on what models can create, and with infrastructure and enterprise partners on a dependable experience at scale.

This is a role for a leader who has built from zero to one and wants to help define a new category of work. You will bring the technical depth to guide hard decisions and the product judgment to know what is worth building, while developing engineers and giving them the clarity and autonomy to ship.

This role is based in San Francisco.

In this role, you will

  • Lead, manage, and grow a product engineering team, creating clear ownership, supporting engineers’ development, and hiring exceptional people

  • Partner with product and design to shape the ChatGPT Space roadmap and translate user needs into focused, well-crafted releases

  • Lead the development of creation, editing, and collaboration experiences for teams and agents, including tools that connect project context and keep work up to date

  • Set technical direction for full-stack product systems, editing and rendering surfaces, and model-facing integrations

  • Partner closely with research teams on artifact tools, model behavior, training needs, and evaluations, turning improvements in model capability into better products

  • Establish a high bar for editor quality, correctness, latency, and reliability, and use user feedback and evaluation results to guide improvements

  • Work with infrastructure and enterprise partners to deliver dependable experiences, align interfaces and ownership, and resolve problems across team boundaries

  • Balance new product development with the technical investments and operational discipline needed to sustain quality as the product grows

  • Build an effective operating cadence that keeps a fast-moving team aligned and gives engineers the context and autonomy to do their best work

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Have a track record of leading engineering teams and helping engineers grow while delivering excellent products

  • Have built products from zero to one and can turn an ambiguous opportunity into a clear direction and practical execution plan

  • Bring strong product judgment and design taste, with a deep interest in how teams and agents create, edit, and collaborate

  • Have strong full-stack engineering fundamentals and can guide technical decisions across frontend, backend, and model-facing systems

  • Work effectively with product, design, research, and infrastructure partners, building alignment without losing momentum

  • Care deeply about craft, performance, correctness, and reliability, and can help a team improve all four while moving quickly

  • Communicate clearly, make thoughtful tradeoffs, and adapt as user needs and model capabilities evolve

title: Hardware Engineer, Test
descriptionHtml:
About the Team:

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

In this role you will:

  • As a Hardware Test Engineer, you will work on Machine Learning/AI hardware system projects to craft the solutions for current and future data center deployments.

  • You will bring a strong understanding of hardware system testing, excellent project management skills, and the ability to collaborate across multiple teams to ensure efficient lab operations.

  • You will be responsible for designing, implementing, and executing comprehensive test plans that ensure the reliability, performance, and scalability of our supercomputing hardware systems. You will develop detailed test plans and methodologies tailored to hardware components, including processors, memory modules, custom accelerators and interconnects.

  • You will collaborate with hardware design, manufacturing, firmware teams and vendors to identify, analyze, and resolve issues affecting hardware, power, thermal and high-speed interconnects. You will perform in-depth debugging on the hardware system

    • Excellent analytical skills to diagnose hardware issues, troubleshoot problems, and propose solutions. Ability to interpret complex test data, identify trends, and draw meaningful conclusions.

    • High-speed links, with a focus on SerDes (Serializer/Deserializer) technology to assess signal integrity, error rates, and overall link performance.

  • You will collaborate with the lab manager to maintain the equipment and hardware systems, including oscilloscopes, thermal test chambers, liquid cooling systems, and other measurement devices.

  • You will utilize advanced diagnostic and measurement tools to capture performance metrics and analyze system behavior. You will develop and maintain automation scripts to streamline testing processes. Proficiency in Python, Bash and test automation frameworks to develop automated test scripts is highly desired.

  • Effective communication to clearly document test results, report defects, and collaborate with cross-functional teams.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have at least 10 years of industry experience, including experience testing or supporting hardware design teams for datacenter applications

  • Proven experience in hardware testing and validation, with hands-on experience with oscilloscopes, power supplies, analyzers, and other test instruments.

  • Have a strong understanding of electrical, power and thermal testing methodologies.

  • Have expertise with protocol of common interfaces such as SPI, I2C, USB, DDRx, and have experience characterizing and verifying compliance of Datacenter Ethernet interfaces.

  • Hands-on experience with high-speed electrical and thermal test equipment such as oscilloscopes, VNA, TDR, thermal cameras, heat sinks, and test chambers.

  • Experience in using Cadence Allegro and automation / scripting.

  • Have a strong bias toward action, and won’t take no for an answer.

  • Have experience and good knowledge of system testing from xPUs, board, rack level to data center level

  • Have a strong intrinsic desire to learn and fill in missing skills; and an equally strong talent for sharing that information clearly and concisely with others.

  • Are comfortable with ambiguity and rapidly changing conditions.

  • Have excellent analytical, problem-solving, and troubleshooting skills.

title: Applied AI Engineer, Digital Natives
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineering teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works.

Production-ready deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.

About the Role

As an Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with leading organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale.

You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations.

This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve.

This role is based in Munich. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees

In this role, you will:

  • Partner directly with enterprise and digital native customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

  • Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes.

  • Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators.

  • Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.

  • Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution.

  • Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact.

  • Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback.

  • Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, product engineering or technical consulting.

  • Are fluent in both German and English

  • Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or engineering of production systems—not only program or stakeholder management.

  • Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across an AI application stack; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.

  • Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment.

  • Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.

  • Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.

  • Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.

title: Manager, Revenue Accounting, Technical (Strategic Commercial Deals)
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI Finance helps ensure the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission of ensuring that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

Within Finance, the Revenue Accounting, Technical team partners with Product, Strategic Partnerships, Business Development, Growth, Legal, Deal Desk, GTM, Strategic Finance, Revenue Accounting, and Finance Systems to enable scalable, operationally sound monetization. We advise on commercial and contract design, establish clear accounting positions under ASC 606, and translate those conclusions into repeatable processes, systems, controls, and reporting.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Manager of Revenue Accounting, Technical to drive the end-to-end technical revenue and operational workstream for OpenAI’s strategic commercial deals—from early structuring and deal-desk review through contracting, launch, and ongoing governance.

Reporting to the Head of Revenue Accounting, Technical, you will serve as a key revenue advisor for complex and non-standard strategic deals, translating commercial objectives into revenue models that are economically sound, accounting-compliant, and operationally executable. You will partner with senior team members on the most novel or high-risk matters across strategic collaborations, cloud marketplaces, platform and distribution deals, licensing and revenue-share models, joint go-to-market initiatives, research collaborations, and other emerging commercial structures.

You will engage from the earliest stages of a deal to shape economics, pricing, commercial terms, contract language, and product design; define the supporting data, billing, settlement, reporting, systems, controls, and revenue-recognition model; and drive cross-functional readiness through launch. After launch, you will help govern amendments, monitor whether the model is operating as intended, resolve execution issues, and evolve the approach as the partnership or business model changes.

This role requires strong technical accounting judgment, commercial fluency, clear cross-functional communication, and the ability to independently drive complex workstreams while knowing when to seek input or escalate.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the day-to-day technical revenue workstream for a portfolio of strategic commercial deals from initial concept and term-sheet development through contracting, launch readiness, post-launch changes, and ongoing governance.

  • Build and pressure-test revenue models for strategic collaborations, cloud marketplaces, platform and distribution deals, licensing and revenue-share arrangements, and other emerging commercial models, including pricing, minimum commitments, incentives, credits, variable consideration, usage mechanics, and settlement flows.

  • Partner through the deal-desk process with Strategic Partnerships, Product, GTM, Strategic Finance, Legal, GTM Deal Desk, Tax, Finance Systems, and Revenue Operations to shape deal economics, pricing, contract terms, product configuration, and operational design from initial proposal through approval and launch.

  • Assist senior team members in evaluating complex transactions under ASC 606, including principal-versus-agent considerations, gross-versus-net presentation, performance obligations, variable consideration, contract combinations, commitments, credits, incentives, and related-party considerations, escalating precedent-setting judgments for senior review.

  • Translate technical conclusions into required commercial and contract terms, practical deal-desk guidance, approval guardrails, and clear intake, escalation, and decision-making processes for material deals, amendments, and renewals.

  • Design revenue models end to end by defining the contracting, product, data, order-to-cash, usage, billing, invoicing, settlement, reconciliation, reporting, systems, and control requirements needed to operate them; partner with operational teams to build, test, document, and scale the resulting processes.

  • Lead cross-functional launch readiness for strategic deals, validate that systems, data, billing, reporting, and controls reflect the approved structure, and help resolve post-launch issues, amendments, or changes in actual deal economics.

  • Develop clear internal decision materials and operating requirements, coordinate concurrent deal workstreams, and improve the playbooks, templates, and guidance that make strategic-deal execution more consistent and scalable.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 5+ years of technical revenue accounting or related advisory experience, with strong ASC 606 expertise and experience independently owning complex analyses and workstreams.

  • Experience working in or closely with a deal-desk function to support strategic commercial deals end to end, including complex collaborations, cloud marketplaces, platform distribution, licensing, revenue-share models, or other multi-party transactions.

  • Demonstrated ability to craft and pressure-test revenue models, influence commercial strategy, pricing, product design, and contract terms, and translate the agreed structure into executable operational flows.

  • Experience navigating emerging monetization models such as advertising revenue, marketplaces/commerce platforms, or other multi-sided ecosystems is a strong plus.

  • Strong working knowledge of principal-versus-agent analysis, gross-versus-net presentation, variable consideration, consideration payable to a customer, contract combinations, and complex performance-obligation assessments.

  • Experience driving cross-functional launch readiness, validating systems and operational processes, and resolving post-launch issues for complex or unfamiliar revenue models.

  • Experience translating evolving commercial structures into operational revenue models spanning contracting, product setup, usage data, billing, settlement, accounting, reconciliation, reporting, systems, and controls.

  • Sound commercial judgment and strong communication skills, with the ability to explain complex accounting issues and practical trade-offs to accounting and non-accounting stakeholders.

  • Demonstrated success managing multiple strategic deals from intake through launch and ongoing governance, improving repeatable processes, and operating effectively in ambiguous, rapidly changing environments; experience mentoring others is valued.

  • CPA preferred; a mix of Big 4 (or accounting advisory), commercial deal support, and technology industry experience in high-growth environments is highly valued.

title: Research Program Manager, Safety Systems
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Safety Systems manages the complete lifecycle of safety efforts for OpenAI’s frontier models. We work across research, engineering, product, and policy to understand risks, develop and validate safeguards, and support responsible deployment.

Our work spans safeguards research and deployment, safety assessments, launch readiness, and trusted-access programs for advanced capabilities. We address risks including biological and cyber misuse and misalignment, with programs that strengthen safety across models and products.

About the Role

We’re hiring Research Program Managers across AI Safeguards and Frontier Risks Safety. You’ll lead programs that develop and improve the safeguards used across our models and products, or assess and mitigate risks associated with frontier capabilities, launches, and trusted-access programs.

You will partner with researchers, engineers, and other stakeholders to turn open safety questions into clear programs of work. You’ll shape technical roadmaps, coordinate execution, and use evidence to guide priorities and inform development and deployment decisions. We’re looking for people who combine strong technical judgment, experience managing complex research programs, and a commitment to AI safety.

These roles are based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Shape safety programs and technical roadmaps. Partner with research and engineering leads to define goals, milestones, dependencies, and success criteria. Prioritize intake and emerging findings, resolve blockers, and balance immediate safety needs with longer-term research and platform investments.

  • Drive safeguards development and deployment. Translate safety research into safeguards across models and products. Maintain an end-to-end view of safeguard coverage, effectiveness, and opportunities for improvement for one or more risk areas, and drive a roadmap that advances across launches.

  • Coordinate evaluations and safety assessments. Organize capability evaluations, alignment and control assessments, adversarial testing, and safeguard stress-testing, including risks from autonomous and multi-agent systems. Support embedded assessments throughout model development, internal use, and deployment.

  • Drive safety readiness and trusted-access programs. Coordinate safety requirements and execution across frontier model launches and deployments. Work with technical teams to define assessment scope and the evidence needed to inform safety and access decisions.

  • Turn findings into improvements. Triage safeguard gaps, jailbreaks, and overflagging with accountable teams. Establish owners and escalation paths, track remediation and regression testing, and turn recurring issues into research and engineering improvements.

  • Strengthen the evidence behind safety decisions. Support safety cases that connect claims to evaluations, safeguards, assumptions, and remaining uncertainty. Surface evidence gaps and unresolved risks, and communicate methods, results, limitations, and follow-up actions through assessment reports, system cards, and updates to decision-makers.

  • Build programs that scale across products. Coordinate shared tooling and feedback workflows, privacy and security requirements, and safeguard user experience and quality assurance. Help teams apply safeguards consistently across product surfaces and upcoming launches.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 5+ years of experience in technical safety work, owning technical programs, or related roles in fast-moving environments.

  • Have led complex research or technical programs involving researchers and engineers, particularly in AI, cybersecurity, biosafety, or another field where failures can have serious consequences.

  • Understand frontier AI safety concepts, including capability evaluations, alignment, control, monitoring, and safeguard robustness, and can engage substantively with technical teams.

  • Can assess what evaluation results do and do not establish, including methodological limitations, uncertainty, and the difference between model capability and real-world risk.

  • Can turn ambiguous questions into clear programs, make practical tradeoffs, and adjust priorities as evidence changes.

  • Have worked extensively across research, engineering, and product teams and can coordinate with policy and communications partners.

  • Exercise sound judgment when findings are concerning or incomplete, raise unresolved risks constructively, and communicate complex technical work clearly.

  • Are motivated to help ensure increasingly capable AI systems remain beneficial and under meaningful human control.

We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. Given OpenAI’s breakneck shipping cadence and growth – and the expectation that it will only accelerate – our ability to architect automation systems and agentic workflows for scale is central to our ability to maintain exceptional support quality in the face of AGI.

About the Role

As a Support Vendor Manager, you will own the health, performance, and long-term scalability of multiple support partner and vendor relationships. This is a vendor leadership role first and foremost: you will drive commercial and operational accountability (SLAs, QBRs, escalation paths, remediation plans), while also building the operating model that enables support to scale without linear headcount growth.

You’ll collaborate closely with User Operations teams (e.g., Trust & Safety, Fraud & Risk), Systems/Tooling, Data partners, and Product/PM stakeholders as we launch new workflows and launch and scale new programs.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. 1-2 weeks of travel per quarter may be required.

You’ll be responsible for:

  • End-to-end vendor leadership: Own day-to-day oversight, relationship health, and executive-level accountability for multiple support vendors/BPOs.

  • 5+ years in vendor/BPO operations management, support operations, or partner performance leadership in a scaled environment.

title: Training: ML Framework Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Training Runtime designs the core distributed machine-learning training runtime that powers everything from early research experiments to frontier-scale model runs. With a dual mandate to accelerate researchers and enable frontier scale, we’re building a unified, modular runtime that meets researchers where they are and moves with them up the scaling curve.

Our work focuses on three pillars: high-performance, asynchronous, zero-copy tensor and optimizer-state-aware data movement; performant, high-uptime, fault-tolerant training frameworks (training loop, state management, resilient checkpointing, deterministic orchestration, and observability); and distributed process management for long-lived, job-specific and user-provided processes.

We integrate proven large-scale capabilities into a composable, developer-facing runtime so teams can iterate quickly and run reliably at any scale, partnering closely with model-stack, research, and platform teams. Success for us is measured by raising both training throughput (how fast models train) and researcher throughput (how fast ideas become experiments and products).

About the Role

As a Training: ML Framework Engineer, you will work on improving the training throughput for our internal training framework, while enabling researchers to experiment with new ideas.  This requires good engineering (for example designing, implementing, and optimizing state-of-the-art AI models), writing bug-free machine learning code (surprisingly difficult!), and acquiring deep knowledge of the performance of supercomputers. In all the projects this role pursues, the ultimate goal is to push the field forward.

We’re looking for people who love optimizing performance, understanding distributed systems, and who cannot stand having bugs in their code.  Since our training framework is used for large runs with massive numbers of GPUs, performance improvements here will have a large impact.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Apply the latest techniques in our internal training framework to achieve impressive hardware efficiency for our training runs

  • Profile and optimize our training framework

  • Work with researchers to enable them to develop the next generation of models

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have run small scale ML experiments

  • Love figuring out how systems work and continuously come up with ideas for how to make them faster while minimizing complexity and maintenance burden

  • Have strong software engineering skills and are proficient in Python

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

At OpenAI, our User Safety & Risk Operations (USRO) team helps protect our products and users from abuse, fraud, safety risks, and other forms of misuse. We translate real-world user and operational signals into timely decisions, practical interventions, and improvements to our products and systems.

This role will take on new, ambiguous, or underdeveloped operational risks and help mature them into scalable capabilities. We work across USRO and partner closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Product Policy, Legal, Safety, Support, and external vendors or partnership stakeholders.

About the Role

We are seeking a Senior Operations Analyst to take on complex, ambiguous safety and risk problems and turn them into practical operational solutions that can scale. This is a senior individual-contributor role for a versatile operator who is comfortable moving between queues, investigation, analysis, workflow design, hands-on execution, and cross-functional leadership. Depending on team needs, the role may focus on emerging-risk incubation, cloud deployment partnerships, or other new operational areas.

You will be expected to move quickly, work hands-on, and create structure without waiting for perfect requirements or a large support team. The work starts with the problem, not a prescribed process. You may investigate unstructured user signals, stand up a lightweight workflow, build an AI-assisted tool, improve an existing operation, or help a new launch become operationally ready. The goal is to produce durable systems that other people can run, not simply complete a series of individual tasks.

The portfolio will change with company priorities and may span established harm areas, emerging-risk incubation, cloud deployments and partnerships, device safety, or new product launches. Some hires may focus primarily on cloud deployment operations, including launch readiness, partner coordination, safety workflows, and operational monitoring. You will typically own a small number of high-impact problems at a time and will be expected to judge what needs to be built, what can stay lightweight, and when the work is ready to scale, transfer, or stop.

Location / work model: San Francisco, CA; hybrid, 3 days/week in-office.

Please note: This role may involve exposure to sensitive or concerning content. Strong discretion, good judgment, and resilience are essential.

  • Are highly data savvy, including the ability to make sense of messy qualitative or unstructured information and combine it with quantitative evidence.

  • Operate independently, make clear tradeoffs, and maintain momentum as priorities and requirements change.

title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer, Gov
descriptionHtml:
About the team

The OpenAI for Government team is a dynamic, mission-driven group leveraging frontier AI to transform how governments achieve their missions. Our team works to empower public servants with secure, compliant AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Gov) and mission-aligned deployments that meet government technical requirements with strong reliability and safety.

About the role

Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSEs) lead complex deployments of frontier models in production. You will embed with our most strategic government and public sector customers—where model performance matters, delivery is urgent, and ambiguity is the default. You’ll map their problems, structure delivery, and ship fast. This includes scoping, sequencing, and building full-stack solutions that create measurable value, while driving clarity across internal and external teams.

You will work directly with defense, intelligence, and federal stakeholders as their technical thought partner, guiding adoption, maximizing mission impact, and ensuring successful deployments at scale. Along the way, you’ll identify reusable patterns, codify best practices, and share field signal that influences OpenAI’s roadmap.

This role is based in Washington DC, Seattle or San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required, including on-site work with customers.

In this role you will

  • Own technical delivery across multiple government deployments, from first prototype to stable production.

  • Deeply embed with public sector customers to design and build novel applications powered by OpenAI models.

  • Enable successful deployments across customer environments by delivering observable systems spanning infrastructure through applications.

  • Prototype and build full-stack systems using Python, JavaScript, or comparable stacks that deliver real mission impact.

  • Proactively guide customers on maximizing business and operational value from their applications.

  • Forge and manage relationships with customer leadership and stakeholders, ensuring successful deployment and scale.

  • Scope work, sequence delivery, and remove blockers early—making trade-offs between scope, speed, and quality.

  • Contribute directly in the code when clarity or momentum depends on it.

  • Codify working patterns into tools, playbooks, or building blocks others can use.

  • Share field feedback with Research and Product to influence model and product development.

  • Keep teams moving through clarity, judgment, and consistent follow-through.

  • Bring 5+ years of engineering or technical deployment experience, ideally in customer-facing or government environments.

  • Active TS/SCI clearance or equivalent

  • Have scoped and delivered complex systems in fast-moving or ambiguous contexts.

  • Write and review production-grade code across frontend and backend, using Python, JavaScript, or similar stacks.

  • Are familiar with cloud deployment models (Azure, AWS), Kubernetes, Terraform, and related infrastructure.

  • Have experience building or deploying systems powered by LLMs or generative models, and understand how model behavior affects product experience.

  • Simplify complexity, make fast, sound decisions under pressure, and communicate clearly across technical and non-technical audiences.

title: Motion Design Producer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

About the Role

OpenAI’s in-house Creative Team is looking for a Motion Design Producer to help shape and scale how our brand comes to life through motion design across every touchpoint — from identity systems and campaigns to product, web, and comms work.

You’ll partner closely with our Brand Identity & Brand Design leadership to manage intake, resourcing, timelines, and creative workflows — ensuring design projects move seamlessly from concept to delivery. You’ll serve as the operational backbone of the design practice, building clarity and momentum across a growing cross-functional team. As Motion Design is a shared function in Creative Design, you will also partner closely with other production functional ecosystems to deliver motion design support.

This is a highly collaborative role that requires both strategic oversight and hands-on execution. You’ll be a key connector across Marketing, Product, Comms, and Web — driving alignment, enabling great design, and creating the systems that keep our creative work consistent, efficient, and impactful.

In this role, you will:

  • Manage Day-to-day Motion Design Operations: Oversee the end-to-end management of design projects — from scoping and prioritization to delivery — ensuring resources, timelines, and dependencies are well-planned and communicated.

  • Produce High-Priority Motion Projects: Serve as a hands-on individual contributor (IC) on large, high-priority motion projects, owning production from kickoff through delivery.

  • Shape Intake & Resourcing: Partner with creative and marketing, creative, production and ops leads to evaluate new requests, define scope, and allocate design capacity across internal and external partners.

  • Build Cross-Functional Alignment: Act as the connective tissue between design and partner teams (Product, Web, Brand, Comms, and GTM), ensuring design work ladders up to broader strategic goals.

  • Elevate Systems & Process: Design and implement operational frameworks that enable the design team to scale effectively — from creative reviews and feedback loops to asset tracking and tool optimization.

  • Manage External Partners: Oversee relationships with design vendors, freelancers, and production partners; ensure output meets OpenAI’s creative and technical standards.

  • Uphold Craft & Consistency: Partner with the Brand Identity and Brand Design team to ensure design work is cohesive, high-quality, and reflective of OpenAI’s evolving visual identity.

You might thrive in this role if you:

title: Head of Enterprise Risk Management
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The OpenAI Risk & Audit team is building an enterprise risk capability for a company operating at the frontier of AI. We help leaders identify, understand, and manage the risks that matter most while enabling responsible innovation and durable growth.

We are developing a modern enterprise risk management (ERM) program and the technology foundation that powers it. Our work connects risk strategy, governance, compliance, and assurance with high-quality data, automated workflows, continuous monitoring, and AI-enabled analysis.

We partner across Finance, Security, Legal, Engineering, Product, People, Operations, and Internal Audit, and provide clear reporting to senior leadership and the Board. We aim to make risk ownership practical, decision-useful, and embedded in how OpenAI builds and scales.

About the Role

As the Head of Enterprise Risk Management, you will help build and lead an integrated ERM program and the ERM platform that supports it. You will establish common risk language, governance, and decision processes while translating them into scalable systems, data products, and workflows.

You will own enterprise risk assessments, maintain a centralized risk register, develop risk appetite and key risk indicators, and help leaders evaluate significant changes such as new products, markets, partnerships, major systems, and strategic investments.

This is a senior individual contributor role for a hands-on leader who will build our ERM capability from the ground up, with the potential to build and lead a team over time. You will work with technical and business teams to connect source systems, improve data quality, automate evidence and control monitoring, and use AI to surface emerging risks and accelerate analysis.

You will also help create a strong risk culture, coordinate assurance across the three lines, and communicate complex issues with clarity and sound judgment. This is an opportunity to build a next-generation capability from the ground up.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and evolve OpenAI’s enterprise risk management framework, including risk taxonomy, governance standards, risk appetite, escalation thresholds, and mitigation expectations.

  • Lead enterprise risk assessments and maintain a centralized, decision-useful risk register that reflects strategic, financial, operational, technology, security, compliance, and emerging risks.

  • Establish key risk indicators, continuous-monitoring capabilities, and executive dashboards that translate complex data into clear signals, trends, and actions.

  • Enable risk-informed change governance for new products, markets, partnerships, acquisitions, major systems, and other high-impact initiatives.

  • Lead effective governance forums working cross-functionally with key partners such as Compliance, Finance, Security and others, and prepare concise reporting for senior leadership and the Board.

  • Define the strategy and roadmap for a modern ERM platform that will connect with systems across the enterprise including identity, finance, HR, ticketing, code, and others through reliable integrations and shared data models.

  • Apply automation, policy-as-code, data analytics, and AI-assisted workflows to evidence collection, control monitoring, issue management, risk analysis, and audit or regulatory responses.

  • Coordinate risk activities across Finance, Security, Legal, Compliance, Engineering, Operations, and Internal Audit, clarifying ownership and reducing duplication across the three lines of defense.

  • Build, coach, and lead a high-performing team, strengthen first-line ownership, and foster a culture of practical risk management, curiosity, accountability, and continuous improvement.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 12+ years of experience across enterprise or operational risk, compliance, internal audit, security governance, finance, or related fields, including significant experience leading ERM or GRC programs.

  • A track record of building or materially scaling an enterprise risk program in a fast-growing, technology-driven, or otherwise complex global organization.

  • Strong command of ERM and assurance practices, including risk appetite, risk assessments, KRIs, controls, issue management, and the three-lines model; familiarity with frameworks such as COSO or ISO/IEC 27001/27017/27018/27701/42001.

  • Experience advising executives and presenting risk information to senior governance bodies, with the judgment to make complex tradeoffs clear and actionable.

  • Technical fluency with GRC platforms, data architecture, APIs, system integrations, cloud environments, and automated workflows; experience with infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD, or policy-as-code is a plus.

  • Experience using data analytics, automation, or AI-enabled tools to improve risk sensing, evidence analysis, control monitoring, and reporting.

  • The ability to connect strategic, financial, operational, technology, security, and compliance risks and to work effectively across technical and non-technical teams.

  • Demonstrated success hiring, coaching, and developing multidisciplinary teams while operating effectively in ambiguity and at high velocity.

  • A relevant bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience; credentials such as CIA, CPA, CISA, CRMA, CRM, or an advanced business, legal, or technical degree are valued.

title: Growth Product Marketing Manager, SMB & B2B Self-Serve
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure the responsible and widespread adoption of artificial intelligence. In support of that mission, the SMB Marketing team helps small and medium-sized businesses understand and adopt ChatGPT Business and OpenAI’s B2B solutions. We build a deep understanding of business owners and teams, shape relevant product narratives, and drive awareness, adoption, and growth.

We take a data-driven approach to understand SMB audiences, uncover customer needs, and translate AI capabilities into practical business value. We partner closely with Growth, Product Marketing, Sales, Partnerships, Product, Research, Communications, and Design to deliver a cohesive customer experience across discovery, evaluation, purchase, adoption, and expansion.

About the Role

We are hiring a Growth Product Marketing Manager to turn product-led growth priorities into clear audience strategies, compelling cross-channel messaging, coordinated go-to-market programs, and drive measurable, incremental growth.

You will partner closely with Growth Product, Consumer & SMB Product Marketing, Lifecycle, Performance Marketing, Brand, Creative, Research, Data Science, and International Marketing to ensure that full-funnel campaigns and initiatives are supported and connected to Growth capabilities and maximize the performance of these campaigns.

In this role, you will:

  • Build the marketing layer across the SMB & B2B Self Serve Growth roadmap: acquisition, access, activation and resurrection, monetization, and the shared Growth Platform.

  • Translate product hypotheses into audience insights, positioning, messaging, launch briefs, lifecycle journeys, landing-page narratives, performance creative, and in-product education.

  • Maintain an integrated plan that connects the Growth product roadmap to the consumer product marketing calendar across lifecycle, performance, social, creators, partnerships, and brand moments.

  • Serve as the subject matter expert across all Growth levers, advising teams across the organization on the most effective ways to integrate Growth into their initiatives.

  • Partner with cross-functional teams to design and interrogate the user journey so we can align our external promises with in-product and owned-channel landing, access, onboarding, continuation, and conversion experiences.

  • Create audience and market playbooks for new users, high-value, or at-risk cohorts, including where acquisition headroom, access friction, weak Week 1 continuation, churn, or monetization gaps are greatest.

  • Turn campaign, lifecycle, research, and product data into clear readouts that improve both marketing execution and future product prioritization.

  • Use AI-enabled workflows to increase research, synthesis, briefing, and iteration speed while maintaining judgment, quality, and user trust.

You might thrive in this role if you are/have:

  • 8-10 years of SMB/B2B Self Serve experience in product marketing, growth marketing, lifecycle marketing, consumer marketing, or a related role; equivalent project experience is welcome.

  • Evidence that you can turn customer or market insight into clear positioning, messaging, and practical execution.

  • Experience supporting a launch, onboarding journey, lifecycle program, conversion initiative, or growth experiment and learning from the results.

  • Comfort working with funnels, cohorts, experiments, and metrics—and knowing when the data does not prove causality.

About the Team

OpenAI’s Procurement team makes working with the world easy, fast, and safe. We connect supplier readiness, purchasing, invoicing, and payment so teams can move with confidence as OpenAI scales. Accounts Payable and Supplier Master Data Operations provide the trusted data, dependable execution, and financial discipline behind that experience.

About the Role

OpenAI’s compute infrastructure depends on controlled execution of significant supplier spend. As Senior Manager, Accounts Payable — Compute, you will own payment readiness and material exceptions across large-value, business-critical obligations. Complex agreements evolve through amendments to pricing, capacity, service credits, billing mechanics, legal entities, and payment schedules. You will translate approved obligations into accurate, timely payments while navigating supplier disputes, late approvals, close deadlines, and cross-system dependencies.

We’re looking for a hands-on technical and operational leader who can interpret complex payment terms, reconcile financial data, diagnose system failures, and build scalable workflows. Coordinating across multiple Compute Finance and Accounting teams is a core responsibility: you will establish decision owners, align deadlines, and move interdependent work forward in parallel. You will set the compute AP operating plan and lead delivery with Procurement, Treasury, Tax, Finance Systems, and existing processing teams, with measurable improvements in controls, service, and capacity.

Location: This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the compute invoice-to-payment operating plan, prioritize material exceptions, and lead supplier escalations across complex, high-value obligations and tight payment deadlines.

  • Interpret executed contracts and approved amendments affecting pricing, capacity, credits, billing mechanics, entities, and payment schedules; translate them into invoice-validation, PO/change-order, approval, control, and payment requirements.

  • Personally investigate discrepancies, supplier disputes, missing credits, duplicate risks, and PO coverage gaps. Trace records, field mappings, approval statuses, and sync failures across procurement and ERP systems; resolve root causes with accountable Finance, Procurement, supplier, and Systems partners.

  • Lead a payment-readiness cadence across Compute Finance and Accounting teams, consolidate the complete obligation and payment view, and resolve dependencies across charge validation, PO coverage, approvals, funding, and close. Track decision owners, deadlines, blockers, and escalation paths so material payments move forward as approval lands.

  • Confirm supplier, site, entity, tax, payment-method, and approval readiness with the relevant owners before payment release.

  • Coordinate funding forecasts and close-period payments with Treasury; reconcile invoice aging, payment registers, and bank/settlement evidence to support Accounting’s completeness and cutoff conclusions.

  • Design matching tolerances, validation rules, exception routing, evidence requirements, and escalation thresholds with control and accounting partners, preserving independent verification and segregation of duties.

  • Map compute workload and usable capacity by task and complexity, assign eligible work across employees, contractors, and shared-service teams, and maintain trained backups and close coverage. Coach task owners and backups, strengthen execution standards, and build greater team autonomy.

  • Set a prioritized improvement roadmap tied to compute business needs. Own requirements and acceptance criteria for workflow and AI improvements; lead operational testing and adoption with Finance Systems and Enablement, verify reconciliation and fallback, and measure service, risk, and verified capacity outcomes.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Bring 8+ years in AP, payments, or related finance operations, or equivalent experience, with personal ownership of complex, high-value supplier obligations and material exceptions from executed contract through invoice approval, payment, and settlement.

  • Bring strong judgment on controls, segregation of duties, supplier verification, reconciliations, and close support in an audited environment.

  • Can interpret complex pricing, capacity, credit, billing, and payment terms and translate contract amendments into executable workflows, matching rules, and clear decision ownership.

  • Have led coordination across multiple finance and accounting teams on material payments, reconciled competing priorities and deadlines, and established clear decisions, handoffs, and escalation paths with suppliers and partners.

  • Have independently led cross-functional operating improvements and delivery teams, built demand-and-capacity plans, maintained peak and backup coverage, and demonstrated measurable results while staying close to execution.

  • Can independently reconcile large financial datasets using advanced spreadsheets or comparable analytical tools, establish complete populations and control totals, and diagnose ERP workflow, data, and integration failures. Oracle Fusion and Zip experience is helpful.

Can translate business and control requirements into testable workflows and lead UAT, with human review, exception handling, reconciliation, fallback, and ongoing monitoring.

title: Principal Software Engineer, Productivity
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Connector Ecosystem team builds the platform and product experiences that let people extend ChatGPT and Codex. We work on plugins, skills, connectors, interactive apps, and open standards like the Model Context Protocol (MCP). We make plugins easy to discover, install, and use, ensure they’re invoked at the right time, and help people find new ways to get value from them.

We want anyone to be able to turn a useful workflow into a plugin, share it, and have other people use it. A plugin can package instructions and skills with connections to the tools and data it needs. Our work spans creation and publishing, reliable execution across our products, clear permissions and approvals, and the controls admins need to bring plugins to their organizations. We work closely with research to improve tool quality as models evolve.

About the Role

We’re looking for a product-minded Principal Software Engineer to set technical direction, build the systems behind plugins, and improve how models use them. Depending on your focus, you may scale generalist infrastructure and identity-related integrations across products, improve plugin quality at the intersection of backend engineering and applied AI, or work on the product experience itself to drive plugin usage. You’ll lead complex initiatives across teams and own problems from diagnosis and design through implementation and release.

You’ll remain hands-on while driving product and design decisions alongside Product, Design, Research, and engineering partners. You’ll help shape what we build and how it works, translate user and developer needs into clear priorities, and guide technical decisions that balance rapid iteration with long-term reliability and maintainability.

This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In This Role, You Will

  • Set technical direction and lead complex initiatives across the Plugin Ecosystem, aligning architecture and execution across teams.

  • Drive product and design decisions with cross-functional partners, helping define priorities and shape intuitive experiences for users and developers.

  • Design and ship APIs, SDKs, and services that developers use to extend ChatGPT and Codex.

  • Build intuitive experiences that help users discover, install, and use plugins to get more done.

  • Make plugins easier to create, test, publish, update, and share.

  • Improve when and how models use plugins, from choosing the right plugin to completing a task. Work with Research to diagnose failures and measure improvements as models evolve.

  • Improve plugin reliability and interaction quality across ChatGPT and Codex, including interactive apps, with clear error messages and recovery paths.

  • Build consistent permissions, approvals, and admin controls that help individuals and organizations confidently adopt plugins.

  • Work with developers and partners to turn recurring problems into improvements to the platform, tooling, and documentation.

  • Collaborate across engineering, Product, Research, Security, and Trust & Safety to scale plugin infrastructure and deliver safe, reliable execution.

  • Raise the engineering bar through mentorship, thoughtful code reviews, and clear technical guidance.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

  • Have 10+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of building and shipping products or platforms that people and developers rely on.

  • Have led complex technical initiatives across teams and driven product and design decisions in close partnership with product managers and designers.

  • Care about product quality and can make complex capabilities feel intuitive, from discovering a useful plugin to completing a task with it.

  • Have strong opinions about APIs and abstractions, and can explain the tradeoffs behind your decisions. Experience with identity, permissions, or integration-heavy systems is especially valuable.

  • Enjoy talking with users and developers, understanding what they’re trying to accomplish, and turning recurring problems into product and platform improvements.

  • Can move between product questions and technical details, collaborate across teams, and take an ambiguous problem through to production.

  • Are comfortable working across web interfaces and backend systems. Experience building applied AI systems, diagnosing model–tool interactions, and measuring reliability and quality is especially valuable.

title: AI Systems Engineer, Codex Agents
descriptionHtml:
AI Systems Engineer - Codex Core Agents


About The Team
The Codex Core Agents team builds the agent harness that turns model capability into real-world action. We own the systems around the model: prompting and interpreting model outputs, executing actions safely in real environments, and feeding production experience back into better models and better agent behavior.
This team sits close to research and works across the stack: harness, model interaction, inference, sandboxed execution, orchestration, evals, production reliability, and the performance envelope around tokens, latency, cost, capacity, and quality. The harness is open source and increasingly part of how models are trained and evaluated, making this one of the highest-leverage layers in Codex.

About The Role
We’re looking for engineers to build the AI systems that make Codex agents dependable in production. The ideal candidate is an agent-systems builder: hands-on across low-level systems and ML workflows, able to debug Codex behavior end to end across the harness, model behavior, inference/runtime stack, GPU fleet, and product surface.

You’ll work with research, infrastructure, and product to design agent harness capabilities, run experiments and ablations across the model + system prompt + harness stack, build frameworks for assessing production agent performance, and turn messy failures into durable improvements.


What You’ll Do

  • Design and build the core agent harness and execution loop that lets Codex agents interpret model outputs, use tools, execute code, and complete long-horizon tasks safely.

  • Build sandboxing, isolation, orchestration, state, and workflow infrastructure for agents operating in real development environments.

  • Develop evaluation, experimentation, and debugging systems that distinguish harness issues, model behavior, inference/runtime issues, and product failures.

  • Run ablations across prompts, model-facing interfaces, context construction, tool-use strategies, and harness behavior to improve solve rate, reliability, latency, and cost.

  • Improve observability, profiling, and diagnostics across the agent stack, from backend systems to inference, GPUs, and fleet capacity.

  • Work closely with research to make the harness trainable, measurable, and useful for improving frontier agentic models.

  • Build shared primitives that make Codex faster, safer, more reliable, and easier for other teams and open-source users to build on.

    You Might Be A Good Fit If You

  • Have built or operated production systems in distributed systems, infrastructure, developer tooling, sandboxing, virtualization, cloud platforms, or ML systems.

  • Enjoy working across layers: Rust systems code, Python configuration layers, APIs, agent orchestration, evals, logs/traces, inference behavior, runtime constraints, and user outcomes.

  • Have hands-on experience with LLM applications, coding agents, evals, model deployment, inference, compiler/runtime performance, or developer platforms.

  • Care deeply about reliability, safety, performance, debuggability, and clean abstractions.

  • Can debug from evidence and move quickly from ambiguous production failures to practical, durable fixes.

  • Want to work close to research while still shipping changes to production

  • Still write meaningful code, show strong ownership, and can lead scoped or multi-team AI systems work.


Bonus Points

  • Deep Rust, systems, sandboxing, isolation, or low-level platform experience.

  • Experience with coding agents, agent harnesses, tool-using LLM systems, model evals, or post-training feedback loops.

  • Background in compilers, kernels, runtimes, inference optimization, GPU systems, benchmarking, profiling, or performance engineering.

  • Experience building production infrastructure used by many engineers or users under demanding reliability and security constraints.

  • Open-source infrastructure or developer-platform work with strong taste for APIs and usability.

title: Technical Program Manager, Global Infrastructure Planning
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Compute Infrastructure team runs the GPU fleet and large compute clusters that support OpenAI’s research, ChatGPT, and the API. Our work spans GPUs, CPUs, storage, networking, and cloud infrastructure, bringing these systems together so teams can train and serve models at scale.

We seek to learn from deployment and distribute the benefits of AI, while ensuring that this powerful tool is used responsibly and safely. Safety is more important to us than unfettered growth.

About the Role

You will own CPU capacity planning and management across Research and Compute. Working with infrastructure owners, you will lead integrated planning for CPU, storage, and network capacity across OpenAI’s global fleet. You will connect workload demand and GPU deployment plans with the foundational resources required to support pretraining, research, and application infrastructure at scale.

You will work closely with workload owners, infrastructure engineering, network deployment teams, Finance, and cloud providers to turn forecasts into supply and allocation plans. You will understand workload architecture, guide decisions when capacity is constrained, and drive opportunities to improve utilization and reduce waste. Your work will span planning over multiple years and ongoing capacity management across regions and providers, including AWS, GCP, Azure, and OCI.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead CPU demand planning across Research, Compute, and application infrastructure, including foundational services, data acquisition, container platforms, robotics, and services supporting GPU clusters. Maintain forecasts that capture workload growth, regional and hardware requirements, timing, and acceptable alternatives.

  • Translate workload growth and GPU fleet plans into integrated CPU, storage, and network requirements. Partner with engineering to determine the capacity, throughput, bandwidth, connectivity, and placement needed to support pretraining and applications at scale.

  • Reconcile current and incoming supply with demand, model constrained scenarios, and drive allocation and prioritization decisions. Lead CPU allocation planning and fulfillment, including quota transfers, rebalancing, and reclaims.

  • Partner with network engineering and deployment teams to translate regional demand into bandwidth and connectivity plans, ordering inputs, and delivery milestones. Coordinate CPU and network allocations as capacity is deployed across the fleet.

  • Understand workload architecture and performance requirements well enough to challenge assumptions and influence technical decisions. Help teams evaluate resource sizing, regional placement, data movement, storage choices, and acceptable alternatives when supply is constrained.

  • Drive fleet efficiency programs that reclaim unused capacity, rightsize workloads, modernize infrastructure, and improve placement or resource sharing. Measure the capacity released and cost improvements while preserving workload performance and reliability.

  • Scale integrated capacity planning across CPU, storage, and network in partnership with resource owners. Improve demand intake, forecasts, scenario models, inventory and allocation records, and the tools that automate recurring workflows.

  • Partner with cloud providers, Finance, Procurement, and engineering to shape capacity orders, commitments, and renewal decisions. Evaluate regional availability, delivery lead times, cost, and technical fit, and drive resolution of supply gaps.

  • Align capacity plans with cluster and application deployment milestones. Work across infrastructure owners to ensure CPU, storage, and network dependencies are ready when workloads need them, and resolve gaps that would delay usable capacity.

  • Give teams and leadership a clear view of demand, supply, allocation tradeoffs, forecast changes, and risks. Turn ambiguous or competing needs into decisions, accountable owners, and executable plans.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 5+ years of experience in technical program management, capacity planning, capacity engineering, or infrastructure management, with ownership of complex programs at scale.

  • Have directly managed demand forecasting, supply planning, allocations, and capacity operations for CPU or cloud compute infrastructure. You understand how forecasts, inventory, quotas, delivery schedules, and utilization inform capacity decisions.

  • Bring technical depth in one or more infrastructure domains and can reason across the dependencies among CPUs, GPUs, storage, and networks.

  • Understand how workload architecture drives CPU and memory needs, storage capacity and throughput, network bandwidth and latency, and regional placement. You can use that knowledge to influence engineering decisions.

  • Have worked across multiple cloud providers and understand how provider capabilities, quotas, regional constraints, and commercial commitments affect capacity plans.

  • Have built or improved capacity planning tools, data models, or automation. You are comfortable working directly with data to validate assumptions, model scenarios, and measure outcomes.

  • Have delivered measurable improvements in infrastructure utilization or cost through reclaims, rightsizing, modernization, workload placement, or other efficiency programs.

  • Can lead decisions across engineering, research, product, Finance, and external providers, balancing technical requirements, delivery risk, and cost. You communicate clearly with both working teams and leadership.

  • Are resourceful in ambiguous environments, take ownership of outcomes, and build simple processes that continue to work as the fleet grows.

  • Are interested in and thoughtful about the impacts of AGI.

title: Dedicated Support Engineering Lead
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s User Operations team shepherds our customers’ adoption of AI and ensures that our customers' product experience is nothing short of exceptional.We are building the very first post-AGI support team.We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others, to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises.

Within Premium Support, Dedicated Support Engineers combine deep technical troubleshooting with an enduring understanding of our most strategic customers’ architectures, critical workloads, and business priorities. Through proactive reliability work, ownership during incidents, and AI-powered support capabilities, we help customers operate successfully as their use of OpenAI grows.

 

About the Role

We are looking for a leader to build and develop a team of Dedicated Support Engineers supporting OpenAI’s most strategic enterprise customers. Reporting to the Head of Dedicated Support Engineering, you will lead a team expected to include approximately 10–15 engineers. Your team will work directly with customers and partner with Product, Engineering, and field teams to resolve complex technical problems and help customers run critical artificial intelligence workloads reliably.

You will combine people leadership with strong technical judgment, guiding challenging investigations and customer escalations while coaching engineers to make sound decisions independently. Beyond resolving incidents, you will help the team develop a deep understanding of customers’ architectures and business priorities, identify recurring risks, and turn those insights into proactive reliability work and product improvements.

You will shape how the team operates as it grows: establishing account ownership, planning capacity and coverage, building shared knowledge, and improving playbooks and handoffs. Working with the function head, you will contribute to reliable, round-the-clock support coverage and broader service improvements, including carefully tested artificial intelligence and automation that increase quality and capacity.

The ideal candidate brings technical depth, a record of developing experienced engineers, and the ability to build effective teams and operating practices in a rapidly changing environment.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role you will:

  • Hire, coach, and develop experienced engineers, with clear expectations for performance, customer ownership, and independent decision-making.

  • Plan account coverage and team capacity, balancing customer support with proactive reliability work and preparation for critical events.

  • Guide technical investigations and customer escalations, coordinate with Engineering, and verify that the customer’s problem is resolved.

  • Use customer issues and service data to improve playbooks, reduce recurring problems, and inform Product and Engineering priorities.

  • Build and test artificial intelligence and automation improvements, with quality checks, human oversight, and measurable results.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 10+ years of relevant technical customer experience, including 5+ years of people leadership in Support Engineering, Technical Account Management, or a comparable team.

  • Have directly managed experienced engineers supporting strategic enterprise customers, with evidence of effective coaching, delegation, and performance management.

  • Bring technical depth in application programming interfaces, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise integrations, with sound judgment during complex investigations.

  • Build trusted customer relationships and work across teams to resolve competing priorities, clarify ownership, and follow through on commitments.

title: Applied AI Engineer, Codex
descriptionHtml:
About the team

The Applied AI Engineering team helps enterprises put Codex to work on their most important engineering workflows. We work alongside customer engineers to turn frontier AI capabilities into systems that improve how software is built, shipped, secured, and operated.

Our work spans unfamiliar codebases, legacy systems, data pipelines, infrastructure, and enterprise integrations. We discover where AI can make a meaningful difference, build and prove solutions, and turn what we learn into reusable architectures, tools, and feedback that help shape Codex.

About the Role

We’re looking for an engineer who enjoys understanding complex systems, building alongside customers, and solving problems where the path forward isn’t obvious.

You’ll work directly with technical leaders and engineers to identify valuable opportunities and take them from discovery through implementation and evaluation. You might build a Codex-assisted release review workflow, modernize a legacy data pipeline, accelerate a dependency migration, or connect an agent to the systems and context it needs to investigate production incidents.

You’ll combine hands-on software engineering, architecture, and technical leadership to make Codex part of how customers get important work done. Success means delivering the agreed solution, demonstrating measurable improvement, and helping the customer sustain and expand its use. Working with our product, engineering, research, and account teams, you’ll turn deployment experience into evidence that informs improvements to Codex.

The position is based in Sydney, Australia, with three office days each week. Relocation assistance is available to new employees.

 

In this role, you will:

  • Lead customer engineering engagements from workflow discovery and architecture through implementation, evaluation, and handoff, with clear customer owners, delivery milestones, and measurable success criteria.

  • Assess customer repositories, data systems, infrastructure, security controls, and development practices to understand constraints, determine readiness, and identify where Codex can have the greatest impact.

  • Build and validate workflows alongside customer engineers, developing integrations, tool gateways, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, and automations, often using Codex in your own development process.

  • Establish baselines, quality and security guardrails, and evaluation methods that demonstrate whether a workflow is reliable, useful, and ready to expand.

  • Turn customer engagements into reusable tools, architectures, and deployment patterns, and translate recurring challenges into actionable feedback for product, engineering, and research teams.

  • Document technical decisions and results for handoff and reuse, establishing clear customer, partner, or delivery-team ownership for production release, ongoing operation, and maintenance.

  • Use evidence to recommend when to expand a workflow, redirect an engagement, or stop work when value or feasibility cannot be demonstrated.

You’ll thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 5+ years of relevant experience in software development, deployment engineering, data or infrastructure engineering, technical consulting, or solutions architecture.

  • Can build, debug, and evaluate production-relevant software and quickly understand unfamiliar systems.

  • Actively use AI coding tools, have adapted them to your own work, and have a clear perspective on how agents can automate complete workflows.

  • Bring technical depth in one or more areas, such as software engineering, data systems, cloud infrastructure, or enterprise integrations, and enjoy learning across disciplines.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

We are looking for an embedded engineer to help build firmware and associated modeling software for OpenAI’s in house AI accelerator. This role involves designing and developing drivers and functional models for a large array of HW components, writing high throughput and low latency firmware code, investigating bring-up and production issues.

Responsibilities
