title: Software Engineer, Infrastructure - Analytics Platform
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Platform Analytics team builds the systems OpenAI researchers use to understand the quality and behavior of the models we train including what models are doing, why they behave in a particular way, and how that behavior changes across experiments.

Neptune is a core part of this work. It ingests, stores, queries, and visualizes large volumes of metrics from pretraining, post-training, and reinforcement learning. Hundreds of researchers depend on these systems in their daily work to compare experiments, debug unexpected behavior, and decide what to try next.

Our scope is broader than metrics. We also build platforms that help researchers analyze samples, traces, evaluation results, and other structured or unstructured data through dashboards, APIs, and increasingly agent-driven workflows. These systems need to remain fast, reliable, and understandable as the scale and complexity of research change quickly.

We are not trying to become a consulting team that builds a separate solution for every research project. We work directly with researchers to understand recurring problems, then turn them into reusable infrastructure and platform capabilities that many teams can build on.

About the Role

We’re looking for a hands-on experienced software engineer who can take ownership of a critical system and drive it from problem definition through production adoption.

This person should be able to own a platform such as CacheHouse end to end: define its technical direction, design its data model and storage architecture, integrate it with several research dashboards and workflows, guide one or two engineers, and ensure the system works reliably for its users.

The right candidate should already bring the technical judgment, ownership, and execution expected at this level. The primary learning curve should be OpenAI’s stack and research problem space, not learning how to lead a complex engineering effort or deliver a production system.

You will work directly with researchers and the engineers supporting them. You’ll need to understand what users are actually trying to accomplish, distinguish the underlying problem from a proposed feature, and translate recurring needs into simple, durable platform components.

In This Role, You Will

  • Own critical systems across architecture, implementation, integrations, deployment, monitoring, adoption, and whatever else is required to make them useful.

  • Design, build, and operate the ingestion, storage, retrieval, and query systems behind research analytics at OpenAI.

  • Build platforms for analyzing both structured metrics and unstructured research data, including samples, traces, evaluation results, and model-behavior data.

  • Reason below typical service abstractions about algorithms, data structures, concurrency, storage layout, distributed systems, query performance, and failure modes.

  • Make architectural tradeoffs across ingestion-time processing, data models, storage formats, indexing, query execution, caching, and visualization performance.

  • Work directly with researchers to understand what they are trying to learn, ask the right questions, and challenge a requested solution when a simpler or more effective approach exists.

  • Recognize when several teams are solving the same problem and turn those patterns into shared infrastructure, APIs, platform components, or agent-driven workflows.

  • Write code, investigate production issues, make realistic estimates, guide other engineers, and think through testing, rollout, observability, and rollback.

  • Keep solutions as simple as the problem allows. Introduce complexity only when correctness, scale, latency, or reliability genuinely require it, and address the largest bottleneck first.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

  • Have owned a critical distributed system or research platform end to end and can explain how you took it from an ambiguous problem to reliable production adoption.

  • Have experience with high performing programing languages (Rust or C++), including performance profiling, concurrency, async execution, memory behavior, serialization, I/O, networking, and failure analysis.

  • Bring deep expertise in at least one relevant area such as distributed databases, storage engines, analytics systems, telemetry, logging, search, ingestion, or query execution.

  • Can reason carefully about partitioning, replication, consistency, retries, backpressure, event lineage, duplicate or delayed data, overload, migrations, and failure isolation.

  • Have experience with ClickHouse or similar OLAP, columnar, time-series, or high-throughput analytical systems. Direct ClickHouse experience is helpful but not required.

  • Bring strong computer science fundamentals and algorithmic reasoning. Competitive-programming experience is welcome but not required.

  • Already use coding agents regularly and have opinions about how AI tools change software development, product interfaces, and engineering leverage.

  • Enjoy working directly with researchers and other highly technical users: understanding their constraints, debugging ambiguous problems, explaining tradeoffs, and closing the loop after shipping.

  • Have the judgment to focus on the largest practical bottleneck rather than expanding every project into a complete platform rewrite.

  • Are a strong engineer first. Clear communication and business judgment are non-negotiable, but your credibility comes from building and operating systems that work.

Why This Work Matters

Researchers need reliable ways to understand model quality, behavior, and reasoning across frontier training and evaluation workflows. When analytics are slow, unavailable, or unable to express a new question, research slows with them.

The systems you build will help researchers move from raw metrics, samples, traces, and model outputs to useful understanding. Better latency, reliability, and reusable platform capabilities can compound across hundreds of researchers and many of OpenAI’s most important research efforts.

title: Deployment Lead (DL), FDE - Seoul
descriptionHtml:
About the team

OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team partners with customers to turn research breakthroughs into production systems. We operate at the intersection of customer delivery and core platform development.

 

About the Role

This is a founding role. As Korea’s first Deployment Lead (DL), you’ll lead some of OpenAI’s most strategic AI engagements from the first executive conversation through production and adoption. You’ll work with executive sponsors to understand what they want to change, spend time with the people who do the work today, and partner with engineers to test what’s feasible. Alongside the account director, you’ll turn what you learn into a case for investment and a deployment plan both teams can commit to.

You will own delivery end-to-end: embedding with customers to map workflows and success criteria, ensuring components ship on time, and leading readiness and change management for adoption. You’ll track progress, manage dependencies, make sequencing decisions, and drive 0→1 prototypes through MVP and scale. You will also share field insights with Product and Research to guide roadmap and priorities.

Success will be measured first and foremost by impact - deployments that deliver measurable value against customer goals, drive adoption, and become critical to their workflows. Additional measures of success include delivery reliability (milestones hit), operating leverage (patterns reused across deployments), judgment under pressure, and product impact (field signal that shifts roadmaps).

This is a high-trust, high-autonomy role. Success requires deep technical project management expertise, extreme ownership of outcomes, and an ability to immerse in customer workflows and partner with customer teams to solve complex engineering problems at pace.

 

This role is based in Seoul. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance.

 

IIn this role, you will:

  • Scope and win strategic customer engagements partnering with the account director. Work with customer teams and engineers to prioritize what to build and map the path to production. Turn those choices into a phased proposal defining each side’s commitments, what phase one must prove, and when to expand.

  • Own value cases and ROI. Set impact hypotheses, baselines, and KPIs; run pre/post deployment measurement and report to exec sponsors.

  • Own the technical delivery plan for multiple work streams. Translate business objectives into a roadmap with milestones, dependencies, and acceptance criteria. Run day-to-day engineering execution and keep progress unblocked.

OpenAI's Legal team plays a crucial role in furthering OpenAI's mission by tackling innovative, fundamental legal issues in AI. title: Software Engineer, Plugin Ecosystem
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Plugin Ecosystem team builds the platform and product experiences that let people extend ChatGPT and Codex. We work on plugins, skills, connectors, interactive apps, and open standards like the Model Context Protocol (MCP). We make plugins easy to discover, install, and use, ensure they’re invoked at the right time, and help people find new ways to get value from them.

We want anyone to be able to turn a useful workflow into a plugin, share it, and have other people use it. A plugin can package instructions and skills with connections to the tools and data it needs. Our work spans creation and publishing, reliable execution across our products, clear permissions and approvals, and the controls admins need to bring plugins to their organizations. We work closely with research to improve plugin quality as models evolve.

About the Role

We’re looking for product-minded engineers to build the systems behind plugins and improve how models use them. Depending on your focus, you may scale generalist infrastructure and identity-related integrations across products, or improve plugin quality at the intersection of backend engineering and applied AI or work on the product experience itself to drive plugin usage. You’ll work across teams and own problems from diagnosis and design through implementation and release.

This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and ship APIs, SDKs, and services that developers use to extend ChatGPT and Codex.

  • Build intuitive experiences that help users discover, install, and use plugins to get more done.

  • Make plugins easier to create, test, publish, update, and share.

  • Improve when and how models use plugins, from choosing the right plugin to completing a task. Work with Research to diagnose failures and measure improvements as models evolve.

  • Improve plugin reliability and interaction quality across ChatGPT and Codex, including interactive apps, with clear error messages and recovery paths.

  • Build consistent permissions, approvals, and admin controls that help individuals and organizations confidently adopt plugins.

  • Work with developers and partners to turn recurring problems into improvements to the platform, tooling, and documentation.

  • Collaborate across engineering, Product, Research, Security, and Trust & Safety to scale plugin infrastructure and deliver safe, reliable execution.

You might thrive int his role if you:

  • Care about product quality and can make complex capabilities feel intuitive, from discovering a useful plugin to completing a task with it.

  • Have strong opinions about APIs and abstractions, and can explain the tradeoffs behind your decisions. Experience with identity, permissions, or integration-heavy systems is especially valuable.

  • Enjoy talking with users and developers, understanding what they’re trying to accomplish, and turning recurring problems into product and platform improvements.

  • Can move between product questions and technical details, collaborate across teams, and take an ambiguous problem through to production.

  • Are comfortable working across web interfaces and backend systems. Experience building applied AI systems, diagnosing model–tool interactions, and measuring reliability and quality is especially valuable.

  • Have built products people rely on or software that other developers use, such as an API or SDK, an open-source project, a developer platform, or internal tools with real users.

About the Team

The Privacy Engineering team builds secure, reliable systems that help OpenAI meet its legal obligations while protecting user data. We partner closely with Legal and engineering teams across OpenAI to support lawful data access requests and other critical legal workflows. Our work turns complex, high-stakes processes into auditable and dependable technical systems with clear human oversight and strong privacy and security controls.

title: Software Engineer, ChatGPT Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

ChatGPT is a rapidly evolving system: new capabilities ship continuously, product surfaces change quickly, and usage patterns shift week-to-week. Supporting that pace requires infrastructure that can handle real production constraints—high concurrency, unpredictable traffic patterns, complex dependency graphs, and frequent change.

The ChatGPT Infrastructure team builds and operates the platforms that enable fast iteration without compromising performance or reliability. We design shared systems, data paths, rollout mechanisms, and reliability guardrails that teams rely on to ship changes to ChatGPT at scale.

We focus on high-leverage infrastructure: primitives and “golden paths” that incorporate operational lessons as defaults, so engineers don’t need to rediscover failure modes, latency pitfalls, or integration issues each time they build something new.

About the Role

We’re hiring Senior and Staff Engineers to design and build infrastructure systems that underlie ChatGPT and multiply the effectiveness of teams building user experiences.

This is not a support-only role. It’s a platform-building role: you’ll define interfaces, develop core abstractions, and create tooling to make safe, fast iteration the norm. Your work will reduce friction, prevent regressions, improve performance, and ensure systems scale gracefully as the product grows.

Where You Can Have Impact

  • You might work on one or more of the following areas (without being restricted to any single area):

    • Platform foundations & frameworks: Core libraries, service frameworks, and shared components that standardize system building, integration, and evolution.

    • Scalability & performance primitives: Patterns and infrastructure that reduce tail latency, improve throughput, and keep costs predictable as demand increases.

    • Reliability guardrails: Mechanisms that prevent outages by design—rate limiting, load shedding, dependency isolation, backpressure, safe fallbacks, and robust regression controls.

    • Developer productivity via golden paths: Paved roads for common workflows (data access patterns, service integration, request lifecycle) that are fast, safe, and easy to use.

    • Observability & debugging systems: Instrumentation, metrics models, and investigative tooling that turn vague symptoms (“it’s slow”) into precise, actionable diagnoses.

    • Safe change management: Deployment and rollout systems that support rapid iteration with confidence—progressive delivery, automated verification, and fast rollback strategies.

    • Interface and contract design across boundaries: Clean APIs and stable contracts that reduce coupling and enable independent evolution across a complex ecosystem.

    What You’ll Do

    • Build and evolve infrastructure platforms used by many engineers and services.

    • Translate real-world constraints into clean abstractions: simple APIs, enforceable contracts, safe defaults.

    • Drive improvements in reliability and performance through principled design, measurement, and iterative hardening.

    • Partner with engineering and product teams to identify systemic pain points and develop reusable solutions.

    • Own outcomes end-to-end: design → implementation → rollout → operational maturity.

    Qualifications

    Minimum Qualifications

    • Experience building and operating large-scale distributed systems in production (high throughput, concurrency, and failure handling).

    • Strong fundamentals in systems design, including caching, consistency, queueing/backpressure, and resilient dependency management.

    • Ability to reason about performance (latency distributions, tail behavior, bottlenecks) and translate analysis into concrete engineering work.

    • Track record of building platforms or shared infrastructure that improves velocity and correctness for other teams.

    • Excellent communication and collaboration skills—aligning on interfaces, navigating tradeoffs, and driving cross-team execution.

    Preferred Qualifications

    • Experience designing paved roads / golden paths (frameworks, libraries, self-serve tooling) that shape engineering behavior at scale.

    • Deep understanding of reliability techniques: graceful degradation, circuit breakers, load shedding, rate limiting, and fault isolation.

    • Experience building systems for safe iteration: progressive delivery, correctness checks, automated rollout gates, and production validation.

    • Strong instincts for API and contract design—how to create interfaces that are stable, evolvable, and hard to misuse.

    • Prior work that demonstrates “force multiplier” impact: enabling many teams via a small set of well-crafted primitives.

title: Compute Electrical Engineer, Robotics
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and advancing toward AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world environments. Working across the full model and systems stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the physical constraints of real-world systems to improve people’s lives.


About the Role

We’re looking for an Electrical Engineer to develop the AI inference compute systems that power OpenAI’s humanoid robots. This role combines compute architecture, high-speed digital design, onboard power electronics, and compact HDI PCB development.

We’re looking for a self-driven engineer who takes ownership from concept through deployment. Above all, you should enjoy hands-on engineering: bringing up boards, characterizing interfaces, and tracking challenging failures to their root cause.


In this role, you will:

  • Own compute hardware architecture and development, from component selection and schematic design through PCB layout, validation, and deployment.

  • Design and integrate high-speed interfaces—including PCIe, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, USB, and DisplayPort—balancing bandwidth, connectivity, power, and signal integrity.

  • Develop onboard DC-to-DC conversion and power distribution to meet efficiency, transient-response, sequencing, and power-integrity requirements.

  • Define HDI PCB stackups, dielectric materials, via structures, and routing strategies that balance electrical performance, manufacturability, reliability, and cost.

  • Lead bench bring-up and validation, including test planning, high-speed interface characterization, power measurements, and debugging through verified resolution.

  • Partner with thermal, mechanical, EMC, and software teams to integrate compute hardware into tightly constrained robotic systems.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 5+ years of experience developing compute hardware or similarly complex high-speed electronics, with demonstrated ownership of complete designs.

  • Bring strong hands-on measurement and debugging skills, including practical experience with oscilloscopes, probing techniques, and interface validation.

  • Understand high-speed digital interfaces deeply enough to make architectural tradeoffs and diagnose issues across hardware and software boundaries.

  • Have strong signal-integrity and power-integrity fundamentals, a solid foundation in power electronics, and practical experience designing complex HDI PCBs.

  • Can use a Linux shell, write simple shell scripts, connect over SSH, and perform basic Ethernet and network troubleshooting.

  • Take initiative, turn ambiguous requirements into concrete engineering plans, and follow through to deliver working systems.

Additional, preferred qualifications:

  • Experience designing around AI inference SoCs or accelerators, including their power, memory, and communication architectures.

  • Familiarity with how AI inference workloads map to silicon capabilities, including compute throughput (TOPS), DRAM bandwidth and capacity, and how workload requirements and DRAM technology choices affect achievable performance and performance per watt.

  • Experience bringing compute hardware into production and resolving fabrication, assembly, or test issues with manufacturing partners.

Reporting to the Head of GTM Partnerships, Europe you will manage and develop a regional team, own the regional partner business, and work alongside OpenAI Sales leadership and strategic partners to generate pipeline, advance complex pursuits, and drive revenue and customer adoption.

You will translate broader partnership priorities into a focused regional plan, set team goals and account coverage, and coach your team to engage the right partners at the right point in the customer journey. You will build relationships with partner field leaders and remain hands-on in priority pursuits, working with technical and delivery teams to turn commercial commitments into sustained customer value.

You will be accountable for both regional business performance and the success of your team. We are looking for an experienced people manager who can hire and develop talent, establish clear expectations, manage performance, and build a culture of accountability, collaboration, and customer focus.

In This Role, You Will:

  • Drive regional commercial outcomes across partner-sourced and partner-attached pipeline, bookings, production adoption, and expansion, with clear accountability for business performance.

  • Establish disciplined pipeline reviews, forecasting, business reviews, and performance reporting. Use evidence to assess partner contribution, diagnose underperformance, and adjust investments and priorities.

  • Navigate complex stakeholder relationships, commercial tradeoffs, and competing priorities with sound judgment, working across Legal, Security, Finance, and other teams as needed.

  • Hire, manage, coach, and develop a high-performing regional partner sales and development team. Set individual and team goals, provide regular feedback, manage performance, and support career growth.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have:

  • Significant experience in enterprise sales, partner sales, strategic alliances, or business development within cloud, AI, SaaS, or enterprise technology.

  • A track record of owning regional or segment-level business outcomes and delivering measurable pipeline, revenue, and customer growth through partners.

  • Demonstrated direct people management experience in partner sales, enterprise sales, alliances, or a related GTM function, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and team development.

  • Deep familiarity with cloud providers, global systems integrators, consulting firms, or technology partner ecosystems, and an understanding of how their field organizations sell and deliver.

title: Software Engineer, Model Runtime
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

You will build the model runtime within the inference engine that executes complex, frontier models at scale on OpenAI’s custom silicon. The runtime will sit between models running on the hardware and the upper layers of the cluster serving software stack, translating demanding inference workloads into efficient execution while optimizing for throughput, latency, utilization, and reliability.

You will work across model architecture, distributed systems, compilers, kernels, and silicon to design a production-grade runtime comparable in ambition to systems such as vLLM and SGLang, but customized and optimized for OpenAI’s AI accelerator. Your work will shape how new model capabilities map onto the platform and how quickly custom silicon can deliver meaningful performance in production.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and implement the LLM inference runtime for frontier models running on custom silicon.

  • Build scheduling, continuous batching, memory management, KV-cache management, and execution orchestration for high-performance inference.

  • Develop distributed execution strategies across chips, hosts, and racks, including model partitioning, communication, and synchronization.

  • Optimize end-to-end latency, throughput, memory efficiency, and hardware utilization across diverse model architectures and serving workloads.

  • Partner with kernel, compiler, architecture, and silicon teams to co-design interfaces and remove performance bottlenecks across the stack.

  • Enable new model features, execution patterns, numerical formats, and hardware capabilities in a reliable production runtime.

  • Create profiling, observability, benchmarking, and performance-modeling tools that make runtime behavior measurable and actionable.

  • Debug complex correctness, performance, and reliability issues spanning model code, runtime software, communication layers, and hardware.

  • Turn workload insights into clear requirements for future generations of silicon and system architecture.

You might thrive in this role if:

  • Have strong systems programming experience in C++, Rust, Python, or comparable performance-oriented environments.

  • Have built or optimized runtimes, distributed systems, compilers, kernels, model-serving infrastructure, or adjacent systems software.

  • Understand modern LLM inference, including prefill and decode behavior, batching, KV-cache tradeoffs, and model parallelism.

  • Can reason quantitatively about latency, throughput, compute intensity, memory bandwidth, communication, and utilization.

  • Are comfortable profiling and debugging performance across multiple layers of a hardware-software stack.

  • Can design clean abstractions while retaining the low-level control needed to extract performance from specialized hardware.

  • Work effectively across model, systems, compiler, kernel, and hardware teams to drive ambiguous technical problems to closure.

  • Care about production quality, including correctness, observability, reliability, maintainability, and graceful behavior at scale.

title: Product Cost Management Lead - AI Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization is building the infrastructure foundation for frontier AI systems. The Supply Chain organization enables scalable, resilient, and efficient supply chains across custom silicon, systems, networking, memory, storage, and rack-scale infrastructure.

Our team connects engineering, supplier strategy, manufacturing, planning, deployment, and finance to make hardware cost, supply, and execution tradeoffs clear from early architecture through production and sustaining operations.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a Product Cost Management Lead to own the official costed bill of materials (BOM), system and cluster cost and price baseline, and platform-to-platform total cost of ownership (TCO) for our 1P AI infrastructure. You will turn component, system, POD, manufacturing, deployment, DC, service, and lifecycle inputs into a trusted view of product economics that informs technical and business decisions, including transition timing.

You will partner with Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, Manufacturing-partner management, Finance, Planning, Supply Chain Program Management, Operations Program Management, and infrastructure teams to evaluate engineering / design changes, compare alternatives, identify cost-reduction opportunities, and track realized benefits.

This is an individual contributor role with broad cross-functional ownership. The ideal candidate combines hardware cost expertise, rigorous modeling, sound judgment, and the ability to explain complex tradeoffs clearly to engineering, operations, and senior leaders.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the official costed BOM and system/pod roll-up by platform, generation, configuration, build phase, volume, and mix. Maintain version control and traceability to quotes, source owners, assumptions, and engineering revisions.

  • Publish and maintain the system/pod cost and price baseline, reconciling component pricing and manufacturing-partner inputs with approved configurations and planning assumptions.

  • Build platform-to-platform TCO comparisons covering component content, non-recurring engineering, tooling, manufacturing labor and overhead, yield, scrap, test, logistics, deployment, housing and site costs, power and cooling, networking, spares, service, warranty, and lifecycle costs.

  • Partner with housing and site teams to integrate their cost inputs into product economics, documenting scope, timing, allocation assumptions, and gaps so platform comparisons are consistent and avoid double counting.

  • Quantify the cost impact of engineering change orders and notices (ECOs/ECNs), architecture, specification, configuration, and qualification changes before approval. Assess recurring and one-time costs, implementation timing, inventory exposure, and expected benefits.

  • Develop a prioritized cost-reduction, value-engineering, and second-source opportunity funnel with Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, and manufacturing-partner management. Evaluate qualification costs, investment, payback, supply improvements, and execution risk.

  • Analyze actual, forecast, quoted, committed, and purchase-price costs against the baseline. Explain material variances, identify root causes, and track recovery actions with accountable owners and dates.

  • Build sensitivity and scenario analyses for supplier and manufacturing-partner options, capacity, volume and mix, yield, configuration, site, deployment timing, and lifecycle tradeoffs. Present clear recommendations with assumptions, confidence ranges, and decision deadlines.

  • Validate savings and cost avoidance with Finance and accountable source owners. Distinguish identified opportunities, approved actions, and realized benefits, including offsets and implementation costs.

  • Establish cost-data definitions, BOM hierarchy, allocation methods, currency and volume assumptions, refresh expectations, and change-control processes. Flag stale, incomplete, or unsupported inputs before they affect decisions.

  • Lead recurring product-cost and TCO reviews. Publish concise cost bridges, opportunity updates, risks, and decision packages while retaining the supporting detail needed for technical and financial review.

  • Build scalable models, reporting, and data workflows that improve baseline completeness, refresh speed, analysis turnaround, and decision quality as the hardware portfolio grows.

  • You will own integrated product economics and the cost-analysis methodology and the cost analysis itself. Strategic Sourcing and manufacturing-partner management retain commercial negotiations; Engineering retains design and qualification authority; DC and site teams own their source inputs; Finance retains budgets, accounting, and financial approvals; Planning owns the demand baseline; SCPM owns material readiness; and OPM owns operational execution.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Significant experience in hardware product costing, cost engineering, supply chain finance, manufacturing cost analysis, or a related role supporting complex technology products.

  • Experience building and maintaining multi-level costed BOMs, system cost roll-ups, and lifecycle or TCO models across product development, production ramp, and sustaining operations.

  • Strong understanding of hardware cost drivers, including component pricing, manufacturing labor and overhead, NRE, tooling, yield, scrap, test, logistics, and service costs.

  • Demonstrated ability to evaluate engineering changes, second-source options, and cost-reduction opportunities using comparable scenarios and transparent assumptions.

  • Advanced spreadsheet and quantitative modeling skills, with disciplined data reconciliation, version control, and source traceability.

  • Ability to turn incomplete or changing technical and commercial inputs into defensible analysis, identify uncertainty, and drive input gaps to closure.

  • Strong cross-functional influence and communication skills, including concise leadership recommendations and detailed working sessions with engineering, sourcing, manufacturing, and finance teams.

  • High ownership and sound judgment in a fast-moving environment with evolving requirements and competing priorities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with AI infrastructure, hyperscale data centers, custom silicon, servers, networking, storage, or rack-scale systems.

  • Experience analyzing JDM, CM, or ODM cost structures and open-book manufacturing models.

  • Familiarity with DC and site economics, power and cooling, deployment timing, spares, and service costs in infrastructure TCO.

  • Experience with ERP, MRP, and PLM systems, BOM change control, and business intelligence or automation/AI tools.

  • A background in engineering, finance, supply chain, manufacturing, or a related analytical discipline.

What Success Looks Like

  • Teams use a complete, current, and traceable costed BOM and system/pod baseline as the source of truth for product economics.

  • Platform TCO comparisons use consistent scope and assumptions, with inputs validated by their owners.

  • Material engineering and sourcing decisions include timely cost-impact analysis and explicit tradeoffs.

  • Cost variances have clear explanations, accountable owners, and recovery actions; savings and cost avoidance are validated.

  • Leadership receives clear recommendations, and cost-management processes scale with the complexity of the 1P hardware roadmap.

title: Partner Applied AI Engineer, Oracle and Cloud ISV
descriptionHtml:
About the team

The Applied AI Engineering team helps developers and enterprises deploy generative AI safely and effectively. We serve as trusted technical advisors, helping customers and partners move from early experimentation to production-scale AI systems.

As a Partner Applied AI Engineer focused on Cloud ISVs, you will work with Oracle Cloud, Snowflake, and Databricks to help customers adopt OpenAI. You will bring OpenAI capabilities to the applications, data platforms, and developer workflows customers already use, then turn successful deployments into approaches the field and partner teams can deliver independently.

About the role

We are looking for an experienced technical leader to work with partner architects, AI specialists, and sales teams across three distinct routes to market. You will lead technical work from joint account discovery and architecture through evaluation and production, alongside OpenAI account teams and partner sellers. You will help customers choose the right deployment and purchasing path for the workload, with clear ownership of security, billing, support, and operations.

In this role, you will:

Strategic partner engagement and influence

  • Build relationships with Oracle, Snowflake, and Databricks field leaders and technical teams. Shape joint account plans, identify the customer problem each partner can help solve, and prioritize opportunities with a clear path to production and reuse.

  • Oracle Cloud: Work with Oracle sellers on eligible, sales-managed Oracle Marketplace private offers for OpenAI API models, ChatGPT Work, and Codex. Distinguish procurement, billing, and eligible commitment drawdown from OpenAI-managed product access, inference, and support. Where customers build on OCI, design the application and data integration without assuming the model is hosted on OCI.

  • Snowflake: Work with Snowflake account and technical teams to qualify data and AI workloads where OpenAI models in Snowflake Cortex AI are a fit. Help customers evaluate use cases such as AI functions over governed data, search, analytics, and agents. Confirm model and regional availability, data boundaries, and operating requirements. Distinguish Snowflake-metered Cortex usage from a customer application that calls OpenAI directly.

  • Databricks: Work with Databricks sellers and solution architects on three joint plays: developer workflows with Codex and Unity AI Gateway, enterprise insights with ChatGPT and Genie where supported, and GPT-powered applications and agents with Mosaic AI Model Serving, Agent Bricks, and Databricks Apps. Validate each route against the customer’s governance and deployment requirements. Distinguish Databricks-billed usage from direct OpenAI billing and confirm commercial eligibility and attribution before making commitments.

Complex deal leadership and execution

  • Lead technical discovery, architecture, prototyping, evaluation, and production readiness. Agree with both account teams on what the customer will deploy, how success will be verified, and who owns the next step.

  • Validate model and feature availability, identity and network boundaries, data handling and residency, capacity, metering, and support ownership. Work with Alliances, Sales, and Billing Ops on technical readiness without taking ownership of pricing, terms, offer acceptance, or billing approvals.

Solution architecture and hands-on building

  • Build reference implementations with OpenAI APIs and partner-native capabilities, such as OCI application and data services, Snowflake Cortex AI, and Databricks Mosaic AI Model Serving. Use the appropriate integration path for the workload and validate permissions and data movement before deployment.

  • Put evaluation, observability, and deployment practices in place to measure quality, safety, reliability, latency, cost, and real workload usage.

Ecosystem enablement and scale

  • Create demos, workshops, reference architectures, and playbooks that partner engineers, field teams, and systems integrators can use independently. Pair on early deployments, then hand off proven patterns with clear prerequisites and support paths.

Cross-functional leadership and feedback

  • Work with Alliances, Sales, Product, Engineering, and Enablement to resolve blockers. Turn patterns across accounts into specific product feedback backed by evidence, and keep field guidance current on what is supported, what is limited, and what is not yet available.

You'll thrive in this role if you:

  • Have substantial experience leading technical engagements with enterprise engineering and business leaders across pre- and post-sales.

title: Early Access Deployment Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About the Team
The Early Access Program (EAP) team leads high-impact alpha programs at the intersection of customers, Product, Research, Engineering, GTM, Security, Legal, and launch teams. We partner with customers to test emerging capabilities with real-world use cases, surface actionable insights, and support launch decisions.

Our team is made up of builders who learn quickly, collaborate deeply, create clarity in ambiguity, communicate openly, and iterate constantly.

About the Role
We’re hiring an Early Access Deployment Engineer to lead technical engagements with customers who are leveraging our frontier capabilities to solve real-world use cases. You will work at the earliest—and often messiest—stage of development, when capabilities are still unclear, tooling and processes are evolving, and the path from promising technology to a valuable real-world application has yet to be defined.

You will be a hands-on builder, problem solver, and technical partner to customers and our research/product team. You’ll push beyond initial assumptions, identify high-value use cases, prototype solutions, design useful evaluations, and troubleshoot what is and is not working.

Managing multiple customer engagements at once, you will help customers navigate ambiguity and difficult technical decisions while translating their experience into clear, actionable feedback for Research and Product.

You will also own the end-to-end execution of early access programs—from onboarding customers, supporting live experimentation, synthesizing findings, and informing launch decisions. You’ll collaborate deeply with Research, Product, Engineering, Applied Evals, GTM, Legal, Security, Marketing, and other launch partners to create clarity, manage risk, and keep programs moving through changing conditions.

Success in this role means turning frontier capabilities into real-world customer value and high-quality research signals. You will develop reusable technical approaches from early deployments, improve how OpenAI learns from customers, and provide strong PoV, based on customer feedback, on what should be built, refined, or scaled.

This role is based in San Francisco. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Engage deeply with strategic customers during the earliest alpha stages to understand their goals, workflows, technical constraints, and highest-value opportunities.

  • Translate emerging and ambiguous model capabilities into scoped use cases, working prototypes, and clear success criteria.

  • Prototype rapidly with customers, Product, and Research through experiment-driven iteration.

  • Design and support evaluations that reveal model behavior, solution quality, workflow impact, and failure modes.

  • Evaluate and troubleshoot based feedback across product, model behavior to determine patterns and gaps

  • Own early access program execution end to end, from customer onboarding and live experimentation through synthesis and launch decisions.

  • Align Research, Product, Engineering, GTM, Legal, Security, Marketing, and launch teams by communicating risks, tradeoffs, and recommendations clearly.

  • Codify architectures, evaluation methods, technical patterns, and program learnings into reusable playbooks that improve future deployments.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 4+ years of software engineering or equivalent technical experience, including meaningful customer-facing delivery and ownership of production systems.

  • Have a track record of rapidly turning ambiguous ideas into working prototypes and carrying the strongest approaches through to reliable solutions. Can demonstrate examples of systems thinking.

  • Be proficient in Python and/or JavaScript or TypeScript, comfortable across modern front-end and back-end development, and familiar with cloud deployment.

  • Bring practical AI and LLM depth, including experience reasoning about model behavior, designing evaluations, and building production-oriented AI applications.

title: Software Engineer, Codex Cyber
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Codex is OpenAI's software engineering agent. Codex Security extends that work into one of the most important product areas in AI: helping organizations find, validate, prioritize, and fix real vulnerabilities in the software they build and depend on.

The Codex Cyber team is building the product and platform foundations for AI-native application security. This includes Codex Security product experiences, cloud-based security analysis, platform controls across Codex, customer deployment and support tooling, and infrastructure that helps security researchers and cyber models improve over time. The team is early, small, and growing quickly, with a mandate to move fast and hire exceptional builders.

About the Role

We are looking for software engineers first: strong full-stack or product-minded generalists who can own ambiguous product and platform problems end to end. Security experience is helpful, and security curiosity is important, but this is not a role for security specialists who only occasionally write code. The right person is an excellent builder who is excited to work in security and can turn complex research, product, and customer needs into reliable systems.

You will work across user-facing product surfaces, developer workflows, backend services, security analysis pipelines, cloud infrastructure, and internal tooling. You may build features that make Codex Security more useful for application security teams, systems that scale cloud-based security analysis, platform controls that make agentic coding safer, or infrastructure that helps security researchers and models become more effective. You will collaborate closely with engineering, product, security research, infrastructure, and customer-facing partners as Codex Cyber becomes a major product and platform investment for OpenAI.

In this role, you will:

  • Build end-to-end product features for Codex Security, from developer-facing interfaces to APIs, backend services, and workflow tooling.

  • Own ambiguous 0-to-1 projects across product pods, platform security controls, customer deployment workflows, and cyber model infrastructure.

  • Design scalable, observable systems for long-running analyses across large codebases and enterprise environments.

title: Product Manager, Frontier Risks Safety
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Frontier Risks Safety team sets out safety requirements and executes planning for frontier model launches, including biological and cyber risks and government models. We work across research, engineering, and policy to assess risks, define and validate safeguards, and drive safety readiness throughout the model development and deployment process.  We also help shape frontier trusted-access programs, ensuring that access to advanced capabilities is supported by appropriate safeguards, clear requirements, and rigorous evaluation.

 

About the Role

As a Product Manager on the Frontier Risks Safety team, you will own product strategy, requirements, and delivery for initiatives that mitigate frontier AI risks and enable responsible access to advanced capabilities.  

You will partner with researchers, engineers, policy teams, and independent experts to identify the most important problems to solve, translate research and risk assessments into product requirements, and prioritize what to build.  You will guide work from discovery through deployment and iteration, making tradeoffs explicit and measuring whether the resulting safeguards and workflows address the risks they are intended to mitigate.

We’re looking for people who combine strong technical judgment, experience building and shipping complex technical products, and a commitment to AI safety. You should be comfortable working through uncertainty, engaging deeply with research, and adapting direction as capabilities, evidence, and user needs evolve.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 

In this role, you will:

  • Set product strategy and priorities. Develop a shared understanding of frontier risks, deployment needs, and gaps in safeguards. Own the roadmap for mitigations, prioritizing investments based on risk, evidence, technical feasibility, and the value the underlying capabilities enable for users.

  • Drive frontier trusted-access programs. Ensure defenders and scientists have access to the frontier capabilities they need to strengthen security and accelerate scientific discovery.

  • Turn safety needs into product requirements. Work with model teams, safety researchers, engineers, and policy partners to translate threat models, evaluation findings, and user needs into clear requirements, acceptance criteria, and measurable outcomes.

  • Drive safeguards from concept to deployment. Partner with research and engineering teams to turn promising safety approaches into effective mitigations across models and products.  Resolve product and technical tradeoffs, manage dependencies, and drive delivery of improvements that close material safety gaps.

  • Own risk-area safety readiness. Own risk assessments and safeguard plans for launches in your area.  Define the requirements and evidence needed for readiness reviews with technical partners, surface unresolved risks early, and bring clear recommendations to accountable safety and deployment decision-makers.

  • Use evaluations to guide product decisions. Partner with researchers to prioritize capability evals, alignment and control assessments, adversarial testing, and safeguard stress-testing, including for autonomous and multi-agent systems.  Assess what the evidence establishes, where uncertainty remains, and how findings should change the roadmap.

  • Align teams and communicate decisions. Build alignment across research, engineering, product, and policy on goals, priorities, and tradeoffs.  Resolve blockers, establish clear ownership, and communicate results, limitations, and remaining risks through decision documents, launch reviews, and contributions to system cards and assessment reports.

 

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 5+ years of product management experience, or equivalent experience owning the direction and delivery of complex technical products.

  • Have defined and shipped products or systems with researchers and engineers, particularly in AI, cybersecurity, biosafety, or another field where failures can have serious consequences.

  • Can turn ambiguous risks and user needs into a clear product strategy, prioritized roadmap, actionable requirements, and measurable outcomes.

  • Understand frontier AI safety concepts, including capability evals, alignment, control, monitoring, and safeguard robustness, and can engage substantively with technical teams.

  • Can assess what eval results do and do not establish, including methodological limitations, uncertainty, and the difference between model capability and real-world risk.

  • Exercise sound judgment when evidence is concerning or incomplete, make practical tradeoffs, and escalate unresolved risks constructively.

  • Have worked extensively across research, engineering, and product teams and can build alignment with policy and communications partners.

  • Communicate complex technical work and product decisions clearly, including disagreement, negative results, and remaining uncertainty.

title: Technical Threat Investigator, Threat Intel Engineering
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Security is at the foundation of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The Threat Intelligence team protects OpenAI’s technology, people, research, and infrastructure by proactively identifying and disrupting adversaries who seek to compromise our systems or misuse our models. We investigate sophisticated threats, build tooling to scale and augment analysis, and deliver intelligence that shapes security strategy and equips leadership with timely, risk-aware insights. We combine technical depth, investigative rigor, and strong cross-functional partnerships to uncover threats and drive impact across OpenAI’s security and research organizations.

About the Role

As a Technical Threat Investigator at OpenAI, you will help protect the company from sophisticated adversaries targeting OpenAI and the broader ecosystem, as well as those attempting to misuse our models in support of cyber operations.

This is a deeply investigative role. You will independently conduct complex, end-to-end investigations into capable threat actors to understand their behavior, infrastructure, emerging techniques, and how AI is integrated into their workflows. You’ll use these insights to proactively identify malicious activity and drive detection, disruption, enforcement, and safety improvements across the company.

You’ll translate your investigative findings into durable solutions that scale impact. You’ll build and own lightweight tooling, automate where it matters, and create AI-assisted workflows to make investigations faster, more repeatable, and more effective over time.

In this role, you will:

  • Conduct deep, end-to-end investigations into sophisticated threat actors interacting with OpenAI’s models, products, and broader ecosystem.

  • Think like an adversary — model attacker behavior, anticipate misuse patterns, and proactively hunt for, identify, and disrupt malicious activity.

  • Leverage internal telemetry, OSINT, vendor data, and in-house safety systems to produce high-confidence findings on adversarial use of our models in cyber operations, platform abuse, and threats targeting OpenAI.

  • Translate investigative findings into concrete improvements across detection, enforcement, intel, and safety pipelines.

  • Build tooling, scripts, automations, and agentic workflows that scale investigative throughput and reduce manual effort.

  • Prototype solutions in ambiguous and emerging problem spaces, including new product surfaces, novel attacker behaviors, and areas where existing coverage may be limited.

  • Partner closely with teams across Security, Safety Systems, Product Policy, and Integrity to operationalize findings and drive meaningful outcomes.

  • Produce clear, high-signal written outputs and recommendations that inform decision-making across technical and executive stakeholders.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Experience in threat intelligence, incident response, offensive security, or a closely related field.

  • Solid experience investigating sophisticated threat actors, including model misuse, platform abuse, or other adversarial activity in complex environments.

  • A strong understanding of adversary behavior, infrastructure, and tradecraft, and the ability to apply that understanding to proactive investigations.

  • Demonstrated ability to independently drive deep technical investigations from ambiguous signals through to clear, actionable findings.

  • Experience using AI to extend or accelerate investigative workflows.

  • Strong scripting ability and comfort building lightweight automation, investigative tooling, or workflows that improve scale and repeatability.

  • Strong ability to leverage telemetry from diverse systems and vendors to drive investigations, including directly querying, extracting, and stitching together data where needed.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, especially the ability to translate technical investigations into high-signal outputs for diverse stakeholders.

  • Comfort operating independently in ambiguous, fast-moving problem spaces with minimal oversight.

This is a remote role with close collaboration required across teams in the US and UK. While the role is remote, regular in-person engagement with our San Francisco (SF) headquarters will be expected. Relocation assistance is available for candidates who wish to relocate to SF.

About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. This long-term undertaking brings together the world’s best scientists, engineers, and business professionals into one organization.

In pursuit of this mission, our Go To Market (GTM) team is responsible for helping customers learn how to leverage and deploy our highly capable AI products across their business. The team is made of Sales, Solutions, Support, Marketing, and Partnership professionals that work together to create valuable solutions that will help bring AI to as many users as possible.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a VC Partnerships Lead to join our Startups team in Asia-Pacific. In this role, you will build and manage senior relationships with leading venture capital funds, accelerators, and startup ecosystem partners, with the goal of helping high-potential startups adopt and scale with OpenAI’s products.

Many of the most important AI-native companies will be built by startups. You will work with investors, founders, and internal OpenAI teams to identify promising companies, support their technical and commercial success, and create repeatable programs that expand OpenAI’s reach across the regional startup ecosystem.

Success in this role requires a distinctive combination of ecosystem credibility, commercial judgment, technical fluency, and operational rigor. You should be comfortable working with founders and investors, designing scalable partner programs, and traveling frequently across the Asia-Pacific region.

In this role, you will:

  • Manage and develop a set of partner-level relationships with top venture capital funds, startup accelerator programs, and other partners in the startup ecosystem

  • Be responsible for adoption and revenue growth for OpenAI’s APIs and applications (e.g. Codex), especially across early-stage companies

  • Work closely with Account Directors to identify and serve high-potential startups

  • Collaborate cross-functionally to design and execute 1:1, 1:few, and 1:many technical engagements with startup teams

  • Represent OpenAI at startup ecosystem events and speaking engagements

  • Develop insights into trends in startup ecosystems based on quantitative metrics and qualitative observations

  • Lead programmatic engagement of “long tail” early-stage companies

  • Serve as an advocate for improving the startup experience building with OpenAI, synthesizing product feedback from insights captured from our work with startups

Qualifications:

  • Passion for the startup ecosystem and supporting the growth of fast-growing companies

  • Experience owning revenue and other business outcomes

  • Background as a founder of a venture-backed startup, a venture capital investor, or early employee at a fast-growing startup

  • Technical understanding of AI technologies and AI product landscape

  • 10+ years experience managing high-value external relationships (e.g., customers, partners, investors, Board of Directors) and working directly with founders and C-level executives

  • Communicating technical concepts to customers and internal stakeholders

  • Leading high-visibility customer engagements (e.g., conferences, 1:many events, product launches, etc.)

  • High degree of comfort for gathering, distilling, and processing complex market (industry, competitor, customer, prospect) intelligence

  • Strong public speaking ability

  • Experience navigating different cultures and ecosystems, spanning everything between Japan, New Zealand, and Kazakhstan

  • [Strongly preferred] Professional proficiency in at least one relevant regional business language, such as Mandarin, Japanese, or Korean

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Are customer- and partner-centric. You are motivated to deeply understand customer and partner priorities and help them achieve their vision. You build strong relationships with executives and professionals across functions and serve as a trusted advisor.

  • Have a passion or deep curiosity in artificial intelligence. You embrace the opportunity to help deploy our technology in a way that benefits humanity. You’re excited to educate our customers on AI and how to plan for the future.

  • Are a builder. You are excited to impact how our company operates and scales. Your passion is building strong systems and processes from the ground up and executing them with precision.

  • Are excited by new challenges. You don’t have the answers to every question up front, but the process of solving them invigorates you. Bespoke issues requiring multidimensional knowledge excite you. You’re willing to experiment with new solutions.

  • Are a strategist. You deeply understand go to market best practices and raise the bar for our organization. You think and plan forward on the order of years and bring internal and external stakeholders along with your strategy.

title: Deal Lead, Special Situations
descriptionHtml:
About the team

Special Situations builds and grows new businesses, capabilities, and first-of-kind or highly strategic partnerships for OpenAI. We take on opportunities with meaningful upside where the offering, commercial model, partnership structure, or delivery approach still needs to be developed.

We bring together commercial judgment, operating experience, and industry expertise to turn these opportunities into results. Our work spans first engagements, expansion into new markets, and longer-term businesses and partnerships that we help build and scale.

About the role

We’re hiring a Deal Lead to develop and execute some of OpenAI’s most consequential commercial opportunities. You’ll identify where our capabilities can create meaningful value, shape what we offer and how we bring it to market, structure and negotiate partnerships, and drive the work from an initial thesis through launch and growth.

You’ll work closely with Product, Research, GTM, Finance, Legal, and delivery teams to connect customer needs, technical capabilities, and viable economics. This is a hands-on role: you’ll drive the commercial strategy and execution.

In this role, you will:

  • Identify and develop high-value opportunities across industries, markets, and emerging capabilities, translating customer needs into concrete AI use cases and commercial opportunities.

  • Shape new offerings and business models: define who we serve, what we offer, how we price it, and how we bring it to market.

  • Originate and grow customer and partner relationships, building executive alignment around the opportunity, desired outcomes, and path forward.

  • Work with FDEs, researchers, Product, and GTM teams to prioritize use cases and define scope, success criteria, resourcing, and a viable delivery approach.

  • Structure and negotiate complex partnerships, including revenue sharing, royalties, outcome-based pricing, and other non-standard commercial arrangements.

  • Drive executive-level decisions on strategy, economics, resourcing, and risk, keeping internal teams and external partners aligned as the work evolves.

  • Drive commercial outcomes beyond signature, including launch, adoption, revenue, viable economics, and expansion.

  • Build on early successes to develop repeatable offerings and partnerships, continuing to lead strategic relationships or establishing clear ownership as they scale.

You may thrive in this role if you:

  • Have significant experience in business development, partnerships, corporate development, private equity, or founding roles where you personally led complex commercial opportunities from concept through execution.

  • Have originated, structured, and closed significant deals—and stayed accountable for what happened after signing.

  • Can turn an ambiguous opportunity into a clear commercial thesis, prioritized use cases, viable economics, and an executable plan.

  • Bring strong commercial and financial judgment, including experience designing pricing, evaluating business models, and negotiating terms that align incentives.

  • Learn unfamiliar industries quickly and bring relevant domain expertise, with an understanding of how sophisticated customers buy, partner, and deploy technology.

  • Work effectively with FDEs, researchers, engineers, and product teams to connect technical capabilities with customer value and realistic delivery commitments.

  • Build executive alignment across organizations, communicating opportunities, risks, and tradeoffs clearly and driving decisions when priorities differ.

  • Are equally comfortable shaping strategy and doing the hands-on work: customer discovery, financial modeling, proposals, negotiations, and resolving execution blockers.

  • Create structure and accountability across cross-functional teams without relying on formal authority.

  • Exercise sound judgment under uncertainty, adapting as evidence changes and recognizing when to invest more, change course, or walk away.

title: Security Incident Response Team Manager
descriptionHtml:
About the team

Ensuring that advanced AI benefits humanity requires protecting the research, infrastructure, and trust that make its development and deployment possible. OpenAI Security defends our model IP, people, products, and users against sophisticated adversaries across GPU supercomputing, multicloud environments, datacenters, and emerging agent systems. The Security Incident Response Team (SIRT) leads the response when those defenses are tested—establishing what happened, limiting harm, and strengthening our ability to protect frontier AI.

About the role

We’re looking for a hands-on technical leader to build the incident response team that protects OpenAI as AI capabilities and the threats surrounding them evolve. You will command consequential incidents, lead technically demanding investigations, and make containment and recovery decisions when evidence is incomplete and the stakes are high. You will also shape how frontier models change incident response: using OpenAI’s own technology to help responders connect evidence, test hypotheses, and act effectively at a scale that manual workflows cannot support. Partnering with Research, Infrastructure, Product Security, Enterprise Security, IT, and Engineering, you will build exceptional responders, dependable AI-powered capabilities, and stronger defenses through every investigation.

In this role, you will:

  • Hire, coach, and develop exceptional incident responders who combine investigative depth, engineering ability, and sound judgment. Build a team that challenges assumptions, surfaces uncertainty early, and uses AI to expand its capabilities. Develop technical leaders who can make and explain difficult decisions under pressure.

  • Lead incident command for complex threats to OpenAI’s research, products, and infrastructure. Establish severity and scope, coordinate investigation workstreams, and weigh containment options against ongoing exposure and disruption to research or production.

  • Build and ship agentic capabilities using OpenAI’s models for evidence collection, investigation context, response coordination, and bounded response workflows. Partner with platform engineers to integrate tools and data, evaluate accuracy and failure modes, and ensure reliable, auditable operation with human approval for consequential actions.

  • Set investigation standards for sophisticated adversaries and insider threats across identity, endpoints, cloud, Kubernetes, and large-scale compute. Help responders reconstruct activity, test competing hypotheses, preserve evidence, and make uncertainty explicit.

  • Drive incidents to verified closure. Work with accountable owners to validate containment and recovery, document remaining risk, and track corrective actions that reduce the likelihood or impact of recurrence.

  • Coordinate with engineering, infrastructure, legal, privacy, and other stakeholders throughout an incident. Give executives clear updates on impact, uncertainty, decisions, and the next update without overstating what the evidence supports.

  • Build sustainable on-call coverage, escalation paths, and handoffs across regions. Balance urgent response with training and planned improvements, and protect the team’s ability to recover after demanding incidents.

  • Build readiness into new research and infrastructure capabilities with their owners. Exercise playbooks, escalation paths, and containment options, including scenarios involving agents operating across systems at scale.

  • Turn incident evidence into stronger defenses with Detection Engineering, Threat Intelligence, Security Observability, and security platform teams. Identify what should have exposed an intrusion earlier, what prevented a faster or more confident investigation, and which capabilities would have changed the outcome. Translate those findings into tested improvements with clear owners.

  • Prioritize improvements using incident outcomes and readiness evidence. Measure response quality and effectiveness, make tradeoffs explicit, and address recurring friction without reducing success to ticket volume or speed alone.

You might thrive if you:

  • You are motivated by the responsibility of protecting frontier AI. You want to understand how powerful new systems can fail or be compromised, help their builders move forward securely, and use the same advances in AI to strengthen defenders.

  • You have managed security responders or a closely related technical operations team, with a record of hiring, coaching, delivering candid feedback, and helping people grow.

  • You bring strong AI fluency and an AI-first builder mindset. You have used models or agents to improve real investigation or response workflows and can show validated results. You understand their failure modes and pair ambitious automation with rigorous evaluations and human judgment.

  • You are a hands-on builder with deep investigation expertise across identity, cloud, host, and infrastructure systems. You can prototype tools, write scripts or code, and coach responders through difficult evidence questions, including unfamiliar parts of the stack.

  • You have commanded consequential incidents involving capable adversaries, leading technical teams and senior stakeholders from uncertain signals through verified recovery. You make timely, defensible decisions with incomplete information, recognize when new evidence requires a change in direction, and remain accountable for the consequences.

  • You communicate clearly with engineers, executives, and legal or privacy partners. You can explain uncertainty, document decision rationale, and keep stakeholders aligned as facts change.

  • You have improved on-call operations, response playbooks, or exercise programs, and understand how workload, handoffs, and team health affect response quality.

  • You can prioritize a small number of meaningful improvements, influence partners who own remediation, and follow through until the agreed outcome has been verified.

title: Treasury, Trade Finance & Cash Flow Forecasting
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI Finance is responsible for ensuring the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission.

The Treasury team is responsible for protecting liquidity, enabling scale, maintaining strong controls, and helping the company operate with clarity and resilience. We work across finance and operational partners to ensure funds move safely, visibility remains high, and Treasury infrastructure keeps pace with a fast-moving business. As hands-on operators and builders, we combine financial judgment with AI, automation, and data to solve problems faster, strengthen controls, and continuously improve how Treasury operates.

About the Role

We are looking for a senior hire to help structure financing for major deals, improve working capital, and lead cash forecasting and liquidity planning. Reporting to the Treasurer, you’ll partner with Compute and teams across OpenAI to design creative financing and payment solutions that support the company’s growth. AI and automation will be core to how you build and scale this capability.

This role can be based in San Francisco, CA, Seattle, WA, or New York, NY. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Structure and negotiate trade finance solutions that improve deal economics and manage risk.

  • Improve cash conversion by working with Billing, Collections, Accounting, and business teams to bill sooner, collect faster, improve supplier terms, and reduce unnecessary deposits or inventory commitments.

  • Free up cash and credit capacity by managing collateral, letters of credit, guarantees, and renewals.

  • Build direct cash forecasts by incorporating business-specific receipts and payments, compute commitments, and financing timing.

  • Partner with Treasury’s Investment team to determine liquidity buffers, investment decisions, and contingency funding plans.

  • Advise on deal structuring Compute, Finance, and Legal, then coordinate execution with Treasury Operations.

  • Improve e-commerce payment economics with Product, Payments, and Strategic Finance, balancing cost, acceptance, risk, and settlement timing.

  • Recommend billing, collection, prepayment, and credit terms for new business models, balancing cash protection with ease of purchase.

  • Use AI and automation to streamline contract review, credit support tracking, cash forecasting, and treasury workflows.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in corporate treasury or banking, including trade finance structuring, working capital management, and cash flow forecasting.

  • A strong track record of negotiating and implementing complex trade finance across multiple instruments.

  • Experience delivering measurable cash conversion improvements through billing, collections, supplier terms, or inventory.

  • Sound judgment on contracts, risk, and approvals, and the ability to explain trade-offs to senior leaders and align business, finance, and legal teams.

  • Built direct cash flow forecasts and reconciled them to an indirect forecast or cash flow statement, with a strong grasp of how commercial terms and balance sheet changes affect liquidity.

  • Leveraged AI or automation to improve finance workflows end-to-end. 

  • Experience in infrastructure, hardware, or other capital-intensive businesses, or familiarity with global e-commerce payments (preferred but not required).

title: Regional Client Partner, Ads Solutions
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure the responsible and widespread adoption of artificial intelligence. In support of that mission, the Ads Solutions team partners closely with advertisers to deeply understand their businesses and needs, helping inform the development of products and solutions that drive meaningful revenue growth and long-term success on the platform—while maintaining strong standards for user trust and platform integrity.

title: Software Engineer, Cyber Safeguards
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

Models are becoming increasingly capable—moving from tools that assist humans to agents that can plan, execute, and adapt in the real world. Mitigating the frontier risks resulting from these capabilities is paramount to OpenAI’s ability to continue deploying models safely.

The Preparedness team is dedicated to addressing these critical risks. Our work includes:

  1. Measurement. Monitoring and predicting the evolving capabilities of frontier AI systems.

  2. Mitigation. Keeping misalignment safeguards, alignment tools, and on track to adequately address extreme threats that might arise in the future.

  3. Coordination. Setting mitigation targets by maintaining OpenAI’s preparedness framework, and partnering with other staff to achieve these targets.

This is urgent, fast-paced work that has far-reaching implications for the company and for society.

We’re looking for a very senior, independent Software Engineer to lead the technical work behind cyber safeguard infrastructure in Preparedness. You’ll bring production-grade engineering discipline to systems that support everything from cyber evaluations and safeguard research internally to enabling the safe deployment of capabilities externally, while working closely with researchers and security partners.
