title: Integrations Architect - Enterprise Systems
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Supply Chain Technology team within OpenAI's Enterprise Platform & Technology organization builds the systems and data foundations that support our supply chain and partner operations. We connect enterprise applications, improve operational visibility, and automate workflows across planning, purchasing, manufacturing, inventory, fulfillment, and returns. We work closely with engineering and business teams to build reliable systems that can evolve with OpenAI's growth.

About the Role

We are seeking an Integrations Architect to set technical direction for enterprise integrations, with a strong focus on supply chain and external partner ecosystems. You will help evolve a growing integration portfolio into a scalable, maintainable foundation through clear architecture, reusable patterns, and strong engineering practices. You will also help establish shared integration architecture and reusable foundations needed to support Finance and Supply Chain systems.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will translate business processes into integration designs, evaluate existing implementations, challenge assumptions, and guide improvements from design through production. Your influence will extend across application engineers, integration engineers, platform teams, and business stakeholders.

You will own integration architecture and partner with the engineering team responsible for the shared integration platform. Through clear requirements, working implementations, and operational evidence, you will help shape capabilities that improve how integrations are developed, tested, deployed, observed, and recovered.

In this role, you will:

  • Own integration architecture across enterprise applications, custom services, and external partners, including e-commerce platforms, logistics providers, contract manufacturers, retailers, and distributors.

  • Translate supply chain processes into clear system boundaries, transaction flows, data ownership, interface contracts, and operational requirements.

  • Partner with Finance and engineering teams to establish reusable integration patterns connecting operational and financial systems, with clear data ownership, reconciliation, and auditability.

  • Assess existing integrations and lead a practical modernization roadmap that improves scalability, reliability, maintainability, and cost while sustaining business delivery.

  • Establish reference architectures, reusable connectors, API and event standards, data mappings, versioning practices, and documented design decisions. Lead design and code reviews and mentor engineers.

  • Select appropriate API, messaging, EDI, orchestration, and batch patterns, balancing platform capabilities with custom development and the needs of each business process.

  • Stay close to implementation by building Python services and reference solutions, reviewing code, resolving difficult production issues, and validating designs through tests and measurable behavior.

  • Define reliability and recovery patterns, including idempotency, retries, reconciliation, replay, and continuity planning. Establish operational objectives and ownership across system boundaries.

  • Enable observability that follows business transactions across systems, connecting technical execution to business outcomes and supporting diagnosis, safe recovery, and ongoing improvement.

  • Turn integration delivery experience into prioritized platform requirements and influence shared engineering roadmaps through prototypes, acceptance criteria, and evidence of value.

  • Enable effective AI-assisted development and agentic workflows through well-defined interfaces, testable behavior, explicit approvals, and controls over execution and cost. Apply MCP tools, plugins, or comparable approaches where useful.

  • Embed security, access controls, segregation of duties, auditability, and change management into integration design. Coordinate partner testing, cutover, and operational readiness.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Bring 10+ years of experience in enterprise integration engineering and architecture, including technical leadership for business-critical systems.

  • Understand supply chain processes well enough to independently translate purchasing, receiving, order management, fulfillment, and inventory needs into integrations and explain the operational impact of missing or incorrect transactions.

  • Can support integrations across Supply Chain & Finance systems, working with subject matter experts to translate business processes, reconciliation needs, and financial controls into reliable designs.

  • Have personally shaped architectures, improved existing implementations, and guided engineers toward reusable, maintainable solutions with measurable results.

  • Have deep experience across multiple integration platforms and approaches, including iPaaS and custom services, and can translate their strengths and limitations into useful platform requirements.

  • Are a strong Python engineer who can connect design recommendations to production code, automated tests, deployment practices, and troubleshooting.

  • Understand API and event design, asynchronous messaging, EDI, data contracts, authentication, transaction integrity, and failure recovery across distributed systems.

  • Have built and operated high-volume integrations and can reason about performance, capacity, reliability, observability, and operating cost.

  • Are comfortable with cloud infrastructure, containerized services, version control, CI/CD, and automated integration testing.

  • Can influence technical direction across teams, explain tradeoffs to business stakeholders, and mentor engineers without relying on reporting authority.

  • Work independently, navigate ambiguity, and take responsibility for outcomes from initial design through sustained operation.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Integrations with Oracle Fusion ERP or SCM and adjacent enterprise applications such as warehouse, transportation, planning, or product lifecycle management systems.

  • Shaping shared integration platforms, developer tooling, or self-service capabilities adopted by multiple teams.

  • Building MCP servers, plugins, or agentic enterprise workflows, and applying AI coding tools such as Codex with rigorous review and validation.

title: Applied AI Architect, Large Enterprise
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Applied AI Architect team partners with organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact. We work with customers across industries and digital-native businesses to identify where AI can create value, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption. The team brings together technical strategy, customer partnership, and practical deployment expertise, working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and specialist delivery teams.

About the Role

As an Applied AI Architect, you will be the senior technical owner for a named portfolio of customers and the primary technical counterpart to their leadership teams. You will act as the “CTO of your book of business”, shaping each customer's AI strategy and guiding their journey from pre-sales discovery and solution evaluation through deployment, adoption, and measurable business impact.

You will own the technical account plan across ChatGPT Enterprise, the OpenAI API, Codex, and other agentic AI solutions. In partnership with the Account Director, you will translate business priorities into a focused use-case portfolio, an actionable adoption roadmap, and a clear path to durable customer value and growth. The Account Director owns commercial strategy; you own the technical strategy, customer journey, and path to production value.

You will remain accountable for the technical outcome while bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, enablement, security, product, and partners to provide deeper expertise and execute work where needed. This role calls for strong industry fluency, sound architectural judgment, and the ability to move confidently between executive strategy and hands-on technical conversations.

This role is based in our Paris office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Serve as the primary technical advisor and long-term technical relationship owner for a named portfolio of existing customers and pre-sales prospects.

  • Partner with Account Directors on account strategy while owning the technical account plan, technical milestones, adoption priorities, and expansion opportunities.

  • Bring strong software and cloud architecture foundations, including APIs, distributed systems, data integration, identity, security, and privacy.

title: Engineering Manager, API Multicloud
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

API Multicloud partners with cloud service providers (CSPs) to bring OpenAI’s frontier models and APIs into the cloud environments where developers and enterprises already build. We own the API end to end across CSP platforms, from API integration and request routing through inference execution, capacity management, and day-to-day operations. Our mission is to make these capabilities available broadly and safely while preserving the reliability and developer experience customers expect from OpenAI.

Delivering that experience requires work across the stack: adapting API services and cloud-native integrations, bringing up model-serving environments, validating new releases, and operating the systems that connect customer requests to available capacity. We work directly with CSP engineering teams and partner closely with OpenAI’s inference, API, infrastructure, security, and Safety Systems teams. Together, we turn new model capabilities and partner requirements into dependable production services, with attention to performance, operational readiness, and efficient use of compute.

Our work contributes to OpenAI’s AWS partnership, including the launch of Daybreak Red and Daybreak Blue on Amazon Bedrock — and OpenAI’s newly announced Google Cloud partnership will bring our frontier models and Codex agentic workflows to Google Cloud’s Model Garden. These efforts let customers use OpenAI capabilities within the cloud infrastructure, security controls, and workflows they already rely on.

About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced Engineering Manager to lead the team responsible for building and operating OpenAI’s API across major cloud service providers. You’ll lead a team of engineers focused on establishing scalable, reliable, and efficient cloud deployment platforms that bring OpenAI’s frontier models to customers across multiple cloud environments.

In this role, you'll own the technical direction, execution, and operational excellence of the API Multicloud platform. You'll guide your team through complex infrastructure challenges, including deploying model-serving environments, scaling capacity, optimizing performance and utilization, and building reusable systems that enable OpenAI to expand across CSP platforms. You'll balance long-term architectural investments with the urgency of delivering new model capabilities and partner integrations.

You'll work closely with engineering leaders across inference, API, infrastructure, security, and Safety Systems, while building strong technical partnerships with CSP engineering teams. Your team will play a critical role in determining how quickly OpenAI can bring new models to market, how reliably those models operate, and how efficiently we scale our infrastructure across cloud providers.

  • Lead, mentor, and grow a high-performing engineering team responsible for building and operating OpenAI's API infrastructure across multiple cloud providers.

  • Set clear priorities, navigate ambiguity, and drive cross-functional execution while balancing near-term business needs with long-term technical investments.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • Experience leading, building, and developing high-performing engineering teams responsible for large-scale cloud infrastructure, distributed systems, or platform engineering.

  • Strong technical background in distributed systems and cloud infrastructure, with the ability to drive architectural decisions and provide technical guidance to senior engineers.

  • Experience building and operating production infrastructure on major cloud platforms such as AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure.

descriptionHtml:
About the Team

OpenAI's Legal team works on the legal questions that arise from developing and deploying advanced AI. Our Security and Public Sector Legal team helps protect OpenAI's people, technology, and services and supports their safe and responsible use. We partner closely with technical and operational teams to provide clear advice, navigate sensitive matters, and build practical safeguards.

We are seeking an Associate General Counsel to advise across national security, cybersecurity, and platform abuse investigations and help build the programs and processes that support our work as OpenAI continues to scale. You will combine exceptional legal judgment with substantial in-house experience, turning complex requirements into effective day-to-day operations.

You will own a varied portfolio, lead sensitive matters, and help teams move from individual solutions to consistent, well-run programs. We are looking for someone who enjoys both counseling on difficult questions and doing the detailed work of implementation: defining responsibilities, securing alignment, developing useful processes, and making sure they work in practice.

You will report to the Deputy General Counsel leading Security and Public Sector Legal and work closely with Security, Product Policy, Global Affairs, and colleagues across Legal.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA or Washington, DC. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

title: Owner-Furnished Equipment (OFE) Demand Planner
descriptionHtml:
About the team

OpenAI’s Industrial Compute team builds the data center infrastructure that supports our research and products. Procurement and Sourcing partners with Engineering, Construction, Deployment, Finance, and suppliers to secure the critical equipment needed to bring new compute capacity online.

About the role

We’re hiring an Owner-Furnished Equipment (OFE) Demand Planner for OpenAI’s self-build data center portfolio. Long-lead equipment decisions often come before site schedules, designs, and funding are final. This role helps OpenAI make those decisions early enough to keep deployments on schedule.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own and publish the OFE demand baseline for self-build data centers. Translate the capacity roadmap and reference designs into equipment quantities and delivery windows by site, building, and phase.

  • Work backward from equipment need-by dates to set deadlines for design decisions, funding approvals, capacity reservations, and purchase orders.

  • Assess supply coverage with Supply Planning using supplier capacity and lead times validated by Sourcing and production and delivery commitments from Manufacturing Operations.

  • Lead planning reviews with Engineering, Construction, Deployment, and Finance to resolve changes in scope, quantities, and delivery dates. Escalate decisions that put deployment milestones at risk.

  • Model the schedule impact of supply shortages and recommend where to shift deliveries, reallocate equipment, or reserve additional capacity.

  • Provide the OFE demand baseline and forecast changes to the broader Compute Supply & Demand Plan.

Qualifications

  • Experience owning a demand, supply, materials, or integrated business planning process for complex hardware or capital equipment.

  • Sound judgment when inputs are incomplete or changing, with the ability to explain assumptions and uncertainty clearly.

  • Experience using supplier lead-time and purchasing data in a project-based planning environment.

  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to explain trade-offs clearly to technical and executive audiences.

  • Experience influencing decisions across teams and with external partners without direct authority.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience with data centers, critical facilities, industrial construction, or another capital-intensive, multi-site environment.

  • Familiarity with owner-furnished equipment or long-lead electrical and mechanical infrastructure.

  • Experience improving forecast accuracy, supply coverage reporting, or planning processes using ERP, planning, or analytics tools.

The Applied team works across research, engineering, product, and design to bring OpenAI’s technology to consumers and businesses.

We seek to learn from deployment and distribute the benefits of AI, while ensuring that this powerful tool is used responsibly and safely. Safety is more important to us than unfettered growth.

title: Researcher, Frontier Robustness
descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The Frontier Robustness team advances the science of securing frontier AI systems. We develop new methods to keep increasingly capable models contained, observable, and under human control, focusing on the sandboxes, shared research infrastructure, and protective systems used during model development and evaluation.

We use our most capable models to discover and combine weaknesses across the security stack, studying how they might escape containment, communicate through unauthorized channels, or evade monitoring. We turn these findings into new defenses and test whether protections hold as models, environments, and attack strategies change.

About the Role

We are looking for a researcher to develop and test new methods for securing frontier AI systems. You will investigate open-ended questions about model behavior, containment, and safeguards—designing experiments, building evaluations, and developing defenses where established approaches may be insufficient. You will work closely with the Security organization to define the problems and translate research findings into practical protections.

You will take research from an initial question and threat model through experiment design, reproducible findings, and tested defenses. You will write code, build tools and prototypes, and work closely with researchers and infrastructure owners to turn new ideas into safeguards that work in practice. This requires sound security judgment, comfort with uncertainty, and the ability to devise solutions to problems without established answers. This role is based in San Francisco.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and run experiments using frontier models and hands-on security techniques to discover failure modes in sandboxes, research infrastructure, and the services models can reach. Reproduce vulnerabilities and assess their impact.

  • Develop threat models and novel adversarial tests for attacks that cross multiple security boundaries, including sandbox escapes, unauthorized communication between agents, and access to sensitive data or systems through shared services.

  • Invent, prototype, and evaluate defenses that strengthen isolation and limit the impact of a compromised boundary. Study agent permissions and tool configurations to identify excessive access and build layered protections with infrastructure owners.

  • Develop and red-team model-based safeguards and monitors of model reasoning and actions. Investigate evasion, test new monitoring techniques, and measure when protections detect or prevent unsafe behavior.

  • Develop automated adversarial tests and repeatable evaluations to measure progress as model capabilities, configurations, and attack strategies change. Assess whether defenses generalize to new attacks, verify fixes, and identify regressions.

  • Partner across Research, Security, and infrastructure teams, including Agent Security, to prioritize risks and turn findings into deployed improvements while accounting for performance and researcher workflows.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have hands-on experience conducting research with large language models, including designing and running experiments and evaluating model behavior.

  • Can turn an open-ended question into a clear hypothesis, build reproducible experiments at scale, and use the results to develop or improve a method.

  • Can design rigorous evaluations, investigate unexpected results, and test whether findings hold across different models, environments, and attack strategies.

  • Write and debug code independently, build research tools and prototypes, and carry ideas through experimentation.

  • Bring practical security experience relevant to this work, such as sandboxing, vulnerability research, adversarial testing, or detection and monitoring.

  • Work effectively with Security and infrastructure partners to develop threat models, interpret findings, and turn promising research into deployed safeguards.

  • Experience with operating systems, containers or virtualization, distributed infrastructure, or AI agents would also be valuable.
